aspect.en: Only sign: cropped grass, slots in the mud, droppings, a game-trail worn through the brush.
A herd seen far off across open country, heads down, never approached.
Caught grazing, drinking at a ford, or a stag rubbing velvet from its antlers; it has not yet noticed him.
It catches his scent and bolts — a flash of rumps and a drum of hooves into cover.
A cornered or rutting beast turns and charges, horns or bulk lowered — give it weight, then let it pass or fall.
A fresh kill, scattered bones, pad-prints crossing the trail, or scat still warm.
A call in the dark — a howl, a cough, a yowl — close enough to raise the hair, the beast itself unseen.
A shape on a ridge or at the wood's edge, watching a moment, then gone.
It sees him first and melts away; only the swaying brush marks where it stood.
It shadows the march — never quite seen, always there — testing whether he is prey.
It breaks cover and comes in low and fast; this is a fight, not a fright.
A cry or wingbeat overhead — birdsong, an owl's call, the clap of a flock taking flight.
Seen on the wing or perched at a distance, a flash of colour or a circling speck.
Fishing a stream, mobbing a hawk, squabbling over carrion, hammering at bark — busy with its own life.
It startles up at his approach and is gone, leaving a settling of feathers.
A raptor stoops, or a blood-hungry flock descends — sudden violence out of the open sky.
A swirl in the shallows, a slick on the bank, fish-scales by a vanished fire.
A break of the surface, a fin, a dark shape gliding under the boat.
Fish rising at dusk, an otter at play, a great slow shape feeding along the bottom.
A nuisance of the crossing — leeches, snapping fish, something that fouls the ford.
It strikes from the water at whatever wades or trails a hand — a sudden, dragging menace.
Wreckage on the shore, a beast washed up half-eaten, water disturbed for no clear reason.
A vast shadow under the surface, a coil or a wake too large for any honest fish.
The water goes still and wrong, as though something below has marked the boat and waits.
It rises — tentacle, jaw or coil — and seizes from the deep; a true horror of the water.
A shed skin, a slither-track in dust or sand, a basking-stone lately vacated.
Seen sunning on a rock or rippling away through the grass.
Basking, swallowing prey, coiled in the shade — sluggish and unbothered if left be.
It flees underfoot, gone into a crevice before he can name it.
It strikes — fang or coil — fast and venomous; the danger is how late it is seen.
A chorus from the marsh at dusk, or a single croak swallowed by silence.
A bright, slick shape on a leaf or a log, jewelled and still.
Hunting flies at the water's edge, or massed in their breeding-season clamour.
Beautiful and best not touched — its skin or spit carries poison for any that handle it.
The rare deadly kind, met in numbers, turns the wet ground itself into a threat.
A paper nest in the eaves, a stripped field, a humming heard before anything is seen.
A torment of the march — biting flies, midges, a swarm that drives man and beast to distraction.
Bees at the clover, ants at their roads, a column crossing the path on business of its own.
A struck or disturbed nest erupts; the swarm comes as a storm of stings.
Webbing strung across the path, husks of drained prey, a wood gone silent and sticky.
Eyes in the dark and a stillness wrong for any forest — something patient overhead or ahead.
It paces them unseen through the branches, drawing the net of its web tighter.
It drops or rushes from ambush, fast and venomous, to bind and poison — a deadly thing.
Hoofprints and dung on a droving-road, a picket-line lately struck.
A wild herd running the open plain, manes streaming, or beasts grazing under herders' watch.
Grazing, watering, foaling — half-wild horses or the great beasts of the South at their ease.
The herd wheels and is gone, thunder fading across the grass.
A war-trained or maddened mount turns on him, or a great beast charges with terrible weight.
Tracks, a burrow-mound, gnawed nuts, a den lately used.
A small shape at the wood's edge or a head raised atop a mound, watching.
Foraging, denning, at play — busy and harmless, comic or wary by turns.
It freezes, then bolts for cover the moment it knows it is seen.
A bold or blood-hungry beast turns aggressor — rare, but not to be ignored.
Smoke from a hearth, cart-ruts, a field lately worked — folk near, but unseen.
Figures on a far road or ridge, about their own business, not approached.
Met at their work — herding, mending, driving cattle, making camp — noticed more than joined.
A short, wary meeting; a few words traded on the road, then each goes on.
They offer news, food, trade or a place by the fire — to take or to refuse.
Armed men bar the way or demand toll; a standoff that may yet come to blades.
They mean harm — a raid, an ambush, a robbery — and steel is drawn in earnest.
A sign meant to be missed: a mark on a tree, a path too well-kept to be chance.
Figures at the wood's edge or on a far hill, there and then not, as if the dusk moved.
Glimpsed at song, at the hunt, or tending some hidden work, unaware or unbothered by him.
He feels watched long before he is greeted; unseen eyes weigh him on their own ground.
A courteous, measured meeting — grace and reserve both, and few words wasted.
Counsel, healing, shelter or safe passage offered to one judged worthy.
Only the renegade or the hostile draws on him — swift, precise, and rare.
Pick-marks on stone, a spoil-heap, a guarded ore-road, a cold camp neatly struck.
A laden party on the road, or a watch posted at a mine-mouth, eyeing his approach.
At the march, the trade, or the work — blunt, busy, keeping their own counsel.
A gruff, guarded meeting; honest words, hard bargaining, slow trust.
Trade, news or the loan of a strong arm, offered once a man proves fair.
A patrol challenges him sharply at the gate of their holds, hands near their axes.
A trim hedge, a wisp of pipe-smoke, a garden too neat for the wild — folk near, well-hidden.
A small figure that ducks from sight the moment it is noticed.
At a meal, a chore or a quiet errand, soft-spoken and easily overlooked.
Gone into the bracken before he is sure they were ever there.
A shy, kindly word or two from folk who would rather be left to their own business.
Trampled ground, a reeking dead fire, gnawed bones, the stink of them on the wind.
Harsh voices, a drum, a tramping in the dark — heard before they are seen.
A file of them on a far slope or skyline, moving by night, shunning the open sun.
He is being hunted: sign too fresh, the wood too quiet — they know he is here.
A patrol picks up his trail and dogs it, closing slowly through cover.
They block a pass or a gate and call challenge, jeering, hungry for sport.
They rush him with blade and bow — no parley, only slaughter or capture.
A reeking den of cracked bones, uprooted trees, boulders flung and shattered.
A heavy crashing and a dull bellow somewhere off in the dark.
A huge, hunched shape against the night, or a man-shaped stone that was not there before.
It lumbers after him through the dark, slow but tireless, between him and the open.
It comes on with club or fist, vast and murderous — to be outlasted or outrun more than fought.
Footprints a man could lie in, a hillside re-shaped, boulders left where none should be.
A booming far off in the heights — laughter, or stones flung in some careless game.
A vast figure striding a distant ridge, indifferent as weather.
Roused or at play, it hurls rock and stride — deadly through sheer size, malice or none.
Scorched ground or rimed stone, a reek of sulphur or cold, a lair of gnawed and gilded bone.
A grinding deep in the rock, a hiss, the slow drag of something immense.
A shape aloft against the cloud, or a long ridge of scale that the eye first takes for stone.
It is awake and aware — the air itself seems to listen — and it is in no hurry.
Fire, frost, fang or flood — it falls upon him with the ruin of a small war.
A wrongness in the air, a heat or a cold and a dread that has no source he can name.
A shape of shadow and flame, or a stillness shaped like a man that should not be.
It knows he is there and lets him feel it — dread laid on him like a hand.
It looses its full terror — a thing to flee, not fight, and barely that.
A sudden chill, a silence with a weight to it, the sense of being watched by what has no warmth.
A barrow lid ajar, cold lights over the bog, a grave that does not look quite closed.
It is simply there — at the treeline, across the water — regarding him without fear or haste.
It comes on without sound or threat-display, unhurried, as if it has all of time — which it has.
It lays cold hands or wields fear itself; no roar, no warning, only the reaching.
A figure on the road that seems ordinary until something about it does not add up.
Found at some work of their own — among beasts, among trees, among books — half in another world.
Speech that carries more than its words; counsel, riddle or warning from one far older than he seems.
Aid given freely and strangely — a rescue, a gift, a door opened — on terms of their own.
A vast, malevolent attention turned his way; dread radiating from a hidden seat of power.
Taken at first for a worn statue, a pillar, a heap of stone — until the eye doubts it.
Old guardian-marks, a threshold too deliberately placed, a watchful carved face.
A sense that the stone has noticed him, though nothing yet has moved.
Roused, it rises and strikes as living stone or iron — what was scenery is now the enemy.
Trees that lean the wrong way, a wood that seems to have shifted when his back was turned.
A creak and groan with no wind behind it, almost like slow speech.
A great tree-shape moving, slow and deliberate, where no tree should walk.
The wood is awake and aware of him; patience and old anger in the gloom.
Roused against those who do harm, they close and crush — slow, irresistible, final.
Part of the land's mood — blossom, bracken, a drift of flowers — colouring the scene, not acting in it.
Noticed for use or beauty: a healing herb by the path, fruit in season, a fair bloom.
It bars or pains the way — thorns, clutching briar, a reek that sickens — or it is poison to touch or eat.
The character of the wood itself — its shade, its gloom, its openness — setting the mood of the march.
Marked for what it gives: timber, mast, fruit, or a landmark grove that tells him where he stands.
Dense, dark or tangled growth that slows the way and closes the sky overhead.
A plenty of the land — food, forage, water, fuel — to be gathered or passed by.
A sign of worked, settled country: tended fields, herds, hives, diggings, and the folk they imply.
What plenty draws: foragers, beasts or raiders gathered to the same bounty.
Shelter or salvage offered — a roof, a hearth, a wall against the wind, a thing worth finding.
A landmark that tells where he stands and what once stood here; the place colours the hour.
It is held or used — folk dwell, guards watch, work goes on — and he must reckon with them.
It is not as empty as it looks; something keeps it, and weighs his coming.
A haunt of beasts, outlaws or worse, where shelter and danger share the same walls.
A peril of the land made plain — a drop, a bog, rotten ice, foul air — read in time and gone around.
The way itself fights the march: treacherous footing, blocked passage, ground that cannot be trusted.
It strikes without warning — a slide, a flood, a fall, a fume — and the land turns killer in a breath.
a troll blocks the road or emerges from cover — slow, deliberate, not yet committed to violence
a troll occupied with its own concerns addresses the traveller with blunt curiosity rather than threat
a ghost or wight speaks — always with the specific ache of something unfinished
an undead entity bars passage directly — bound to a threshold, a barrow, or an oath
an Ent or awakened tree speaks — the question comes slowly and the expectation of a real answer is absolute
orcs address the traveller directly — not yet attacking, assessing, or delivering a message
orc activity visible at a distance — a column, a camp, scouts on a ridge — without direct contact
a Maia presence watches from a distance — felt more than seen, its attention specific and unmistakable

disposition.en: Recognizes him by posture and gear before he is close enough to speak. Waits without hand on weapon.

presence.en: Patrol on the Weather Hills is short two men — pulled north without explanation ten days ago. He has been running the circuit alone. Asks if the north reported anything unusual.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He shares the gap in coverage as a peer, not a report. Expects the traveller to know what it means.

disposition.en: More guarded than the greeting would usually warrant. Something has made him careful with his own.

presence.en: A supply cache on the red hills road — three nicks on the eastern stone — was emptied three weeks ago and not replenished. Someone used it and did not report it. The cache-keeper in Bree does not know who.

situation.en: A breach in their network, reported to the only other Ranger he has trusted with it. The breach could mean desertion, capture, or something else entirely.

disposition.en: Tense in a way that has become posture. Has been reading a compromised landscape for too long alone.

presence.en: Three farms on the Minhiriath road gone dark in sequence — doors open, fires cold, animals still penned. Moving south to south-east. Not raiders — something methodical.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: He wants the traveller on the northern circuit while he continues south. He cannot cover both and he does not trust anyone else he has met on this road in a month.

disposition.en: Formal. The posture of a man who was told to show respect to Elves and has remembered it.

presence.en: He asks whether she has seen movement further north. Three abandoned steadings he does not remember being empty before. He has no other Elf-source on this circuit.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He is doing his duty. She is a resource he would not normally have. There is no warmth in it but the respect is real.

disposition.en: The caution is wearing thin. He has been alone long enough that the formal approach has cracked.

presence.en: He asks directly: did she know Cardolan, before. Not as a test — as a question from a man whose entire history is book-knowledge, standing in the place where it happened.

situation.en: He wants to know what it was actually like. She is the only person he has ever met who could tell him. He is slightly afraid she will refuse.

disposition.en: He watched her on the road for ten minutes before speaking. Something in the way she moves through a landscape of ruins stopped him from the usual approach.

presence.en: He asks, carefully, if she is well. The question lands differently than it should. He does not know why he asked it.

situation.en: The question is more perceptive than expected from a mortal on a cold road. She is not well. She is not going to say so.

disposition.en: They move through the dusk as if they belong to it. One pauses and looks at him for a long moment, then continues.

presence.en: They are heading west — always west, in the end. The one who paused has Rivendell-silver in his gear, a design he has seen in the archives at Fornost. He has read about this company. He did not expect to see them.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: They will not stop unless he speaks. The pause was acknowledgment, not invitation.

disposition.en: One of them has already turned to face the road where he is approaching, waiting.

presence.en: A patrol in the Trollshaws has gone silent — an Elven patrol, not a Ranger one. They noticed because the patrol was supposed to pass through the Elven road three days ago and did not. They are telling him because it is his circuit.

situation.en: They give him the information because he is Dúnedain and it concerns his land. Not a gift — what is done between those who watch the same darkness.

disposition.en: The company stops when they see her. Not in surprise — in recognition. Someone makes a sound that is not quite a word.

presence.en: One of them knows her name, not from meeting her but from a song about something she did in the First Age that she does not think of as notable. Hearing it described back to her is disorienting.

channel.en: Have them bring up an age-old loss — a drowned realm, a kinsman long dead — as though it were last night.

situation.en: They want to know where she is going. They mean it as kin-concern, not challenge.

disposition.en: The eldest of the group speaks, the others are quiet. Careful with her.

presence.en: He mentions someone who sailed — someone she knew. He says the name gently, watching her face, offering it as if asking whether she already knew. She did not.

channel.en: Have them bring up an age-old loss — a drowned realm, a kinsman long dead — as though it were last night.

situation.en: He is not being cruel. He thought she should know. She is not yet certain she is grateful.

disposition.en: One breaks away from the group and comes to her directly. The others continue without stopping.

presence.en: He says quietly that this company is the last to use this road for some time. He does not explain why. He looks at her the way you look at someone choosing to stand in a place others are choosing to leave.

channel.en: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

situation.en: He is not asking her to reconsider. He is witnessing her choice. The acknowledgment is both comfort and weight.

disposition.en: One steps into view deliberately and stops. Not a threat — an acknowledgment. He is letting him see.

presence.en: He leaves a carved marker at the trail junction — a Wose sign meaning this path is watched, use it. The marker was not there this morning.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: This is the Woses giving what they give: knowledge of the land, in their own language, to those who know how to read it.

disposition.en: Two of them moving parallel to the road, matching his pace exactly. Escorting without being asked.

presence.en: They stop when the road bends and a disturbed barrow-mound comes into view ahead. They will not go closer. The escort ends here and both of them know it.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They have told him what they can tell him. He continues from this point alone.

disposition.en: A low deliberate sound from the scrub — not voice, not animal. A warning.

presence.en: Something on the trail ahead that the Woses do not want him to walk into. They will not show themselves to explain what it is.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: The warning was given. The explanation was not. He has enough.

disposition.en: One is standing at the road's edge, so still she almost passed him. He is old — older than he looks.

presence.en: He carries a staff carved with marks she has seen before. Not Wose marks. Older ones. Marks that were used in the late First Age for a specific purpose that almost no one living remembers.

situation.en: He knows what those marks mean. She knows what those marks mean. They are possibly the only two on this road who do.

disposition.en: A group from the treeline, still and watching. Not decided yet whether to acknowledge her.

presence.en: One of the oldest wears a bone-carved token at his neck — made during the Wars of the First Age, for a specific purpose. The token should not exist anymore. She knew who made them.

situation.en: She has not seen one of those tokens in ages beyond counting. Its presence here, in T.A. 1950, worn by a Wose in Minhiriath, is something that requires more thought than she can give it right now.

disposition.en: One comes to the edge of the road and looks at her directly. The others stay back.

presence.en: He points — once, briefly — at the road ahead. Then at the sky to the north. Then he draws a specific shape in the air with one finger that she has not seen drawn by a living hand in two thousand years.

situation.en: Someone taught a Wose a warning-sign from the First Age. That is not possible through memory alone. Something showed it to him recently.

disposition.en: Names what he has, names what he needs. Expects the same. Will not haggle but will deal.

presence.en: He has current maps of the mine-tracks in the Misty Mountain foothills — not for sale, but tradeable for road conditions. He wants to know what the barrow-field road looks like right now.

channel.en: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.

situation.en: Exact, bounded, symmetrical. He will not give more than he gets and will not try to take more than offered.

disposition.en: Testing what the traveller knows before committing to anything.

presence.en: He found something in a collapsed shaft — old, made, pre-Númenórean. He will not describe it precisely until he knows who he is talking to. He asks first about the shaft's location to see if the traveller knows it.

channel.en: Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.

situation.en: He is deciding whether this is someone who can help identify old artifacts or someone who will try to take them.

disposition.en: Blunt. Not rude — constitutionally incapable of the social padding mortals use. Says what he means.

presence.en: He is looking for a specific vein on a map drawn before Moria fell. He asks, without embarrassment, whether she was alive when Moria fell and whether she knows what the landmarks on the map were called before they got their current names.

channel.en: Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.

situation.en: He does not know this is a strange question to ask. To him it is simply efficient.

disposition.en: Quieter than a Dwarf alone on the road usually is. Adjusting back to speech after a long time without it.

presence.en: He says, after a pause, that he came out of the western passages two weeks ago. Fast. He does not elaborate but his hands have not stopped moving since he sat down.

channel.en: Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.

situation.en: He is not going to say what was in the western passages. He is telling her he was there so she knows someone has been there recently.

disposition.en: Watching her the way someone watches a thing that has been around long enough to carry weight they cannot see.

presence.en: He asks point-blank if she knew Durin. Not which Durin — just Durin. He wants to know how old she actually is. He asks because something in the western passages bore a mark only someone who was there at the beginning would recognize.

channel.en: Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.

situation.en: He may be right that the mark requires a witness. She is not that witness — but she knows someone who was.

disposition.en: Gone into the bracken so fast he almost missed them. One small face still watching from cover.

presence.en: The face belongs to a Harfoot who has decided Rangers are safe but not comfortable. The look is someone waiting until he is well past before coming back out.

channel.en: Have them chatter about their hole, their garden, their kin and the doings of the next farm over.

situation.en: He is big and armed on their road. That is enough. He does not need to be a threat to be a problem.

disposition.en: Working at the bog's edge. Appear to be ignoring him. Are not.

presence.en: Two Stoors sorting a marsh catch. They have been camped here for weeks and know this bog the way a farmer knows a field. They will answer a direct question. They will not volunteer anything.

situation.en: They know about the ford. Whether they will say depends entirely on how he asks.

disposition.en: On the road alone with a pack that is too large for him. He does not flinch when the traveller comes around the bend.

presence.en: He is looking for a cousin who went east to trade and did not come back. He has been looking for three weeks. He asks if the traveller has seen a hobbit-sized camp east of the Weather Hills.

situation.en: He is more determined than afraid and it is the determination that is concerning. He is going to keep looking.

disposition.en: Vanished into the grass before she fully registered they were there. One left a half-eaten apple on the road.

presence.en: The apple is still warm. They were eating lunch and she came around a bend and they simply ceased to be visible. The apple is real and sitting in the middle of the road.

channel.en: Have them chatter about their hole, their garden, their kin and the doings of the next farm over.

situation.en: She has lived through ages beyond counting and a hobbit's abandoned lunch is briefly, absurdly touching.

disposition.en: Three of them at a campsite — cooking, arguing gently, not particularly interested in her arrival.

presence.en: The argument is about whether the mushrooms in this region are worth the detour. One is passionately in favor. The others are unconvinced. They have strong opinions about mushrooms.

channel.en: Have them talk of the next meal, good ale, a warm fire and a soft bed — the real business of life.

situation.en: They live so entirely in the immediate that the weight she carries does not register on them. She is briefly just a person near a fire.

disposition.en: One sitting on a tussock above the waterline, watching the bog. Has been there long enough that his clothes are damp.

presence.en: He says, without looking at her: the lights came back last night, closer than before. He says it the way someone reports weather — a fact, not a fear.

situation.en: He has been living next to the bog long enough to develop a working relationship with its dangers. He is not afraid of the lights. He is cautious, which is a different thing.

disposition.en: Blocking the road. Not drawn yet. Asking questions in the manner of men who expect to be answered.

presence.en: Three of them. The captain wants to know what he is carrying and where he got it. There is a description circulating — partial, inaccurate enough that it probably does not match — of a Ranger carrying dispatches north of the Lefnui.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: He is being checked against a description. If the dispatches are found the conversation ends differently.

disposition.en: Four of them in a formation that closes the road when he stops. They positioned well before he arrived.

presence.en: The captain has a specific bounty — not a vague report, an actual sum — for a Ranger carrying Arthedain dispatches. He is not certain this is the man. He is certain enough to try.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: The formation is the argument. What the traveller says in the next thirty seconds determines whether this stays a conversation.

disposition.en: Formal obstruction. Following a pattern they were told to follow. The captain is professional about it.

presence.en: There is a report from Umbar — circulating among men who work for southern interests — of a lone elf-blooded traveller moving north of the Lefnui. The description is vague. It fits her and does not fit her.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: He does not know what he is looking for precisely. She is clearly old enough to be what the report describes. He is deciding if challenging her is worth it.

disposition.en: Three of them. The captain's eyes do not move from her face. He knows something more specific.

presence.en: There is a real bounty — recent, out of Umbar, substantial — for an elf woman travelling alone in this region. He knows what she is. He is calculating whether he can take her and what it will cost him.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: She is not afraid of three Corsairs. He cannot know this yet. What he can see is that she has not moved and has not looked away from him.

disposition.en: Four of them, already in formation. One has moved behind her without her appearing to notice. She noticed.

presence.en: She watched Númenor drown. She was at the shore when the wave came. These men are the inheritors of a specific corruption she has seen ruin entire bloodlines across the ages. The contempt she feels is not anger — it is something older and quieter.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: She has decided what she will do before they finish arranging themselves. The decision is not about fear.

disposition.en: Looks him over — armed, northern, alone — and decides he is not a threat before speaking.

presence.en: Southern ford at the estuary washed out last month. The Gwathuirim crossing upstream is still passable but needs a guide. She knows a Stoor who will show it for information from the north, not coin.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: She has something he needs and is willing to deal. The deal is information for information.

disposition.en: Assessing him. Her experience with Rangers on this road is mixed.

presence.en: Saralainn from the eastern clan burned three farmsteads last month — not her clan. She says this with the precision of someone who expects to be blamed for it anyway. She needs word carried north to the garrison naming the eastern clan, not hers.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: She is asking him to carry a message that matters to her survival. She knows he might refuse. She asks anyway.

disposition.en: Stopped him on the road on impulse. Afraid and trying not to show it.

presence.en: The lights in the marsh came back last night, closer than before. Three men went in after them last week. She does not know what happened to the three men but she knows nobody is going near the eastern bog.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: She needed to tell someone. The fear has been sitting in her chest for a week.

disposition.en: Curious about the traveller. Cautious, but the curiosity is winning.

presence.en: The sandbanks at the estuary mouth shifted after last month's storm — the ford she is heading for does not exist anymore. The Gwathuirim know the new safe crossing but what they want for it is not coin.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: She is giving useful information without being asked. She wants company on the road to the next settlement, just until the exposed stretch is past.

disposition.en: Cautious. Gives less than she knows. Reads the traveller before speaking.

presence.en: Southern ford is gone. Saralainn burned three farmsteads west of the marsh last month — not her clan, another one, and she says it like the distinction matters. The coastal road has been empty since.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: She is giving the bad news and holding the actionable news back. The actionable news costs something.

disposition.en: Suspicious. Gives nothing first. Watches the traveller's hands throughout.

presence.en: The marsh is being watched — not by Saralainn. Three men went in last week following lights that moved. None came back. The Gwathuirim will not say what the lights are.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: She is afraid and trying not to show it. Saying it out loud makes it more real.

disposition.en: Stepped out of a side-track directly in front of him. Startled but not hostile.

presence.en: Something has been taking animals from the high pasture — there and gone by midday, no tracks. He wants someone with him when he goes to look. He already asked his neighbors. They refused.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: He is not ashamed of not wanting to go alone. He is being practical.

disposition.en: Watchful. Takes the time to look at the gear before speaking.

presence.en: He has a Gondorian road-permit issued to his father, no longer valid. He does not know what to do with it. Asks if the traveller knows where the nearest garrison would reissue one.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: A practical question about a bureaucratic system he was never taught. Slightly embarrassing to ask.

disposition.en: Formal. Uncertain. Has not spoken to an Elf before and is trying to do it correctly.

presence.en: He has been trying to read the old stones at the eastern ridge for two years — not the Gondorian stones, the older ones underneath. He asks if she can read them.

situation.en: He is right that she can. He is asking because he has exhausted every other option.

disposition.en: Came down from the ridge specifically to speak to her. Was watching the road from above.

presence.en: Two people in his village have something wrong with them that started after they went near the old mine shaft. The healer does not know what it is. He is asking the only person on this road who looks old enough to have seen something like it before.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: He is out of options and he knows it. She looks like someone who has answers to questions people do not usually ask.

disposition.en: Old man on the road, alone, no pack, no staff. Just standing.

presence.en: He was a healer's apprentice at a Gondorian outpost abandoned after the Plague. He has been in this country ever since. He asks only whether she has seen the old mine at the eastern fork. He asks it with a calm that means he will go there alone if she says no.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: He is going regardless. The question is only whether she is curious enough about what is in that mine to go with him.

disposition.en: Fresh territorial marks on a post at a track junction.

presence.en: Clan claim on this stretch of road, placed within the last day. A patrol establishing presence after something happened nearby.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: He is on claimed ground. The claim will be enforced if he is seen on it.

disposition.en: Stopped him on the road. Not aggressive yet — testing first.

presence.en: Three men. The speaker wants to know if he is Gondorian, Arthedain, or something else. The question has a correct answer and a wrong answer and the traveller needs to give the correct one.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: Dunlendings sort travellers by what they are, not who they are. The category matters here.

disposition.en: Letting him pass but just barely. One hand resting on a belt-knife.

presence.en: He wants to know if the traveller has seen Gondorian soldiers on this road in the last week. Not asking for help — checking whether the road is being watched.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: The question is information-gathering. He answers it and the answer will determine whether the traveller's road gets easier or harder.

disposition.en: Territorial marks on the road. Fresh, deliberate.

presence.en: She has watched the rise and fall of the kingdom these marks oppose. The marks themselves are grief dressed as hostility — a people trying to hold what was taken with symbols on wood.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: She does not cross marked territory she has not been invited into. Not from fear — from respect for a kind of claim she understands better than they know.

disposition.en: Two of them on the road. They step aside but not far. One watches her with the specific attention of someone looking for evidence of something he was told.

presence.en: He was told Elves serve the enemy. He is looking at her for proof of this.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: She has been looked at this way before, in better centuries. The accusation is older than the people making it.

disposition.en: A gathering visible from the ridge — twenty men at a flat stone, arranged in a circle.

presence.en: The formation is pre-war. He has read about it in Ranger records. The last time this pattern was used was before the Battle of the Crossings of the Poros two centuries ago.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are binding themselves to something. When the Daen Iontis bind themselves, it becomes a military problem within months.

disposition.en: Aftermath of a gathering — stone marked, fire still warm, men dispersing into the hills.

presence.en: Three of them notice him on the road below and stop dispersing.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: He has two seconds to give them a reason not to make him the problem.

disposition.en: A ritual preparation at a flat stone. Seven men handling objects with deliberate care.

presence.en: The objects are old. Older than Gondor, older than Arnor. She knows what they were originally used for. It is not what the Daen Iontis think they are used for.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They have found something they do not understand and are building a belief system around it. The belief system will cause deaths.

disposition.en: A larger gathering on a ridge. The chant is audible from the road below.

presence.en: The chant is a corruption — the words are Dunlending but the rhythm is from something spoken before the Dunlendings existed. She knows the rhythm. She knew the original context. Someone stripped the context away and handed them the form.

situation.en: Something taught these men a ritual from the First Age without giving them the meaning. That is not accidental.

disposition.en: Moving through the treeline parallel to the road, tracking him without hiding it.

presence.en: Three of them checking his route — they want to know where he is going because the path ahead splits and one branch is theirs. They will not approach but if he takes the wrong branch, that becomes a different conversation.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: He is being assessed from cover. The assessment determines what the road ahead costs him.

disposition.en: One of them standing on a rock above the trail, watching him below.

presence.en: He has marked the trail — a stone moved to a specific position, a cut in bark. He is watching to see if the traveller reads the marks or misses them.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: This is a test. Reading the marks correctly may open something. Missing them closes it.

disposition.en: Three of them working at the base of a specific oak. Re-marking something the storm displaced.

presence.en: The marks they are cutting are older than the tree they cut them into. These marks were transferred here from something that no longer exists — she can see the formula, the deliberate preservation of a sign that should have died with whatever originally bore it.

situation.en: She knows what these marks mean. They have not been actively used since the Second Age.

disposition.en: A group of them visible at the cape, still and watching. Not decided whether to acknowledge her.

presence.en: One of the oldest has a specific carved token at his neck — she knew the hands that made that design. The token was made as a key to something, and whatever it opens has been waiting a long time.

situation.en: She has not seen that specific token in two thousand years. It should not be here. It is here.

disposition.en: Three of them at a camp, debating. They stop when she approaches. One stands.

presence.en: They are documenting disruptions in the Second Age road-wards on this stretch — places where the wards have been broken deliberately, from below. They are finding the disruptions moving north. They want to know if she has seen anything that maps to the same pattern.

channel.en: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

situation.en: Their pattern and the things she has noticed point to the same source.

disposition.en: One separates from the group and comes to her directly. His expression is not warm.

presence.en: He says without preamble that he knows why she is still in Middle-earth and that he does not think it is entirely her choice. He thinks something is holding her here. He asks if she knows what it is.

channel.en: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

situation.en: He may be right. She has never examined the possibility that staying is not fully chosen.

disposition.en: Three figures at a camp — clearly Elves, occupied with something that looks like both study and ritual.

presence.en: He has read reports from Noldorin scholars who travel the old roads documenting Second Age wards. He did not expect to actually encounter them. They are doing work that intersects with his from a completely different angle.

situation.en: They are occupied. Interrupting would gain him nothing. But knowing they are on this road means something.

disposition.en: An Elf on the road, moving west. Moving with the weight of someone who has decided something final.

presence.en: He pauses when he sees the traveller — a Dúnedain on this road is unusual. He studies him for a moment with a look that is not quite sympathy and not quite warning. He sees in the traveller the child of a people carrying what the Elves are leaving behind.

channel.en: Have them turn the talk to the call of the Sea and the road West: who will take ship, and who will stay and dwindle.

situation.en: The look acknowledges this without being able to do anything about it.

disposition.en: An Elf she does not know, moving west. The particular lightness of someone going home.

presence.en: He sees her and stops. She is clearly not going west. The divergence is its own statement. He does not ask her to come — he knows she has been asked. He says only: it is still there.

channel.en: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

situation.en: The it does not need to be named.

disposition.en: He was waiting on the road. He knew she would be here today. He does not explain how.

presence.en: He has a sealed letter from someone at the Havens — someone she has not heard from in years. He will not say the message aloud. He hands her the letter and the seal is one she recognizes.

channel.en: Have them bring up an age-old loss — a drowned realm, a kinsman long dead — as though it were last night.

situation.en: She has not received a letter from the Havens in a very long time.

disposition.en: A farm family on the far side of a field. The child waves. The mother shades her eyes.

presence.en: The farm is maintained — animals present, fire going. This road has been his circuit for six years. The child who waved is the grandchild of the child who waved the first time he came through.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: He has not mentioned this to anyone.

disposition.en: A farmer and a child on a far hill, working together. The child is trying to carry something too heavy.

presence.en: The child will carry heavier things soon. The farmer will grow old. The child will carry those things alone eventually.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: She has watched this sequence more times than there are names for it. The scene is ordinary and inexorable at once.

disposition.en: A man mending a fence at the road's edge. Looks up. Speaks without preamble.

presence.en: Strangers on the south road at night for a week — not camping, moving. No lights. He has not gone to look at the tracks because he has children.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He is telling the traveller because the traveller looks like someone who deals with strangers-on-roads-at-night. He is right.

disposition.en: A woman at a well, drawing water. Looks at the traveller. Then speaks.

presence.en: Her husband went north three weeks ago with a trading party. The party came back without him. They said he stayed on voluntarily. She does not believe this.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: She is telling a stranger because she has told everyone she knows and no one will help. She is not asking for anything. She is saying it out loud one more time.

disposition.en: A merchant caravan moving north on the road. Three wagons, faster than the road warrants.

presence.en: Tharbad-registered pennant — guild cloth. Moving fast means they have the same road intelligence he does, or something spooked them out of Tharbad in a hurry.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: Merchants moving fast on a bad road are a weather-vane.

disposition.en: A Tharbad factor at a wayhouse, drinking alone. Looks up when the traveller enters.

presence.en: Stranded four days — the Gwathlo crossing closed without notice. Gondorian authority he thinks, though no Gondorian livery. He is losing money every day. He knows who closed the crossing, or believes he does, and will tell anyone who buys him a drink.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: The name costs him nothing to give and he wants to give it.

disposition.en: A merchant party on the far road, moving north. The city that made them is visible in how they carry themselves.

presence.en: Tharbad was magnificent once. What it produces now are people who move with the posture of a place that remembers being great but has been spending that memory for centuries.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: She watched the city when it was great.

disposition.en: He saw them before they saw him. Three men in old ruins, too comfortable for vagrants.

presence.en: A chokepoint at a bridge ahead — the only crossing for two miles. He has already identified the approach angles and the alternative.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: This is a tactical problem with a tactical solution. He does not need to fight them.

disposition.en: Four men. He can see two swords and a bolt-case — crossbow somewhere he cannot yet locate.

presence.en: They have not positioned well — visible from the ridge, obvious approach. The crossbow is the problem. The others he can manage. The crossbow requires a different decision.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: He is running the geometry of the encounter before it happens.

disposition.en: A camp in old ruins. Four men. She was watching them before they noticed the road.

presence.en: They have been here at least a week — the refuse pile is old. They are waiting for something specific, not opportunistically raiding. Something on this road is worth waiting for.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: They are a symptom. She does not know yet of what.

disposition.en: She has seen men with this expression — boredom plus readiness — outside the walls of kingdoms she watched fall.

presence.en: They have a captive. Someone sitting against the far wall, bound at the wrists. A traveller, by the gear still visible.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: She has seen this before, in better centuries and worse. The question of whether to intervene has different weight depending on who is asking it.

disposition.en: Fresh tracks crossing the road — heavy boots, irregular spacing, moving east. Made last night.

presence.en: Seven or eight of them. They crossed here after dark heading toward the old ruins on the ridge. They did not camp — they kept moving, which means they have a destination.

situation.en: They passed through. They are ahead now, not behind. The road is clear but the ridge is not.

disposition.en: Five of them blocking the road. The one in front is doing the talking. The others are watching the flanks.

presence.en: They want to know what the traveller is carrying. They are not asking to decide whether to rob them — they have already decided. They are asking to decide how much violence the robbery requires.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: The question buys thirty seconds. The answer determines whether those seconds cost anything.

disposition.en: Three of them at a chokepoint — a defile between rocks, unavoidable. They saw the traveller before the traveller saw them.

presence.en: The captain — bigger, scarred across one eye — has a specific instruction: no killing on the road, bring back anyone found alive. This is unusual. Someone above him wants information, not corpses.

channel.en: Have them fling harsh demands at a captive — who are you, who sent you, what do you carry — backed by the lash.

situation.en: The restraint is not mercy. It is orders. The orders may be more dangerous than simple violence.

disposition.en: A full patrol — eight, plus a warg on a chain held by the largest. They have been tracking for a while.

presence.en: The warg has a scent. It is pulling toward the traveller. The captain is watching the warg and watching the traveller and making the same calculation simultaneously.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: The warg knows. The captain knows the warg knows. The moment the captain decides to trust the warg is the moment the conversation ends.

disposition.en: A smear of dark grease on a rock at the trail's edge — orc scout-mark. They passed here within six hours.

presence.en: The mark faces back the way the traveller came, not forward. They are behind the traveller on this road, moving in the same direction.

situation.en: They are scouts, not raiders. They are following to report, not to engage. Not yet.

disposition.en: Two of them in the rocks above the road. One is watching the traveller. The other is looking back the way the traveller came.

presence.en: They have not moved since the traveller came into view. They are deciding whether to signal or stay quiet. The one watching the road behind keeps checking — they are waiting for something larger to follow the traveller.

situation.en: They are a forward element. What they are waiting for is behind the traveller on this road.

disposition.en: One of them in a hollow, motionless. Visible only because of a mistake in wind direction.

presence.en: Alone scout, likely separated from a larger group. Watching a specific point on the road ahead — a junction, or an approach to something he is meant to mark.

situation.en: He has not seen the traveller. If he reports back, the road ahead is compromised. If he does not report back, the group he serves knows within hours.

disposition.en: One of them in a hollow, motionless. She saw him before he settled — the way he moved to cover was practiced but not perfect.

presence.en: She has seen orc scouts for longer than this particular breed has existed. This one is young by the signs — the crouch is right but he keeps shifting weight. He is watching the road junction ahead, not her approach.

situation.en: If she passes, he will see her and report. The question is whether she is willing to be reported.

disposition.en: Three of them, moving fast on a scent. They run into the traveller coming the other way on the road.

presence.en: They are on the trail of someone specific — not the traveller. For ten seconds they are unsure whether to abandon the trail and deal with the obstacle or push past. The captain is deciding.

channel.en: Have them fling harsh demands at a captive — who are you, who sent you, what do you carry — backed by the lash.

situation.en: The scent they are following went through here recently. If the traveller knows where it leads, they are suddenly useful alive.

disposition.en: The tracks on the road are layered — someone passed here running, and then, later, something followed them.

presence.en: The first tracks are a day old. The second set are hours old and moving fast. The second set are orc-boots, wide-spaced. Pursuit gait.

situation.en: Someone on this road is being hunted. They are ahead of the trackers. Both of them are ahead of the traveller.

disposition.en: A column on the road below — forty, fifty, moving south with supplies. Torches though it is still light. They are not hiding.

presence.en: They have a specific destination and they know the road is theirs right now. The banner they carry is one that has not been seen on this road in decades.

situation.en: A warband this size moving openly means someone has decided the road belongs to the Enemy again. That decision was made recently.

disposition.en: A warband crossing a ridge ahead — visible for sixty seconds before they drop into the valley. Forty at least.

presence.en: Their direction takes them across the Ranger patrol circuit at a point he knows. If they reach the circuit before he does, three villages lose their warning system.

situation.en: He cannot stop them. He can get ahead of them.

disposition.en: A warband crossing a ridge ahead. She has seen larger. She has seen what they leave.

presence.en: The banner. She knows that banner. She has seen it before, in a different Age, on a different ridge. It should not exist anymore — the line that carried it was broken in the Second Age.

situation.en: Something reconstituted that banner. Something that remembers the Second Age well enough to reconstruct its symbols.

disposition.en: A supply caravan on the road below — slow, heavily loaded, ill-tempered guards. Some of the figures at the center are not orcs.

presence.en: The non-orc figures move differently from the guards — shorter steps, heads down. They are captives being moved, not cargo. Three of them.

situation.en: The guards are watching the road, not the captives. The captives are watching the ground.

disposition.en: A caravan from above — slow, supply-laden, three captives at the center under light guard.

presence.en: The guards are four, plus a drover at the front who is not paying attention to anything but the pace. The captives are bound at the wrist but their legs are free.

situation.en: He has run the calculation three times and the numbers are the same each time. Four guards, three captives, open road. The question is not whether he can do it — it is whether he can do it without the captives dying in the confusion.

disposition.en: A caravan below. Three captives. She has seen this before more times than she can count.

presence.en: The captives are alive and moving under their own power. Alive and moving means there is still time. She has never once convinced herself that was enough reason not to act.

situation.en: She is not going to walk past.

disposition.en: A column of driven captives — mixed, twenty of them — moving under orc-whip along a side-track below the road.

presence.en: One of the captives at the edge of the column catches sight of the traveller above. Does not call out. Holds the gaze for three seconds, then looks back at the ground.

situation.en: The captive saw them. The guards did not. The captive made a choice not to endanger the traveller. That choice cost something.

disposition.en: The column has stopped — a broken wheel on the supply cart, guards occupied. One captive at the edge, close enough to the treeline to speak quietly.

presence.en: He was a farmer from a settlement three days north. They were taken eleven days ago. He does not know where they are going. He asks for nothing except that someone knows they are here, that someone saw them.

situation.en: He is not asking to be saved right now. He is asking to be witnessed.

disposition.en: A traveller on the road — unremarkable, moving south, nods in passing.

presence.en: Something is slightly wrong about the face. The proportions are almost right. The nod was timed correctly but not reflexively.

situation.en: They are passing as human. They are nearly doing it successfully.

disposition.en: A trader at a wayhouse — dark-complected, broad, asking questions about the road north in a way that sounds casual but is building a picture.

presence.en: The questions are too specific to be traveller-curiosity. He wants to know where the patrols are, not where the road conditions are. He is gathering operational intelligence dressed as conversation.

situation.en: He does not know yet that the person he is asking knows what he is.

disposition.en: A mercenary at the same wayhouse fire. Has been there when he arrived, will still be there when he leaves.

presence.en: The jaw is wrong. The hands are wrong — the knuckles sit differently, the reach is too long for the body. He has been watching everyone who enters and noting who they speak to.

situation.en: the traveller has seen half-orcs before. This one does not yet know he has been identified.

disposition.en: A figure on the road ahead, waiting. Standing in the middle, not to the side. He has been waiting for her specifically.

presence.en: He has a message. He delivers it without ceremony: she is known on this road, she has been seen, and there are those who would prefer she did not continue south.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: The message was crafted by someone intelligent. The messenger was chosen because he could deliver it without being dismissed as an animal.

disposition.en: Three of them on the road in full daylight, not bothering to hide. That alone is the warning.

presence.en: The captain speaks in rough Westron. He wants the traveller to stop, turn around, and not use this road again. He says this once, clearly, without threat in his voice. The threat is in what he is.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: The message is orderly. The instruction is reasonable enough to follow. That is what makes it worse than a simple ambush.

disposition.en: Five of them at a bridge. They have been there for a day at least — the camp-sign is established. They are not raiders. They are a garrison.

presence.en: The bridge is the only crossing for miles. They are not here by accident and they are not here temporarily. Someone placed them here to control this crossing.

situation.en: This is not a patrol. This is occupation. The difference matters for what comes next.

disposition.en: Five of them at the bridge. The captain looks at him with the specific attention of someone who has been given a description to look for.

presence.en: The description partially matches. The captain knows this. He is going to confirm before acting, because he is disciplined enough to not kill the wrong person.

channel.en: Have them fling harsh demands at a captive — who are you, who sent you, what do you carry — backed by the lash.

situation.en: The confirmation question will come. The answer determines whether this ends as a conversation or something else.

disposition.en: Warg-prints crossing the road at speed — four sets, all heading east. The prints are deep and fresh.

presence.en: They were moving at a run. Four wargs running east on this road within the last two hours means a patrol, a pursuit, or a message being carried fast.

situation.en: Whatever they were doing, they are east of here now and moving.

disposition.en: A sound before the sight — hooves but wrong, too heavy, wrong cadence. Then three of them cresting a rise ahead at speed.

presence.en: They have not seen the traveller yet. They will in approximately eight seconds. They are moving too fast to stop cleanly.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: Eight seconds is enough if used correctly.

disposition.en: A chamber off the main passage — three of them around a flat stone. Ritual, not preparation for violence.

presence.en: They are speaking in a dialect she has not heard in centuries — not Black Speech exactly, something older, something that predates the standardization of the Enemy's tongue.

situation.en: They have not heard the traveller. The dialect they are using is a version of something she knows.

disposition.en: One of them in a passage, alone, carrying something wrapped. He sees her before she sees him. He does not run.

presence.en: He speaks — not in threat, in shock. He says a name in a tongue she has not heard used by orcs before. The name is for something she knows. He has no right to know it.

situation.en: He knows that name. That name should be known only by those who were there when it was given. She was there. He was not.

disposition.en: A passage that seemed clear until it was not. Three of them blocking the way back, not forward — they came from behind.

presence.en: They are not fighting. They are herding. They want the intruder away from a specific section of the passage — whatever is there, they are protecting it.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: They are not going to let the traveller go back toward whatever they are guarding. Forward is the only option they are offering.

disposition.en: A checkpoint — two orcs and one Man, at a gap in a collapsed wall that serves as the only pass through a ridge.

presence.en: The Man does the speaking. He asks for papers. Not a robbery — a genuine administrative checkpoint. Whatever Angmar is doing in this territory, it has bureaucracy.

channel.en: Have them fling harsh demands at a captive — who are you, who sent you, what do you carry — backed by the lash.

situation.en: Papers exist for people who are supposed to be here. The traveller is not supposed to be here.

disposition.en: A patrol that knows exactly what a Ranger looks like. The orc-captain speaks better Westron than expected.

presence.en: He says that Rangers of the North are not welcome in the Witch-king's lands and that this one has two choices: leave the road immediately or be escorted to the nearest tower, from which he will not leave.

situation.en: The Witch-king's lands extend further south than they did a year ago. the traveller is standing in them.

disposition.en: Three of them at the edge of the ice, in daylight — they do not flinch from it. Watching the traveller on the snowfield below.

presence.en: They endure sunlight. This alone is the warning — whatever adjustments made common orcs into these, the result is something that does not have the usual weakness.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: They are deciding whether the traveller is worth the effort of the snowfield between them.

disposition.en: Sound before sight — many footsteps in the dark, coordinated. Then torchlight. Too much torchlight for a patrol.

presence.en: A hunting-party, not a patrol. They were not looking for the traveller specifically — they were sweeping the passage. The traveller was in the passage.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: The sweep is methodical. They have done this before. This passage has one exit behind and one exit forward.

disposition.en: A single old orc at a junction — not patrol, not hunting. Sitting.

presence.en: He has been in these halls since before Durin's Bane came. He says this without boasting — a statement of fact from someone too old to care about impressions. He watches her with the specific recognition of someone who knew this place when it was something else.

situation.en: He knew Khazad-dum when Dwarves still lived in it. She also knew Khazad-dum when Dwarves still lived in it. They are the only two in this passage who share that.

disposition.en: A court — rough, filthy, loud — and at the center of it a thing that is very large and very old and speaks with the ease of someone who has not needed to hurry in a long time.

presence.en: He already knows who the traveller is. He says this first. He has been told. He does not say by whom. He says there is a negotiation to be had before he decides what to do with them.

channel.en: Have them fling harsh demands at a captive — who are you, who sent you, what do you carry — backed by the lash.

situation.en: He is old enough to prefer manipulation to violence when manipulation is available. That is more dangerous, not less.

disposition.en: Three of them around a fire on the road, arguing about whether last week's shepherd was better roasted or boiled. They have not noticed the traveller yet.

presence.en: The argument is genuine — they have strong opinions about cooking methods and the debate has been going since before the fire was lit. They are not watchful. They are occupied.

situation.en: Three Stone-trolls arguing about food are, for the moment, not paying attention to anything else. Dawn is four hours away.

disposition.en: One of them blocking the road. The other two are somewhere behind him — audible but not visible.

presence.en: He wants to know if the traveller has seen any sheep in the last valley. He genuinely wants to know. He has lost his flock.

situation.en: He is asking a question and waiting for an answer. He is not going to move until he gets one. He is also blocking a road at night, which is its own problem regardless of his intentions.

disposition.en: Three of them at the crossroads, and they have seen him. The largest one speaks first.

presence.en: He says — slow, deliberate — that he remembers a man who looked like this man coming through here three years ago and that man had a good knife. He wants to know if this man has a good knife.

situation.en: He is not asking to rob it. He genuinely wants a good knife. The previous man gave it to him voluntarily. The memory is oddly specific.

disposition.en: Three of them at a fire. One looks up when she passes — she is apparently the most interesting thing that has happened since the shepherd argument.

presence.en: He asks what she is. Not threatening — he genuinely does not know. He has seen Elves before but they were smaller and they ran away. She is not running away.

situation.en: The question is curious, not hostile. Curiosity is a window.

disposition.en: One on the road — not a full ambush, just one, and it is looking at the traveller with the specific dull focus of a creature that has decided something is going to happen.

presence.en: It does not speak first. It is waiting to see what the traveller does. This is how it hunts — it lets the prey decide whether to run, because running is interesting.

situation.en: Running is interesting. Standing is boring. Boring might be survivable.

disposition.en: Two of them, and they have been waiting — the approach was too convenient, the gap in the rocks too obvious. This is practiced.

presence.en: The first one speaks — three words, badly articulated, but in Westron: give it here. It does not specify what it. Everything the traveller is carrying qualifies.

situation.en: The other one is circling. The circling is the real danger.

disposition.en: It moved — something that had been a fallen trunk is not a fallen trunk anymore. It is standing up.

presence.en: It has been waiting in place long enough that moss has grown on its back. This is a troll that understands patience. It is between the traveller and the path forward.

situation.en: It did not try to hide, exactly. It simply did not move. The forest made it invisible by being itself around it.

disposition.en: One on the road in full daylight. Armored. Not a foraging beast — a soldier.

presence.en: It does not speak. It is not here to speak. It is here because it was placed here and it will remain here until it is removed or its purpose is accomplished.

situation.en: This is a weapon pointed at a road. The traveller is on the road.

disposition.en: A soldier at a garrison post — large, dark, speaks Westron with a southerner's accent. The garrison is Harad-aligned.

presence.en: He asks for road-papers in the manner of someone following procedure. The procedure is real. He is following it correctly. He is also seven feet tall and the wrong color for what he is claiming to be.

situation.en: The procedure is a distraction. The question is what happens when the procedure is satisfied.

disposition.en: Three of them — small for trolls, which still means large — circling something dead on the road ahead. They have not noticed the traveller yet.

presence.en: They are arguing over the dead thing. One of them wants it, the other two want it, and none of them have worked out a resolution. The argument is escalating toward something physical.

situation.en: Three young trolls about to start fighting over food is a window. The road goes around them on the right.

disposition.en: A figure at the far end of a ruined hall — standing still, looking at the traveller. It has no shadow.

presence.en: It does not move. It is waiting to be acknowledged. Ghosts of this kind — the old ones, the ones who remember themselves clearly — need acknowledgment before they can speak.

situation.en: It has been here a long time. Whatever it is waiting to say has not diminished in the waiting.

disposition.en: A man in old Arnorian gear — the cut is two centuries out of fashion — at the edge of a barrow. He speaks when the traveller approaches.

presence.en: He says he was the last warden of a specific tower on the Weather Hills. He wants to know if the tower is still standing. He asks it simply, like a man asking after a house he built.

situation.en: The tower has been rubble for a hundred and forty years. He does not know this.

disposition.en: A woman — Dúnedain, by the gear, Second Age by the style — standing at a crossroads and looking at the two roads with the expression of someone who cannot remember which way she was going.

presence.en: She asks Celebrian which road leads east. She says her husband is east, waiting. She says this with the certainty of someone who has been saying it for a very long time.

situation.en: She died before Celebrian came to this road. She has been at this crossroads since. The husband she is waiting for is dust.

disposition.en: It appears as someone she knew — the resemblance is close enough that she stops.

presence.en: It is not him. The face is right but the eyes are wrong — they are looking at her but seeing something she cannot see. It speaks in a voice that is almost his and says her name in a way that is almost how he said it.

situation.en: It is a ghost that has learned to wear a shape it found in her memory. Ghosts do not do this spontaneously.

disposition.en: A ghost at a barrow-mound — Dunedain, old, carrying wounds that never healed. It speaks before he can.

presence.en: It says: you are one of us. It says: you will be here too, soon enough, if you keep walking this road. It says it without malice — a statement of fact from someone standing on the other side of it.

situation.en: The ghost is not threatening him. It is warning him. The distinction is the most unsettling part.

disposition.en: The road empties ahead. Sound drops out. The cold comes first, then the shape on the road — and the shape has been there the whole time, it was always there, the traveller simply did not see it until now.

presence.en: It does not speak first. It waits. The waiting is the weapon — every second of it drains something.

situation.en: Whatever the Witch-king wants from this road today, the traveller is now in the calculation.

disposition.en: The shape on the road. The cold. The specific silence that precedes it.

presence.en: It speaks. It says his name. Not his road-name — his true name, the one only the Dunedain records carry. It says: I have read those records.

situation.en: It knows who he is. It has taken the time to know who he is. That is not a good sign.

disposition.en: The shape on the road. The Noldor feel the cold differently — not fear exactly, but the specific recognition of something that has been enemy longer than most things have existed.

presence.en: It speaks. In a language she has not heard spoken aloud since the Second Age — the court tongue of Númenor in its darkest years. It says, in that language: you should have sailed.

situation.en: It knows what she is and what she chose and it is using that choice against her.

disposition.en: Something white and cold at the passage's end — not a light, not a figure exactly, but something that is organizing itself into a shape.

presence.en: It has not attacked. Specters do not attack — they approach, and the approaching is the attack. It is between the traveller and the forward exit.

situation.en: Moving toward it makes it worse. Moving away from it is also moving away from the exit.

disposition.en: A man in brown — very brown, and some of it is not dye — crouching beside the road examining something in the grass. He does not look up when the traveller approaches.

presence.en: He says, without looking up, that there is a nest of harriers three miles north that has been disturbed — not by a fox, by something heavier, moving on two feet, three nights running. Then he looks up and seems mildly surprised there is a person here.

channel.en: Have them turn the talk to beasts, trees and growing things, and the keeping of them.

situation.en: The animal intelligence is specific and accurate. The information about what disturbed the nest is more useful than he realizes he has given.

disposition.en: He appears out of the forest at the road's edge with two ravens on his shoulders who are arguing with each other about something he keeps trying to mediate.

presence.en: The ravens have been following something south from the Carrock for a week. They are arguing about what it is. He translates both positions with the patience of a man who has been doing this for a very long time. The disagreement is: one says orc-warband, the other says it is organized differently.

situation.en: He is giving them this information because he believes travelers should know what the ravens know. He does not consider whether the traveler wants it.

disposition.en: He steps onto the road and stops the traveller specifically — he has been waiting.

presence.en: He says that the animals on the north road have gone quiet for two miles in a specific direction, and that this kind of quiet has happened twice before that he remembers, and both times it preceded something the Rangers needed to know about.

situation.en: He is not sure what it means. He is sure enough to stop a Ranger and say it.

disposition.en: He recognizes her immediately — or rather, one of the ravens on his shoulder does, and tells him, and he reacts to what the raven says rather than to her directly.

presence.en: He says the raven says she smells like someone who has been in Aman and chose to leave it. The raven is apparently very specific about this. He apologizes for the raven.

situation.en: The raven is right. The apology is genuine. He is faintly embarrassed by his own ability.

disposition.en: He comes to her directly, without the usual roundabout. He looks at her with the specific attention of a Maia who has seen something he did not expect to see.

presence.en: He says that the forest between here and the mountains is wrong in a way it has not been wrong since the Second Age. He says it in the voice of someone who has been trying to dismiss this observation for a week and can no longer.

situation.en: He wants to know if she has felt it too. He is asking because if she has not felt it, he can continue to dismiss it. If she has, he cannot.

disposition.en: He is already there when the traveller arrives at the river crossing — sitting on a log singing something about kingfishers that is not quite a song and not quite a spell and is definitely working on something in the water.

presence.en: He looks up and says: there you are! As if he was expecting them. He may have been. He invites them to dinner without asking their name, which he already knows.

situation.en: He is the most helpful and least explicable thing on this road. The help is genuine. The inexplicability is permanent.

disposition.en: He appears on the path ahead, walking in the opposite direction, and greets the traveller as though they are old friends who have not seen each other in a week.

presence.en: He has been watching something in the Old Forest that has been behaving unusually for the past month — Old Man Willow, he says, has been dreaming worse than usual, and the dreams are coming from outside Old Man Willow, not from inside. He says this the way someone reports a neighbor's cough.
