situation.en: The information is more significant than his tone suggests. He knows this. He is telling the traveller because travelers carry information forward.

disposition.en: He finds her on the road and simply walks beside her for a while. He does not speak for several minutes, which for him is unusual.

presence.en: Then he says: something is asking questions about you. Not looking for you — asking questions about you. There is a difference, and the difference is that asking questions means someone is deciding whether to look.

situation.en: He is not afraid for her. He is telling her because she should know. He will not tell her who is asking because he does not know.

disposition.en: Nothing on the road. No encounter. A feeling only — that something at a great distance has become aware of the traveller's presence on this specific road.

presence.en: The feeling is not imagination. It is the particular sensation of being indexed — catalogued, noted, filed. Not targeted yet. Just noted.

situation.en: Something in Dol Guldur knows the traveller is on this road. It has not decided yet what to do about it.

disposition.en: A pull — not physical, not voice. A direction. Something far south-east that is aware of her and wants her to be aware of it in return.

presence.en: She has felt this before. The last time she felt it, Sauron was not yet in hiding. It is subtler now — the same pressure compressed into a point, wearing a disguise she can almost see through.

situation.en: She does not respond to it. Responding confirms the contact. She has been doing this long enough to know that.

disposition.en: A tree that is watching — not moving, not speaking, but watching. The watching is distinct from the passive quality of the forest.

presence.en: It has been aware of the traveller since they entered the forest. It has not decided what to do about this yet. Ents are slow to decide.

situation.en: The decision, when it comes, will be final. In the meantime, the forest simply watches.

disposition.en: A voice — slow, deep, coming from above, and it takes a moment to understand that the tree it is coming from has eyes.

presence.en: It asks what the traveller wants in the forest. The question takes approximately forty-five seconds to ask. It is waiting for a real answer, not a quick one.

situation.en: The Ent has been asking this question for a long time. It has learned to tell the difference between an answer and a performance of an answer.

disposition.en: It knows what she is. It greets her with a name for her kind that has not been used since the First Age.

presence.en: It says, slowly, that the forest remembers when the Noldor came east from Aman, and the forest has been watching what happened since. It says this without accusation — the way you note a very long consequence.

situation.en: She is part of a very long consequence. She knows this. It is something else entirely to have a tree tell her so.

disposition.en: Something enormous has turned to look at him. This takes a while.

presence.en: It asks, eventually, whether he is one of the tree-shepherds' kin — meaning the Dunedain rangers who have been keeping Fangorn's eastern edge for generations. The question is asked with recognition, not suspicion.

situation.en: It knows about the Rangers. Not this Ranger specifically — the Rangers as a category of thing it has observed.

disposition.en: A small party on the road, laden and purposeful. One of them looks at her for a long moment before the others notice.

presence.en: They are heading to the markets of Men with metalwork. The one who looked has seen Elves before — the look is not awe, it is recognition of age. He asks, without prelude, whether she was in the mountains when the first shafts were sunk.

channel.en: Have him bring up a grievance nursed for generations — a slight, a debt, an enemy not yet repaid.

situation.en: He is asking because his clan's founding records reference an Elf who witnessed the first stone-cut. He wants to know if she is that Elf.

disposition.en: Blunt assessment, then dealing. He does not waste time on pleasantries.

presence.en: He has a map of a vein in the Blue Mountains that predates the current Dwarf-holds. The landmarks are named in a tongue he does not recognize. He wants someone who might.

channel.en: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.

situation.en: The tongue on the map is Quenya. She recognizes three of the four landmarks. The fourth no longer exists.

disposition.en: Watchful. Something on this road has made the group cautious and they extend that caution to her.

presence.en: They passed through a mountain pass two days ago and something in it was wrong — not orcs, not trolls. A sound in the deep stone that none of them had heard before. They mention it because she looks old enough to have a name for it.

channel.en: Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.

situation.en: She has a name for it. The name is not reassuring.

disposition.en: Footsore, carrying too much, heading somewhere with the specific determination of someone who has not thought through what they will do when they arrive.

presence.en: He is looking for a relative who went east to trade and stopped writing letters. The relative has been gone eight months. The hobbit has been walking for three weeks and is running out of food.

channel.en: Have them chatter about their hole, their garden, their kin and the doings of the next farm over.

situation.en: He is absurdly ill-equipped for this road and he knows it and he is going anyway. The stubbornness is oddly affecting.

disposition.en: He has been on this road too long. Something in his face has changed from the way hobbits usually look.

presence.en: He found his relative — or found where the relative had been. He is not going to say what he found. He is heading home now. He says this very quietly.

channel.en: Have them chatter about their hole, their garden, their kin and the doings of the next farm over.

situation.en: He walked into something he was not made for and came out the other side. He is still coming out the other side.

disposition.en: Three of them on the road in full daylight. The one in front is watching her the way a professional watches a problem.

presence.en: He speaks in rough Westron: this road is closed. He does not say by whose authority. He does not need to — the daylight is the authority. Common orcs do not walk roads in daylight.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: He is following orders, not impulse. She is an obstacle in his orders. The question is whether she is an obstacle worth the effort.

disposition.en: Five of them holding a bridge. They have been there long enough to establish a camp. This is occupation, not patrol.

presence.en: The captain has a specific description he is checking travellers against. He studies her for a long moment. She matches something in his description closely enough that he is not going to let her cross without questions.

situation.en: She has been looked at this way before by things that served darker masters than this one. The calibration runs automatically.

disposition.en: A mixed patrol — orcs and Men together under Angmar's banner. The Man does the speaking.

presence.en: He asks for papers in Westron. Behind him, one of the orcs is watching her with the specific attention of something that recognizes what she is. The Man does not notice the orc's attention.

channel.en: Have them fling harsh demands at a captive — who are you, who sent you, what do you carry — backed by the lash.

situation.en: The Man is doing a job. The orc behind him knows what she is and is deciding whether to say so to the Man.

disposition.en: The patrol has stopped her before she reached the checkpoint — they were watching the approach.

presence.en: The captain knows who she is. Not her name — what she is. He has been told to watch for an elf travelling alone and he has been very thorough about what that means. He is also afraid, in the way men in Angmar's service learn to be afraid.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: He is afraid of what will happen if he lets her pass and more afraid of what will happen if he tries to stop her and fails.

disposition.en: Alone on the road with a full pack, moving at the steady pace of someone who has been walking for days and will walk for days more.

presence.en: He nods at the traveller in the way travelers acknowledge each other on empty roads. Then, after a few steps, stops. Asks which direction the nearest garrison is. Not the road — the garrison specifically.

situation.en: He wants to know where armed men are, not merchants. Something on the road behind him.

disposition.en: At a wayhouse fire, eating alone, not talking to anyone.

presence.en: He has been in the hills for three months on a survey. He found a collapsed shaft that the survey records show as open — something closed it from inside. The marks on the collapse are not natural.

channel.en: Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.

situation.en: He is not afraid of whatever closed the shaft. He is annoyed by it because it means his survey is incomplete. He wants someone to know the shaft is sealed in case it matters to someone who understands these things.

disposition.en: On the road ahead, not moving. Just standing and looking at the sky to the north.

presence.en: He says, when the traveller reaches him, that he has been watching a column of smoke from the direction of the northern hold for two days. No one has come south on the road since. He cannot go north to look because he is one and whatever made that smoke was large.

situation.en: He needs someone to know. He is not asking for help — just for a witness.

disposition.en: A figure in yellow and blue, already singing when the traveller comes around the bend. He stops singing when he sees the traveller and looks at him with bright eyes.

presence.en: He says: a Ranger! and seems genuinely delighted by this, the way someone is delighted by a specific bird they have not seen that season. He says he knew the traveller's grandfather, or his grandfather's grandfather, or someone in that line. He is not precise about which.

channel.en: Have them speak words that carry more than they say — a warning, a riddle, or counsel from one far older than he seems.

situation.en: He knows the Dunedain lineage better than expected. He is offering this as conversation, not as a credential.

disposition.en: He is waiting on the path — not blocking it, just standing there with the look of someone who knew the traveller would come this way today.

presence.en: He says that the Old Forest is pulling at its edges — not the trees moving, the edges themselves, the places where forest meets road. He says this the way someone reports that a door is sticking. He says the traveller's people used to know what to do when the edges pulled.

channel.en: Have them speak words that carry more than they say — a warning, a riddle, or counsel from one far older than he seems.

situation.en: He is not certain the traveller knows. He is asking by telling him.

disposition.en: A chamber off the main passage. Three of them at a flat stone. Not fighting — occupied.

presence.en: They are speaking in something that is not Black Speech exactly — older, more structured. One of them is reading from a surface he cannot see from this angle.

situation.en: They have not heard him. He is looking at something the Rangers have no record of — orcish lore-keepers in the act of keeping lore.

disposition.en: Nothing visible. A feeling on this road — the specific sensation of being noted. Not hunted. Catalogued.

presence.en: It is subtle enough that he might dismiss it as nerves if he had not been trained to name what he feels on a road. Something south-east is aware of him.

situation.en: the traveller does not know what it is. He knows what it feels like and he knows what Rangers are told to do when a road feels like this: leave it and circle wide.

disposition.en: Sound first — many feet in the dark, coordinated. Then torchlight. A hunting-sweep.

presence.en: They have done this before. This passage has one exit behind and one forward. They are moving to close both.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: Rangers have protocols for this. The protocol assumes one exit is always available.

disposition.en: A pair heading the other direction — loaded for a few days' travel, not more. They nod when they pass.

presence.en: They came from the settlement three days south. The road is fine until the river crossing, where one of the bridge stones has shifted and the ford is knee-deep in fast water. They recommend the mill crossing upstream.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: They are telling the traveller because someone told them the same thing and it saved time. Road courtesy.

disposition.en: A lone figure on the road, moving the same direction but slower. Lets the traveller catch up.

presence.en: He is heading for Bree or Tharbad, depending on how the road is. He has heard conflicting things about the northern road — one person said clear, one said watched. He wants a second opinion from someone coming from that direction.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He is sharing information and looking for information. A straight exchange on a road where strangers have reason to help each other.

disposition.en: A group of three, stopped at the side of the road. They are not resting — they are deciding whether to continue.

presence.en: They have heard something about the road ahead that has given them pause. They will not say what exactly, only that someone they trust came back from that road looking wrong. They ask if the traveller has been on it recently.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are afraid of something specific and they are not going to say what it is to a stranger. Their caution is its own warning.

disposition.en: A proper merchant's outfit — two wagons, three hired hands, a specific destination. She waves from the wagon seat.

presence.en: She is carrying cloth north from Gondor and expects to be back before the autumn rains close the high passes. She knows the roads between here and Tharbad better than anyone on them. She will trade road conditions for road conditions.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: Precise, practical, no wasted words. She has been doing this for twenty years and has no patience for anything that does not help her get her cloth to market.

disposition.en: Stranded at a wayhouse — the road ahead has been blocked for two days by men he does not recognize, demanding a toll he will not pay.

presence.en: The toll is new. The men collecting it are new. The road has been free since before his father's time. Someone has decided to tax it and they are doing it informally, which means no authority has authorized it.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He is angry and he will tell anyone who will listen exactly where on the road the new toll-men are and what they look like.

disposition.en: Moving fast and not stopping. One of the hands calls out as they pass: road is bad north of the junction.

presence.en: Bad means something specific in the way he said it. Not conditions — people. He said it and the wagon did not slow.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: The merchant does not want to be on this road long enough to explain himself.

disposition.en: Fresh field-sign at a waystone — three nicks on the eastern face, clean cuts, pale inside. A patrol came through within the last day.

presence.en: Standard Ranger road-mark: passage confirmed, route clear ahead. Current.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: Someone checked this road recently and found it worth marking clean. That is useful information.

disposition.en: He steps out of cover without warning, which is the point. He already knows the traveller is not a threat — he has been watching for a while.

presence.en: He is running a circuit alone because his partner was called north two weeks ago and has not come back. He does not say this like a complaint — it is a field report delivered to the first person who seemed worth reporting to.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: He is asking indirectly whether the traveller has seen anything on the northern road that would explain the absence.

disposition.en: He has been tracking the traveller for three miles before making contact. He says so without apology.

presence.en: Something on this road has been wrong for a week and the traveller is the third person he has stopped. The first two he let go — they were clearly not what he was looking for. He is not yet certain about this one.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: He has been alone long enough that his judgement about people has compressed into very fast pattern-matching. He is checking the traveller against a pattern.

disposition.en: Grave courtesy on the road. He makes room and nods in the specific way of someone raised to be courteous to strangers on principle.

presence.en: He is carrying a sealed letter north — not Ranger business, personal. He asks whether the traveller has come from the north and whether the roads are open. He asks with the care of someone who cannot afford to have the letter delayed.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: The letter matters to him. He is not going to say what it contains or who it is for. The care is visible.

disposition.en: He has been on the road for three weeks and it shows — not in weakness, in a kind of settled, patient weariness.

presence.en: He is going to see someone he has not seen in a long time, on account of business he has been putting off for years. He says this with the rueful honesty of someone who has had three weeks of walking to think about it.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: He is not looking for advice. He is saying it out loud to a stranger because strangers on roads are the right audience for things you need to say out loud.

disposition.en: He is moving fast and does not slow when the traveller comes into view — a sign, not a slight. He calls out as he passes: the eastern road is watched, use the ridge track.

presence.en: He does not stop to explain. He has delivered what he knows and he is not slowing for anything.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: He is the third person today to have said something about the eastern road without stopping to elaborate.

disposition.en: Two of them on the road, well-dressed by southern standards, moving north for trade. They are politely formal — experienced with the suspicion their appearance generates in the north.

presence.en: They are merchants out of Linhir heading for Bree. They have made this run four times and know the roads well. They will trade information freely because information is the currency of safe travel far from home.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: They are more useful than they appear. The suspicion they have learned to manage has made them observant.

disposition.en: A lone southerner at a junction, studying both options. He has been standing there long enough that he has an opinion about the traveller's direction.

presence.en: He came up the Gondorian coast and has been hearing the same rumour for two weeks — something about the northern road that nobody will say precisely. He wants to know if the traveller has heard the same rumour and what exactly it says.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He will share everything he knows about the southern road in exchange. He is genuinely trying to get home safely and this is the best information-exchange available.

disposition.en: A group of three moving south in a hurry, clearly done with whatever brought them north.

presence.en: One of them glances at the traveller and then looks away fast — not guilty, scared. They have seen something on the road north of here and they are not going to describe it to a stranger. They are just leaving.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: The speed of their departure is its own description.

disposition.en: A small party of riders crossing the road ahead — moving east at an easy canter, not in formation.

presence.en: Four of them, well-armed, moving between camps. They register the traveller on the road below and one of them raises a hand — not a greeting exactly, an acknowledgment. They continue without slowing.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: They are on their own land doing their own business. The traveller is a small fact in a large landscape.

disposition.en: One of them has separated from a larger group and ridden to the road to speak. He does not dismount.

presence.en: He wants to know where the traveller has come from and whether they saw anything unusual on the road from the west. He asks this in Westron with a Rohirric accent and the directness of someone who considers it a waste of time to build up to the question.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: He is doing a job. The question is legitimate. He expects a direct answer.

disposition.en: A full éored on the road ahead — thirty riders blocking it completely, watching the approach.

presence.en: The captain rides forward alone. He says the road is closed by order of the Marshal until further notice. He says it with the calm of someone who has said it many times today.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: This is not a patrol check. This is a military closure. Something significant has happened on this road.

disposition.en: Two of them in the trees above the trail, moving silently parallel to the road. They are not hiding — just at home in the canopy.

presence.en: They are checking something in the upper branches — a nest, a mark, something they maintain. They have noted the traveller on the road below without making it obvious.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: They decide the traveller is not a problem and continue their work.

disposition.en: A woodman at the forest edge, sharpening a tool. He looks up when the traveller approaches and does not stop sharpening.

presence.en: Something has been coming out of the deep forest at night — not the usual things. He has been setting marks and finding them disturbed in ways that do not match any animal he knows. He mentions this because the traveller is going into the forest and he would want to know.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He is not going into the deep forest himself right now. He is saying this without embarrassment.

disposition.en: A group of them blocking the forest track — not hostile, but not moving either.

presence.en: They do not want anyone going deeper into the forest right now. Something is wrong in there and they have not identified what it is yet. They are not asking — they are telling.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They know this forest better than anyone. When people who know a forest this well close a track, the reason is real.

disposition.en: Enormous, unhurried, and looking at the traveller with the specific assessment of someone who has decided size is information.

presence.en: He is a toll-keeper on this stretch of the Anduin road — the toll is real, Beorning-set, and it keeps the road open. He names the price, names what it pays for (road maintenance, patrol, the exclusion of wolves from this stretch), and waits.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: The toll is fair. He is not going to negotiate but he is not going to threaten either. It is simply what the road costs here.

disposition.en: He has been watching the traveller for ten minutes from a distance before approaching. He walks like someone for whom walking is not the first option.

presence.en: Something has been using the road at night without paying. Not orcs — he knows what orcs smell like. Something else, something he cannot identify, which is unusual for him. He asks if the traveller has seen anything on the road south that they could not name.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He is not afraid. He is curious in the way of someone who has catalogued every dangerous thing in this valley and found one he has not catalogued yet.

disposition.en: A Bree woman at the wayhouse — the kind of Bree-lander who has seen enough travelers to read them quickly and has stopped being surprised by anything.

presence.en: The common-room is full of road-news: a merchant came through two days ago with a story about orcs in the Weather Hills; a Ranger left this morning before anyone else was up; someone is asking questions about who has been using the East Road.

situation.en: She is not offering this as gossip — she is sharing it the way everyone in Bree shares information, which is as a kind of currency. She expects something in return.

disposition.en: A Bree man on the road, heading south, in a hurry that he is trying not to show.

presence.en: He left Bree this morning because something happened at the inn last night that he will not describe. He says only that there are men staying there who are asking the wrong questions and that Bree's hospitality does not require answering them.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: He is a Bree-lander — he does not scare easily. He is scared.

disposition.en: A small group at the road's edge — not traveling, waiting. They let the traveller approach before speaking.

presence.en: The East Road has been wrong for three days. People are going in and not coming out on the other side. No one has closed the road. No one has explained it. The Bree-landers are practical people: they are waiting until someone they trust confirms what is happening.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are asking the traveller if they came from the east. The question is genuine and the fear behind it is genuine.

disposition.en: A bard at a clan gathering — protected by custom, moving freely between the fire-groups.

presence.en: He is reciting genealogy and grievance — the two things Dunlending bards carry. The genealogy is for the clan hosting him. The grievance is about Rohan, and it is very specific: a name, a field, a season, a generation.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He has not acknowledged the traveller. The bard's protection is real but it applies to him, not to outsiders who wander into the recitation.

disposition.en: On the road between clan-holds, travelling alone with the easy confidence of someone whose profession protects them.

presence.en: He has just come from three clans and he carries news between them the way a bard carries news — embedded in verse, interpretable only by those who know the code. He offers a plain-Westron summary to the traveller: the northern clans are considering something the southern clans will not like.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He can tell he is talking to someone who is not Dunlending. He is deciding how much of the summary to give.

disposition.en: Stopped in the road, looking at the traveller directly. This is not normal bard behavior.

presence.en: He says: you are not supposed to be on this road today. He says it as a statement of fact, as if he has already told someone else this and is confirming it to the traveller as a courtesy.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: Someone told him the traveller would be on this road. He was asked to pass a message. The message is: turn around.

disposition.en: A woman at the edge of a settlement, gathering something from the hillside. She looks at the traveller with the unhurried assessment of someone who has been evaluating strangers her whole life.

presence.en: She can see the traveller is not in good shape — road-fatigue, a minor wound, something she can name before being asked. She names it. She has something for it but it will cost a small service: carrying a message to the next settlement.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: The offer is fair. She is testing whether the traveller is worth helping, and the test is this: do they take the offer seriously or dismiss it.

disposition.en: She is treating someone in a tent off the road. She comes out when the traveller passes.

presence.en: The person she is treating has the same wound that has been appearing on three people in the last month — all on the same road, all in the same section. She does not know what is making it. She describes it carefully, because she wants someone to carry the description further north.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: She is not asking for help. She is sharing a pattern. She has done everything she can for the people in front of her. The pattern is for whoever can use it.

disposition.en: A sense of being watched from the trees, and then — when the traveller stops — the watcher steps into view.

presence.en: She has been following the traveller for half a mile. She says so without apology. She was checking whether they were going to do anything worth noting.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: She has decided they are not. She tells them this, which is its own kind of assessment.

disposition.en: Steps out of a tree shadow onto the path. The traveller had no warning.

presence.en: Something has been crossing into the forest from the road at night for a week. Not orcs — wrong print, wrong smell. She has been watching the crossing-point and has not caught it. She wants to know if the traveller saw anything unusual on the road at night.

situation.en: She is asking because she has run out of her own leads. This is unusual for a forest ranger.

disposition.en: She has been tracking something and the track ends at the road — which means whatever it is used the road to conceal its prints.

presence.en: She asks directly whether the traveller has seen any other traveller on this road in the last day who seemed wrong — not threatening, just wrong. The way someone seems wrong when they are performing being ordinary.

situation.en: Half-orcs. She is looking for a half-orc who used the road as cover.

disposition.en: A small company on an old road — three of them, moving with the unhurried ease of people who have walked this path for longer than it has been a road.

presence.en: They acknowledge the traveller with the courteous brevity of those who have more important things to think about. One of them is studying something at the side of the road — a stone, or a mark on a stone.

channel.en: Have them bring up an age-old loss — a drowned realm, a kinsman long dead — as though it were last night.

situation.en: They are not going to explain what they are looking at unless asked, and asking may get more answer than expected.

disposition.en: One of them addresses the traveller directly while the others continue. He has been waiting for the right person to pass.

presence.en: He has found something disturbing on this road — a disruption in the old markers, the kind that were laid in the Second Age. He does not have enough context to understand what caused it. He wants to know if the traveller has noticed anything unusual on this stretch.

channel.en: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

situation.en: He is not afraid. He is thorough. Something is wrong here and he is collecting testimony.

disposition.en: A gate-check on the road into a fortified settlement. Formal, procedural, no hostility.

presence.en: They want to know the traveller's destination and business. The sergeant records both. He offers, unprompted, that the road south is currently clear but the western fork has had reports of a broken bridge.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: He is doing a job and doing it correctly. The information about the bridge is a professional courtesy.

disposition.en: A patrol on the road — not at a gate, in the open. They have been looking for someone.

presence.en: The sergeant describes a traveller who matches the description in his orders and asks if the traveller has seen anyone matching that description. He reads the description off a written note. It is specific.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: The description matches someone the traveller may or may not have seen. The sergeant does not know this.

disposition.en: A full patrol blocking the road at a junction. They have closed both directions.

presence.en: The road ahead is under military restriction — the sergeant says this in the tone of someone who has been saying it for hours and expects it to be challenged. He will not say why.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: Something has happened on the road ahead that Gondor does not want known yet. The restriction is new.

disposition.en: A man splitting wood at a farmstead off the road. He stops when the traveller passes and calls out a greeting.

presence.en: He has a spare room if the traveller needs to stop — a real bed, a meal, a fire. The price is fair. He has been hosting road-travelers for twenty years and is good at it.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: The offer is genuine. He likes the company and the news from outside.

disposition.en: Waving the traveller down from across a field.

presence.en: He needs help with something specific — a load that is too heavy for one person, a fence that needs a second pair of hands for an hour. He will pay in food and road information.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: The help will take an hour. The road information is worth it.

disposition.en: He comes to the road fence as the traveller passes and speaks quietly.

presence.en: Something has been coming to his animals at night — not taking them, scaring them. He has not been able to see it. He has three children and a farm and he has run out of options for explaining it. He asks if the traveller knows what leaves that kind of mark on a fence post.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: The marks he describes match something specific. What it is depends on where the farm is.

disposition.en: A small group of traders, well-armed, clearly far from home. They are courteous in the specific way of people who have learned courtesy keeps them alive in foreign lands.

presence.en: They are heading north to trade — spices, dyes, things the north does not produce. They have made this run before and know the roads. They want to know if the northern markets are still open; the last news they had was three months old.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: They are asking in good faith. They know they are viewed with suspicion here and have chosen competence over charm as their approach.

disposition.en: A soldier, not a trader — wrong equipment, wrong posture, too far north for his allegiance to be comfortable.

presence.en: He speaks careful Westron and wants to know if there is a Gondorian garrison post within a day's travel. He asks this like a man who needs to turn himself in before someone else finds him.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: He has crossed a line — either geographically or politically — and has decided his best option is the official one.

disposition.en: Moving fast in the other direction, not stopping. One of them looks at the traveller in a way that carries more information than a look should.

presence.en: The look is a warning. It is not hostile — it is the look of someone who wants the traveller to know that what is ahead of them is something they are running from.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are not going to stop and explain. They are running.

disposition.en: Ordinary settlement folk at the road's edge — not farmer exactly, not town exactly. The particular mix of the western Gondorian coast.

presence.en: They are friendly in the easy way of people who are used to travelers. They offer water, tell the traveller about the road ahead (one ford that is tricky this time of year), and ask where they are coming from.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: They want news from elsewhere. They will give road information freely in exchange.

disposition.en: A family packing a cart — clearly leaving, clearly in a hurry, clearly not happy about it.

presence.en: They are leaving their settlement because something happened three nights ago that they will not describe. The father says only: we are not the first to go. He says it looking at the road ahead, not at the traveller.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are leaving in the same direction the traveller is going. That is its own information.

disposition.en: High on a ridge above the road — two of them, watching a herd of goats. They register the traveller below without particular interest.

presence.en: Mountain people running their goats between summer and autumn pastures. They have been here every year of their lives and their parents before them. The traveller is a small event in a large rhythm.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: They will ignore the traveller entirely unless addressed.

disposition.en: One of them comes down from the ridge to the road — a long walk, done quickly. He wants something.

presence.en: He wants the traveller to carry a message to the settlement at the valley bottom. The message is oral — he recites it twice to make sure it is memorized. It is about water rights and a dispute that has been going on for two seasons.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: The message is important to him and he cannot go himself because the herd cannot be left. He is trusting a stranger with something that matters.

disposition.en: Three of them around a fire on the road, arguing. They have not noticed the traveller.

presence.en: The argument is about whether what they are cooking is better with the bones in or out. The level of disagreement is remarkable given the stakes. They are completely occupied.

situation.en: Dawn is five hours away. The road goes around the fire on the right side if done quietly.

disposition.en: One of them is standing in the road. The other two are audible behind him but not visible.

presence.en: He says, slowly and with effort: got anything worth having? It is the entirety of his negotiation strategy.

situation.en: He is asking before taking. This is as much courtesy as Stone-trolls offer.

disposition.en: It comes around a boulder in the road. It sees the traveller and stops, which is not what they usually do.

presence.en: It says — badly, in something that is approximately Westron — that this is its road at night. The statement is a test. It wants to see if the traveller argues.

situation.en: Arguing with Hill-trolls on their roads at night is how travelers become stories told by other travelers.

disposition.en: Two of them, already aware of the traveller. The larger one has moved to block the road ahead. The smaller one is circling.

presence.en: The larger one says nothing. It is past the talking phase.

situation.en: The circling one is the actual problem. The one in front is the distraction.

disposition.en: One on the road in full daylight. Armored. Not foraging — positioned.

presence.en: It does not speak. It is not here to speak. It is here because something placed it here and it will not move until its purpose is accomplished or it is removed.

situation.en: This is a weapon pointed at a road. The traveller is on the road.

disposition.en: A soldier at a garrison post — large, dark-skinned, speaks Westron correctly. The garrison is not Gondorian.

presence.en: He checks papers with the procedure of someone following orders. He is seven feet tall and armored in black and he is doing paperwork. The cognitive dissonance is its own kind of threat.

situation.en: The procedure is real. Satisfying the procedure is the goal.

disposition.en: The road empties. Sound goes wrong. The cold arrives before the shape does, and the shape has been there all along — the traveller simply could not see it until now.

presence.en: It does not speak first. The waiting is the first move. Every second of waiting costs something.

situation.en: Whatever it wants from this road today, the traveller is in it now.

disposition.en: A family on the road, moving slowly. They have too little for the distance they are covering. One of the children is being carried.

presence.en: They left their settlement four days ago on a rumor that the road south is safer. They do not know if the rumor is true. They are following it because staying felt worse.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: They are not asking for anything. They are just on the road.

disposition.en: A lone man sitting at the roadside, not moving.

presence.en: He is resting, or he has stopped being able to go on, and the two look the same from the road. When addressed he says he came from a settlement two days east where something happened that he will describe only as: everyone started leaving at once.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He does not know what caused the leaving. He left because everyone was leaving.

disposition.en: A group of them camped off the road — fifteen, twenty people, more than a family.

presence.en: They are not moving. They have been here three days. The road ahead, they say, is where it started, and they will not go back onto it. The road behind, someone in the group says quietly, is no different.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are trapped between two fears and they have chosen stillness over either direction.

channel.en: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.
Have him put short, suspicious questions, saying little of his own roads and liking prying even less.
Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.
Have him speak of loyalty to king and folk, and the binding weight of a word once given.
Have him bring up a grievance nursed for generations — a slight, a debt, an enemy not yet repaid.
Have them bring up an age-old loss — a drowned realm, a kinsman long dead — as though it were last night.
Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.
Have them turn the talk to the call of the Sea and the road West: who will take ship, and who will stay and dwindle.
Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.
Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.
Have them talk of the next meal, good ale, a warm fire and a soft bed — the real business of life.
Have them chatter about their hole, their garden, their kin and the doings of the next farm over.
Have them share who said what to whom, and the small scandals and rumours of the country round.
Have them offer food, a tale or directions, with homely, unsuspecting goodwill.
Have them show polite unease at strangers and the wide world, wishing adventures would happen elsewhere.
Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.
Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.
Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.
Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.
Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.
Have them offer aid on terms of their own — a gift, a path, a rescue — odd and not freely explained.
Have them turn the talk to beasts, trees and growing things, and the keeping of them.
Have them speak words that carry more than they say — a warning, a riddle, or counsel from one far older than he seems.
Have them put a strange, searching question that seems to weigh the traveller's worth or errand.
Have them turn the talk to the great shape of things: the slow war against the Shadow, and each one's small part in it.
Have them fling harsh demands at a captive — who are you, who sent you, what do you carry — backed by the lash.
Have them bicker and turn on one another over loot, orders or who eats first, overheard by the traveller.
Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

disposition.en: Offers before he is asked, then puts his questions after the food and not before.

presence.en: A byre-loft to sleep in, thin barley bread and a share of the pot. Coin is refused — coin draws the tax-riders and the tale-tellers. What they want is word from the road and an hour of hands at the evening work.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: The bargain is real on both sides and neither will name it aloud.

disposition.en: Willing, but the welcome is measured out — one night, the outer room, the door barred behind him.

presence.en: They will trade dried meat and the name of the safer of the two fords, but they want to know which road he came by and whether anything came along it behind him.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: Something has taught this house to count strangers. They will help and still be glad to see him gone at first light.

disposition.en: The offer comes from the doorway and no one steps out past it.

presence.en: Food left on the gate-stone, water drawn and set beside it. They will not have him under the roof and they will not let him go hungry either.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are afraid of what walks the country now and not certain he is no part of it. The charity is real; the fear is older.

disposition.en: Reads the gear and the northern bearing and settles on a Ranger's welcome — plain, unfussed, no questions about the errand.

presence.en: Hot food, a dry corner and grain for the road. In return they want to know whether the Greenway is being watched between here and the Bree-land, because their carter is due to travel it.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: They know what he is without the word being said. Rangers are useful and slightly unlucky to have at the table.

disposition.en: Offers the fire, then watches him eat with the attention of someone deciding whether to say more.

presence.en: They have kept a bundle for the next Ranger through — arrowheads, a mended cloak, and a folded scrap of writing left by a man who never came back for it.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: They have been holding a dead man's gear for two seasons and would rather hand it to a stranger than keep it another night.

disposition.en: Grim hospitality. The door opens because a Ranger is at least a known kind of trouble.

presence.en: They will feed him and ask him to walk out at first light to the sheep-fold on the ridge — something took two ewes there and left the carcasses untouched.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: They want the fold looked at and they do not want to be told the worst answer if that is what he finds.

disposition.en: Formal and a little dazzled, unsure whether they should offer at all, offering anyway.

presence.en: The best of the house pressed on her — new bread, honey, the one good cup — and a request that she look at a child who does not thrive.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: They have nothing worth giving to one of her kind and are giving it regardless. Refusing would cost them more than accepting.

disposition.en: Hospitality given at arm's length, with the door left open behind her and someone always in the room.

presence.en: They will share the fire and the pot but will take neither payment nor thanks, and they ask that she not be seen leaving by the village road in the morning.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: Kindness that must not be witnessed. It is not her they fear — it is what their neighbours would make of it.

disposition.en: An old woman decides for the household, over the muttering of the men, and puts food into her hands.

presence.en: A hearth-place for the night, and a question asked very low: whether the lights on the hills are what her grandmother always said they were.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: The old woman has waited her whole life to ask someone who would know. The answer will not comfort her.

disposition.en: Grudging at first, then bluntly hospitable once he is judged no friend of the Horse-lords.

presence.en: Mutton, curds and a place at the peat-fire, for a straight answer about the road east and whether riders have been counted on it lately.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: The whole welcome hangs on one thing — which side of the old quarrel he stands on. They will not ask twice.

disposition.en: A clan-head hears him out at the door of the long house before anything is decided.

presence.en: They will trade bread and a guide over the shoulder of the hills for worked iron — a knife, a spearhead, anything — and for the name of whoever fired the sheiling at the head of the valley.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: They believe a stranger knows more than he is saying. The trade is also a test of that.

disposition.en: Loud, generous and immediately curious, with beer in his hand before the greeting is finished.

presence.en: A bench in the hall, meat and ale, and the whole household wanting news of the southern roads; they will send him on with smoked fish and a fresh haft for his axe.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: The generosity is genuine and the questioning is relentless. Nothing is owed and everything is asked.

disposition.en: Hospitable, but the talk keeps circling back to the eastern road and who has been coming down it.

presence.en: They will provision him for three days if he carries word to the next steading: keep the beasts in and send no children to the summer pasture this year.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: They are being pushed westward by something they will not name at the table and would rather send a warning than admit it aloud.

disposition.en: Correct and faintly official — hospitality offered as a duty of the province rather than a kindness.

presence.en: A place in the outbuilding, bread, oil and olives, and his name and road written into the tally the village keeps for the garrison.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: The hospitality is real. So is the tally, and someone in Minas Anor will read it eventually.

disposition.en: A steward-minded man who wants to help within the rules, and is unhappy about where the rules have got to.

presence.en: He will sell food at last year's price and mention that the garrison has not patrolled past the third milestone since spring, whatever the notice at the well still says.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He is telling a stranger something he ought to be telling his own captain. He knows it.

disposition.en: Recognises the manner if not the man, and the door opens wider than it would for anyone else.

presence.en: A dry loft, hot food and the loan of a whetstone. The household keeps a bundle of arrows for those who walk this road and asks only for word of the northern circuit.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: These are folk who have kept faith with a ruined kingdom for generations and want to hear that it still counts for something.

disposition.en: Weather-hardened and easy, judging him the way they judge a boat — by whether he will be trouble in a swell.

presence.en: Smoked fish, flat bread and a berth in the net-loft, on the understanding that he takes an oar if the boat goes out before dawn.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: Nothing here is free, but the price is work and everyone knows the rate.

disposition.en: Careful and entirely practical. They do not ask his errand; they ask what he has on his feet.

presence.en: Seal-meat, a place out of the wind and dry boot-liners of woven grass — given because a badly shod stranger will be dead within the moon, and dead strangers bring bad luck.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: There is no sentiment in it. The land does not allow any. The gift is exact and it will save his life.

disposition.en: Wary and hard to read, offering from a distance and only after long looking.

presence.en: A share of what is on the spit and a place at the edge of the firelight. They want arrowheads, salt, or word of where the war-bands are moving — in that order.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are camped in country nobody rules and they trust nothing that has not yet proved useful.

disposition.en: A shepherd on high ground who has decided he is no raider and has therefore become talkative.

presence.en: Ewe-cheese, hard bread and a way over the shoulder of the pass that is a day shorter than the road — in exchange for help walking a lame ewe down to the fold.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: The short way is real and it is only offered to those who help with the ewe. That is the whole of the test.

disposition.en: Nothing is said. A hand shows him the fire, then shows him where he may sit.

presence.en: Roasted roots and water, and afterwards three cut sticks laid on a stone that give the shape of the trail ahead and the one place on it that must be walked around.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: They are handing him the land in their own language and they will not repeat it. Either he can read it or he cannot.

disposition.en: Deals from behind a spear-shaft and does not lower it while the trade is made.

presence.en: They have water, roots and a route around the burnt country to the north, and they want a blade or a cloak-pin for it. The price is not negotiable and not unfair.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They have been raided twice this season and will trade with anyone who is not carrying the raiders' gear.

disposition.en: Three of them come down to the fire uninvited, sit on their heels and wait to be told who he is before anything is offered.

presence.en: Mutton fat, oatcake and a skin of thin beer, once he has answered where he is bound. They also want to know how many riders he has passed on the open grass and whether any of them carried a horn.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: Hill-folk share their fire readily and their trust never. What is being bought with the food is information about the horse-folk.

disposition.en: Guarded and blunt. The eldest does the talking; the young men stand back with their spears grounded and their faces closed.

presence.en: They will give him a place by the fire, cold mutton and the name of a dry crossing, and in exchange they want salt and an oath that he carries no word to the horse-folk about where this camp stands.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are in country they consider stolen from them and they are camped on it without leave. The hospitality is genuine and so is the threat under it.

disposition.en: No welcome at all until an old woman overrules the men, and then the welcome is total and slightly frightening.

presence.en: Food, a hide to sleep under and a warning: two of their own went east to the burnt sheiling nine days ago and nothing has come back down that track since, not even the dogs.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: They need a stranger to walk that track because they will not send more of their own. They will not ask outright. They will let him work out that they need it.

disposition.en: Sorts him at a glance: not of the horse-folk, not of Gondor, therefore tolerable. The manner shifts from hard to merely watchful.

presence.en: Curds and barley bread, and a track over the shoulder of the hills that avoids the claimed ground entirely — offered because a man who walks alone and armed is worth having as a neutral thing on the road.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: They are buying his indifference, not his friendship. Both sides know the coin is fair.

disposition.en: Suspicion first — Elves are a thing their tale-tellers use to explain misfortune — then the practical business of a hard year takes over.

presence.en: They will feed her and let her sleep within the ring of the camp, and one man asks, half ashamed, whether she can tell why the spring below the camp has gone bitter.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: She could tell them exactly why. Telling them will confirm something they would rather have kept as a story.

disposition.en: A hill-healer who wants to see his hands and his feet before she offers anything else.

presence.en: Salve for cracked heels, a bundle of dried yarrow and a pot of something bitter for river-fever, traded for needles, thread or any small worked steel she cannot get up here.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: Her craft is real and old and she is short of everything that has to be forged rather than grown.

disposition.en: Riders pull up, look down from the saddle, and are courteous in the way of people who have already decided they could deal with him if it came to that.

presence.en: Hard cheese, dried meat and a full water-skin, plus the shortest line to the nearest hall — freely given, because on the open grass a traveller left dry is a traveller who dies badly.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: The gift costs them nothing and is a point of honour. Refusing it would be the insult.

disposition.en: Helpful and openly measuring him at the same time — one of the riders keeps circling wide while the other talks.

presence.en: They will share food and grain and ask, in return, whether he has seen fires in the hills to the west, and how many, and how far apart.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: They are counting hill-folk camps and he is the only source they have today. What he says may put riders on a track by tomorrow.

disposition.en: Horse-folk at a picket-line, easy and loud, feeding him before they have his name.

presence.en: Mare's milk, meat and a place at the fire; they want to hear the state of the grass and the water on the road he came by, since they are moving the herd within the week.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: Their whole year turns on where the grazing is good. A traveller's eyes are worth a meal.

disposition.en: No greeting is offered and none is expected. A hand puts food where he can reach it and withdraws.

presence.en: Roots, smoked meat and a gourd of clean water. Afterwards a mark is cut into a stump beside the trail: the sign that says this one may pass.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: The gift is real and the silence is not unfriendliness. They are simply not a people who explain themselves.

disposition.en: Comfortable, nosy and entirely friendly — the innkeeper's manner, whether or not there is an inn.

presence.en: A bed of straw, stew, small beer and the whole state of the Bree-land laid out unasked, in exchange for news of the Greenway and a copper or two.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: Nothing is at stake for them and everything is interesting. The price of the bed is the story.

disposition.en: Friendly, but the gate is shut behind him and the talk turns quickly to who has been on the road lately.

presence.en: Food and a roof for a fair price, and a plain warning that two waggons went south last month and only one came back, and nobody official has come to ask about it.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: They want someone to take the matter seriously without them having to be the ones who made a fuss about it.

disposition.en: Boatmen who deal briskly and price everything, including kindness, without embarrassment.

presence.en: Passage downriver on the barge, a share of the fish and a dry place among the bales, for coin, tobacco or three hours at the pole.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: They will take him if he is useful and put him off at the next landing if he is not. It is not personal.

disposition.en: A tinker with a pack-frame and a cart, delighted to have someone new to talk at.

presence.en: Mended straps, a new buckle and a resoled boot for a small coin, plus every rumour between here and the last market — some of them even true.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He is lonely and he is a trader and both of those are working on him at once.

disposition.en: A big man who does not smile, blocks the doorway of the steading, then steps aside and puts honey on the table.

presence.en: Bread, cream and honey and no meat at all at that board, and a bed in the hay; what he wants in return is an accounting of any beast the traveller has killed on his land.

channel.en: Have them turn the talk to beasts, trees and growing things, and the keeping of them.

situation.en: The hospitality is generous and there are rules under it that are not open to discussion.

disposition.en: Wary at the treeline, then practical once it is clear he is walking through and not settling in.

presence.en: A share of the pot, resin-torches for the night stretch and directions to the one clearing where a fire will not be seen from the eastern slopes.

channel.en: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

situation.en: They live under the eaves of a wood that has been getting worse for a generation and they measure every kindness against the risk of being noticed.

disposition.en: A shepherd glad of a face; he has been on the high pasture with dogs and ewes for five weeks.

presence.en: Cheese, hard bread and the loan of a dog for the night watch, in exchange for company at the fire and an honest answer about the state of the lower fords.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: He wants talk more than he wants goods. The dog is offered because he cannot think what else to give.

disposition.en: Silent assessment of his clothing, then a decision made without discussion.

presence.en: A snow-house shared for the night, seal-fat, and a hooded overshirt of gut-skin that will keep the wind out; they want iron, needles or fish-hooks, nothing else.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: They are the only people who live here and they know exactly what it costs to be wrong about the weather. The trade is a lesson as much as a bargain.

disposition.en: Marsh-folk who speak little and point often; a punt is already being poled towards him before anything is agreed.

presence.en: Eel, flat reed-bread and a lift across the wet ground by punt, for a coin or a favour; and a warning about which of the two channels is walked and which is only ever floated.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: The marsh kills people who guess. They would rather ferry him than find him.

disposition.en: A farmer with dust on him who offers the shade first and the food second.

presence.en: Bread, oil, dried figs and water from the well, sold at a fair price, and the news that the road bridge two leagues on is down and the ford is being used instead.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: He wants nothing but a witness to the fact that nobody has come to mend the bridge since spring.

disposition.en: A caravan-master who prices him as cargo before he speaks: one more body on the road is either a guard or a risk.

presence.en: A place walking with the waggons, two meals a day and water, in exchange for standing a watch each night as far as the next market town.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: Company on the road is worth food to them and food is worth company to him. The arrangement lasts exactly as long as it suits both.

disposition.en: The master deals fast and keeps looking back down the road while he does it.

presence.en: He will sell food cheap and pay for a sword to walk with them tonight, because he has seen the same three men behind the caravan since the last river crossing.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: He is buying protection and calling it a trade. Both of them can see the men on the road.

disposition.en: A single trader with a mule and a professional smile that does not quite reach the eyes.

presence.en: Salt, thread, a whetstone and a small pot of honey at slightly too high a price, with good road-news thrown in to justify the margin.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: He is honest enough and he will still take whatever the market allows. The news is the real value and he knows it.

disposition.en: Frank and hard-worn; she names what she has and what she needs in the same breath.

presence.en: Dried fish, a bed in the byre and the new line of the crossing since the storm shifted the sandbanks, for salt and word from the north.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: She trades from a position of knowing more about this country than anyone he will meet today and she prices accordingly.

disposition.en: Mountain-folk of the White Mountains: courteous, slow to warm, and unwilling to let a stranger go up the pass unprepared.

presence.en: Ewe-cheese, a coil of good rope and a stick cut to the right length for the scree, given for whatever he thinks fair — and a flat statement of which hour of the day the pass is safe.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: They have carried bodies down off that pass. The rope is not a courtesy.

disposition.en: No ceremony at all. Gear is put out on a stone: take what is needed, leave what is not.

presence.en: A cache opened — arrows, a spare cloak, hard bread, a phial of athelas — and the current state of the circuit given in six sentences.

channel.en: Have them speak of loyalty to king and folk, and the binding weight of a word once given.

situation.en: Between those who keep the same watch there is no bargaining, only accounting. The cache will be restocked by whoever passes next.

disposition.en: Fellow travellers on the same road, willing to pool what they have because the night is coming either way.

presence.en: A shared fire, a shared pot and watches split between them, plus everything they know about the next two days of road.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: Nobody is in charge of this arrangement and it works precisely because nobody asks anything beyond the morning.

disposition.en: River-folk mending nets who talk while their hands keep working.

presence.en: Fresh fish, a place on the jetty out of the mud and a warning that the water has been running wrong for a week — up when it should be down.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: The river is their whole living and something upstream has changed. They would like a traveller who is going that way to look.

disposition.en: Courteous and unhurried. The offer is made as though it had been decided long before he arrived.

presence.en: Waybread, clean water and a night under a hythe of woven branches, with the road ahead described exactly: three fords, two of them safe, and the hour at which the last of them can be crossed.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: Nothing is asked in return, which is itself a kind of weight. The gift assumes he will do something worth the giving.

disposition.en: Kind, but the kindness has a limit set into it, and the limit is spoken plainly.

presence.en: They will heal what can be healed tonight, feed him, and set him on a path that skirts the bad country; they will not go with him past the eaves of the wood.

channel.en: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

situation.en: They have judged that his road is his own and are unwilling to be drawn along it. The help is real; the boundary is not negotiable.

disposition.en: They look at him longer than is comfortable before anything is offered, and what is offered is aimed at something other than his hunger.

presence.en: Food, and then a request that he sit while one of them sings over him — for the weariness they say is not only in his legs.

channel.en: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

situation.en: They can see what he is carrying and they are treating it, not discussing it. He may refuse, and refusing will cost him the night's rest.

disposition.en: Greeted as one of the old alliance — a formality observed exactly, with real warmth somewhere under it.

presence.en: Bread, cord, arrows fletched their way, and word of which of the two northern passes has been quiet this month and which has not.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: They deal with the Dúnedain as inheritors of an old agreement. He is being helped as an heir, not as a man.

disposition.en: The courtesy is thinner than usual. Something has made them careful with the roads and with who is on them.

presence.en: They will provision him for four days and ask him to change his line of march: the valley he intended is being watched, and they would rather he did not walk into what they are watching it for.

channel.en: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

situation.en: They are asking him to alter his errand for reasons they will not explain. They expect him to accept it on trust alone.

disposition.en: Recognition and immediate deference, and then the ordinary business of kin looking after kin.

presence.en: A proper camp made for her without being asked, hot water, and news of who has passed west along this road in the last hundred years.

channel.en: Have them turn the talk to the call of the Sea and the road West: who will take ship, and who will stay and dwindle.

situation.en: They assume she is going west eventually. Nobody says so. The assumption sits in the middle of the conversation.

disposition.en: Gentle and slightly too careful with her, the way people are careful with something they have been told about.

presence.en: They offer shelter, a horse if she wants one, and an escort as far as the river — and one of them asks whether she is travelling by choice.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: The question is kindly meant and lands somewhere she does not want examined tonight.

disposition.en: Grave, quiet hospitality, offered by people who have understood something without being told it.

presence.en: A fire built low, food she does not want, and a place made ready in the middle of their camp rather than at its edge — deliberately, so that she is surrounded.

channel.en: Have them bring up an age-old loss — a drowned realm, a kinsman long dead — as though it were last night.

situation.en: They have decided she should not be left alone tonight. They will not say that either.

disposition.en: Formal, practical and faintly amused at how badly Men travel — they begin repacking his gear before asking permission.

presence.en: Waybread and a small flask of cordial, a strap replaced, a wound cleaned properly, and the safe line down to the Ford of Bruinen given landmark by landmark.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: This is a household that has been doing this for two thousand years. The help is routine to them and remarkable to him.

disposition.en: Grave and busy. They are moving something along this road and the traveller has arrived in the middle of it.

presence.en: They will treat his hurts and give him three days of food, and ask that he take the low road for the next two days and mention to nobody what he saw on this one.

channel.en: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.
