situation.en: Their errand is larger than his and they are buying his silence with real kindness. It is not a threat and it is not free either.

disposition.en: Unseen until they choose otherwise; then grave, close-mouthed and exact about what is permitted.

presence.en: Lembas-cake, a coil of grey rope and a flet to sleep on above the ground, on the condition that he does not walk the wood after dark and does not cut anything living.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: The gift and the rule are one thing. They are lending him their forest for a night on very specific terms.

disposition.en: Cheerful on the surface and entirely unyielding underneath. Wine appears before questions do.

presence.en: A hot meal, a skin of strong wine and a guide as far as the forest gate, in exchange for word of the eastern road and how the river ran where he crossed it.

channel.en: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

situation.en: They are generous within their bounds and they have no intention of letting him wander their wood unescorted.

disposition.en: A company on the march halts for him, which is more than they were obliged to do.

presence.en: Food from their own store, a lantern of the sort that is not lit with fire, and the road west laid out with the two places on it where a fire should not be built.

channel.en: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

situation.en: They are going west and he is going the other way. Whatever they give him, they will not be here to see it used.

disposition.en: A guardian of a border who has decided to help him leave rather than help him stay.

presence.en: Water, dried fruit and a blunt instruction: the way he is going is closed, and here is the way that is not, and it costs him a day.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: The kindness is a means of moving him off ground they are keeping. He gains a safe road and loses a day, and that is the whole bargain.

disposition.en: Grey-clad and preoccupied, courteous in the manner of people whose real attention is on the harbour behind them.

presence.en: Ship's bread, salt fish and passage across the firth in a boat going that way regardless, and news of which havens still keep a light.

channel.en: Have them turn the talk to the call of the Sea and the road West: who will take ship, and who will stay and dwindle.

situation.en: Everything here is arranged around departure. He is being helped on his way by people arranging their own.

disposition.en: A single ranger of the green wood, spare with words, generous with practical things.

presence.en: Arrows, a mended boot-sole and the exact position of the one clean spring in a day's march of bad water.

channel.en: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

situation.en: He has been alone in the wood a long time and gives what is useful because that is the only currency he keeps.

disposition.en: An Elf of learning who would rather trade knowledge than goods, and says so at once.

presence.en: Copies made of two road-maps, the true name of a ruin on his route and an hour of instruction on what the boundary-stones there mean — in exchange for a full account of what he has seen on the road.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: He wants the traveller's eyes and is paying properly for them. It is the most honest transaction of the journey.

disposition.en: Pale, quiet and utterly at home in the cold; they appear beside him without any sound of arrival.

presence.en: A hot drink he cannot identify, dry wrappings for his hands, and the safe line across the ice, which is not the line the ground suggests.

channel.en: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

situation.en: They are helping a traveller who would otherwise be dead by morning, and they are not sentimental about it.

disposition.en: A fisher of the shore-folk, weathered and easy, who offers a place in the boat before any talk of payment.

presence.en: Grilled fish, fresh water and a lift along the coast past the headland that cannot be walked around at this tide.

channel.en: Have them turn the talk to the call of the Sea and the road West: who will take ship, and who will stay and dwindle.

situation.en: The sea sets the terms here and the Elf simply knows them. He is being carried because walking would kill him.

disposition.en: Ordinary to look at and entirely unsurprised to find him here, as though the meeting were on a list somewhere.

presence.en: Food he did not know he needed, a name for the thing that has been troubling his road, and directions given by landmarks that turn out to be exactly right.

channel.en: Have them offer aid on terms of their own — a gift, a path, a rescue — odd and not freely explained.

situation.en: The help is freely given and the terms are not explained. Something is being served that has nothing to do with him.

disposition.en: Kindly and abstracted, and the kindness lands like a decision that was made about him rather than for him.

presence.en: A hot meal, a night's shelter that should not exist where it is standing, and one piece of counsel that will only make sense in three days.

channel.en: Have them speak words that carry more than they say — a warning, a riddle, or counsel from one far older than he seems.

situation.en: He is being helped for reasons attached to something much larger than his journey. Refusing would be permitted and would cost him.

disposition.en: Attentive in a way that is not comfortable, and the offer is made only after a long, weighing look.

presence.en: A rescue, more or less: a way out of the country he has walked into, given on the single condition that he turns back now and does not go on to look.

channel.en: Have them put a strange, searching question that seems to weigh the traveller's worth or errand.

situation.en: The condition is the whole of it. He can have the help or he can have the road. Not both.

disposition.en: A shabby brown-clad old man surrounded by too many birds, who talks to the traveller and to a hedgehog with the same courtesy.

presence.en: Herbs sorted into twists of leaf with instructions for each, a warm mash of something wholesome, and a message about the road ahead delivered second-hand from a crow.

channel.en: Have them turn the talk to beasts, trees and growing things, and the keeping of them.

situation.en: He is entirely serious about the birds and the birds are entirely accurate. Taking him lightly is the only mistake available here.

disposition.en: Distracted, fussing over a hurt animal, and only half his attention on the traveller until something in the answers catches it.

presence.en: He will physic the traveller and the traveller's blisters and then ask for help carrying an injured beast two miles out of the way to a place where it can be left safely.

channel.en: Have them turn the talk to beasts, trees and growing things, and the keeping of them.

situation.en: The detour is real and inconvenient and it is also the whole test, though he does not think of it as one.

disposition.en: Absurdly cheerful, singing more than speaking, and entirely unbothered by anything the traveller might be afraid of.

presence.en: Yellow cream, honeycomb, bread and butter, a bed of dry rushes and a rhyme to call by if the ground turns treacherous — none of it asked for, none of it refusable.

channel.en: Have them offer aid on terms of their own — a gift, a path, a rescue — odd and not freely explained.

situation.en: The gift is total and the terms are nonsense and the nonsense works. His country, his rules, and the rules are kind.

disposition.en: Booming and hospitable, and once or twice startlingly serious for about four words at a time.

presence.en: A night's lodging, all the food he can hold, his gear dried by morning, and directions out of the forest that only work if followed exactly and without cleverness.

channel.en: Have them speak words that carry more than they say — a warning, a riddle, or counsel from one far older than he seems.

situation.en: He will give everything and explain nothing. What he says about the willow and the barrows is not a story and should not be treated as one.

disposition.en: Greets her by a name in a tongue older than her father's house, and then offers her breakfast as though that were the greater matter.

presence.en: Bread, honey and yellow cream, and a remark made in passing about the water under the Downs that is worth more than any map she has been given this year.

channel.en: Have them offer aid on terms of their own — a gift, a path, a rescue — odd and not freely explained.

situation.en: He is older than her grief and treats it as weather. It is the first time in a long while that nobody has been careful with her.

disposition.en: Nothing appears. The offer arrives as a road that has become easy, a wind at his back, a door standing conveniently open.

presence.en: Everything he needs is suddenly available on the eastern line of march: water, shelter, dry wood, an unguarded track. Only the eastern line.

channel.en: Have them offer aid on terms of their own — a gift, a path, a rescue — odd and not freely explained.

situation.en: This is not generosity. It is a hand on the small of his back, and the destination is not his.

disposition.en: A courtesy without a body: the dread lifts, briefly, in exchange for nothing that can be named.

presence.en: Rest is offered — real rest, the first in weeks — if he will sleep in a particular place, on ground that some old instinct says has been chosen for him.

channel.en: Have them turn the talk to the great shape of things: the slow war against the Shadow, and each one's small part in it.

situation.en: The bargain is being made with the part of him that is tired, not the part that decides. That is the whole method.

disposition.en: Startled, then polite, then talkative once it is clear nothing is going to be demanded of them.

presence.en: Where the next farm is, whose dog to avoid, how bad the rain was last week and how good the plums will be if it holds off — delivered in one breath.

channel.en: Have them share who said what to whom, and the small scandals and rumours of the country round.

situation.en: There is nothing at stake for them beyond politeness, and politeness is taken very seriously.

disposition.en: Polite and plainly wishing the conversation elsewhere; one keeps a hand on the gate the whole time.

presence.en: They will confirm the road and mention, reluctantly, that strangers came through nine days ago and did not behave like traders.

channel.en: Have them show polite unease at strangers and the wide world, wishing adventures would happen elsewhere.

situation.en: They do not want to be involved in whatever this is. Saying it out loud is already more than they meant to do.

disposition.en: Frightened and stubbornly courteous anyway, which is a thing hobbits can do that almost nobody else manages.

presence.en: They have moved the children to the far farm and they are not saying why; they ask only whether the road east is passable, and press a wrapped seed-cake on him.

channel.en: Have them offer food, a tale or directions, with homely, unsuspecting goodwill.

situation.en: They are more afraid than they will admit and the cake is what they have instead of words.

disposition.en: Brown, small and immediately at ease once the traveller sits down, which lowers him to a reasonable size.

presence.en: Talk of the burrow, the state of the bank it is dug into, whose mushrooms are whose, and a warning about the ditch further on that has swallowed a pony.

channel.en: Have them chatter about their hole, their garden, their kin and the doings of the next farm over.

situation.en: Nothing here is dangerous and nothing here is trivial to them. The ditch is the most important news in the district.

disposition.en: Bolder than the rest of their kind and openly delighted to have found somebody new to interrogate.

presence.en: Questions about where he has been, in order, with follow-ups — and in exchange the whole gossip of the district and an offer to walk part of the way for the novelty of it.

channel.en: Have them share who said what to whom, and the small scandals and rumours of the country round.

situation.en: Their curiosity outruns their caution. Somebody in that family is going to leave home eventually.

disposition.en: Broad, slow-spoken river-folk who go on with their work while they talk and do not look up much.

presence.en: Which channel takes a boat and which takes a leg, where the eels are running, and the fact that the reeds have been cut on the far bank by somebody who does not live there.

channel.en: Have them share who said what to whom, and the small scandals and rumours of the country round.

situation.en: They notice everything on this water and mention about a third of it.

disposition.en: Barely willing to be seen — the talk happens across ten feet of bracken and could end at any moment.

presence.en: Two sentences about where the water is good and one about a place further on where the birds have gone quiet, and then they are finished with him.

channel.en: Have them show polite unease at strangers and the wide world, wishing adventures would happen elsewhere.

situation.en: They live out here precisely to avoid conversations like this one. Every word is a concession.

disposition.en: On the road with a pack far too big for him and pathetically glad of company at the fire.

presence.en: Where he is from, where he thinks he is going, and a request for an honest opinion on whether the eastern road is as bad as people say.

channel.en: Have them talk of the next meal, good ale, a warm fire and a soft bed — the real business of life.

situation.en: He has no idea how far he actually is from home. Telling him the truth might turn him around, which would be the kindest outcome.

disposition.en: Stops, looks him over from boots to hood, and gives a greeting that is closer to a receipt than a welcome.

presence.en: Where the road is bad, where the water is good, and a flat refusal to say where he himself is going or what is under the oilcloth on the pony.

channel.en: Have him put short, suspicious questions, saying little of his own roads and liking prying even less.

situation.en: Everything he offers is accurate and nothing he withholds will be prised out. That is the whole shape of the exchange.

disposition.en: Short with him, and it is not personal — something on this road has already annoyed him and the traveller is merely next.

presence.en: A complaint about a toll being taken at a crossing where no toll was taken last year, with the exact sum, the exact place and the exact name of the man taking it.

channel.en: Have him bring up a grievance nursed for generations — a slight, a debt, an enemy not yet repaid.

situation.en: He wants a witness more than he wants sympathy. The grievance will be repeated in front of the right people eventually.

disposition.en: Grim and abrupt, with the shoulders of someone who has been walking fast for days and would rather not explain why.

presence.en: He says one useful thing and one dark one: the eastern gallery road is closed, and whatever closed it did not do it with tools.

channel.en: Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.

situation.en: He has decided to give the warning and not the story. The story is his folk's business and not the traveller's.

disposition.en: Names what he has, names what he wants for it, and stands there until an answer comes.

presence.en: Iron rations, a decent whetstone, a strap-buckle and a mended boot-nail, priced fairly and not one copper below it.

channel.en: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.

situation.en: He will not haggle and he will not cheat, and he considers the second a matter of honour and the first a waste of daylight.

disposition.en: Deals warily and keeps the pack between them while he does it.

presence.en: He will trade food and a place at his fire for the traveller standing the first watch, because he has not slept properly since the pass and will not say what is behind him.

channel.en: Have him put short, suspicious questions, saying little of his own roads and liking prying even less.

situation.en: He needs someone else's eyes for four hours and he hates needing it. The trade is an admission he will not make in words.

disposition.en: Blunt to the point of rudeness and entirely without deference, which is the closest thing to respect he offers anyone.

presence.en: He will give her food and the road-notes she needs, and wants in exchange the correct old name of a landmark on his map, which nobody alive has been able to give him.

channel.en: Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.

situation.en: He is not awed by her age; he is interested in it, which is rarer and easier to bear.

disposition.en: Well-armed, well-provisioned and openly proud of both; the greeting is loud and the questions are practical.

presence.en: News of the eastern road, the price of iron three markets away, and an unprompted opinion on the folk of the Long Lake that lasts some time.

channel.en: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.

situation.en: They have nothing to fear on this road today and it shows in how much they are willing to say.

disposition.en: Closed as a shut door on the subject of where he is from, and grimly talkative about everything else.

presence.en: He wants to know whether anyone has been up the Dimrill Stair this season, and who, and whether they came back down it.

channel.en: Have him speak of a mansion or mine lost to dragon or goblin, and the wealth and kin buried with it.

situation.en: He is asking about a doorway his folk lost long ago and will not say why he is counting the people who go near it.

disposition.en: Business-like, unhurried, and visibly pleased to have found a customer this far from a market.

presence.en: Salt, nails, a good knife and a length of chain, sold at market price plus carriage, with the state of the Great Road thrown in at no charge.

channel.en: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.

situation.en: This is a trading party and he is a small piece of a long ledger. The fairness is professional, not sentimental.

disposition.en: A merchant who has the goods unpacked before agreement is reached, because he knows what a tired man looks at first.

presence.en: Boot-nails, a spare buckle, hard biscuit, and a small mirror he is oddly determined to sell; and news of every market between here and the mountains.

channel.en: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.

situation.en: He is going to make a profit and be entirely honest about how much. The mirror is a matter of professional pride by now.

disposition.en: Suspicious on sight — a man alone near his diggings is a claim-jumper until proved otherwise.

presence.en: Short questions about which way the traveller came and whether he stopped anywhere near the stream-head, and a grudging note on where the ground is safe to walk.

channel.en: Have him put short, suspicious questions, saying little of his own roads and liking prying even less.

situation.en: He is standing on a find he has not registered with anyone and he is not subtle about guarding it.

disposition.en: A patrol that halts him with a raised axe-handle and then talks to him quite civilly from behind it.

presence.en: They want his name, his road and whether he has seen anyone moving on the high tracks; in return they will say which of the two gates is open this month.

channel.en: Have him speak of loyalty to king and folk, and the binding weight of a word once given.

situation.en: They are keeping a border and he is a data point. The civility is real and so is the axe-handle.

disposition.en: Half-wild and hard to place, speaking a rough Westron and watching the traveller's hands rather than his face.

presence.en: He trades furs and worked bone, wants iron above everything, and mentions that the northern ice has been giving up things this year that were better left under it.

channel.en: Have him put short, suspicious questions, saying little of his own roads and liking prying even less.

situation.en: He is used to being taken for something less than he is and has stopped minding. The remark about the ice is not a joke.

disposition.en: Filthy, cheerful and glad of any face that has not been underground for a month.

presence.en: A hot meal at the mine-mouth, water, and a lantern refilled, in exchange for news from outside and a hand at the windlass for an hour.

channel.en: Have him talk of fine work, rich seams and fair trade — gold, gems and the worth of things — and speak of them bluntly.

situation.en: They are lonely, well-fed and slightly bored, and company is worth more to them than the lamp-oil.

disposition.en: Standing across the road with the easy confidence of men who have done this before and not been punished for it.

presence.en: They want a toll for a bridge they did not build, and they are prepared to call it a toll for as long as he is prepared to call it one.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: Nobody has drawn yet. What happens next depends on whether he looks like more trouble than a few coins are worth.

disposition.en: Four of them spread across the way in a formation that closes as soon as he stops walking.

presence.en: They want the pack opened and the contents named, and they have already decided which items they will be keeping.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: The positions were taken before he arrived. Talking is still possible; walking away is not.

disposition.en: No demand at first — only silence and a slow closing of the distance, which is worse.

presence.en: They are not after goods. They want to know who he is and who sent him, and one of them keeps checking his face against something he has been told.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: This is not robbery. Someone is looking for someone and he resembles the description closely enough.

disposition.en: Ragged, hungry and dangerous in the specific way of men with nothing left to lose and no discipline to lose it with.

presence.en: They want the pack, the boots and the water, in that order, and they are arguing among themselves about the boots while they say it.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are badly organised and there are five of them. The disorganisation is the opening and it will not last.

disposition.en: Better armed than bandits should be, and two of them still wearing pieces of a uniform they have not bothered to remove.

presence.en: They demand a toll and give a garrison's name while doing it, and are visibly uncertain whether the traveller will know that the garrison disbanded two years ago.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are deserters trading on an authority they no longer have. Naming that out loud would end the pretence and start something else.

disposition.en: Two in front talking pleasantly while a third moves round to where he cannot comfortably watch.

presence.en: A friendly conversation about the road, whose only purpose is to keep his eyes forward for the count of twenty.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: The talk is the weapon here. Answering it politely for too long is how travellers lose their packs.

disposition.en: Not hostile so much as inconvenienced: he has walked into the middle of something and now they must decide what to do about him.

presence.en: They want to know what he saw at the landing, and they are willing to buy an answer of none at all, in coin, on the spot.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: Nobody wants a fight here. They want a witness who is either paid or gone, and they are offering him the choice.

disposition.en: Perfectly polite, unarmed to look at, asking questions in an order that is far too well constructed to be casual.

presence.en: He wants the traveller's name, his last three stopping-places and the name of anyone who vouched for him, and he already knows two of the answers.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: This is an interrogation dressed as a courtesy. Every answer is being checked against something written down elsewhere.

disposition.en: Spears grounded but held, and the speaker stands close enough that the conversation cannot be a long one.

presence.en: This ground is claimed, the claim is older than any map he is carrying, and they want to hear him say that he is only passing through.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are not looking for plunder. They are looking for an acknowledgment, and they will take it in words if he offers them.

disposition.en: Chariot-folk of the eastern plains, unhurried, treating the encounter as a matter of administration rather than violence.

presence.en: They want tribute — a weapon, a beast, or a day of labour — and they have a formula for it that has been used on this road for generations.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: Refusal is permitted and has a known price. They will not be insulted by it; they will simply apply the price.

disposition.en: Horsemen who circle once before anyone speaks, and the speaking is done from the saddle at a distance.

presence.en: They demand to know whose service he is in, and the question has only two answers they accept, and neither of them is none.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They cannot place him and they dislike what cannot be placed. The wrong answer here costs more than the pack.

disposition.en: Disciplined and unhurried, in the manner of men who are part of something much larger and know it.

presence.en: An officer asks for his road and his purpose through a translator, and writes the answers down, which is worse than if he had shouted them.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: He is being recorded, not robbed. Whatever he says here will be somewhere in a file by the next full moon.

disposition.en: Tall, courteous and entirely cold; the courtesy is the frightening part, since it costs them nothing to maintain it.

presence.en: He is asked, in excellent Westron, what his lineage is — and it is clear from the phrasing that the answer matters more to them than his errand.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are the inheritors of a specific old treason and they can hear the North in his speech. The politeness will last exactly as long as it is useful.

disposition.en: A checkpoint where no checkpoint should be, manned by men who serve something they do not name aloud.

presence.en: They demand papers that were never issued in this country, then a name, then an account of the last four days — and they are hoping he lies about one of them.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: The demands are designed to produce a false answer they can act on. There are six of them and one road.

disposition.en: Come up from a beached boat, loud and quick, and dealing in threats because threats have always been cheaper than work.

presence.en: They want whatever is in the pack and any coin on him, and they want it before whoever else is on this shore arrives.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: They are in a hurry, which makes them dangerous and also makes them stupid. The hurry is the lever.

disposition.en: Desperate rather than wicked, blocking the path with a stick and a shaking voice and no plan at all beyond stopping him.

presence.en: They want food and they are asking for it in the worst possible way, because asking properly has not worked twice already this week.

channel.en: Have them raise a trouble of their own — a beast, a feud, a missing kinsman — and hope the stranger might aid it.

situation.en: There is no real threat in it and there is real danger anyway: cornered people do things they did not intend.

disposition.en: They come out onto the road in a spread line and start with noise, because noise has worked for them before.

presence.en: Demands to know what he carries, mixed with jeering about what they will do with him afterwards, and no interest at all in the answers.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: There is no negotiation available here. The talk is only the space before the rush.

disposition.en: They hold the way with the confidence of a company that has been given orders about this road.

presence.en: The one in charge wants him alive and says so, and the others are audibly unhappy about that instruction.

channel.en: Have them bicker and turn on one another over loot, orders or who eats first, overheard by the traveller.

situation.en: The order to take him alive is the only thing keeping this a conversation, and their discipline is thin.

disposition.en: A rabble that stops short when it realises he has not run, and covers the hesitation with shouting.

presence.en: Threats, a demand for his gear, and an argument breaking out at the back over who will take his boots.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: They are more numerous than brave and they know exactly how the count stands. The shouting is to keep their own nerve up.

disposition.en: Mounted on wargs, circling wide, and the beasts are less patient than the riders.

presence.en: No demands worth the name — only the shape of a hunt being arranged around him while one of them talks to keep his attention forward.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: Every second spent listening is a second they use to close the circle. The wargs will decide the timing, not the riders.

disposition.en: Two of them only, and they are as unhappy to be seen as he is to see them.

presence.en: A snarled demand that he turn back the way he came, which is the first thing they have said that they actually mean.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: They are scouts and a fight will bring attention neither side wants. There is an ugly little deal available here.

disposition.en: One of them steps forward and speaks in a Westron far too correct, and the others go quiet for it.

presence.en: He asks the traveller three questions that are not about the road at all — about a name, a date and a place — and he is patient about waiting for answers.

channel.en: Have them fling harsh demands at a captive — who are you, who sent you, what do you carry — backed by the lash.

situation.en: This is not a patrol. Something is being confirmed, and the questions themselves say more than any answer would.

disposition.en: A column halted on the road, and the challenge comes as a matter of procedure from men and orcs who have somewhere else to be.

presence.en: An officer demands the road be cleared and the traveller kneel while the column passes, and gives him about four seconds to decide.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: He is an obstruction on a military road. Dignity is expensive here and the price is fixed.

disposition.en: Man-shaped enough to pass in poor light and openly enjoying the moment when the traveller works out that they are not men.

presence.en: A toll demanded in the manner of ordinary brigands, with the language slipping into something else halfway through.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: They trade on being mistaken for men and they resent it at the same time. The resentment is the dangerous part.

disposition.en: A laden column halts, and the challenge is bad-tempered rather than eager: they are carrying cargo and do not want the delay.

presence.en: Snarled orders to get off the road and stay off it until the last cart has passed, with threats attached but no real appetite behind them.

channel.en: Give them no real talk — only snarled threats, jeering, and the promise of a cruel end.

situation.en: They want him gone, not dead. Whatever is on those carts matters more to them than he does.

disposition.en: Disciplined, silent and in armour that fits, which is the worst sign of all. Nobody jeers.

presence.en: One question, asked once, about what he is doing on this road — and then they wait, and the waiting is not a bluff.

channel.en: Have them fling harsh demands at a captive — who are you, who sent you, what do you carry — backed by the lash.

situation.en: These are not raiders. There is no confusion to exploit and no argument among them to use.

disposition.en: Greets him first, which is unusual, and the greeting is exactly as long as it needs to be.

presence.en: A remark about the season that turns out to be a warning about the river, and a question about where he slept last night that is not idle.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: They are deciding, in the space of four sentences, whether he is the sort of traveller this country needs fewer of.

disposition.en: Appears at the edge of the path without any of the usual noise of arrival, and does not come closer.

presence.en: A short, unfriendly enquiry about his business under these trees, followed by one piece of information he badly needs about the trail ahead.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: They do not like strangers in the wood and they dislike deaths in it more. The help is given grudgingly and given.

disposition.en: Courteous in an older, heavier fashion, and something in the phrasing belongs to a country that no longer exists.

presence.en: He speaks of the land as it was before the coast changed, then corrects himself to the present, and the correction is the saddest part of the exchange.

channel.en: Have them bring up an age-old loss — a drowned realm, a kinsman long dead — as though it were last night.

situation.en: He has been in these lands since before the first Men walked them and is not entirely living in this century.

disposition.en: Formal, precise and faintly distant, as though the conversation were being conducted from further away than it appears.

presence.en: A question about what Men are saying in the west this year, asked with genuine interest and a slight air of collecting specimens.

channel.en: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

situation.en: The interest is real and the distance is real. Both are permanent features.

disposition.en: Sea-grey and easy-mannered, with the particular calm of people who measure time in tides rather than years.

presence.en: Talk of the weather turning, of a wreck on the sand two winters back, and of a light kept on a headland further along the shore that is worth walking to.

channel.en: Have them turn the talk to the call of the Sea and the road West: who will take ship, and who will stay and dwindle.

situation.en: Nothing is urgent to them. The information is still exactly what he needs.

disposition.en: Speaks from ten paces away, in a Westron worn thin from lack of use, and does not close the distance at all.

presence.en: A warning that the ice on the inlet is a week from breaking and a question about whether he has seen fires in the north.

channel.en: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

situation.en: They speak to almost nobody and this exchange costs them something. It is being spent on purpose.

disposition.en: Easier to talk to than most of their kin, and quicker to ask the sort of question a mortal would ask.

presence.en: Ordinary road-talk conducted with unusual attention, and one question about how long he means to keep walking roads like this one.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: The question is asked by someone who has had to make a choice about mortality, or will have to, and it lands harder than intended.

disposition.en: Charming in a way that does not fit the place or the hour, and the charm does not reach the eyes at all.

presence.en: He offers an easy road, a shorter way and pleasant company for it, and every detail he gives about the country is subtly wrong.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: Something in this one broke a long time ago. The errors are not ignorance and the courtesy is bait.

disposition.en: Two of them, already knowing his name from somewhere, and unwilling to say from where.

presence.en: They tell him what is on the road two days ahead and ask him to describe, exactly, what he passed at the ruin behind him.

channel.en: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

situation.en: They are running a border and he has walked through part of it. The trade of information is not optional so much as obvious.

disposition.en: A patrol on old business, armoured, correct, and in no mood for a long conversation with anyone.

presence.en: A brisk warning that the northern shore of the lake is not to be walked this month, delivered as an order and not a suggestion.

channel.en: Have him speak of loyalty to king and folk, and the binding weight of a word once given.

situation.en: They are the last remnant of something and they hold their small piece of country absolutely. He is not being asked.

disposition.en: Walking west alone and glad enough of a word on the road, in the manner of someone who has already left everything else behind.

presence.en: Where the road runs from here to the sea, which houses on it are still keeping their doors, and how few of them there are now compared with the last time this journey was made.

channel.en: Have them turn the talk to the call of the Sea and the road West: who will take ship, and who will stay and dwindle.

situation.en: He is going to the harbour and will not be coming back. Nothing about the conversation is heavy and everything in it is final.

disposition.en: Immaculate courtesy that manages to make the traveller aware of every stain on his cloak without a word being said about it.

presence.en: Formal questions about his road and his errand, and an answer about the state of the country that is more useful than the manner suggests.

channel.en: Have them probe courteously, measuring the traveller's purpose and heart before they give any trust.

situation.en: The condescension is unconscious and the information is excellent. Taking offence would cost him the second thing.

disposition.en: Grave and welcoming at once, and clearly used to Men — the greeting is pitched for a mortal ear.

presence.en: News of the havens, the state of the coast road, and a mention that fewer ships come to their quay each decade and none of them are new.

channel.en: Have them speak of the slow fading of the Elves and the lands they must leave, with a sorrow worn smooth by long years.

situation.en: They have lived beside Men for an age and are the last of their kin who do. The friendliness is genuine and elegiac.

disposition.en: Green-clad and half-invisible until they speak; the voice arrives before the shape resolves.

presence.en: A statement that the wood is not what it was, given as a fact about the trees rather than a complaint, and a route that avoids the worst of it.

channel.en: Have them turn the talk to beasts, trees and growing things, and the keeping of them.

situation.en: They are the oldest kind of woodland folk and they measure the sickness of a forest in centuries. This year is worse than last.

disposition.en: Veiled against the sun and formally polite, with a courtesy that has rules he does not know.

presence.en: Talk of water — where it is, who owns it, what it costs — and a question about whether the northern wells are held by anyone this season.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: Water is the only real subject here and he is being assessed as a competitor for it.

disposition.en: Cautious, sun-dark and quick to end the conversation if it turns to anything official.

presence.en: Where the next cistern is, and a flat statement that the tax-riders came through eleven days ago and took more than the tally allowed.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: They are being squeezed by their own overlords and a stranger is the safest possible audience for saying so.

disposition.en: Talkative traders of the wine-country, immediately friendly and immediately calculating.

presence.en: The price of wine three markets downriver, the state of the eastern road, and an offer to carry a letter for him if he is going the other way.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: Everything is business and the business is pleasant. There is no hidden edge to this one.

disposition.en: Hard-faced hill-men who stop him with a question rather than a weapon, which is itself a decision.

presence.en: They want to know whether he came through the valley by the standing stone, and whether anyone was camped there when he did.

channel.en: Have them probe in a guarded, even hostile way, mistrusting an unknown face in hard times.

situation.en: There is a feud running in these hills and his answer places him in it whether he wants to be placed or not.

disposition.en: Curious rather than hostile; a young one is sent forward to talk while the others watch from the slope.

presence.en: Questions about where he comes from and what he is carrying, asked plainly, and a warning about the herd of something large moving north of here.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: The youth is being tested by his own people and the traveller is the test. Both of them know it.

disposition.en: Loud, cheerful and already halfway through a story that started before he arrived.

presence.en: News from three ports, a wildly exaggerated account of a storm, and one entirely accurate detail about a captain who is hiring.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: Nine parts noise and one part gold, and the gold is the hiring. Sorting them is his problem.

disposition.en: Correct, bored and thorough — a patrol going through a procedure it has performed four hundred times.

presence.en: Name, road, purpose, and then, unprompted, a genuinely useful warning about the state of the bridge and where the last robbery on this stretch happened.

channel.en: Have them ask frankly but carefully who the traveller is, and where they are going, and why.

situation.en: The procedure is dull and the men are decent. The warning is not part of their orders.

disposition.en: Appears out of ground that looked empty, speaks quietly, and is plainly annoyed that the traveller is walking this line at all.

presence.en: A short, exact account of what is ahead, and an instruction to be off this ground by dusk and not to light a fire on it.

channel.en: Have them ask quietly about the growing shadow, and rumour of orcs, wolves and fouler things abroad.

situation.en: They are watching something and he is interfering with the watching. The information is given to move him along faster.

disposition.en: Recognition on both sides within two sentences, and then the conversation becomes very economical.

presence.en: Where the roads are watched, which house will still open its door, and a name that has stopped appearing on the circuit reports.

channel.en: Have him speak of loyalty to king and folk, and the binding weight of a word once given.

situation.en: Two people who keep the same kind of faith, comparing ledgers on a road neither of them will describe to anyone else.

disposition.en: Serene, footsore and entirely unworried about anything the traveller might be worried about.

presence.en: Where the shrine-stones are on this road, which spring is thought to be blessed and which is only clean, and an offer to share bread on the strength of nothing at all.

channel.en: Have them offer food, a tale or directions, with homely, unsuspecting goodwill.

situation.en: There is no calculation in it, which is rare enough on this road to be worth a moment of suspicion and then of shame.

disposition.en: Town-bred, brisk and less interested in him than in whether the road he came by is fit for a waggon.

presence.en: The market days in the next three towns, the current price of grain, and a complaint about the tolls that is at least half accurate.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: Purely transactional and quite friendly with it. He is a source of road conditions and nothing more.

disposition.en: Guarded and tired, in the manner of people who live in a town that used to matter and now mostly floods.

presence.en: Which of the causeways still carries a man, what the bridge-works are charging this month, and a request that he not mention having come from the north side.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: Their whole living depends on the crossing and the crossing is failing. Strangers from the north are a subject with history.

disposition.en: Gracious from horseback, with an attendant who does the practical parts of the conversation.

presence.en: A courteous enquiry about his road, an invitation to make use of a well on their land, and a piece of political news he was not supposed to hear.

channel.en: Have them trade news of the road — war, bandits, strange sights — hungry for word from elsewhere.

situation.en: The courtesy is genuine and the news was a mistake. Whether it was a mistake is worth thinking about later.

disposition.en: Brief, unbothered and standing far enough back that the wind carries most of the words away.

presence.en: Where the ice is thin, where the seals are, and a warning that the weather will turn within the day whatever the sky is currently doing.

channel.en: Have them talk plainly as working folk do: crops, beasts, the turning season, hard times or good.

situation.en: They speak to strangers rarely and never at length. Everything said is chosen for its usefulness.

disposition.en: Claw-rakes on a rock face, ten feet off the ground. Whatever made them came down from above.

presence.en: The gouges are deep and fresh — made within two days. The spacing suggests something large, four-limbed, moving fast across vertical stone. No blood. Whatever it hit, it carried away.

situation.en: It is above the treeline, or it was. The marks face the direction the traveller is heading.

disposition.en: A kill-site on the hillside — the carcass of a large elk, stripped to the spine in one feeding. The bones are blackened.

presence.en: Not scorch-marks. The bones themselves are darkened, changed by something in the saliva. Recent. The drag-marks coming in are from above; the departure tracks are none — it lifted off.

situation.en: Whatever fed here is still in the region. Elk this size are not easy prey.

disposition.en: A village at the valley bottom — not burning, not attacked. Abandoned. Every door left open.

presence.en: They left fast enough that food is still on the tables. The direction of the footprints leads east, away from the high ground. Something drove them out without violence. The silence that drives people out before it arrives.

situation.en: The shadow that made them run is still somewhere in the heights above.

disposition.en: A sound from the high ground — not a bird, not rockfall. Something between a resonant hiss and a low sustained note.

presence.en: The sound repeats at irregular intervals from the same direction. It is not communication. It is something breathing at altitude, the chest-cavity resonance of something large.

situation.en: It is not coming closer. It is where it is, doing what it does. The question is whether the road passes under it.

disposition.en: A vibration in the rock under the feet — not an earthquake. A rhythmic resonance. Something moving through a passage in the mountain.

presence.en: The vibration comes up through the soles and into the bones. It is moving parallel to the surface road, below it, in the direction of travel. Fast.

situation.en: It will emerge somewhere ahead. The question is where the passage opens.

disposition.en: A shape on a distant ridge — long, low, four-limbed, moving along the skyline without haste.

presence.en: It is visible for approximately thirty seconds before it drops below the ridge. It did not look in this direction. The size at that distance suggests something between twelve and twenty feet long.

situation.en: It was heading north. The road ahead goes north.

disposition.en: A shape in the air — not a bird. Wrong wingbeat, wrong proportion, wrong altitude.

presence.en: It is circling. Whatever it is circling is approximately two miles north and slightly west. The circling is methodical, not thermal-riding. It is watching something below it.

situation.en: The road passes approximately a mile east of whatever it is watching.

disposition.en: On the mountainside across the valley — a drake, sunning on exposed rock. Not moving. Aware.

presence.en: It has seen the traveller. It has been watching since before the traveller saw it. It is not moving because it has decided the distance is sufficient. The distance is perhaps four hundred yards.

situation.en: It is deciding. The decision will take approximately as long as it takes the traveller to cross the open ground.

disposition.en: From the cave-mouth above the road, something is watching. Two points of amber light in the dark, unblinking.

presence.en: It has been there since before the traveller entered this stretch of road. It is not the darkness of the cave that is dangerous — it is the patience. Drakes watch what they are considering.

situation.en: It has not moved. This is not reassurance. They do not move until they decide.

disposition.en: The drake is on the road. Not blocking it — beside it, facing the traveller. Watching.

presence.en: It is not in attack posture. It is in assessment posture: head low, neck extended, reading the traveller the way a predator reads something unfamiliar before deciding what category it falls into.

situation.en: The decision will happen. It is happening now. The window where walking away is still possible is brief.

disposition.en: Nothing visible. A wrongness in the air — the specific quality of attention that should not exist in an empty place.

presence.en: The temperature did not drop. The light did not change. But something became aware of the traveller's presence here. Something far away, or something close and very still.

situation.en: It has not acted. It is noting. The difference between those two things is not permanent.

disposition.en: A sound that the ears process as a word, though no voice made it — a name, or something that functions as a name.

presence.en: It came from no direction. It did not repeat. But it was specific — the kind of specific that means something knows exactly what it is addressing.

situation.en: Something named the traveller. Whatever that means in the context of where the traveller is standing, it is not nothing.

disposition.en: The shadow ahead of the traveller bends wrong — not with the light, against it.

presence.en: It is the traveller's own shadow doing it. Something between the traveller and the light is distorting the projection. Nothing visible is between them and the light source.

situation.en: It corrects itself after a moment. That moment was not nothing.

disposition.en: On a distant ridge at dusk — a shape that is too tall, too narrow, moving with a stride that covers ground too fast for its apparent size.

presence.en: It is visible for less than ten seconds. It is moving parallel to the road, heading the same direction as the traveller. It did not look in this direction.

situation.en: It knows the road because it has used the road. That is worse than if it didn't.

disposition.en: In the smoke above a burning structure — a shape that is not smoke. It is moving through the smoke the way something moves through water.

presence.en: The fire is old enough that no one is near it. The shape in the smoke is paying attention to the direction the survivors went, not to the traveller. It has not seen the traveller yet.

situation.en: Yet.

disposition.en: It is standing at the far end of the passage. It is not moving. It is not the darkness — it is in the darkness, which is different.

presence.en: It is aware of the traveller. The awareness is total — not the awareness of an animal that has heard something, but the awareness of something that knew before the traveller entered the passage.

situation.en: It is deciding whether the traveller is worth the effort. That is a question the traveller should leave the passage before it answers.

disposition.en: A boulder on the road that was not there yesterday — moved from the cliff face above, recently. The marks where it sat are fresh.

presence.en: It was not a rockfall. The base-fracture is clean, as if something lifted it rather than it falling. The boulder is twice the height of a man.

situation.en: Something moved this for a reason. The reason was not to block the road — it is offset to the side. The reason was to move it.

disposition.en: Handprints on the cliff face — man-shaped but eight feet across, pressed into the rock at a height of thirty feet as if the cliff was used for leverage.

presence.en: Something climbed here recently, using the cliff-face as a handhold. The impressions are shallow but visible. Whatever made them was heavy enough to press into stone.

situation.en: It went up, not down. It is above the traveller on this cliff.

disposition.en: From the high pass — a sound like boulders striking each other, but rhythmic. Not rockfall.

presence.en: It repeats at irregular intervals. The direction is consistent: the high ground to the left of the pass. It sounds like a game, or an argument conducted in stone.

situation.en: The pass goes between those high points. The sound comes from both sides.

disposition.en: A voice — if it can be called that — from somewhere above. A single syllable that resonates in the chest cavity at a frequency that is more felt than heard.

presence.en: It did not repeat. It may have been directed at the traveller or at something else entirely. The size of the voice implies the size of the thing that made it.

situation.en: The pass ahead narrows. Whatever is above is still above.

disposition.en: On the high peaks across the valley — movement that resolves into a figure. A very large figure, moving between crags with the ease of someone walking a flat road.

presence.en: It is perhaps a mile away and three thousand feet above. It is carrying something — a section of cliff-face, approximately. It does not appear to have noticed the traveller.

situation.en: The pass the traveller needs goes under those crags.

disposition.en: Two of them on a ridge above the pass — visible only because one of them stood up, and standing up brought it above the skyline.

presence.en: They are sitting. They appear to be in conversation, or something that functions as conversation. They have not looked this way. The road goes through the gap between their ridge and the cliff-face.

situation.en: The gap is narrow. If one of them stood and moved to the cliff edge, the road would be directly below it.

disposition.en: Strands of web across the path — not a full web. Anchor lines, thick as a finger, spanning the trail between trees.

presence.en: They were placed deliberately at neck height. Not a trap exactly — a marker. Something claiming the path ahead as its hunting ground.

situation.en: The strands are old enough to be dry but not decayed. The marking was made within a week.

disposition.en: A cocooned shape hanging from a branch fifteen feet off the path. Large enough to be a person.

presence.en: It is not moving. The cocoon is recent — the silk is still pale and untarnished. Whatever is inside was put there within two days.

situation.en: There may be others. The cocooning means the spider hunts this path regularly.

disposition.en: The path ahead is walled in web — not crossing it, filling it. A corridor of silk from ground to canopy, deliberately constructed.

presence.en: It is a funnel. The open end is here, at the traveller's position. The closed end is ahead, invisible behind the white of the silk. The construction is patient and considered.

situation.en: This is not an obstacle. It is an invitation that the traveller did not accept.

disposition.en: In the canopy above — eyes. Eight of them, arranged in two rows, reflecting the light from between the leaves.

presence.en: It is not moving. It registered the traveller's presence some time before the traveller registered its. It is waiting to see if the traveller will stop.

situation.en: Stopping is the wrong answer. Stopping means it has time to drop.

disposition.en: The tree directly above has too much stillness in it — no movement even in a light wind, every branch weighted down by something that is not leaves.

presence.en: It is one spider or it is several, and they have been there long enough to stop the tree moving. The weight of them is visible in how the branches sit.

situation.en: It — or they — have been watching the approach for several minutes.

disposition.en: A stone post at the junction — plain iron-grey, four feet tall, unremarkable. Except it was not there on the way in.

presence.en: It has no inscription. It has no obvious purpose. It is positioned exactly at the center of the junction, equidistant from all three paths.

situation.en: It moved. Between when the traveller entered the valley and now, it moved here.

disposition.en: Among the carved stones at the forest edge — one that looks like the others until the light changes and it doesn't.

presence.en: The shadows fall wrong on this one. The proportions are almost right but the stone's grain doesn't match the carvings around it. It is newer, or it is different, or it is not stone.

situation.en: The Woses placed these carvings for a reason. Whatever this one is, it is not their work.

disposition.en: The stone figure at the path's edge has turned since the traveller last passed it.

presence.en: It was facing east. It is now facing the traveller. The base has not moved — only the figure, from the waist up. It is watching.

situation.en: It has not attacked. The constructs do not attack unless the boundary is crossed. The question is where the boundary is.

disposition.en: There are more of them than there were. The path that had three guardian-stones now has seven. Three of the new ones have no moss, no weathering.

presence.en: They are closing in incrementally. The path is being narrowed. Whatever the boundary was, the traveller has been moving inside it and the constructs are adjusting.

situation.en: The Woses who made these are somewhere close, watching through the constructs' awareness.

disposition.en: One sitting on a boulder at the road-side, eating something it would be better not to identify. It looks up when the traveller passes.

presence.en: It says — slowly, with the effort of someone who doesn't use speech often — that the traveller is small. It says this as an observation, not as a threat. It is genuinely noting the size.

situation.en: The observation has no follow-up. It goes back to what it was eating.

disposition.en: It comes out of a cave-mouth at the bend and stops when it sees the traveller. It did not expect company.

presence.en: It says: you're not supposed to be on this road. It says it with the specific confusion of something following instructions it doesn't fully understand. Someone told it the road would be clear.

situation.en: Someone gave it instructions. Someone expected the road to be clear. The traveller is the problem in that plan.

disposition.en: A barrow-entrance, and in front of it a figure that occupies the threshold — not blocking it, being it.

presence.en: It does not speak first. It is the threshold. Whatever is in the barrow behind it is what it was in life, and it has been in that barrow a long time.

situation.en: It will not move. It cannot move. It is bound to this place in a way that is complete.

disposition.en: It is on the road. Not beside it — on it. Standing in the middle, occupying the center, facing the traveller's direction.

presence.en: It is not one of the mindless ones. Its eyes track. It has something it wants to say, or something it wants to do, and it has been waiting on this road for the right person.

situation.en: The traveller may or may not be the right person. It is making that determination now.

disposition.en: It appears at dusk — not suddenly, just present where it was not. Standing at the edge of the road, looking at the traveller's fire.

presence.en: It remembers fire. The memory is old and the connection between the memory and the fire is broken in ways it cannot articulate. It looks at the fire the way the very old look at things that remind them of something they cannot name.

situation.en: It is not threatening. It is homesick for something it can no longer reach.

disposition.en: It speaks before the traveller sees it — from behind, already close.

presence.en: It says a name. Not the traveller's name. Someone else's name, spoken with the particular urgency of the long-dead looking for someone who has also long since died.

situation.en: It will not stop until it understands that the person it is looking for is gone. That understanding may take a long time to arrive.

disposition.en: A creak from above — not wood settling, deliberate. The tree has something to say and this is how it begins.

presence.en: It says, after a long pause, that this path has been used more often recently. It says this with the interest of something that has been watching the same stretch of ground for four hundred years and noticed a change.

situation.en: The change it noticed is recent enough to be meaningful. It is asking, in the way Ents ask, whether the traveller knows what is causing it.

disposition.en: It steps onto the path from the treeline — the motion takes approximately forty seconds and the sound of it is the sound of the forest rearranging itself.

presence.en: It says that something has been entering the forest from the east for several nights and that it smells wrong in a way the Ent does not have precise language for. It says: wrong in the way the forest was wrong in the second age, before we understood what was happening.

situation.en: An Ent saying this is not hyperbole. It has comparative data spanning thousands of years.

disposition.en: A flooded section of the road ahead — shallow enough to wade but the current pulls sideways.

presence.en: The ford here is normally reliable. Something upstream has changed the drainage. The far bank is firm.

situation.en: A minor cost of time and wet boots, nothing more. The road continues beyond it unchanged.

disposition.en: A section of cliff-face above the road shows fresh scoring — recent rockfall, the debris still white against the older stone.

presence.en: The fall happened within the last day. Loose material still hangs on the upper face. The debris field across the road is passable but the passage under the unstable rock is perhaps thirty metres.

situation.en: The risk is real but brief. The alternative is a long detour.

disposition.en: A section of the road has subsided — not collapsed, sunk, the surface intact but the ground beneath it no longer solid.

presence.en: The subsidence is several metres across. The surface holds weight for now. Something underground has changed — water, rot, a cavity. It will not hold indefinitely.

situation.en: The road is still technically passable. The word technically is doing a great deal of work.

disposition.en: A tree across the road — freshly fallen, root-ball still tearing free of the soil on the uphill side.

presence.en: It came down in the last few hours. The crown is thick and tangled; going over it is possible but slow. Going around it on the uphill side means climbing the root-ball, which is unstable.

situation.en: Neither route is dangerous, only awkward. The road is clear on the far side.

disposition.en: A bog has encroached onto the road — the surface looks firm but the footprint sinks two inches on the first step.

presence.en: The bog extends perhaps fifty metres. The road skirts the edge of it but the road itself is compromised. Deeper in, the ground is black water with a grass skin over it.

situation.en: People have crossed here before — there are marks on the verge where travelers pushed through. The marks are old.

disposition.en: The bridge is out — not collapsed, removed. The timbers are gone and only the stone piers stand in the river.

presence.en: The river here is not crossable on foot. The nearest ford is a full half-day upstream. Someone removed those timbers deliberately.

situation.en: Who removes a bridge and why is the question. The answer is somewhere upstream near the ford.

disposition.en: The ledge-path crumbles underfoot — a section approximately two metres gives way without warning.

presence.en: One foot goes through. The drop below is not fatal but the recovery requires immediate action — push back, redistribute weight, find the solid edge.

situation.en: Two seconds of real danger, then it is past. The path is narrower on the other side of the gap.

disposition.en: Flash of movement and a loud crack — a branch the width of an arm falls from directly above, misses by less than a foot.

presence.en: The dead wood was sitting in the canopy. Something — wind, a bird, nothing visible — dislodged it. The impact crater in the soil beside the path is considerable.

situation.en: Nothing to be done about it. It either hits or it doesn't.

disposition.en: The ground opens — a sinkhole, perhaps two metres across, directly in the path. The near edge crumbles inward as the traveller stops.

presence.en: The hole is deep enough that the bottom isn't visible. The soil around it is still settling. It opened within the last hour — the broken turf edges are fresh.

situation.en: The path is gone here. The way around requires going fifty metres off-track into steep ground.

disposition.en: Fresh deer-slots in the soft ground beside the path — a doe and two young, moving toward the stream.

presence.en: Made within a few hours, heading downhill. The slots are clean and unworried — no sign of flight. The deer have not been alarmed recently.

situation.en: Deer moving calmly means the forest ahead is quiet. That is worth knowing.

disposition.en: The ground around a waterhole has been heavily churned — large hooves, many animals, recently.

presence.en: A herd came through here within the last day. The mud is still wet. Whatever brought them here in numbers — a long dry spell, or something drove them off their usual ground.

situation.en: Driven animals mean something was behind them. The direction they came from is worth noting.

disposition.en: The carcass of a large elk, untouched. Not killed — starved, recently, in a region where starving elk make no sense.

presence.en: The body is intact, no predator-sign, no disease-sign. It simply stopped and did not move again. The grass around it is ungrazed.

situation.en: Herbivores do not starve in good country in this season unless something has made them too frightened to graze.

disposition.en: A herd on the hillside above the road — moving uphill in the late afternoon, which is the right direction at this hour.

presence.en: Thirty or forty animals, the usual mixed herd. Moving at a natural pace, no sign of disturbance.

situation.en: The land up there is good. Nothing has disturbed it today.

disposition.en: A large solitary animal on the skyline — not a deer. Too large, wrong proportions, standing still on the ridge.

presence.en: An aurochs, or a giant breed the traveller has not seen before. It is watching the road below. It does not move.

situation.en: Animals that watch roads from ridges without moving are worth taking note of. This one is not afraid of the road.

disposition.en: A herd grazing the meadow beside the road — unperturbed, heads down, moving slowly in the late morning light.

presence.en: Perhaps twenty animals. They registered the traveller's approach and decided the traveller was not interesting.

situation.en: The herd being calm means the road ahead has been undisturbed. Frightened animals do not return quickly to a feeding ground.

disposition.en: A stag at the water's edge, drinking. It looks up when the traveller approaches, holds for a long moment, then retreats into the trees without urgency.

presence.en: It held long enough to assess. The assessment came back: not a threat. That assessment has been running correctly for this animal so far.

situation.en: Nothing alarmed it before the traveller arrived. The forest behind it was quiet.

disposition.en: The herd at the meadow-edge scatters as the traveller rounds the bend — not in panic, in the unhurried retreat of animals that are startled but not truly frightened.

presence.en: They move uphill and stop at the treeline to look back. A normal response. They will return within the hour.

situation.en: Nothing else spooked them. This was the traveller.

disposition.en: A boar on the path ahead — huge, old, scarred. It faces the traveller for a full three seconds, then turns and crashes into the undergrowth.

presence.en: It chose to leave. That is unusual for a boar this size. Something on the traveller read as more dangerous than a large boar was willing to deal with.

situation.en: The shadow, perhaps. Or something that the boar could smell that the traveller cannot name.

disposition.en: Wolf-prints crossing the path — a pair, moving at a trot, heading north. Made last night.

presence.en: Both adults, by the size. Not a pack, a bonded pair. Moving purposefully, not hunting — the stride is too regular for active hunting.

situation.en: They have a destination. The direction is north, same as the traveller.

disposition.en: The remains of a kill on the road — bones, hide, scattered. Something large fed here recently.

presence.en: The kill is clean-stripped in the way of bears, not wolves or cats. The bones are crushed. The hide is turned inside-out, which bears do systematically.

situation.en: A bear large enough to turn a deer's hide inside-out and crush the long bones is significantly larger than average.

disposition.en: Claw-marks on a tree beside the path at head height — five parallel gouges, deep, in hardwood.

presence.en: Marking territory. The height means the animal stood on its hind legs to make them — eight feet minimum. The marks are recent enough that the wood inside the gouges is still pale.

situation.en: Something very large is marking this path as its territory. The marks face the direction of travel.

disposition.en: Something is following. Not seen, not heard — felt. The specific quality of being tracked by something that knows how to stay out of sight.

presence.en: It has been there for perhaps twenty minutes. It matches pace changes. It does not come closer, but the distance between them has not increased either.

situation.en: Whatever it is, it is waiting for something — a change in terrain, a moment of inattention, a decision to stop.

disposition.en: Two of them, one on each side of the road. The one on the right is visible when it moves between trees. The one on the left is inferred from the behavior of the first.

presence.en: They are coordinating. The one on the right is the visible element — the one that makes the prey watch right. The one on the left will move when the prey is watching right.

situation.en: This is a practiced technique. These animals have done this before.

disposition.en: The ruins of a small tower at the road's junction — foundation stones clear, the upper work long fallen.

presence.en: Dunedain-built, by the cut of the remaining stones. Three hundred years old at minimum. The road junction it guarded still functions. The tower no longer does.

situation.en: The road has outlasted the people who built the tower to protect it. That is not unusual in the north.

disposition.en: A village — inhabited, smoke from chimneys, faces at windows — but the gate is shut and nobody comes out.

presence.en: The gate is new. The bar is heavy. The faces at the windows are watching the traveller in the specific way of people who have decided to wait and see.

situation.en: Something happened here recently. The caution is fresh.

disposition.en: The village is empty. Not abandoned-empty — fled-empty. Doors open, fires cold, food left on tables.

presence.en: Everything suggests speed. Animals are still in the paddocks, which means they left on foot and in a hurry.

situation.en: Whatever made them leave fast enough to leave the animals — it was visible, not rumoured.

disposition.en: A wayhouse at the road's edge — solid, maintained, with the universal signal of travelers' hospitality: a lit lamp in the window.

presence.en: The offer is readable from the threshold: a real fire, a basic pot, a dry bed for a small coin. The keeper asks no questions beyond which road the traveller came from — road-courtesy, not interrogation.

situation.en: A night spent here costs a small coin and restores something that cannot be easily named.

disposition.en: A farmstead off the road, the farmer visible in the yard, who raises a hand as the traveller passes.

presence.en: The gesture is an invitation as much as a greeting — the way of the frontier, where hospitality is extended to travellers because travellers extend it in return.

situation.en: The farm has a barn. The barn is dry. The farmer has news from the eastern road that the traveller has not come from.

disposition.en: A market at a crossroads — temporary, six or eight stalls, the kind that assembles on one specific day of the week.

presence.en: Merchants from two directions. The goods tell the story of where they have been: northern furs beside southern cloth, which means both roads are open.

situation.en: Open roads and working markets mean the region is currently stable. That is worth knowing.

disposition.en: A fortified waystation with a small garrison — the gate is open and the guards are watching the road with professional attention.

presence.en: The guards note the traveller. One of them moves to the gatepost but does not call out. The attention is heightened beyond normal duty.

situation.en: They are watching for something specific. The traveller does not match it.

disposition.en: The ruin watches. Not literally — but the way old places watch when their history is heavy enough to give them presence.

presence.en: A keep that was besieged and taken and taken again and finally abandoned. The walls still hold. The gate-arch is intact. Nothing is inside except the weight of what happened there.

situation.en: It is not dangerous to stop here. It is uncomfortable in a way that has nothing to do with physical danger.

disposition.en: The barrow-mound at the road's edge was not here before — or it was, but it was flat, and now the capstone has shifted and the opening is dark.

presence.en: Someone opened it recently. The marks on the capstone are not old. The inside is dark and the air from it is cold in a way that has nothing to do with underground temperature.

situation.en: Things inside barrows do not open barrows from inside unless something has changed.

disposition.en: The road through the settlement is closed — a rope across it and a man sitting beside the rope who does not look up when the traveller arrives.

presence.en: He says, without looking up, that the road is closed until tomorrow morning. He does not explain why. He does not appear to be armed.

situation.en: The rope is a formality. The closure is not.

disposition.en: A natural overhang above a dry, flat floor — the kind of shelter that has been used for exactly this purpose for as long as travelers have used this road.

presence.en: Old fire-rings, cleared ground, the beam of a previous traveler left notched against the wall as a hanger. Everything needed, nothing extra.

situation.en: Someone thought to leave the beam. It is still there. The traveller is glad of it.

disposition.en: A stand of medicinal herbs beside a spring — athelas among them, unmistakeable to those who know it.

presence.en: The spring is clean and the herbs are well-established, which means this ground has not been poisoned or disturbed recently. A gift from the road.

situation.en: Taking a modest amount costs nothing. Leaving the plants rooted means they will be here for the next traveller.

disposition.en: A colony of beehives on the south-facing bank — tended hives, not wild, with the keeper's mark on the posts.

presence.en: The keeper is not here but the hives are active and the marks are current. Someone is working these hives. The honey here is available for trade at whatever settlement owns the mark.
