situation.en: Road knowledge: honey at the next settlement is fresh and reliable.

disposition.en: A fishery on the river — nets strung across a narrow, weirs directing the fish into a trapped pool. Nobody working it at this hour.

presence.en: The equipment is good and well-maintained. The settlement that runs this fishery has enough people to do it properly and enough stability to maintain it across seasons.

situation.en: Stability in the settlements means the road is safe. This is indirect evidence but it is evidence.

disposition.en: A logging operation across the road — felled trunks being moved by a team of men and horses, the road temporarily blocked while they work.

presence.en: The foreman sees the traveller and raises a hand: ten minutes. He means it.

situation.en: Normal commerce on a working road. The delay is genuine and brief.

disposition.en: The road runs through a long meadow of wildflowers — unmanaged, brilliant, the kind that grows where no one has ploughed for a generation.

presence.en: Cornflowers and poppies and things that have no common name in this part of the world. The contrast with the road-stone is absolute.

situation.en: A visual gift. Nothing else.

disposition.en: A dead zone — a stretch of fifty metres where nothing grows. The soil is dark and the ground is flat and the silence is the silence of absence.

presence.en: No visible cause. The trees on either side are healthy. The ground here has no rock, no water problem. Something made it stop supporting life.

situation.en: Old battleground, perhaps. Or something was buried here. Or the shadow of something passed over it once and the ground remembers.

disposition.en: A patch of Old Man's Beard covering a section of the treeline — the lichen that signals clean, wet air and old growth.

presence.en: Old Man's Beard only grows in undisturbed forest with good air quality. Its presence here means this forest has been undisturbed for a long time.

situation.en: The forest ahead is old. Old forest has its own rules.

disposition.en: Thorny scrub has closed over the path — not a little, a wall of it, three metres high and clearly established over years.

presence.en: The path has not been used in a long time. The scrub did not grow overnight. Someone stopped using this path and did not tell the map-makers.

situation.en: There is a reason this path was abandoned. It might be as simple as a better road was built. It might not.

disposition.en: The vegetation on both sides of the road has moved across it — not grown, moved. The stems are bent inward, not grown inward.

presence.en: Something on the road is being closed off. The bending is recent — the stems are still green and supple where they cross the road surface.

situation.en: The Old Forest does this. Fangorn does this. If the traveller is in neither of those places, they should wonder what has learned to do it here.

disposition.en: An ancient oak at the road's turning — a landmark, clearly, its trunk marked with generations of travellers' initials and the occasional waymark cut.

presence.en: The oldest initials near the base are worn to illegibility. The tree was a waymark before writing was common in this region.

situation.en: It has been watching this junction for a very long time.

disposition.en: The forest has changed — the canopy here is older and the trees are different in character. Not hostile, not welcoming. Simply ancient.

presence.en: The oldest trees do not acknowledge travelers. They have been here too long to find travelers interesting. That is not the same as being safe here.

situation.en: Old trees have their own gravity. This section of forest pulls the road through it, not the other way.

disposition.en: The trees in this section are breathing — not literally, but the movement of air through them is patterned in a way that suggests something other than wind.

presence.en: The rhythm is approximately twenty seconds. The movement is coordinated across trees that are not touching each other above ground.

situation.en: The roots are connected. What moves through one moves through all. The forest is aware of the traveller's passage in a way it has not been further back.

disposition.en: A root has heaved across the road — not a new root, an established one, which has lifted and moved to the surface since this section of road was last maintained.

presence.en: The root is as thick as a torso and the road-stone has been pushed up on both sides of it. The crossing is awkward but manageable.

situation.en: The tree it belongs to is sixty feet back from the road. The root traveled a long way to get here.

disposition.en: The path through the forest has narrowed to nothing — not fallen trees, growing trees, their trunks moved close enough over years to close the gap.

presence.en: This was a path once. The distance between the trunks was enough. Now it is not. The trees did not do this quickly.

situation.en: Old paths close for old reasons. The forest chose to close this one.

disposition.en: Ravens in the canopy — not one or two, a gathering. The specific quality of raven noise that means something dead nearby, or something about to be.

presence.en: They are calling to each other, not at the traveller. The subject of their interest is further along the road.

situation.en: Ravens know things. What they are gathered about is ahead.

disposition.en: A sound from above in the dark — not a bird in any normal category. Too large, the wingbeat wrong, the occasional sound between wingbeats suggesting a rider.

presence.en: It is circling. The circle is centered approximately on the traveller's camp.

situation.en: Fell-beasts have riders. The rider can see in darkness better than the traveller can.

disposition.en: Eagles above the pass — two of them, circling on the thermal above the high ground. Not hunting. Watching.

presence.en: Great Eagles watch roads and passes with purpose. What they see they remember. What they decide to act on, they act on decisively.

situation.en: They have registered the traveller. The registration is neutral. So far.

disposition.en: A murmuration of starlings over the marshland ahead — thousands of them, moving in coordinated sheets that bend and fold without colliding.

presence.en: The murmuration is moving away from the direction the traveller is heading. Something in the marsh is driving them. Something changed there recently.

situation.en: Birds in mass flight tell the story of what is below them.

disposition.en: A hawk working the open ground beside the road — quartering back and forth in the systematic sweep of an active hunt.

presence.en: It ignores the traveller completely. The hunt is genuine — it has a target below in the grass that the traveller cannot see.

situation.en: A hawk hunting means the field is quiet. Nothing larger has disturbed it recently.

disposition.en: A large owl from a hollow in the road-side tree — disturbed by the traveller's passing, it drops from the hollow and beats away into the forest.

presence.en: Larger than expected. The wingspan clears four feet. It does not call, just leaves, which is owls.

situation.en: The hollow is empty now. The road is undisturbed.

disposition.en: Otter-slides in the mud bank beside the river — two lanes worn smooth into the clay, angled into the water.

presence.en: Active, recently used. The clay at the bottom of the slides is still wet. A family group, by the size difference between the tracks.

situation.en: Otters in good numbers mean the river is healthy — clean water, good fish, no upstream disruption.

disposition.en: Something large in the lake — a wake moving against the wind, no visible source, then gone.

presence.en: The wake was V-shaped in the way of something swimming near the surface. The width of the V at its point suggests something perhaps eight to twelve feet long.

situation.en: The lake looks still again. The wake did not come toward the shore.

disposition.en: Beavers working a dam upstream of the ford — the sound of them carrying and placing timber audible from the road.

presence.en: The dam is new. The pond behind it is expanding. The ford below it will be shallower for the next few weeks as the pond fills.

situation.en: Useful road knowledge: ford conditions changed upstream.

disposition.en: The ford is blocked — not by water level, by crocodiles. Three of them, sun-bathing across the shallows in positions that make crossing impossible.

presence.en: They are not aggressive — yet. They are using the ford because it is warm stone and shallow water, which suits them perfectly. They will not move willingly.

situation.en: Crocodiles at a ford are not a fight worth having. There is a boat crossing a mile downstream.

disposition.en: The fish are gone from this stretch of river — not a hook-point to be found, the banks empty of birds, the water simply empty.

presence.en: Fish do not leave a stretch of water without reason. Something in this section of river drives them away or feeds on them until they are gone.

situation.en: The emptiness is recent — the bird-droppings on the rocks show last week's activity, nothing this week.

disposition.en: A shape under the surface of the deep pool at the river's bend — too large for any fish of this river, moving slowly along the bottom.

presence.en: It turns at the pool's end and comes back. It has been doing this for some time — the silt at the bottom is disturbed in a regular pattern.

situation.en: Whatever it is, it is aware of the traveller at the bank. It has turned to parallel them each time they move.

disposition.en: The lake surface is still — completely still, in a wind that should be making it move.

presence.en: The stillness is localized. Twenty metres out, where the water should be responding to the wind, it is flat and dark. Something below the surface is suppressing the movement.

situation.en: The Watcher in the Water is a name given to things like this. The name implies others have been watched from the same bank.

disposition.en: Snake-track in the dust of the road — sinuous, continuous, freshly made, crossing from the sunny verge to the shade under the opposite hedge.

presence.en: Moving in the mid-morning means it is warming up. Large, by the track width — perhaps four feet of snake, minimum. Not hunting, just relocating.

situation.en: An active snake moving means the ground ahead is warm and undisturbed.

disposition.en: A large snake on the warm rock above the road — visible because the sun catches its scales and it is not moving.

presence.en: Basking. The scale pattern is distinctive — a viper of the large southern variety, not the common small one of northern roads.

situation.en: It will not move unless approached or disturbed. The gap between the rock and the road verge is sufficient.

disposition.en: A dozen lizards on the sun-warmed stones of the road-wall — small, quick, disappearing into crevices as the traveller passes.

presence.en: Normal. They are thermally regulating. Their presence means no large predator has disturbed these stones today.

situation.en: Small reptiles in quantity on a sunny wall are a proxy for a calm stretch of road.

disposition.en: A snake across the path, absorbing heat. It feels the vibration before it hears anything and is gone before the traveller reaches it.

presence.en: Not aggressive — the fastest-moving thing the traveller will encounter all day and it is using that speed to disappear.

situation.en: The path is clear. The snake is in the undergrowth watching.

disposition.en: Dumbledoors working the clover at the verge — large, unhurried, producing that specific sound that is halfway between a drone and a grumble.

presence.en: Healthy meadow, no disturbance. The big bumble-bees are only this relaxed when the ground around them is undisturbed.

situation.en: A quiet road ahead. The bees say so.

disposition.en: An empty nest on the road — a wasps' nest the size of a helm, freshly torn from the eave above. Recent disturbance.

presence.en: Something pulled this nest down within the last few hours. The wasps have dispersed — most of them, not all. The stragglers are still around.

situation.en: Something large enough to pull down a nest this size either wanted the grubs or didn't notice it. Neither is reassuring.

disposition.en: A swarm on the road — bees or wasps, moving as a single organism, crossing the road at exactly the worst moment.

presence.en: The swarm is not aggressive. It is in transit, following its queen, completely occupied with itself. The road happens to be in the way.

situation.en: Waiting is the answer. Three minutes and they are gone.

disposition.en: Hummerhorns above the path — not a swarm, four or five scouts, which is the worst possible configuration: enough to alert the colony, few enough to be difficult to track.

presence.en: They found something that disturbed them. The traveller or whatever the traveller is carrying. They are moving in the specific pattern that precedes summoning.

situation.en: Three minutes before the colony arrives. Two of those minutes have already passed.

disposition.en: Fireflies in the dusk meadow — hundreds of them, the cold green light rising and falling in patterns that seem almost deliberate.

presence.en: This is normal and beautiful and means the meadow is healthy and the evening is quiet.

situation.en: The fireflies are the evening news: nothing alarming, air is clean, moisture is good.

disposition.en: Fox-sign on the path — a scatter of pheasant feathers and the distinctive sharp scent. Recently, in the last hour.

presence.en: The fox was successful. A successful hunt means an undisturbed wood. The pheasant was moving normally until it wasn't.

situation.en: Quiet road.

disposition.en: Squirrels working the beech-mast beside the road — industrious, unhurried, moving up and down in the canopy with the specific busyness of autumn storage.

presence.en: Late season behaviour. The squirrels are hurrying because the season is shortening. The nuts are ready. The year is turning.

situation.en: A calendar observation as much as a wildlife encounter.

disposition.en: A bear on the hillside above the road — foraging in the berry-scrub, aware of the traveller, not interested.

presence.en: A bear that makes the choice to ignore a traveller is a bear that has made this calculation before and found travelers not worth the trouble.

situation.en: The indifference is a good sign. A habituated, well-fed bear in berry season is the least dangerous version of a bear encounter.

disposition.en: Something large in the undergrowth — the sound of something heavy moving away fast, the branches shaking in a retreating line.

presence.en: It was close enough that the traveller almost walked into it. Whatever it was, it wanted no contact as much as the traveller did.

situation.en: The withdrawal was fast and clean. Whatever it was, it knew how to move through this undergrowth.

disposition.en: A grey ape — huge, shaggy, five feet at the shoulder — steps onto the path ten metres ahead, sees the traveller, and immediately turns and leaves.

presence.en: The speed of its departure is surprising for its size. It was more frightened than the traveller.

situation.en: Something the traveller is carrying, or the shadow the traveller carries, read as dangerous to an animal that is not easily frightened.

disposition.en: Horse-sign on the road — shod hooves, three horses, moving at a canter heading south. Made this morning.

presence.en: Shod means riders, not wild horses. Three horses at a canter heading south means a message or a patrol moving with purpose.

situation.en: Three riders with a purpose, somewhere south on this road.

disposition.en: Wild horses on the horizon — a small band, perhaps eight, moving in the specific unhurried drift of animals with no predator pressure and nowhere they need to be.

presence.en: Free horses in good condition mean this land is currently safe. Wolves would have thinned them or changed their behaviour.

situation.en: A useful read on the region.

disposition.en: A horse-herd at a water-hole — a dozen animals, mixed, the foals still close to their mothers. Unafraid of the road.

presence.en: Habituated to road-traffic, which means this road is regularly used. Road-traffic means relative safety and commerce.

situation.en: Active roads are safe roads. The horses confirm it.

disposition.en: Wild horses that were grazing the road-verge scatter as the traveller rounds the bend — all moving upwind in a single line, which is the flight pattern of horses responding to something they have scented, not seen.

presence.en: They scented the traveller before seeing them and decided the scent was wrong. Not predator-wrong — dark-wrong.

situation.en: Animals read the shadow differently than people do. What the horses smelled is not visible.

disposition.en: The marsh beside the road is loud with frogs — the full chorus of an undisturbed spring night, every pond and ditch contributing.

presence.en: Frogs chorus when they are safe and the air is right. A full chorus means no snake or heron has disturbed this marsh in the last hour.

situation.en: The marsh is clean and safe. The frogs are saying so loudly.

disposition.en: Toads on the road in the rain — dozens of them, moving in the same direction with the specific purposefulness of migration.

presence.en: Toad migration on a wet night means the road will be slow and careful or it will involve a great deal of accidental toad-murder.

situation.en: The toads have priorities. The traveller is not among them.

disposition.en: The ford is active with frogs — thousands of them, breeding in the shallows, the water barely visible through the mass of movement.

presence.en: Not dangerous. Deeply unpleasant to wade through. The frogs will be done in three days.

situation.en: The ford is technically passable. Three days would be better.

disposition.en: A woman at a farmstead gate — she stops what she is doing when the traveller passes, neither welcoming nor unwelcoming.

presence.en: She asks which road the traveller came from — not curiosity, she is waiting for someone from that direction and the traveller is not them.

situation.en: She will not say who she is waiting for. The question is whether the traveller saw anyone on the road behind them.

disposition.en: A man on the road moving fast in the opposite direction — he slows when he sees the traveller, just enough to exchange a word.

presence.en: He says the eastern garrison road is being watched — not by soldiers, by something else, and he cannot say more clearly than that. He does not stop.

situation.en: He is frightened enough to keep moving but not so frightened he said nothing.

disposition.en: A group of three at a wayhouse fire — Gondorian by their dress, quiet in the way of people who have been quiet for several days.

presence.en: They came from Minas Tirith three weeks ago on a courier errand. The errand is done. They are not going back yet, which they will not explain.

situation.en: Three Gondorian couriers who have finished their errand and are not returning is an unusual configuration.

disposition.en: A horseman who has dismounted to check a shoe — he raises a hand when the traveller passes, the universal greeting of someone with their hands occupied.

presence.en: He asks if the traveller saw any wolf-sign on the southern road. His flock was hit two nights ago and the track led that way.

situation.en: A single wolf taking from a flock is normal. A wolf that moves south after is unusual.

disposition.en: Two of them at a ford — they check the traveller with a quick professional assessment that is not unfriendly, just thorough.

presence.en: They are running a circuit for a local lord and they want to know what the road east looks like. They share: the road west had fresh Orc-sign two days ago, above the tree-line.

situation.en: Orc-sign above the tree-line means scouts, not raiders. Scouts report back.

disposition.en: A lone rider on the road, moving at a walk, which is wrong — a Northman on a road at this hour should be moving faster.

presence.en: His horse is tired and so is he and he has been riding for two days with minimal sleep. He is carrying something he will not describe, to someone he will not name, and he needs to know if the road ahead is clear.

situation.en: The urgency and the secrecy are both real. What he is carrying is important enough to exhaust both horse and rider.

disposition.en: A man on the road with the particular self-contained manner of someone who has been walking alone for a long time and has stopped expecting company.

presence.en: He is going to Bree. He has been going to Bree for eleven days, which means he started from somewhere far enough north that few people go there voluntarily.

situation.en: Men coming south from the deep north are either Rangers, refugees, or carrying information. He does not look like a refugee.

disposition.en: A woman at a crossroads, reading a posted notice nailed to the waypost. She looks up when the traveller arrives.

presence.en: The notice is a missing-person notice — a man, forty years, last seen on the Weather Hills road three weeks ago. She says she knew him. She says this in the past tense before catching herself.

situation.en: The past tense is involuntary. She already knows he is dead. The question is how she knows.

disposition.en: He steps out of cover — not threateningly, but he was in cover and now he is not, which is its own message.

presence.en: He is a Ranger running a circuit that should have had three men. The other two have not reported back in six days. He is continuing the circuit alone because the circuit must be run, not because it is a good idea.

situation.en: A Ranger continuing a three-man circuit alone, on day six of silence from his partners, is a man running on duty and not much else.

disposition.en: A clan-man on the road with a pack-load of something he is not advertising. He eyes the traveller steadily.

presence.en: He is moving between clan-holds and he has business that is his own. He will trade road-news but nothing else.

situation.en: The pack is heavy and he is not making detours. Whatever he is carrying, the destination is specific.

disposition.en: Two of them at a fire off the road, who watch the traveller approach without invitation or hostility.

presence.en: They let the traveller come to the fire because the night is cold and they are Dunlendings, not animals. One of them speaks enough Westron to communicate. He says the road north of the river is being watched by men he does not recognise.

situation.en: Men watching roads who the Dunlendings do not recognise are a category worth paying attention to.

disposition.en: A woman on the road — elderly, moving with the specific deliberate pace of someone who does not hurry because she has not needed to hurry in a long time.

presence.en: She is a clan-healer making a circuit of the outlying steadings. She looks at the traveller with the diagnostic attention of her profession and says: you have been carrying something heavy for a long time.

situation.en: She means the shadow, not the pack. She does not know the word shadow but she can read its signs.

disposition.en: A sailor off a river-boat, killing time at a wayhouse while the boat is loaded. He is relaxed and conversational in the way of men who spend most of their time in small spaces with the same people.

presence.en: He has been running the river between Pelargir and Harlond for twelve years and he knows every sandbar and garrison and toll-point on it. He will tell you anything you want to know about the river in exchange for news from inland.

situation.en: He has not been inland in months. He is genuinely curious.

disposition.en: A man at the harbour-side who looks at the traveller for a moment too long before looking away.

presence.en: He is watching for someone. The description he was given is close enough to the traveller that he checked, then ruled it out. He relaxes fractionally.

situation.en: Someone is being looked for on this waterfront. The traveller almost matched the description.

disposition.en: A tribesman on the high path, carrying game — he stops when he sees the traveller and waits to see what happens next.

presence.en: He does not speak Westron well but the gesture language of the road is universal. He shows the road ahead: one finger, then a horizontal gesture, then both hands moving apart. One road, a split, choose.

situation.en: He knows which fork to take. He is deciding whether to share that with an outsider.

disposition.en: A mountain-man at a spring, filling a skin. He looks up without alarm — he heard the traveller long before they arrived.

presence.en: He says, in accented but serviceable Westron, that the pass ahead had fresh rockfall three days ago. Still passable, but one section is unstable and loud — anything large moving under it risks more fall.

situation.en: He chose to pass this on. Mountain-folk do not waste words on strangers without reason.

disposition.en: A garrison soldier at a checkpoint — bored, following procedure, not hostile.

presence.en: He checks for papers. The check is real — he records what he finds in a ledger. He does not explain what the ledger is for.

situation.en: The ledger is the problem. The information in it goes somewhere.

disposition.en: He comes out of a building alone to intercept the traveller before they reach the main road. This was coordinated.

presence.en: He says: someone wants to speak with you. He says it in a tone that makes clear the want is not a request. He does not say who.

situation.en: The coordination means the traveller was identified before they arrived here. The route was anticipated.

disposition.en: A knot of villagers at a well — they go quiet when the traveller approaches, then resume when the traveller is obviously not a threat.

presence.en: One of them, bolder than the rest, asks where the traveller is coming from. The question carries the specific anxiety of people waiting for news from a direction they are watching.

situation.en: They are waiting for something. The traveller is not it, but might know something about it.

disposition.en: A woman drawing water who looks at the traveller with the frank assessment of someone who has seen enough travelers to read them quickly.

presence.en: She says the village headman wants to speak with anyone coming off the northern road. She says this without urgency — it is a standing request, not an emergency.

situation.en: A standing request means it has been standing for some time. Something on the northern road is being tracked through traveler reports.

disposition.en: A group outside a farmhouse who watch the traveller pass with the still attention of people who have been told to watch.

presence.en: One of them calls out: which road did you come from? They want to know if the traveller saw anything on the road that would explain the smoke column visible to the north this morning.

situation.en: Smoke to the north that nobody can explain and a village watching the road with attention is a village that already suspects something.

disposition.en: Four soldiers on the road — not blocking it, standing at the side in the manner of a patrol that has stopped to check something.

presence.en: The sergeant asks the traveller for the road they came from and anything notable they saw. The question is standard patrol procedure, delivered without threat.

situation.en: The procedure is real and the sergeant is competent. The answer will be recorded and reported.

disposition.en: A patrol at a crossroads — six, in reasonable order, the sergeant studying a section of the road with more attention than the road warrants.

presence.en: They are tracking something on this road. The sergeant looks up, assesses the traveller in two seconds, and asks: how long ago did you pass through the valley?

situation.en: They are following a trail. The traveller may have been on the same road as whatever left it.

disposition.en: A patrol blocking the road — not aggressively, but completely. The sergeant comes forward alone.

presence.en: The road is closed ahead. He says this once, clearly, without explanation. He is following orders he may not have been given the full reason for.

situation.en: A road closure with no explanation means the reason is either classified or unknown to the sergeant himself.

disposition.en: A patrol that has identified the traveller as a specific subject of interest — the formation changes when they see them.

presence.en: The sergeant has a description. He reads it off a written order. The description matches closely enough that he is obligated to detain the traveller for questioning.

situation.en: The sergeant is not hostile — he is following procedure. The procedure may lead somewhere the traveller does not want to go.

disposition.en: Eight of them, and the sergeant has sent two around the back of the traveller before speaking. This was planned.

presence.en: They are looking for someone specific. The traveller is the closest match they have found. The sergeant is professional enough to want confirmation before acting.

situation.en: The question that confirms or denies will come. The answer determines what happens next.

disposition.en: Boot-prints on the road — military-pattern boots, six sets, moving in loose formation heading east. Made this morning.

presence.en: A patrol heading east at dawn on this road. Their spacing is correct and their stride is even. A disciplined patrol on a purpose.

situation.en: The purpose that takes a disciplined patrol east on this road at dawn is worth knowing.

disposition.en: A patrol visible on the ridge above the road — moving parallel, watching the road below without interacting with it.

presence.en: They are not on the road. They are above it, watching it. This is either overwatch for something on the road or they are watching for something they expect to come down from above.

situation.en: Patrols above roads watch the road. What they are watching for is the question.

disposition.en: Three of them on the road — armed, watching. The one in front has the bearing of someone who has been appointed to speak.

presence.en: He asks what the traveller is carrying and where they are going. The question is territorial — this is Dunlending land and he is exercising that fact, not starting a robbery.

situation.en: The distinction between a territorial question and a robbery depends entirely on the answer.

disposition.en: A small group at the road's edge — Easterlings, by their dress and gear, far enough west that they are watching every approach carefully.

presence.en: One of them speaks rough Westron. He wants to know which power holds this road — who patrols it, whose authority it answers to. He is asking because he does not yet know, and he needs to.

situation.en: An Easterling far west of his usual range who does not know who holds the road is either a scout, a refugee, or both.

disposition.en: A man on the road who adjusts his route to intersect the traveller's in a way that looks accidental and isn't.

presence.en: He asks, conversationally, if the traveller saw any patrol activity in the last valley. He phrases it as casual curiosity. It is not.

situation.en: He is checking whether the road behind the traveller is clear. The reason he needs it clear is not stated.

disposition.en: One of them, separated from a larger group, on the road with the easy manner of someone who has decided that appearing dangerous is more useful than being dangerous right now.

presence.en: He asks if the traveller needs a boat. He says it like an ordinary commercial offer. He has a boat, the boat is going south, and he has room.

situation.en: A Corsair offering a boat to a stranger on a road is offering something, but it may not be transportation.

disposition.en: Two of them at a wayhouse who make room at the fire without being asked and without warmth — the courtesy of people who follow rules about hospitality even when they do not feel them.

presence.en: One of them says, unprompted, that the eastern road is closed three days out. He says it as information, not as a warning. The distinction is deliberate.

situation.en: Variags do not share information without reason. The reason here is not stated.

disposition.en: One of them on the road alone — unusual, since they generally move in pairs at minimum. He looks at the traveller with the assessment of someone deciding whether to be bothered.

presence.en: He says he is looking for someone. He describes that person in enough detail to be deliberate — the description is a message to anyone who knows the person described.

situation.en: The description may or may not match someone the traveller knows. If it does, the message is clear. If it doesn't, it is still a warning about what is being hunted on this road.

disposition.en: A small Sagath party who intercept the traveller at a ford — not aggressively, using the ford as a natural chokepoint for a conversation.

presence.en: Their leader asks where the traveller is going and whether they have seen Gondorian military movements on the road. The question is intelligence-gathering and they are not being subtle about it.

situation.en: They are collecting information about Gondorian movements. They are doing it in the open, which means they are either very confident or very visible for a reason.

disposition.en: One of them on the road inland, out of context — sailors have a way of carrying the sea with them that makes them visible on land roads.

presence.en: He is looking for a specific inn and is comprehensively lost. The combination of competence at sea and helplessness on land is genuine and oddly disarming.

situation.en: A pirate lost on a road is still a pirate. The helplessness may or may not be the whole story.

disposition.en: A man on the road who greets the traveller with easy friendliness — too easy, the kind that is practised.

presence.en: He is running a quick read of the traveller: what are they carrying, where are they going, are they alone, what are they worth. The conversation is the read.

situation.en: He is deciding. The decision is not yet made.

disposition.en: One of them on the path — visible, which is unusual. He is watching the traveller directly.

presence.en: He says, in rough Westron: you are going wrong way. He does not elaborate. He points, once, in another direction.

situation.en: The Woses know this forest better than anyone. If he says the way is wrong, the way is wrong.

disposition.en: Two of them appear from the undergrowth at the forest edge — not threateningly, but without any attempt at subtlety either.

presence.en: One of them holds up three fingers, then points down the road, then makes a slow closing gesture with his hand. Three of something on the road ahead, waiting.

situation.en: He chose to warn the traveller. That is not nothing from a Wose.

disposition.en: It comes around the bend in the road already moving — no warning, no posture, simply in motion toward the traveller.

presence.en: A Hill-troll, running. The stride covers eight feet. It is not angry — it is hungry, which is more dangerous because hunger has no off-switch.

situation.en: Fifteen seconds to impact at this closing speed. The road has no cover on either side.

disposition.en: Three of them, from three directions simultaneously. This is not coincidence.

presence.en: Stone-trolls coordinating an ambush means someone organized them, or they have done this before and learned. The three directions close all obvious exits.

situation.en: Three Stone-trolls who understand tactics are qualitatively different from three Stone-trolls who argue about cooking.

disposition.en: An arrow from the treeline — not a miss, a ranging shot, telling the traveller that they are within range and the orcs know it.

presence.en: A ranging shot before the attack means they want the traveller to stop, which means they want the traveller alive. That is both better and worse than a kill-shot.

situation.en: The next shot will not be a ranging shot.

disposition.en: They come out of the dark on both sides of the road — too many to count quickly, too coordinated to be a random patrol.

presence.en: This is an ambush set specifically for this road at this time. Someone told them the traveller would be here.

situation.en: The ambush was prepared. That means information was passed. The traveller was tracked or betrayed before this road.

disposition.en: It does not approach — it is simply closer than it was, without having moved in any observable way.

presence.en: Barrow-wights do not chase. They close distance in the moments when the prey blinks or looks away. The gap between them is now half what it was.

situation.en: Looking at it directly does not stop it. Not looking at it is worse.

disposition.en: A strand of web across the path that was not there a moment ago — anchor-line, thicker than a finger, at throat height.

presence.en: The web appeared because something moved above the canopy to place it. The spider is above, not on the ground. The anchor-line is not a trap — it is the beginning of one.

situation.en: Two seconds before the next strand drops.

disposition.en: The path behind is sealed. At some point while moving forward, the way back became web — strong, anchored, impassable without a blade.

presence.en: This was done quietly while the traveller was watching ahead. The spider — or spiders — sealed the retreat first, which means they intend to take their time.

situation.en: The way back requires cutting through. The way forward may be equally closed by now.

disposition.en: The temperature drops ten degrees in two steps — not weather, localized, wrong. The darkness ahead is darker than the darkness behind.

presence.en: Something is standing in the path. It is not visible so much as the absence of everything else — light bends around it, sound drops out, the air pressure changes.

situation.en: Running is the wrong answer. Running is what it expects.

disposition.en: The ford feels different underfoot — the bottom that was firm on the first step is shifting on the second.

presence.en: Something below the surface has changed the bottom. The ford is being unmade from underneath while the traveller is crossing it.

situation.en: The centre of the ford is now above whatever is moving below. The banks are twenty feet in either direction.

disposition.en: An arm from the water — wrong proportion, too many joints, too long — closing around the nearest ankle.

presence.en: The Vodyanoi does not surface. It reaches from depth. The grip is cold and strong and it is already pulling.

situation.en: The water is its element. The bank is three steps away.

disposition.en: No warning. It was on the rock above and now it is not, and the shadow passes over before the sound of the wings reaches the ground.

presence.en: A drake stooping from height covers the distance in under two seconds. The first pass is a grab-and-rake, not a breath-weapon — it wants to assess what it has before committing to more.

situation.en: The first pass determines whether there is a second.

disposition.en: It is closer than it was. This is the only way to describe what happened — nothing was observed, no movement was registered, it is simply closer.

presence.en: A barrow-wight or bound ghost closing distance is not moving in any physical sense. It is the distance that changes, not the entity. This makes it deeply difficult to respond to conventionally.

situation.en: Looking away is the mechanism. Keeping it in continuous sight may not be possible.

disposition.en: It has been following for three hours. Not approaching — following. The distance has been constant. Until ten minutes ago.

presence.en: Whatever changed ten minutes ago, the undead thing behind the traveller felt it and acted on it. Shadow rising, energy falling, the traveller weakening in some way that the dead can read.

situation.en: It has been patient for three hours. Its patience has run out.

disposition.en: The barrow is sealed. There is nothing visible. But the air near it costs something to breathe — not physically, in another sense that has no precise name.

presence.en: Barrows sealed by Dúnedain ward-work do not leak. This one is leaking. Whatever is inside is old and the warding has weakened.

situation.en: The leaking is recent. The warding held for decades before now.

disposition.en: The Nazgûl does not pass close enough to be seen. But the shadow it casts moves ahead of it, and the shadow reaches the traveller before the Nazgûl does.

presence.en: A cold that is not temperature, a silence that is not quiet, and then the shadow — moving against the light, independent of the source, touching everything it passes over.

situation.en: The shadow notices what is in it. The traveller is in it.

disposition.en: A snapped tree beside the road — not wind-snapped, the break is clean and the trunk has been moved, not fallen.

presence.en: Something used this tree as a handhold or a lever. The size of the break and the displacement suggest something very heavy moving through here in the dark.

situation.en: The tree was healthy. Whatever broke it did so without effort.

disposition.en: From the valley — the sound of large rocks being moved. Not rockfall. Deliberate.

presence.en: Trolls stack rocks. Hunting caches, territory markers, the beginning of crude shelters. The activity is purposeful. There is at least one of them in that valley doing something intentional.

situation.en: The valley is between the traveller and the next road section.

disposition.en: On the hillside above the road at dusk — a shape too large for any man, moving with the slow certainty of something that does not expect to be challenged.

presence.en: A Stone-troll on open ground in the last light before dark. It is going somewhere specific — the stride is purposeful. The road below it is where the traveller is standing.

situation.en: Trolls are active at night. Dusk is the beginning of their day.

disposition.en: Drums, distant — the specific rhythm of Orc military communication, not celebration.

presence.en: The rhythm is a signal, not music. It repeats four times, stops, resumes. A call-and-confirm pattern. Someone sent a message and someone confirmed receipt.

situation.en: Military drum communication means organized forces. Organized forces on this road means they know the road.

disposition.en: A patrol visible on the far ridge — dark shapes against the sky, moving in single file. Counted: eight.

presence.en: Eight Orcs on a ridge at midday means either they are confident this ground belongs to them or they are moving fast enough that concealment is secondary to speed.

situation.en: Eight Orcs moving confidently on a ridge in daylight is a message about who controls this ground.

disposition.en: The sign has been there for an hour — the same set of prints, keeping pace. Not running, not closing, just there.

presence.en: One Orc tracking a traveller without closing is a scout, not a raider. It is maintaining contact and reporting position.

situation.en: Somewhere ahead of or behind the traveller, the scout's information is being received.

disposition.en: A howl — not nearby, a mile or two, but answered within seconds from a different direction.

presence.en: Call and response. Two wolves at minimum, coordinating. The calls establish position relative to something — probably the traveller on this open road.

situation.en: Wolves that call to each other about a moving target are hunting it. The calls were honest about the direction.

disposition.en: A wolf on the ridge above the road — visible because it is sitting and watching, not because it moved.

presence.en: It has been there for some time. It registered the traveller's approach far enough back that it was already settled when the traveller came into view.

situation.en: A single wolf watching a road from a ridge is either a scout or an individual with a territory claim on this road.

disposition.en: A wolf in the road ahead — it sees the traveller and leaves. Not flees, leaves. At a steady trot toward the treeline.

presence.en: A wolf that chooses to leave rather than test an encounter has made a calculation about the outcome. The calculation went in the traveller's favour.

situation.en: The wolf went into the trees. It did not go over the ridge.

disposition.en: A shape in the canopy above the path — not a bird, moving too deliberately, from branch to branch without sound.

presence.en: An Elf moving through the canopy in the direction the traveller is heading. Not following — preceding. Moving ahead on a parallel path.

situation.en: Elves who move ahead of travelers on their roads are either escorting them or evaluating them. The distinction becomes clear when they stop.

disposition.en: At the forest edge, for a moment — standing, watching the road, then gone between one blink and the next.

presence.en: A Silvan Elf at the wood's edge is either a border-watcher or someone who came to look at something specific on the road. The watching was deliberate and the departure was deliberate.

situation.en: It saw what it came to see. The traveller may or may not be what it was looking for.

disposition.en: The forest is being watched. Not the traveller specifically — the whole section of road. From multiple points.

presence.en: Silvan border-watch. Three separate positions visible only because the light shifted. They have been watching this road for some time and they are watching it now.

situation.en: The watch means the forest has reason to watch this particular road at this particular time.

disposition.en: Survey marks cut into the rock face above the road — fresh chisel-work, specific angles and depths that are not decorative.

presence.en: Dwarven survey-marks mean a Dwarven survey team has been through this area recently. The marks will tell a Dwarven geologist about the rock composition and the depth of a potential shaft. They are probably still in the area.

situation.en: Survey teams precede mining operations. Mining operations change roads.

disposition.en: A Dwarven caravan on the road ahead — four ponies, two wagons, moving at the pace of heavily loaded animals.

presence.en: Trade goods heading somewhere with value. The escort is three Dwarves visible, probably more not visible. They are not going to be robbed and they know it.

situation.en: Heavily loaded Dwarven caravans move on roads they consider safe. Their presence is its own assessment of the route.

disposition.en: A Dwarven camp off the road — organized, fires banked, the tools and equipment of a working party rather than travelers.

presence.en: They are doing something in this location deliberately — surveying, mining, repairing a structure, or marking territory. The equipment determines which.

situation.en: Dwarves working in a specific location have a purpose for that location. The purpose shapes how they will respond to the traveller.

disposition.en: The birds are behaving strangely — not frightened, organized. Moving in a specific direction in species-groups, as if something has asked them to.

presence.en: Radagast moves through this region periodically and the creatures know it. What the traveller is seeing is the aftermath of a Maia's passage — the wood responding to him.

situation.en: He was here recently. He may have left for a reason or he may return.

disposition.en: A column of smoke from the forest — too deliberate to be accidental, too large to be a campfire.

presence.en: A Maia signal, or something a Maia is watching, or the remnant of a Maia's working. The smoke has a colour that is not entirely consistent with any fuel that should be burning there.

situation.en: Smoke of that colour in a forest that should not be burning means something is being done here that has consequences.

disposition.en: An ancient tree at the road's edge — larger than any tree nearby, different species, with a presence that makes the traveller slow without knowing why.

presence.en: Not an Ent. A tree that has been here long enough to accumulate something that the younger trees around it lack — not consciousness, exactly, but age that has become weight.

situation.en: Nothing here is dangerous. But this tree has been at this crossroads for longer than the road has existed.

disposition.en: The trees in this section of the forest are oriented differently — their main branches face the road in a way that is not sun-seeking.

presence.en: This section of the forest has been awake for some time. Not hostile, not welcoming. Attentive. Something on this road has been worth watching recently.

situation.en: A forest that is paying attention is a forest that has a reason to pay attention.

disposition.en: A sound from the trees — not wind, not animal. Slow, low, resonant. Like language at a frequency just below comprehension.

presence.en: The trees are talking to each other. The subject is the traveller, most likely, or what the traveller carries, or what the traveller represents to something that is also in this forest.

situation.en: The communication is ongoing. The topic has not been resolved.

disposition.en: A Hobbit visible at the top of a hill above the road — distinctive silhouette, standing and watching the traveller pass.

presence.en: They are curious. They are always curious. This one has climbed a hill specifically to get a better view of the road, which is more initiative than most people show.

situation.en: The watching is benign. It is the watching of someone who will describe this to seven people tonight.

disposition.en: Hobbit-feet in the mud at the road's edge — unmistakeable, large and hairy and bare-soled. Two sets, heading toward the village.

presence.en: They walked here recently, at a comfortable pace, and they were carrying something — the depth of the prints suggests a full pack. Moving toward home at the end of the day.

situation.en: Nothing threatening here. The Shire is close, or a Hobbit community is.

disposition.en: Villagers going about their day at the road's edge — a woman hanging cloth, two men unloading a cart, children who stop to watch the traveller pass.

presence.en: A settlement that is working normally. The cart is fully loaded with produce coming in, not going out — market day was yesterday or will be tomorrow. The children watch with uncomplicated curiosity.

situation.en: Nothing is wrong here. The normalcy is its own information about the road recently travelled.

disposition.en: A village where more people than usual are visible outdoors, gathered in small groups that break up when the traveller approaches.

presence.en: Something happened here recently that has people talking. The groups reforming after the traveller passes confirms the conversation is ongoing. Nobody is going to tell a stranger what it is.

situation.en: A village that stops talking when a stranger approaches and resumes when they pass is a village sitting on something.

disposition.en: A village that is quiet in the wrong way — people inside, shutters not fully open, the normal sounds of settlement life reduced to almost nothing.

presence.en: Not abandoned. The smoke from chimneys is real and recent. They are inside by choice, which means they have a reason to be inside that the traveller cannot see from the road.

situation.en: People hiding indoors in the middle of a working day have either seen something, been told something, or are waiting for something to pass.

disposition.en: A Northman settlement visible from the road — longhouses behind a low palisade, smoke, horses in the paddock.

presence.en: A working community going about its ordinary business. The horses are in good condition and the paddock is maintained. A community that keeps its horses well is a community that is not in crisis.

situation.en: Nothing is wrong here. The road through this region is stable.

disposition.en: A group of Northmen on the road ahead — four, on foot, moving in the same direction as the traveller but slower.

presence.en: They are moving between settlements carrying tools and supplies — a work-party, not a patrol. They are talking among themselves and not watching the road behind them.

situation.en: They have not registered the traveller yet. When they do, their response will indicate how this territory treats strangers.

disposition.en: A Northman encampment off the road — temporary, military in organization, more than a dozen men visible.

presence.en: Not a patrol camp — too large, too settled. A gathering point. Men arriving from different directions over the last day or two, judging by the varied state of the horses. Someone called them here.

situation.en: An armed gathering of Northmen that the traveller did not know was here means information has been moving through this region that did not reach the road.

disposition.en: A Gondorian village at a river crossing — the ferry operator working the morning crossings, merchants waiting on the near bank.

presence.en: The ferry is running and the merchants are waiting normally. A working crossing on a clear morning. The ferryman will have road-news from both directions.

situation.en: Nothing hostile here. A functioning crossing is an opportunity for information.

disposition.en: A Gondorian garrison post visible from the road — the gate is open, two guards at their stations, watching the road with professional attention.

presence.en: The garrison is on heightened watch — not full alert, but the guards are actually watching rather than occupying their posts. Something has them paying attention.

situation.en: A garrison watching the road more carefully than usual has a reason. The reason is not posted.

disposition.en: A Gondorian settlement where the gates are closed in daylight hours — a decision someone made recently, given the fresh timber on the reinforcing bar.

presence.en: The gate was reinforced within the last week. Someone decided the existing bar was not sufficient. The decision was made quickly — the carpentry is functional, not careful.

situation.en: A settlement that reinforces its gate in a hurry has seen something that changed its assessment of what the gate needs to stop.

disposition.en: A Dúnedain settlement — small, maintained, quieter than its size should produce.

presence.en: The settlement is real and occupied but the people here move with the practised quietness of those who have learned not to draw attention. The roads in and out are watched.

situation.en: A community that moves quietly and watches its roads is a community that knows it is in a landscape that notices things.

disposition.en: A patrol coming the other direction — three of them, Dúnedain, moving fast and reading the road ahead as they come.

presence.en: They register the traveller, make their assessment in two seconds, and continue without stopping. One of them gives a brief nod — the road-acknowledgment of people who share a landscape.

situation.en: They were looking for something on this road. The traveller was not it.

disposition.en: A Dúnedain way-house with more horses tethered outside than its size suggests it should hold.

presence.en: Four horses, two of them still steaming from recent travel. Whoever arrived last came fast and recently. The way-house has been turned into a meeting-point.

situation.en: Dúnedain meeting in numbers and in haste means a circuit has found something that requires more than one Ranger.

disposition.en: A Dunlending clan-settlement on the hillside above the road — visible from below, not on the road itself.

presence.en: A settled community in their own territory. The longhouses are occupied, smoke rising, livestock visible. They are not going to bother a traveller on the road below unless the traveller gives them reason.

situation.en: Their territory, their road. The traveller is a guest whether they know it or not.

disposition.en: A gathering of Dunlending men at a crossroads — not blocking it, occupying it, the way people occupy a space they consider theirs.

presence.en: A clan-moot or the tail end of one. Several men, mix of ages, the oldest one doing most of the talking. They stop when the traveller approaches but do not become hostile.

situation.en: Interrupting a clan-moot uninvited is a social error. Not acknowledging them at all is a different kind of error.

disposition.en: Armed Dunlendings visible on the ridgeline above the road — watching the road below with the attention of people expecting something specific.

presence.en: Four or five of them, armed, positioned to observe rather than descend. They are watching for something on this road. The traveller is not it — they would have moved if the traveller was.

situation.en: Armed watchers above a road who ignore a traveller are waiting for someone or something else. The road ahead leads toward whatever that is.

disposition.en: A river-landing with boats being loaded — a normal morning on a working waterway, commerce and noise.

presence.en: Goods going downstream, empty boats returning upstream for the next load. The workers know this river and this rhythm and move accordingly. The landing master is keeping a tally.

situation.en: Nothing hostile. A working waterway means the route is open and commerce is moving.

disposition.en: A coastal settlement where several boats are pulled high on shore and their crews are not preparing to launch.

presence.en: The boats are fit to sail and the weather is adequate. The crews are on shore by choice or instruction. Something on the water has stopped the fishing.

situation.en: Fishermen who do not fish when the weather permits have seen something on the water worth not going near.

disposition.en: A military column on the road — organized, moving at pace, not looking at the road's edges.

presence.en: Soldiers in transit between postings or responding to orders. Their attention is forward, not lateral. The traveller at the road's edge is below the threshold of their concern.

situation.en: A military column this organized on this road means the road belongs to someone the traveller has reason to avoid.

disposition.en: A work-party of captives on the road — chained at the wrist, moving under armed guard toward somewhere north.

presence.en: They are exhausted and moving on will alone. The guards are professional — minimum force, maximum control, eyes front. The captives are not from this region; their clothing is wrong for the latitude.

situation.en: Captives being moved north on an enemy-held road means a supply chain is operating that has not been disrupted.

disposition.en: A tribal hunting-party visible at the forest edge — they see the traveller and hold position, watching.

presence.en: Three or four of them, armed for hunting, not for war. They are deciding whether the traveller is a problem. The pause is the decision-making interval.

situation.en: They will decide. The traveller's behavior during the pause will influence the decision.

disposition.en: Signs of a tribal camp recently vacated — fire-circles cold, brush shelters abandoned, refuse cleared in the thorough way of people who do not want to be tracked.

presence.en: They left within the last day and they left carefully. The clearing is deliberate. Whatever moved them, it moved them with enough time to clear their traces.

situation.en: Tribes that clear their traces when they leave have a reason to not be found. Something in this region is looking for them or they believe it is.

disposition.en: Mountain-folk visible on the high ground above the pass — two of them, watching the road below from a position they know well.

presence.en: They are the permanent watchers of this pass, or the generation currently doing what their parents did. They note the traveller the way they note everything that moves through.

situation.en: Being noted is not the same as being threatened. They are cataloguing, not deciding.

disposition.en: A mountain settlement where the usual watchers are not in their usual positions.

presence.en: Empty lookout posts on a clear day with travellers on the road means the watchers are either inside or somewhere else. The absence is wrong.

situation.en: People who watch passes do not stop watching them without reason.

disposition.en: A Lossoth encampment at the ice-edge — low structures, sledges, the smell of seal-oil fires.

presence.en: A winter camp between the permanent ice and the open water. The equipment suggests a group that has been here for weeks and expects to be here for weeks more. They are not mobile right now.

situation.en: Lossoth who are settled and not mobile are in a phase of their seasonal cycle. They are neither welcoming nor hostile by default.

disposition.en: Riders visible on the plain ahead — moving parallel to the road, not on it. Too distant to count accurately.

presence.en: A patrol or a herding-circuit — the pace and spacing suggest purpose rather than leisure. They have not registered the traveller.

situation.en: Riders moving parallel to the road in this direction may converge with it further on.

disposition.en: A column of soldiers visible on the road ahead — too far to read the banner but close enough to count: twenty at least.

presence.en: A Gondorian military column on this road means the road is considered important enough to move troops on. The direction they are heading is the question.

situation.en: Twenty soldiers moving on this road are not going somewhere unimportant.

disposition.en: A figure on the ridge above the road — still, watching. Gone when the traveller looks directly.

presence.en: The specific behavior of a Ranger maintaining observation. They registered the traveller and made a decision not to make contact. The decision implies the traveller passed assessment.

situation.en: Being assessed and found acceptable is reassuring. Being assessed at all means the ridge is being watched.

disposition.en: A group of Dunlendings on the hillside above — watching the road below with the patience of people who have been there a while.

presence.en: They are not descending. They are observing. Their presence on that hill is a territorial statement about this road, not a threat.

situation.en: Territorial observation and hostile observation look identical at this distance.

disposition.en: A patrol visible at the road's far end — holding position at a junction, watching the approaches.

presence.en: They are waiting at that junction deliberately. Their attention covers the road the traveller is on. They have not moved in the time the traveller has been watching them.

situation.en: A patrol holding a junction and watching approaches is either a checkpoint or an ambush depending on who is behind the traveller.

disposition.en: Horse-prints and wheel-ruts on the road — a loaded wagon, two riders flanking it, heading south. Made this morning.

presence.en: A trade caravan moving with its own escort. The hoofprints of the escort horses are positioned defensively — flanking, not following. Someone is moving goods on this road that are worth protecting.

situation.en: Trade caravans with defensive escorts mean the road is not completely safe. But they are also moving, which means it is not completely unsafe.

disposition.en: A campfire at the road's side, cold but recent — last night's camp, correctly built and correctly cleared.

presence.en: Gondorian field-discipline in the fire-ring and the refuse-clearing. Soldiers or Rangers, by the tidiness. Three or four of them, heading the direction the traveller is going.

situation.en: Someone a day ahead on this road with Gondorian training.

disposition.en: A Ranger sign on the waypost — three nicks, fresh, pale inside. Current.

presence.en: Passage confirmed, route checked. Someone ran this section of road within the last day and found it worth marking clear.

situation.en: The mark is reassurance. It is also a reminder that the road needs checking.

disposition.en: Boot-prints leaving the road on both sides simultaneously — a coordinated departure into the undergrowth, made within the last hour.

presence.en: Several people who were on this road have left it at the same point and in the same moment. Either they heard something coming or they were moving into position for something coming.

situation.en: People who leave a road simultaneously and silently do it for one of two reasons. Either is worth knowing.

disposition.en: A Northman farmer at the field-edge who sees the traveller and moves back toward his farmstead without hurry.

presence.en: Not fear — caution. The practiced withdrawal of someone who has learned that travelers on this road are sometimes worth engaging and sometimes worth not engaging, and who has no immediate way to tell which.

situation.en: He made a decision. He decided not to interact. The reason is his own.

disposition.en: A Gondorian merchant on the road who sees the traveller, checks something over their shoulder, and turns down a side-track.

presence.en: The check over the shoulder was not for the traveller. He was checking whether something behind him had come around the bend yet. He is avoiding something on the main road, and the traveller is now on the main road.

situation.en: He is not avoiding the traveller. He is avoiding the road itself, or something on it behind the traveller.

disposition.en: A figure on the road ahead who sees the traveller, holds for a moment, and steps off the road into the trees.

presence.en: The hold was an assessment. The retreat was a decision. Dúnedain do not retreat from travelers on their own roads without reason. They retreated from the traveller specifically, or from what the traveller is carrying.

situation.en: Being retreated from by someone who does not retreat easily is worth thinking about.

disposition.en: Children at the road's edge who scatter when the traveller appears — back toward a farmstead, not in panic, in the practiced way of children told to come inside when strangers pass.

presence.en: A household precaution, not a fear-response. Someone in that farmstead has taught the children to come inside for strangers. The precaution is reasonable and common in this region.

situation.en: Normal caution. Nothing hostile. The farmstead is aware the traveller passed.

disposition.en: Tended land running up to the road's edge — someone's work on it, recent enough to read.

presence.en: A corner out of the wind can be found where land is kept: a hedge lee, a stacked-stone angle, ground that drainage has kept dry.

situation.en: Worked land has owners. Owners mean questions — or a roof, if the evening goes that way.

disposition.en: Signs of work on the land beside the road — recently used, recently tended, not abandoned.

presence.en: Whoever works this ground keeps it in order. Order in the land usually means order on the road.

situation.en: Tended ground says the region is fed and governed. The road is safer where the land is kept.

disposition.en: A made place with weather-worth left in it — a standing wall, a corner out of the wind, ground that builders chose well once.

presence.en: Travellers before this one have used the same corner; the ground shows it.

situation.en: A made place remembers use. What it once kept out can still be kept out of one corner of it.

disposition.en: The place is used — not abandoned. Marks of work, of coming and going, none of them a traveller's.

presence.en: Whoever uses it keeps it for their own reasons. The road takes no part in them.

situation.en: A used place has users. Users keep watch over what they use.

disposition.en: Old work beside the road — a line of stones, a mound, the plan of a place still readable in the ground.

presence.en: Whoever built here meant to stay. They did not stay.

situation.en: The north is full of places people meant to keep.

disposition.en: Wings on the far side of the sky — a flock moving with the wind, too far for names.

presence.en: They are going about their own business. Their business does not include the road.

situation.en: A calm sky is information too.

disposition.en: Birds working the ground beside the road — feeding, unsettled only by the usual things.

presence.en: Feeding birds mean a quiet field. Disturbed birds would already be up.

situation.en: What the birds are doing says what has been through here lately. Lately: nothing.

disposition.en: Wings or calls from above — out of sight, close enough to hear, not close enough to read.

presence.en: The sound is bird-shaped and moving away. Whatever it is, it is leaving.

situation.en: A sound that leaves is better than a sound that circles.

disposition.en: A bird bursting out of the near cover — startled by the traveller, not by anything behind them.

presence.en: One bird, one alarm. It climbs away and the cover settles again.

situation.en: A single startled bird means the traveller was the only surprise.

disposition.en: Tracks in the soft verge — fresh enough to read, left at a walk.

presence.en: Grazing animals passed within hours, unhurried. Nothing pushed them.

situation.en: Calm tracks mean a calm wood ahead.

aspect.en: Fierce clan-warriors of Dunland with spear, axe and round shield, nursing an old hatred of Rohan for lost lands, fighting in loose bands under their headmen and raiding the Westfold when they can. Toward travellers: dangerous and quick to violence, above all toward Rohirrim and their friends.

lore.en: Fierce clan-warriors of Dunland, armed with spear, axe and round shield, who nurse an old hatred of Rohan for the lands their forefathers lost. They fight in loose bands under their headmen and raid the Westfold when the chance comes.

aspect.en: A small, extremely timid wild roe-deer of south-central Eriador — the commonest wild herbivore of Cardolan and Minhiriath, keeping to small groups and shunning settled land; the most hunted game of the North. Toward travellers: harmless and shy, bolting from any sign of people, a mainstay of hunters' pots.

lore.en: Thriving on the scant grasses of south-central Eriador, the Fiara is the most common wild herbivore in Cardolan and Minhiriath. They keep to small groups of four or five does and a buck and range all over the region. Extremely timid, though, they shy away from settled areas and seem much rarer than their real numbers would dictate. It is fortunate that these small beasts are prolific, for no creature in northwestern Endor is hunted as often as the Fiara. Eriadoran hunters have long relied on the Fiara as a food staple, and cooks from Bree to Tharbad create dozens of dishes using this tasty Deer meat.

aspect.en: One of the roving Elf-companies that cross the lands at dusk, singing as they go, keeping to the old paths between the havens and the eastern realms. Toward travellers: gracious and otherworldly; they share fire and counsel with the worthy and are gone by morning.

lore.en: One of the roving companies of Elves that cross the lands at dusk, singing as they go, much as Gildor's folk once passed through the Shire. They keep to the old paths between the havens and the eastern realms, share fire and counsel with worthy travellers, and are gone by morning.

aspect.en: A huge predatory viper of the plains south of Mirkwood, yellow-brown to match the soil, hunting in the evening for rodents, young beasts and (the largest) even Men and cattle — and able to spit its venom. Toward travellers: a serious danger on the open plain, striking or spitting poison from hiding.

lore.en: A huge, poisonous, predatory serpent, Egil's Viper is one of the strangest hazards of the plain of Talath Harroch, south of Mirkwood. It is said that these remarkable snakes were driven out of other areas of Rhovanion into the Talath Harroch, but this seems unlikely at best. They prey upon eggs, rodents, young animals, and (in the case of the largest Vipers) Men and Kine. Of a yellowish-brown color that blends well with the soil and grasses of the plain, Egil's Viper hunts in the late afternoon or early evening. It may spit its venom into a victim's eyes from a distance of up to thirty feet, or it may bite and inject venom in the normal manner. The Viper's fangs reach up to three inches in length and can penetrate leather and, in some cases, even chain armor.

aspect.en: A fierce wild cat of the northern wilds, larger and bolder than a common wildcat, hunting alone through forest and fell for hares, fowl and young deer. Toward travellers: keeps away from people, but quick and savage if cornered.

lore.en: A fierce wild cat of the northern wilds, larger and bolder than a common wildcat, hunting alone through forest and fell. Quick and savage when cornered, it preys on hares, fowl and young deer.

aspect.en: A small, inconspicuous "leopard viper," grey speckled with brown and black to blend with stone and fond of basking on rocky ledges — easily overlooked, but its bite is deadly. Toward travellers: a real peril to climbers and barefoot folk who set a hand or foot on a sunny ledge without looking.

lore.en: An inconspicuous little creature, the Rock Viper would not be worth mentioning, save that those climbing cliffs and mountains in Endor would be well-advised to watch where they place their hands or their bare feet (Hobbits, especially), for this snakeling is fond of sunbathing on rocky ledges. Their grey skin is speckled with brown and black spots, enabling the serpent to blend in with rock surfaces (the creature is also called the Leopard Viper). Although it is small, the Rock Viper's bite is quite deadly (20th lvl). There has never been a proven case of anyone surviving such a bite without some sort of medical treatment, either magical or herbal. The victim first suffers swelling, massive bruising, and discoloration around the wound. Then, within 60 seconds, his heart begins to palpitate, his breathing becomes irregular, his endocrine system fails, and he dies of total system shock within 6-10 minutes.

aspect.en: A ranger of the Green-elves warding the eaves of the forest realms — a silent woodsman and deadly archer who patrols the wild marches, shadows intruders and keeps the old paths. Toward travellers: unseen until he chooses; a guardian who watches strangers closely and aids the worthy.

lore.en: A ranger of the Laegrim, the Green-elves of the woods, warding the eaves of the forest realms. Silent woodsmen and deadly archers, they patrol the wild marches, shadow intruders and keep the old paths between the Elven lands.

aspect.en: Killing weather — blizzards, ice-storms, hail, gales and freezing rain — that can fell the unsheltered through cold and exhaustion alone, deadliest in the high country and far North when the sky turns. Toward travellers: a deadly test of shelter and endurance; seek cover before it closes in.

lore.en: Killing weather — blizzards, ice-storms, hail, gales and freezing rain — that can fell the unsheltered traveller through cold and exhaustion alone. The high country and far North are deadliest when the sky turns.

aspect.en: Large, intelligent bats of Moria and the Misty Mountains that hunt in directed packs under a dominant leader, slashing prey to shreds with razor claws; their low calls give a little warning, though they are too quick for it to help. Toward travellers: a coordinated, deadly swarm in the dark of caverns.

lore.en: Cavern Wings are large, intelligent Bats found predominantly in Moria, although they have been reported in other caverns in the Misty Mountains. They seem to have a very sophisticated "biting order," culminating in a leader which directs the other bats in their group hunts. Their weapon is their razor sharp claws, with which they rip their victims into bite-sized shreds. Their voices are low-pitched for bats, allowing most victims some warning of their approach, although this rarely helps as the Cavern Wings are very quick and maneuverable. They have dark gray to black fur, often speckled in younger individuals; the best defense is to slay the leader, after which the rest retreat until the flock chooses a new leader.

aspect.en: A collection of swarthy, compact nomad-peoples east of the Sea of Rhûn — restless confederations ever seeking land and plunder and apt to invade their neighbours, often in the Enemy's service. Toward travellers: warlike and frequently hostile, raiders and invaders dangerous on their own ground or at war.

lore.en: This term refers to a collection of peoples who live in north-central Middle-earth, the area to the east of the western shore of the Sea of Rhûn. These nomadic confederations are ever in search of territory and wealth and periodically invade the lands of their neighbors. The Balchoth and Wainriders are two such peoples. Each group has its own subculture and language, although most are related. Physical Character: Compact and agile. Men average 140 pounds, women 100 pounds. Swarthy, with a tan or yellowish/tan quality. Normal endurance, although they can ride horses, wagons, or chariots for long periods without exhaustion. Short to medium. Men average 5'6", women 5'1". Lifespan: Short, about 40-65 years. They are superb with riding animals and produce fabulous horsemen. +10 bonus to Offensive Bonuses when fighting from a horse or chariot. +20 to any attempt to train, befriend, or subdue a horse. They are nomads who live in mobile camps and move their camps using great wagons (wains). Warriors all, they also herd horses and cattle. Easterlings have little regard for anyone except their own people. They hate the Dúnedain.

aspect.en: Large black swans of river valleys from Wilderland south to Mordor's edge, common along the Anduin; they will mob and even capsize boats that stray too near their huge nests. Toward travellers: usually peaceable, but aggressively territorial around their nests on the water.

lore.en: Black Swans are found from Mordor and northward into Wilderland, as far as the southern reaches of Mirkwood. They are also quite common in the river valleys of Nurad and Rhovanion, especially along the River Anduin. They are large for Swans and have been known to mob and overturn boats, usually because the vessels had come too close to the Swans' huge nests.

aspect.en: Hunting cats of the foothills and mountains, smaller than the snow leopard but — unusually for cats — highly social, living in prides and hunting large game together with wolf-like tactics; tameable if taken young. Toward travellers: keep to the heights and shun people, but a hunting pride is not to be trifled with.

lore.en: Hunting cats of the less extreme foothills and mountains throughout Endor, smaller than the Snow Leopard but effective hunters and fishers. Unusually for cats their size, they are highly social, living in prides of 5-8 with an intricate structure and hunting large game as a group using wolf-like tactics. Taken young, they make loyal and protective pets.

aspect.en: The ruins of Calenardhon — Gondor's grassland province before it became Rohan — abandoned forts, road-stations and steadings standing empty on the plains, slowly swallowed by grass and weather. Toward travellers: a melancholy open ruin; shelter of a sort, but a haunt of beasts and brigands as much as a refuge.

lore.en: The ruins of Calenardhon, the grassland province of Gondor before it became Rohan — abandoned forts, road-stations and steadings standing empty on the plains, slowly reclaimed by grass and weather.

aspect.en: A rare deep-water clam of the southern seas, prized for an ingredient in a healing balm that soothes burns, and for its beautiful silvery shell. Toward travellers: harmless; a valued find for healers and a thing of beauty.
