lore.en: The Vessino Clam is a rare mollusk which is found only in the deep waters of the Haragaer and the southern Belegaer. A source of a valuable ingredient for a healing balm that soothes and heals burns, it is prized by Lay Healers and Medicinists. Its beautiful, silvery shell is also noted as an exquisite ornament.

aspect.en: The hereditary Dúnedain lords of Dor-en-Ernil, ranking just below King and Steward — a line carrying Elven blood, ruling almost as their own masters from Dol Amroth under the silver Swan-ship banner. Toward travellers: noble, gracious and high-bred lords of the sea-coast, courteous to the worthy and commanding in bearing.

lore.en: Hereditary Dúnedain rulers of Dor‑en‑Ernil, holding a status just below the King and Steward; their line carries Elven blood and rules almost autonomously from Dol Amroth, symbolized by a silver Swan‑ship on deep blue.

aspect.en: A rare, cunning lion of Cardolan — burnt-orange above with a spotted near-white belly — living in small family groups, lairing in trees and caves, hunting deer and sheep, locked in an old feud with the wolves, and killing men only in self-defence. Toward travellers: shy of people and not aggressive, but a powerful predator that will fight if cornered.

lore.en: Named for the black spots on its almost-white underbelly above a burnt-orange coat, the Spotted Lion is now quite rare from hunting but still ranges throughout Cardolan. Not evil but extremely cunning and speechless, its old, bitter feud with the wolves has hastened its decline alongside the efforts of Men. It lives in small family groups, lairs in trees and caves, prefers to hunt Fiara (sheep will do), and will kill men in self-defence.

aspect.en: The otters, minks, beavers and water-rats of river and lake-shore — sleek swimmers that fish, forage and burrow along the banks. Toward travellers: shy and harmless; their dams, slides and tracks mark a healthy waterway.

lore.en: The otters, minks, beavers and water-rats of river and lake-shore — sleek swimmers that fish, forage and burrow along the banks. Mostly shy of Men, their dams, slides and tracks mark every healthy waterway.

aspect.en: Descendants of the eastern horse-lords, once prosperous farmers and horse-breeders, now hardened by plague and war into wary defenders of isolated steadings and fortified camps. Toward travellers: tough, watchful frontier folk — guarded with strangers, staunch once trusted.

lore.en: Descendants of Vidugavia's horse-lords in the plains and East Bight, formerly prosperous farmers and horse-breeders, reduced by the Plague to hard-edged defenders of isolated homesteads and fortified camps.

aspect.en: The stockiest hobbits, broad-built with unusually large hands and feet and sometimes a beard — river- and flatland-dwellers, more at home near water than other hobbit-kinds. Toward travellers: easy-going, sturdy riverside folk, cautious with strangers but not unfriendly.

lore.en: The Stoors are the stockiest Hobbit folk and often appear shorter than some of the Harfoots because of their wide profile. Generally, however, they are taller than Harfoots and shorter than Fallohides. Their coloration is also somewhat of a compromise, although they have curly brown hair which resembles that of their shorter cousins. Nonetheless, the most distinguishing features of Stoors are their huge hands and feet (large even by Hobbit standards) and frequent beard growth. Stoors prefer riversides and flatlands. Some have begun relying on surface dwellings of wood, brick, or stone. Stoors trace their lines through the female. River- and marsh-loving folk, they are met poling boats and tending weirs in Dunland, the wetlands of Eriador and the Gladden country, and are warier of strangers than other Hobbits.

aspect.en: True water-dragons — often called sea-serpents — agile swimmers of fresh and salt water that seize prey with six fin-claws; their weakness, besides fire, is being lured from the water. Toward travellers: a lethal hunter of lakes, rivers and coasts, safest fought by drawing it onto land.

lore.en: True Water-drakes, often called Sea Serpents, are agile swimming Dragons (freshwater and saltwater) that seize prey with six fin-claws; their one weakness, besides fire, is being lured from water.

aspect.en: Huge, feared sea-reptiles — dark blue with black-striped backs and long grasping fangs that jut from the snout, thought kin to water-drakes — that attack small ships, punching holes in hulls and waiting for them to founder. Toward travellers: a deadly menace at sea, a wrecker of boats and devourer of those it spills into the water.

lore.en: Uncommon but well-feared, the huge Sea Crocodiles resemble Fell Beasts without wings. They are gracile, dark blue, and have black stripes running down the backs of their horny backs. Many chroniclers believe they are related to Water Drakes, for Sea Crocodiles have elongated conical grasping teeth in the forward part of their snouts that extend well outside their mouths. Like sea monsters, Sea Crocodiles are prone to attack smaller ships, seeking to puncture hulls with their mighty jaws, then waiting for the ship to founder. Nesting in secluded bays or in coastal caves, they also present a danger on land.

aspect.en: A Wizard dwelling at Rhosgobel on the edge of Mirkwood, who gives his care to birds and beasts rather than the affairs of power — a rare friend and refuge in the shadowed woods. Toward travellers: gentle, eccentric and kindly, a possible helper (often through the creatures he befriends), though caught up in his own concerns.

lore.en: The Wizard dwelling at Rhosgobel on the western edge of Mirkwood, devoting his power and attention to birds and beasts rather than politics, and providing a rare point of light and refuge in the shadowed woods.

aspect.en: Ghoul-like undead of the southern wastes, lairing in dry-hill caves and dune-graves; their withered eyes see a victim's life-energy as painful light, and they ignore pain and stun. Toward travellers: a relentless desert haunt that hunts by the glow of the living.

lore.en: Ghoul-like undead that prowl the southern wastes, lairing in the caves of dry hills or among the dunes over unmarked graves; their dried eyes perceive the life-energy of victims as painful light, and they ignore stun and pain.

aspect.en: A small, rare day-hunting owl — intelligent and perceptive, taught speech by the Elves and keeping its own tongue; those close to nature can learn much from it. Toward travellers: harmless and wise, a possible source of knowledge to one who can speak with beasts.

lore.en: A rare day-hunting Owl, the Short-eared Owl is quite small. Like many other Endorian birds, however, it is an intelligent and perceptive creature. They were taught by the Elves to speak and have their own language. One who is close to Nature can derive helpful information from them.

aspect.en: Broad-crowned hardwoods of temperate forest, in some lands only remnants of once-greater woods, giving strong timber, acorns for wildlife and shade for farm and road. Toward travellers: harmless; sturdy shade and a sign of old woodland.

lore.en: Oaks are broad-crowned hardwood trees common in the temperate forests of Middle-earth. In Lamedon they survive as remnants of once greater woods, providing strong timber, acorns for wildlife and shade for farms and roads.

aspect.en: Kept hives and wild bee-trees worked for honey and wax, tended in meadow and orchard. Toward travellers: a sweet, valued harvest where sugar is unknown — and well-guarded by its bees.

lore.en: Kept hives and wild bee-trees worked for honey and wax — a sweet and valuable harvest where sugar is unknown. Bee-keepers tend their skeps in meadow and orchard, and a good honey-year is cause for celebration.

aspect.en: A single Dwarf met far from any hold — a wanderer, exile, craftsman seeking work, or one bent on a private errand or grudge; gruff with strangers but steadfast to those who earn it. Toward travellers: wary and close-mouthed but honest and stout-hearted, a good companion once trust is won.

lore.en: A single Dwarf met far from any hold — a wanderer, exile, craftsman seeking work, or one bent on a private errand or grudge. Gruff with strangers but steadfast to those who earn it, such travellers turn up almost anywhere in the wide lands.

aspect.en: A Dwarven trader on the road with a laden pony or wagon, dealing in metalwork, tools and weapons between the Dwarf-holds and the towns of Men and Elves — a shrewd bargainer travelling well-guarded. Toward travellers: open to trade and news, canny and close with their accounts, but fair to honest dealers.

lore.en: A Dwarven trader on the road with a laden pony or wagon, dealing in metalwork, tools, weapons and worked goods between the Dwarf-holds and the towns of Men and Elves. Shrewd bargainers, they travel well-guarded and keep their accounts close.

aspect.en: Sea-elves of the western coasts, masters of shipbuilding and sailing — fishers and net-menders in the river-mouths, shipwrights and captains in the havens, crews of the grey ships that ward the shores. Toward travellers: courteous coast-dwelling Elves, bound to sea and ship, reserved with strangers but not unkind.

lore.en: Sea-elves who dwell by the coasts, skilled in shipbuilding and sailing. Along the shores of Lindon and Harlindon they appear as fishers and net-menders in the river-mouths, as shipwrights and sea-captains in the havens, and as the crews of the grey ships that keep the western coasts.

aspect.en: The commonest and smallest hobbits — brown-skinned, beardless, rarely over three feet — hole-dwelling, home-loving folk of hill and highland, the very picture of the ordinary Shire-hobbit, and friendly with Dwarves. Toward travellers: peaceable, shy, hospitable little folk who keep to themselves and hate orcs and wargs.

lore.en: The most common Hobbits are Harfoots. They are the smallest in size and the darkest in color, rarely exceeding 3 feet in height and having brown skin and hair. Neat and uniformly beardless, they are in many ways the picture of the average Hobbit. Harfoots favor hillsides and highlands. They have traditional sites for their traditional smials or Hobbit-hole houses. They prefer to interact with the grim Dwarves. All Hobbits share in hating Wargs and Orcs. They are the stay-at-home, hole-dwelling folk of the Shire, Bree and the old Hobbit-lands of Eriador, and are seldom met far afield.

aspect.en: Camels of the southern lands — hardy desert beasts that store water and fat, walk soft sand on broad pads, go long without drinking and endure fierce heat without sweating. Toward travellers: stolid, ill-tempered but invaluable desert mounts and pack-beasts, harmless unless provoked.

lore.en: The Devevi (Ap. "Camels"; sing. "Deve") of southern and central Endor are hardy animals who store water in their stomach linings and can go long periods without drinking. Their humps absorb heat and metabolize fat to provide energy and water, while wide foot pads enable them to walk on soft, sandy soil; a three-chambered stomach permits digestion of virtually any vegetation. With a refined temperature regulation system, a Deve has no need to sweat; it can lose over a quarter of its body weight and restore it in an orgy of drinking lasting only ten minutes (intaking 7-8 gallons a minute). There are two subgroups: the runners (light, graceful riding mounts built for speed) and the workers (thickly-built, slow, capable of heavy loads). Both are easy to domesticate but are loud, filthy, spit, and are virtually impossible to keep clean. The most prized is the rare two-humped Deve Póa, bred in and around the desert city of Tûl Póac in Far Harad and hailing from the Yellow Mountains of southern Endor; adapted for both temperature extremes, more docile, with a natural saddle and a smooth, rolling gait.

aspect.en: The Oliphaunt — a colossal relative of the elephant, "lord" of the southern wilds, up to thirty feet long and seventeen high at the shoulder, with huge tusks and an agile trunk; a vegetarian with few natural foes, ridden to war by southern peoples. Toward travellers: peaceable while grazing, but a charging or war-driven Mûmak is an unstoppable, earth-shaking force.

lore.en: The huge, fearsome, and majestic Mûmak (W. "Oliphaunt"; P. "Tembo"; pl. "Tembovi") is a close relative of the Andamunda (Elephant) and is often referred to as the Gorsandamunda (Q. "Giant Elephant"). It is the "lord" of Endor's southern wilds, growing up to thirty feet in length and standing up to 17 feet in height at the shoulder, with few foes. Fortunately for their rivals, Mûmakil are vegetarians; they rest in the midday heat and roam in search of nutritious roots, leaves, shoots, twigs, and fruits, using their agile trunks and huge tusks (which grow as long as 7'). These social beasts travel in herds and adapt (albeit reluctantly) to domestication. When aroused, they can be deadly fighters; both the Úsakani and the Mûmakani have long prized them as mounts for war, and the Haradrim build great fighting towers to place on their backs, decorating the legs and tusks. The thick hides of Mûmakil make them almost invulnerable to arrows except for their eyes, but when blinded they often run mad with pain, trampling and destroying everything in their paths.

aspect.en: Folk upon the road for their own reasons — bound for market or kin, fleeing hard times, or simply going from town to town — usually harmless and glad of company on a lonely stretch. Toward travellers: generally friendly fellow-wayfarers, though the road draws all sorts and not every one is what they seem.

lore.en: Folk upon the road for reasons of their own — bound for market or kin, fleeing hard times, or simply going from one town to the next. Usually harmless and glad of company on a lonely stretch, though the road draws all sorts and not every traveller is what they seem.

aspect.en: A large golden-brown eagle of the high country — a powerful hunter of hares, marmots and the young of mountain herds, soaring on broad wings over crag and valley and guarding a wide range. Toward travellers: no threat to people, a majestic sight over the heights.

lore.en: A large golden-brown eagle of the high country, a powerful hunter of hares, marmots and the young of mountain herds. It soars on broad wings over crag and valley and defends a wide hunting range.

aspect.en: Powerful toothed sperm-whales of the western deeps that hunt fish and squid — their great rival the giant squid — and are wily enough to upset a good-sized vessel. Toward travellers: no hunter of men, but its sheer size can capsize a ship that crowds it.

lore.en: Powerful Sperm Whales, the Cherethrynd (S. "Hallmaw"; sing. "Charothrond") reside in the deep waters of the Belegaer, off the western coasts of Middle-earth. Unlike most Whales, they sport teeth (nine inch long teeth) and they hunt fish and Squid rather than consuming krill through a baleen strainer. The Charothrond favorite food and most dangerous rival is the Giant Squid. Although wily and capable of upsetting a good-sized vessel, Cherethrynd are vulnerable to the ruthless Umbarean whalers who sail the oceans near the Bay of Belfalas. These Men hunt lone Whales for their oil, bone, and ambergris (an indigestible chalky substance that forms around Squid beaks and, in spite of its hideous smell, makes wonderful perfumes).

aspect.en: A strange, near-blind, mute white bird of Moria that finds the fungus it eats by smell and senses danger by inaudible cries like a bat; serrated beak and strong talons, but almost wholly fungus-eating. Toward travellers: harmless unless surprised or starving, when an old predatory instinct may stir.

lore.en: White, mute, and almost blind, the odd, fungus-eating Chamber Bird is one of the many strange inhabitants of Moria. They seek out the fungus by their remarkable sense of smell (odd indeed for a bird) and note enemies by their inaudibly high cries, in the manner of bats. Their large, gaping beaks have serrated edges and their bluish talons are both sharp and strong. Totally herbivorous (primarily fungivorous), they rarely attack animals unless surprised or starving, though some instinct for meat seems to remain from a predacious ancestor.

aspect.en: The "Hillmen" of the highlands west of the Anduin — rugged, stocky, tan-skinned mountain folk, mostly settled farmers and herders and superb on rough ground, though some keep to the old wild ways in the foothills. Toward travellers: proud and often suspicious of outsiders, and old foes of the Rohirrim — wary, but not always hostile.

lore.en: Also called "Hillmen", this group of Common Men traditionally lives in the hills and highlands west of the Anduin valley. Most have become settled farmers and herders and make up majority populations in Eriador. Others remain pure and live in the foothills and mountain vales. Physical Character: They are of medium to stocky build and rugged, with little body hair. Men average 175 pounds, women 135 pounds. They have a tanned or ruddy complexion and brown hair. They are superb mountaineers and handle tough terrain with little additional effort. Men average 5'10", women 5'6". Lifespan: Short; about 50-80 years. +20 for Climbing and Acrobatic maneuvers. +20 for Public Speaking and Acting activity. Crude wool and hide tunics with leggings. They also wear rough over-coats, short cloaks, and fur hats. Dunlendings are herders, hunters, and gatherers who live in extended families and reside in villages. Dunlendings generally hate the Rohirrim and Woses above all, although many also despise the Dúnedain, Dwarves, and Orcs.

aspect.en: Cold-drakes of the far North marked by an icy breath, dwelling in the frozen reaches. Toward travellers: a frost-breathing dragon of the polar wastes, deadly in its cold domain.

lore.en: Ice-drakes are Cold-drakes of the Earth element distinguished by an icy breath, dwelling in the frozen reaches of the far North.

aspect.en: Small, ancient wingless dragons that hunt on instinct near their high mountain-cavern lairs, with short powerful legs and muscular bodies. Toward travellers: a deadly ambush predator of the deep hills — less cunning than the great dragons, but lethal.

lore.en: Cave-drakes (Q. "Rondoleki") are relatively small, ancient wingless Dragons that rely on instinct rather than plots, hunting near their high-mountain cavern lairs with short powerful legs and muscular bodies.

aspect.en: Seafaring and river-going men met in port or aboard ship — crewing trade-vessels, fishing boats and ferries; hardy, superstitious and free with a tale, knowing the coasts, currents and harbours. Toward travellers: easy company and a source of passage and sea-lore, harmless ashore unless badly crossed.

lore.en: Seafaring and river-going men met in port or aboard ship — crewing trade-vessels, fishing boats and ferries. Hardy, superstitious and free with a tale, they know the coasts, currents and harbours of their waters.

aspect.en: An obscure order of Noldorin mystics keeping a hidden valley-haven in the far north — a refuge for the Free Peoples and a base of resistance against the Witch-king. Toward travellers: secretive, wise and benevolent; a hidden help to the hunted who can find them.

lore.en: An obscure order of Noldorin mystics maintains Evermist, a hidden valley on the Cape of Forochel that serves as a haven for the Free Peoples and base for resistance to the Witch-king of Angmar.[file:39]

aspect.en: A black, nocturnal lizard with a prehensile tongue and tail and three layers of hollow insulating scales — the greatest climber of its kind, swinging across caves and cliffs to leap on prey and rend it with steely claws. Toward travellers: a clinging cave-and-cliff predator; small, but its claws and ambush make dark rock dangerous.

lore.en: The Andodaio, or "Gate-shadow" (pl. "Andodailion"), is a black, nocturnal lizard with a prehensile tongue and tail. It is without doubt the greatest climber among all the Rávatsar. Rugged landscapes and subterranean settings accommodate it well, for the Andodaio is insulated with an unusual array of three layers of hollow scales that enable it to survive in environments far too cool for its brethren. Hanging from rocks, it swings across the caves and precipices, leaping onto prey and tearing its victims apart with its steely claws. Larger creatures would have little to fear from the Andodailion, except that they live in large communities and often hunt in groups of 10-100 individuals. Unusually social, a horde of Andodailion can easily fell a Man by attacking in concert.

aspect.en: Treacherous soft ground — quicksand, quagmire, sucking mud or slime-filled pools — that grips and swallows whatever blunders in, the deeper for every struggle. Toward travellers: a silent trap of marsh and bog; test the footing, and do not thrash if caught.

lore.en: Treacherous soft ground — quicksand, quagmire, sucking mud or slime-filled pools — that grips and swallows whatever blunders in. The more a victim struggles, the deeper they sink.

aspect.en: A deep cleft, crevasse or sinkhole — sometimes plain, sometimes hidden under brush or thin crust — into which the unwary may plunge; karst country, old quarries and glaciers are riddled with them. Toward travellers: a silent pitfall; test the ground in broken or hollow country.

lore.en: A deep cleft, crevasse or sinkhole — sometimes plain, sometimes hidden under brush or thin crust — into which the unwary may plunge. Old quarries, karst country and glaciers are riddled with such pitfalls.

aspect.en: The largest and most powerful of sheep — a stout black-and-silver beast standing four to five feet at the shoulder, its silvery head-fur running up its curved, forward-facing horns, which it is quick to use and which make it hard to tame. Toward travellers: a wild herd-beast, harmless if left alone but dangerous with those lethal horns if pressed.

lore.en: The largest and most powerful of Endor's Sheep, the Rútorasse (Q. "Eastern Woolhorns"; pl. "Rútorassi") is a stout, black and silver beast that stands about 4-5 feet at the shoulder. It is aptly named, for its silvery head fur grows up the sides of its curved horns. These two forward-facing weapons can be lethal, and the Woolhorn is quick to employ them for defense; thus, this beast is difficult to domesticate. Native to the lands of Dalpygis, Chey, and the Kargagis Ahar in central Middle-earth, Woolhorns roam at night in small, segregated herds. Males run apart from the females except during the mating season, which lasts from late summer until early fall. When united, the mixed herd is relatively stationary for about a month, the first half of which is devoted to courting rituals, including brutal duels between males seeking dominance (and their choice of mates).

aspect.en: Handsome black-and-white swans, perhaps the cleverest of plant-eating birds — they remember kindness and harm, and are said to have led fog-lost travellers to safety in the marshes; revered as sacred by the Marshmen. Toward travellers: gentle and intelligent, a possible helper to the lost, and sacred to some.

lore.en: Handsome aquatic birds, Pied Swans may be the most intelligent of herbivorous avians. They seem able to remember those who have harmed or helped them (at least for periods of several weeks), and there have been reports of pied Swans leading fog-lost travellers to high ground in marshes. Various rural and primitive peoples, such as the Marshmen of the Nindalf, revere these birds as being sacred to the Vala Yavanna. They are creamy white in color, liberally splotched and speckled with black and gray. Unfortunately, their flesh is tasty and their feathers soft, so that those with more greed than reverence hunt them. Pied Swans are most commonly found in the Nindalf and along the shores of the Anduin in the relatively unspoiled areas of Ithilien.

aspect.en: A dreadful wolverine-like predator — solitary, dark-furred and badger-shaped — unbelievably quick, fierce and seemingly mad, attacking even armed groups unprovoked and fighting to the death. Toward travellers: wildly aggressive for its size; it may set upon a whole party without cause, a danger out of all proportion to its bulk.

lore.en: Dreadful wolverine-like predator (pl. Glutani), solitary, dark-furred and badger-shaped, found throughout northwestern Endor with its greatest concentration in western Minhiriath. Unbelievably quick, fierce and seemingly insane, it attacks armed groups without provocation and fights to the death. Two varieties: the reddish-brown Lowland Glutan (~2 ft) and the bulkier, dark Highland Glutan of the Dunland hills. A 25 gp bounty sits on their heads; Dunlanders buy live ones for fights against Bears or Wolves.

aspect.en: Wild dogs of the eastern fens and moors, ranging in small packs to fish, scavenge and take small game — and to prey on weak, stranded or sickly Men; easily driven off with fire and torchlight. Toward travellers: a danger mainly to the lone and the weak, readily scared off with flame.

lore.en: Wild dog (pl. Merisc Tyka) found throughout Rhovanion, Rhun and the lands of the Kykurian Kyn, related to the feral dogs of the Talath Harroch south of Mirkwood. Frequenting fens and moorlands in small packs, it fishes, scavenges carrion and attacks small mammals, and will prey on weak, stranded or sickly Men. It is afraid of fire and easily driven off with torchlight; its dappled yellowish-tan and brownish-grey coat grants a +40 Hiding bonus.

aspect.en: A chance meeting with Dwarves on the road — usually a small party travelling between their mountain-holds and the markets of Men — blunt, watchful and quick to take offence or oath, keeping their own counsel. Toward travellers: gruff and guarded but honest, fair to fair dealing and staunch once a bond is made.

lore.en: A chance meeting with Dwarves abroad — usually a small party on the road between their mountain-holds and the markets of Men, rather than a delving in their halls. Blunt, watchful and quick to take offence or oath, they keep their own counsel and rarely tarry.

aspect.en: Ordinary working people of town and country — farmers, herders, craftsfolk and labourers going about daily life. Toward travellers: they want mainly to be left in peace, and their welcome to strangers swings from kindness to wariness.

lore.en: Ordinary working people of town and countryside — farmers, herders, craftsfolk, labourers and their families going about daily life. Met wherever folk dwell, they want chiefly to be left in peace, and their welcome to strangers ranges from open hospitality to wary suspicion depending on the times and the road.

aspect.en: A man-like troll-breed — about seven feet, jet-black skinned with red eyes and long red tongues, smaller and quicker than full trolls and as clever as Men, going armoured in crude black gear. Toward travellers: dangerous, disciplined fighters, cunning enough to ambush and fight like soldiers rather than mere brutes.

lore.en: Half-trolls are the product of a union of Olog-hai and Variag Men. For this reason, they are sometimes confused with Black Trolls, but they are smaller and quicker and vaguely resemble Men. Their 7' height, jet-black skin, long sharp red tongues, and glowing red eyes should also serve notice of their uniqueness. Half-trolls differ from Olog-hai in other ways: (1) they wear crude black clothing and considerable amounts of armor; (2) they are kept away from other Trolls; (3) they are as intelligent as Men; and (4) they are more agile. Given their increased minds, they get two background points.

aspect.en: A Northman folk of the Anduin vales akin to the Beornings — bee-keepers, herders and woodsmen who hold the river-lands and keep them clear of orcs and wolves. Toward travellers: independent folk, hospitable to friends but fierce to foes.

lore.en: The Beijabar, a Northman folk of the Vales of Anduin akin to the Beornings — bee-keepers, herders and woodsmen who hold the riverlands and fight to keep them clear of Orcs and wolves. Independent, and hospitable to friends but fierce to foes.

aspect.en: Folk of a clan or tribe beyond the settled realms — hillmen, marsh-dwellers, herders or hunters bound by kin and custom rather than king. Toward travellers: proud and wary of outsiders, peaceable if respected but fierce in defence of their own ground.

lore.en: Folk of a clan or tribe living beyond the settled realms — hillmen, marsh-dwellers, herders or hunters bound by kin and custom rather than king. Proud and wary of outsiders, and fierce in defense of their own ground.

aspect.en: Great droning bumble-bees of meadow and heath — furred, harmless, blundering from flower to flower; their deep hum is one of the sounds of a warm summer's day. Toward travellers: entirely harmless, a peaceful note of the countryside.

lore.en: Great droning bumble-bees of meadow and heath, furred and harmless, blundering from flower to flower. An old country name for them is 'dumbledors', and their deep hum is one of the sounds of a warm summer's day.

aspect.en: Small fire-drakes of the wetlands whose secretions are extremely toxic, like diluted dragon-blood. Toward travellers: a deadly lurker of fen and bog whose very fluids burn and poison.

lore.en: Marsh-drakes are small Fire-drakes of the wetlands whose extremely toxic secretions act like diluted Dragon-blood.

aspect.en: Massive humanoid beings of the mountains and wild places, far larger and stronger than Men. Toward travellers: dangerous through sheer size and strength — some merely aloof and brutish, others openly hostile.

lore.en: Massive humanoid creatures found in mountains and wilderness.

aspect.en: Orcs mounted on the great evil wolves of the North — fast, far-ranging raiders and shock-troops that strike at speed across open country and harry fugitives and caravans before vanishing. Toward travellers: a swift, deadly threat in the open; they run down the slow and the lone.

lore.en: Orcs mounted on Wargs — the great evil wolves of the North — fast, far-ranging and deadly. Used as raiders, outriders and shock troops, they strike at speed across open country and harry fugitives and caravans before melting back into the wild.

aspect.en: One of the most vicious insects alive — a rare, lethal giant wasp the size of a small animal (6-8 lbs), with a transparent horn-like proboscis it uses to gore prey to death before feeding with three sets of jaws. Its one weakness is the loud hum that heralds its approach. Toward travellers: deadly if it attacks, though its hum gives a moment's warning.

lore.en: Surely one of Endor's most vicious insects, the rare but often lethal Hummerhorn is the stuff of legend. Each weighs 6-8 lbs and has a razor sharp, pointed proboscis of chitin (transparent horn). It gores a victim to death, then feasts on the corpse with three sets of mandibles. They resemble gigantic black and grey wasps, and their only failing is the noise they make whenever they approach.

aspect.en: Privateers, pirates and smugglers working from coves, swamps and hidden harbours along the coasts, raiding trade and dodging the king's duties. Toward travellers: lawless and dangerous — they prey on shipping and trust no one they cannot use.

lore.en: Semi-legal privateers, outright pirates and smugglers operate from coves, swamps and hidden harbors along the coasts and the Ethir Anduin, raiding trade and dodging royal duties despite the Sea-lords' efforts.[file:30]

aspect.en: Among the most powerful undead — beings of pure spirit with no body, roused by the presence of the living of their former kind. They appear as they remember themselves, and can shape that illusion into something larger and more terrible at will. Toward travellers: a hateful, fear-wielding haunt of ruins and old places, perilous to face after dark.

lore.en: These can be the most powerful of undead, save the Nazgûl (see below). They are totally energy, having no physical component at all, and are activated solely by the presence of living beings of the same type that they once were (most often Men). They appear as they remember themselves being, with varying degrees of effectiveness: lesser Ghosts often neglect pertinent details, such as appropriate clothing for the occasion. They also do not realize that, since their appearence is nothing but illusion, their will can affect it. A Ghost who wishes to be larger and more menacing is so, with nothing but a thought. Greater Ghosts, whose instincts are under more control, avoid this giveaway and behave in a very lifelike manner, enabling them to drain the constitution (and hence l i t e energy) of a victim while engaging him in conversation or merely being near him. It is a strange fact that most Ghosts seem not to realize that they are dead; often, if they can be convinced of their true nature, they will dissipate and go forth to their appointed rest. (Note that Elves do not have Ghosts, since their spirits always know where to go. It is notable that Elves do not fear Ghosts, perhaps for this reason). However, Ghosts are remarkably impervious to reason on this score (How would you. Reader, react if someone insisted that you were dead?), and would-be persuaders are well-warned that there is no way that the Ghost can avoid draining their life-energy, any more than they themselves can avoid having their hearts beat. Anyone near enough to a Ghost to speak to it is near enough to be drained. Some Ghosts are bound to a place or object that was very important to them in life or that figured strongly in their deaths: a sentry killed while guarding a crucial post, for instance, whose spirit remains "on duty" long after the fortress that he guarded has fallen to ruins; the murder victim haunting the gold that she was killed for; the child plague victim still holding fast to the wooden doll that comforted its last hours.

aspect.en: Burrowing desert dragons — one of the two kinds of Were-worm — that move unseen beneath the sands of arid and desert lands. Toward travellers: a hidden horror of the dunes, erupting from below to seize prey crossing its waste.

lore.en: Sand Drakes are one of the two breeds of Were-worm, burrowing Dragons of arid and desert lands.

aspect.en: Tall, broad-crowned trees of moist river-vales, their arching branches forming shaded avenues along banks and field-edges, deep roots binding the soil. Toward travellers: harmless; welcome shade along the watercourses.

lore.en: Elms are tall, broad-crowned trees common in moist river-vales such as the Anduin Vales. Their arching branches form shaded avenues along banks and field-edges, and their deep roots help bind alluvial soils.

aspect.en: Pale, cold-hardened trolls of the northern wastes and high snows, white as the drifts they hunt in and among the few trolls that brave the daylight of the polar lands. Toward travellers: a deadly hunter of the frozen North that the dawn does not drive off.

lore.en: Pale, cold-hardened Trolls of the northern wastes and high snows, ranging Forochel and the frozen reaches. White as the drifts they hunt in and thick-hided against the cold, they are among the few Trolls that brave the daylight of the polar lands.

aspect.en: A solitary, grey-dappled cat of the high cold peaks, superbly suited to crag and snow — a patient stalker of goats and sheep among the heights, shy of Men and rarely seen low. Toward travellers: shuns people; a danger only to one who surprises it or strays into its high hunting-ground.

lore.en: A solitary, grey-dappled cat of the high cold peaks, superbly suited to crag and snow. A patient stalker of goats and sheep among the heights, shy of Men and rarely seen in the lowlands.

aspect.en: An inhabited place — a village, steading, herders' camp or wayside hamlet — where folk dwell and travellers may find shelter, supplies and news. Toward travellers: a likely refuge; the welcome depends on who lives there and how the times sit.

lore.en: An inhabited place — a village, steading, herders' camp or wayside hamlet where folk dwell and travellers may find shelter, supplies and news. The welcome depends on who lives there and how the times sit.

aspect.en: Small dragon-kin — horrible winged monsters bred up from winged-drakes by Sauron to serve as flying steeds for the Nazgûl. Toward travellers: a terror of the sky; their shadow and shriek alone bring dread, and they hunt at their riders' command.

lore.en: Small, Dragon-related monsters, Fell Beasts are horrible and terrifying creatures bred from Winged-drakes. Sauron found them roosting in the remote highlands of the North and refined them in order to produce swift, aerial steeds for his Nazgûl.

aspect.en: A tiny scarlet songbird with an extremely high, sweet chirp — one of the most beloved birds of lost Númenor, now all but vanished and known mostly from old verse and art, though a few may yet survive (rumour gives Radagast a pair). Toward travellers: harmless and wondrous, a vanishingly rare jewel of a bird and a marvel to glimpse.

lore.en: The Kirinki is a tiny scarlet bird with an extremely high chirp that was one of the most beloved songbirds of Numenor. After the Downfall in S.A. 3319, knowledge of these wondrous singers became confined to verse, illustrations in books, and works of art depicting the little creatures. Some of the Faithful who escaped from Numenor, however, brought their pet Kirinkir with them. Whether any survived or thrived is another matter, although there have been rumors that Radagast the Brown has a pair at his home at Rhosgobel (near the southwestern eaves of Mirkwood).

aspect.en: Mixed herds of grazing beasts — deer, wild cattle, antelope and the like — moving together across plain and meadow, ever-wary and hard to approach. Toward travellers: harmless, but where they gather, predators follow.

lore.en: Mixed herds of grazing beasts — deer, wild cattle, antelope and the like — moving together across plain and meadow. Their numbers and constant wariness make them hard to approach, and they draw predators wherever they gather.

aspect.en: Men of the southern lands — Haradrim and their neighbours, dark-haired and richly or strangely arrayed — met as traders, envoys, mercenaries or soldiers far north of home, often eyed with mistrust in the West. Toward travellers: their intent varies by errand and allegiance; treated with suspicion in northern lands, friend or foe by circumstance.

lore.en: Men of the southern lands — Haradrim and their neighbours, dark-haired and richly or strangely arrayed — met as traders, envoys, mercenaries or soldiers far north of their homes, and often eyed with mistrust in the lands of the West.

aspect.en: An immense elk of the northern wilds, far larger than the common kind, with a towering spread of antlers — rare and magnificent, a great bull fearing few beasts. Toward travellers: leaves people be, but a cornered or rutting bull can gore or trample, and little can stop it.

lore.en: An immense elk of the northern wilds, far larger than the common kind, with a towering spread of antlers. Rare and magnificent, a great bull fears few beasts and can gore or trample any that corner it.

aspect.en: A broad label for the common country folk of Eriador and Gondor — of mixed blood, plainly dressed, working farm, pasture and trade. Toward travellers: ordinary working people whose welcome to strangers ranges from kindly to wary with the times.

lore.en: This is a generalized label for the rural folk of Eriador and Gondor, the Common Men of northwestern Middle-earth. These folk contain varying degrees of Harnadan, Dunlending, Northman, and Dúnadan blood. Physical Character: All types, but normally medium. Males average 160 pounds, women 125 pounds. Variations of fair to tan or olive skin. All colors of hair and eyes. Average endurance. Males average 5'10", women 5'4". Lifespan: Moderate, averaging 60-80 years. Practical wool and linen garb, including cloaks, boots, etc. Tunics are worn in warmer areas; shirts and pants or leggings are worn in cooler locales. Rural folk are mostly farmers and herders, with little contact with areas outside their village or region. Rural folk are suspicious of most outsiders, and might be in awe of some. They hate no race, aside from the Orcs and Wargs.

aspect.en: Gondorian rangers who wage a hidden war in Ithilien — stealthy raiders who ambush Sauron's troops from cover and melt back into the wild. Toward travellers: watchful and unseen until they choose; allies to the free, but they challenge strangers in their secret country.

lore.en: Gondorian rangers who launch stealth raids against Sauron's forces.

aspect.en: A mine or quarry cut into hill and rock — galleries, shafts, spoil-heaps and stone-faces, worked or long abandoned — a source of metal and stone, and of cave-ins, foul air and whatever has crept into empty workings. Toward travellers: shelter or salvage, but unstable ground and bad air make old workings treacherous.

lore.en: A mine or quarry cut into hill and rock — galleries, shafts, spoil-heaps and stone-faces, worked or long abandoned. A source of metal and stone, and of cave-ins, foul air and whatever has crept into the empty workings.

aspect.en: A tiny, bright-red bat with a long probing tongue, haunting the deeps of Moria — it licks insects from crevices, but also coats its tongue with a potent nerve-poison to paralyse larger prey, then shreds them with needle teeth; named for its eerie shrieking cry. Toward travellers: small but venomous, a swarming peril in the dark places it haunts.

lore.en: The Vault Shrike is a tiny, bright red Bat with a long nose and tongue with which it pokes into holes and crevices for insects to eat. It also secretes from its tongue a highly toxic nerve poison that enables it to deal with larger prey. These Vault Shrikes paralyze or kill by means of the poison. It then rips its victims to shreds with its tiny sharp teeth. The Vault Shrike diet is further enhanced by its ability to catch small frogs in an ironically froglike manner: by snatching them in midleap with that long tongue. Vault Shrikes get their name from their unnerving, shrieking cry. They are only found in Moria and the caverns of the Misty Mountains.

aspect.en: Singers and lore-keepers of the Dunlending clans, carrying genealogies, feuds and grievances in memorized verse; welcome at any hearth, their praise or mockery can make or unmake a man among the clans. Toward travellers: protected by custom and no fighters, but a powerful voice in the clans — and a keen source of local news and feud.

lore.en: Singers and lore-keepers of the Dunlending clans, carrying the genealogies, feuds and grievances of their people in memorized verse. Welcome at any hearth, a bard's praise or mockery can make or unmake a man's standing among the clans.

aspect.en: Cunning scavenging wild dogs of arid and desert country, hunting and scavenging in packs. Toward travellers: little threat to the able, but bold around carrion and camps, and ever watchful for weakness.

lore.en: Scavenging canines found in arid and desert regions, known for their cunning.

aspect.en: Semi-nomadic horse-people — superb riders, herders and hunters who follow their flocks between seasonal pastures. Proud and honour-bound, though split into many independent groups. Toward travellers: wary but hospitable to those who show respect; quick to take offence at insult or trespass.

lore.en: Superb equestrian warriors, semi-nomadic herders, and hunters who move between seasonal pastures and maintain a disunified but highly honorable society.

aspect.en: A large, flat, black sting-ray — diamond-shaped with broad wing-like fins — that glides along the coastal sea-bed and buries itself in sand. Its whip-like tail bears sharp venomous barbs, and its fin-tips can deliver a stunning shock. Toward travellers: a hidden danger to anyone wading or swimming shallow coastal waters.

lore.en: The Shadowhorn, or "Morchaithras" (pl. "Merchaithrais" or "Morchaithrais"), is a large, flat, black Ray equipped with a long, whiplike tail. Its tail is studded with short but exceptionally sharp barbs that deliver knifelike cuts and inject victims with a powerful (3rd lvl) muscle venom. The Ray expanded pectoral fins form triangular wings that extend along its head and trunk, giving the fish a diamond shape. The tips of these wings are equipped with electricity-producing organs that can stun or immobilize a swimmer. Merchaithrais prefer to swim along the bottom of the coastal shelf, burrowing themselves in the sand near shoals in order to await their prey. While swimming, they flap their pectoral fins and move gracefully and quickly through the water, as if flying.

aspect.en: A rare, cannibalistic undead spirit that haunts dark swamps, graveyards and ruins by night. Looks almost human but hunched and wrong, with clammy greenish-brown skin and damp, filthy rags; it moves in silence and kills with strangling hands or jagged rusty blades, craving blood and coveting gold. Toward travellers: a lurking predator that stalks and ambushes the isolated, and never parleys.

lore.en: hnwmskt-FM,CDHJP,EQRY-8; 6-11 ft Mewlips are an evil, semi-legendary race of exceedingly rare, cannibalistic spirits. These shadowy spirits exist to drink blood, which they need almost as much as other undead need life-energy. Denizens of graveyards, ruins, and other pleasant sites, they are often found surprisingly near inhabited areas, especially if they have not found much sustenance farther afield lately. Mewlips are rare even for Undead. Fond of the most noisome and darkest swamps and marshes, they have a silent tread and strangling hands, although they typically use jagged weapons of rusty steel or stone. They are deceptively human in appearance: however, their backs are horribly hunched and their skin shines with a clammy, greenish-brown palor. Even their ragged clothing is moist and foul. Mewlips feed on most anything and they covet shiny objects, especially things of gold. It is said that such items remind them of uncursed life, of the nature of beingsnot in the thrall of Darkness.

aspect.en: The tallest, fairest and fewest hobbits, the most Man-like and the boldest — woodland folk of the cool north, the readiest of hobbits to mingle with the Big People and to wander. Toward travellers: adventurous and relatively open for hobbits, friendly and curious about outsiders.

lore.en: The Fallohides are the tallest and average between 3 and 4 feet in height. They have fair skin and, of all the groups, resemble Men the most. Their numbers are small, however, and some observers have confused them with nearby mannish groups. Fallohides enjoy the woodlands found in cool northern climes. Some have begun relying on surface dwellings of wood, brick, or stone. Fallohides are the most prone to mingle with Big People. Harfoots and Fallohides trace their lines through either the male or female. Those Hobbits who dare venture away from home are assumed to be extraordinary, and therefore get five background points.

aspect.en: Mixed folk of Bree — Men of various stocks and hobbits together — living in and around a hedged, trench-ringed village at a great crossroads, once a busy trade-town and now somewhat faded. Toward travellers: used to strangers and the road; generally welcoming but cautious, with a homely, gossipy good sense.

lore.en: Mixed folk of Bree and its environs, including men of various stocks and hobbits, living in and around a trenched, hedged village at the junction of the Greenway and Great East Road, once a vibrant trade-town but fading by T.A. 1640.[file:25]

aspect.en: The wild horses of the plains — good mounts but hard to break, much used by Easterlings and now herded in Rohan; some live in the marshes, untroubled by swimming. Toward travellers: skittish free-roaming horses, harmless, and prized if one can catch and tame them.

lore.en: The Wild Horse, or Horse of the Plains (S. "Rechelaid"), make good mounts, although they are hard to break. Much used by Easterlings, they are now herded in Calenardhon (Rohan). A few may be found in the marshes, for they do not mind swimming.

aspect.en: The largest bear in Middle-earth — a vast, slow, dim brute of the southern lands near Umbar, up to 4,000 lbs, that digs huge tunnel networks with its claws, even through rock, and is hard to kill thanks to its bulk and thick skull. Toward travellers: slow and incurious, but near-unstoppable if roused.

lore.en: Dark-brown Sloth Bear (Q. Meglituika), native to northwestern Harad and especially prevalent around Umbar, the largest bear in Middle-earth at 2,500-4,000 lbs. A huge, slow, stupid beast like a cross between a bear and a rainforest sloth, it uses formidable claws to dig vast tunnel networks, even through crumbling rock, large enough for Men to live in. Little-fearing and hard to kill thanks to its bulk and unusually thick skull, it eats whatever it can claw in the mass it needs to sustain itself.

aspect.en: Wild, dim-witted giants of the high mountains, here the rock-throwing stone-giants of the Misty Mountains — playful in their way, favouring cold desolate heights, eating huge quantities of meat and running down or stoning their prey. Toward travellers: a deadly hazard of the high passes; their hurled boulders and careless games can crush a party even without malice.

lore.en: Wild, playful, dim-witted Giants (Q. "Norsar") of the alpine regions, here the rock-throwing stone-giants of the Misty Mountains; they favour cool, desolate heights, eat great quantities of meat, and run down or stone their prey.

aspect.en: Big, shaggy grey apes of the southwestern forests — up to five feet and three hundred pounds, with long arms and powerful hands for swinging through trees but short, weak legs that make them awkward on the ground. Toward travellers: keep to the canopy and shun people; powerful and dangerous if threatened, but no hunter of men.

lore.en: Grey, shaggy-haired, heavily-built apes (P. "Cijuvu Niavi", S. "Peredrugwath") that live alone, in pairs or in small family groups in the forests of Pel in southwestern Middle-earth. They stand up to 5 ft tall and weigh up to 300 lbs; long arms reach the ankles when erect, and broad opposable-digited hands plus great upper-body strength let them swing tree to tree with ease. Their short, weak legs make for an awkward, halting gait on the jungle floor, whether upright or on all fours.

aspect.en: Firebeards and Broadbeams of the Blue Mountains, dwelling in the fourteen holds of their valley and keeping vigorous traditions of smithing and weapon-craft. Toward travellers: skilled, proud mountain-Dwarves; reserved with outsiders but renowned for their work and fair in trade.

lore.en: Firebeards and Broadbeams of the Blue Mountains, living in the fourteen holds of Nan-i-Naugrim; they maintain active smithing traditions and weapon-crafting at Merlost.

aspect.en: A small, hardy, pugnacious roe-like deer that browses by night; only the stags fight, skittish and aggressive in spring, using mail-piercing horns and marking territory by scratching bark — a sign the Dúnadan Rangers have learned to imitate to hide their own trail-marks. Toward travellers: shy but feisty; a startled stag can lash out, and its bark-scratches may not be what they seem.

lore.en: Akin to the Roe Deer (Fiara) of Eriador, the Dappled Deer is small, hardy, and pugnacious. Only the stags fight, but they are exceptionally skiddish and aggressive, especially in Spring. They usually employ their tough horns, which can effectively penetrate mail. Nocturnal creatures, Dappled Deer browse for food at night. They feed on shrubs and broad-leafed trees. During breeding season, males mark their territory by scratching the bark off trees. Note: The Dúnadan Rangers have frequently used this trait to their advantage by disguising their own trail markings as Deer scratches; only the Rangers understand the subtle differences.

aspect.en: A six-foot plains snake with a thick triangular head and a dark diamond pattern on cream, hunting rodents and birds by stealth in the tall grass. Quick to anger, it stands and fights rather than flees, and its venom is highly toxic. Toward travellers: dangerous if disturbed in the grass — it defends itself fiercely rather than fleeing.

lore.en: The Plains Snake (Si. "Nathair"; pl. "Nethairin") is roughly six feet long. It has a thick triangular head and a cream-colored body overlaid with a dark diamond pattern. Hiding in shallow burrows and hunting amidst the tall grass of the steppes or plains, the serpent is a quiet creature that relies on stealth and patience to defeat its foes. Rodents, birds, and small lizards make up its diet. Although ostensibly cunning, the Nathair angers easily and will vigorously defend itself rather than flee, even in a fruitless confrontation. Its venom is rather toxic (level 6); symptoms include swelling, weak pulse, shock, and wide discolorations.

aspect.en: The rank-and-file orc — squat and heavy with thick hides, short legs, long arms and grotesque fanged faces, descended from Elves twisted by Morgoth; tireless, cruel and culturally bent toward darkness. Toward travellers: hostile and dangerous, especially in numbers and after dark — they hunt, rob and kill.

lore.en: These hideous creatures are members of a race descended from Elves who were twisted and perverted by Morgoth during the First Age. Although they are not inherently evil, they are culturally and mentally predisposed toward Darkness. Physical Character: Heavy, with thick hides, short legs, and long, thin arms. They have grotesque, fanged faces and random hair growth. Black or grey hair, black or reddish-brown eyes, and deep grey or black hides. Tremendous endurance. Ores can travel for 2 days without rest. Alternatively, they can run for up to 12 hours without stopping. 3-5 feet. Indefinite lifespan; certainly hundreds of years, but the nature of their warlike life permits few to live past the age of 50. +30 bonus versus heat/fire attacks. Orcs sleep during daylight hours, although they need rest only once every 3 days. In most darkness Orcs can see like Elves, and in absolute darkness they can see 10'. Bred as laborers and warriors, Orcs respect power and terror above all things. They join and cooperate in substantial groups only when led by a "focused will", some overwhelmingly strong individual. Across the lands they are met in different masters' service: as Sauron's soldiery in Mordor and Dol Guldur, as the goblins of the Misty Mountains and Gundabad under their own chiefs, and as the war-bands of Angmar and the cold North.

aspect.en: A man-eating water-beast like a giant black frog that lurks in dark pools, dragging prey under to drown or swallowing it whole by unhinging its jaw; its huge eyes can hypnotise and bewilder a victim. Toward travellers: a hidden killer of dark waters whose hypnotic gaze and sudden lunge make pools and meres treacherous.

lore.en: Aquatic carnivore and relative of the Giant Hellbender, resembling a giant black frog and preferring the flesh of people. It lurks in dark pools, dragging prey underwater to drown or swallowing it whole by dislocating its jaw like a snake; its huge eyes can hypnotise and distract its victims (5th-level RR).

aspect.en: A wild goat of the high crags, agile and sure-footed where no predator can follow, the rams bearing heavy curved horns and the herds keeping to the heights. Toward travellers: harmless; a sure-footed sight on cliffs far above the road.

lore.en: A wild goat of the high crags, agile and sure-footed on cliffs that would daunt any predator. The rams bear heavy curved horns, and the herds keep to heights where few hunters can follow.

aspect.en: Immensely long-lived, reclusive giants of the high peaks who shun other peoples and keep to the heights. Toward travellers: usually avoid all contact, but catastrophic if angered or disturbed in their mountains.

lore.en: Extremely long-lived, reclusive beings of immense size who dwell in the high peaks and avoid contact with other races.

aspect.en: An Elf making the last journey west to the Grey Havens to take ship into the Undying Lands — passing quietly through Lindon, alone or in small companies, thoughts already on the sea and the weariness of ages plain upon them. Toward travellers: gentle and sorrowful, wholly turned westward; courteous but already half-departed from the world.

lore.en: An Elf making the last journey west, bound for the Grey Havens to take ship into the Undying Lands. Such pilgrims pass quietly through Lindon, alone or in small companies, their thoughts already half upon the sea and the long weariness of the Ages plain upon them.

aspect.en: Animated guardian constructs that stand like plain iron pillars until disturbed, then move as deadly iron man-shapes; if destroyed they slowly reconstitute over decades of undisturbed rest. Toward travellers: a hidden sentinel — what seems a mere pillar may wake and kill.

lore.en: Pukel-creatures that look like iron pillars until disturbed, when they become deadly iron manlike forms; like other Pukel they can reconstitute themselves, though this takes at least 50 years of undisturbed repose.

aspect.en: Rare white, shaggy-furred elephants of the frozen North — huge, cold-adapted behemoths, seldom tamed; the northern tribes either worship or hunt them. Toward travellers: peaceable grazers unless threatened, when their sheer bulk makes them deadly.

lore.en: The rare white, long-haired Losandamunda (Q. "Snow Elephant") of the Far North is related to the Andamunda of southern Endor. These furry behemoths, though, are rarely domesticated. Instead, they are worshipped (notably by the Uax, but also by the Myri and Angcla tribes) or hunted (notably by the eastern Lossoth and Lotan).

aspect.en: Hobbits living rough at the edges of settled country — in the eaves of old forests, hedges and lonely downs — warier and more weather-hardened than their kin, trusting no big folk and vanishing into bracken at the first alarm. Toward travellers: shy and elusive and no threat, gone from sight before you know they were there.

lore.en: Hobbits living rough and un-Shirelike at the edges of settled country — in the eaves of the Old Forest, the Bree-land hedges and the lonely downs. Warier and more weather-hardened than their kin, they trust no big folk and vanish into bracken and burrow at the first sign of trouble.

aspect.en: The Green-elves of Ossiriand — a reclusive woodland Elf-folk of the Elder Days, deeply bound to forest and river. Toward travellers: secretive and seldom seen, keeping to their woods; wary of strangers but not hostile without cause.

lore.en: Green-elves of Ossiriand.

aspect.en: A tall, foul-scented shrub up to twelve feet, with huge white trumpet-flowers that puff pollen explosively; the pollen causes nausea and temporary blindness, and its black seeds are potent psychoactive poisons — one intoxicates, several can kill (Elves are said to be immune). Toward travellers: dangerous to brush against or harvest carelessly — its pollen blinds and its seeds poison.

lore.en: A tall, foul-scented shrub up to twelve feet in height, with huge white trumpet-flowers that shed pollen explosively. The pollen can cause nausea and temporary blindness; the black seeds are potent psychoactive poisons—one intoxicates, several can be fatal to most races, though Elves are said to be immune.

aspect.en: A patrol of soldiery from the stronghold of Cultirith, warding its district against raiders and brigands, keeping the roads and challenging strangers in their lord's lands. Toward travellers: lawful men-at-arms; no threat to the honest, but they will stop and question those who pass.

lore.en: A patrol of soldiery based at the stronghold of Cultirith, warding its district against raiders and brigands, keeping the local roads and challenging strangers passing through their lord's lands.

aspect.en: A snow-people of the Bay of Forochel who live on drifting icebergs and frozen shores, hunting whales, seals and walrus — short, stocky, fair-haired and astonishingly cold-hardy, though many are lost to the sea. Toward travellers: hardy, isolated ice-hunters, reserved with outsiders but not hostile.

lore.en: Ystvät Talven who dwell on moving icebergs and along the Bay of Forochel's shores, hunting whales, seals and walruses; they are stocky, short, fair-haired and remarkably resistant to cold and immersion, but suffer high mortality from the hazards of the sea.[file:39]

aspect.en: The slender, fire-breathing winged dragons descended from cold-drakes — the greatest worms of the North, Smaug among them, lairing in the Grey Mountains and the Lonely Mountain. Toward travellers: the most terrible of dragons; fire, cunning and a deadly voice make any one a doom.

lore.en: Fire-drakes (Q. "Uruloki") are the slender, fire-breathing winged Dragons descended from true Cold-drakes; the greatest Worms of the North (including Smaug) belong to this family and lair in the Grey Mountains and Lonely Mountain.

aspect.en: A rare meeting with hobbits beyond their usual haunts — small, soft-spoken folk easily overlooked, usually a family or two strayed from the settled lands. Toward travellers: shy of big folk and quick to slip from sight, wanting little more than to be left to their meals and pipes.

lore.en: A rare meeting with Hobbits beyond their usual haunts — small, soft-spoken folk easily overlooked, generally a family or two strayed from the settled lands of the Shire, Bree or Dunland. Shy of big folk and quick to slip from sight, they want little more than to be left to their meals and pipes.

aspect.en: A wildfire racing across dry grassland or scrub, wind-driven and faster than a galloping horse, that can trap herds and travellers in the open — and the smoke alone can choke or blind. Toward travellers: a swift, deadly danger of dry plains; flee crosswind, never ahead of it.

lore.en: A wildfire racing across dry grassland or scrub, wind-driven and faster than a running horse. It can trap herds and travellers in the open, and the smoke alone can choke or blind.

aspect.en: A cave-dwelling raptor fully adapted to lightless depths, hunting by echo-location, scent and night-sight; pale and near-colourless, with beak and talons hard enough to pierce most armour. Toward travellers: an unexpected, dangerous predator to meet underground, striking from the dark.

lore.en: The Echo Hawk is a large subterranean bird and a menace that few would expect to meet underground in a cave. It is a raptor that has totally adapted to life in a lightless environment, utilizing both infravision and echo-location for its hunting. The echo Hawk nostrils are unusually large, giving it a keenness of scent quite rare in a bird. Its beak and talons are large, hard, and sharp, so much so that the Echo Hawk can pierce through most types of armor. As is usual with the raptors, the female Hawk is larger than the male. Otherwise the sexes are similar, with dull white feathers, colorless skin, and beaks and talons like translucent horn.

aspect.en: A site of the mingled folk of Eriador — a village, mill, shrine or roadside ruin of the ordinary Men between the mountains, humble and well-worn. Toward travellers: the stuff of everyday life rather than legend, a likely place for food, rest or simple news.

lore.en: A site of the mingled folk of Eriador — a village, mill, shrine or roadside ruin of the ordinary Men of the lands between the mountains. Humble and well-worn, the stuff of everyday life rather than legend.

aspect.en: A solitary wading bird of the northern deltas — a kind of heron known for a strange, mournful, resonant cry. A slow, patient, cunning hunter of fish, snakes and crayfish that winters on temperate coasts. Toward travellers: harmless; its eerie call carries far across the marsh at dusk.

lore.en: A wading and fishing bird found in the deltas of northwestern Endor, the Bittern, or Northern Heron, is known for its strange resonant, mournful cry. It is a slow, cunning, deliberate hunter that feeds on snakes, crustaceans, and fish. Bitterns migrate, spending their winters in the wetlands along the temperate seacoasts and their summers in the lakes and deltas of the North.

aspect.en: The wild and half-tame cats of farm, town and field — small hunters of mice, rats and birds, kept by folk as mousers or gone feral about settlements and ruins. Toward travellers: harmless and aloof; a barn-cat by the hearth, or a wary shape slipping through a ruin.

lore.en: A handsome, long-legged hunter of the plains of Calenardhon, the Grass Cat is now quite rare. Men have killed or domesticated most of its prey and actively hunt the Cats for fear of losing Sheep, Goats, or Kine. A Grass Cat has a thick, short, buff-colored fur that easily absorbs grass pollen in the summer months, giving it an eerie and unnatural yellow-green coloration. The Cat hunts by leaping upon the backs of its prey, digging its long claws into the victim's throat and neck. Even if its victim is not killed by the severing of some vital vein or nerve, it will run itself into a stupor or even to death. There have been cases of Grass Cats killing Men in this same manner. When in heat, courting, or fighting. Grass Cats give off highpitched, raucous shrieks that are terrifying to hear, especially during the long winter nights.

aspect.en: Great tawny cats of the warm southern plains and scrub, hunting deer, wild cattle and the herds of Men by ambush and stealth — and a hungry pride will not shrink from a lone traveller. Toward travellers: a serious danger in their country, above all to the solitary and after dark.

lore.en: Great tawny cats of the warmer plains and scrublands of the South, hunting deer, wild cattle and the herds of Men. They hunt by ambush and stealth, and a hungry pride will not shrink from a lone traveller.

aspect.en: A herding-and-hunting sub-folk of the far north, working inland herds across the cold uplands and dealing with both the snow-peoples and Angmar's frontier forces. Toward travellers: hardy northern herders, wary and self-contained on a bleak, contested frontier.

lore.en: A land-focused Ystvät Talven sub-culture relying heavily on herd management and inland hunting, occupying central Talath Uichel and interacting with both Lossoth and Angmar's frontier forces.[file:39]

aspect.en: The largest of all mussels — a giant black-shelled bivalve of the eastern shores, prized for its huge, reputedly enchanted pearls; it squirts a foul acidic ink that stuns large prey and dissolves flesh. Toward travellers: no hunter, but its acidic spray and the lure of its great pearls make harvesting it perilous.

lore.en: Largest member of the mussel family, the Mulkana is a giant, hard-shelled bivalve with a black shell that protects its soft, white body. This molusk is related to the Giant Clam, although it is larger, quicker, and has a long, vaguely oval, shell. It secretes a foul, acidic, ink (3rd lvl) which stuns larger prey, kills smaller victims, and slowly eats away skin. Found off the eastern shores of Endor, Mulkanar are hunted for their huge (and reputedly enchanted) pearls. At least one of these precious jewels, the priceless Womaw Moon, exceeds six inches in diameter. Legend proclaims that the larger of these pearls serve as Seeing-stones, although none is as powerful as a Numenorean Palantir.

aspect.en: One of the largest of the rabbit kind, dwelling in the year-round snows of the high Misty Mountains, its silvery-white pelt prized for warmth and perfect for camouflage. A larger, fiercer kind is rumoured near high cave-mouths, said to show cruel cunning and to frenzy when provoked. Toward travellers: the common kind is harmless game; the rumoured greater sort is a half-legendary terror of the heights.

lore.en: The snow hare is one of the largest members of the rabbit family. It inhabits the upper elevations of the Misty Mountains where there is snow cover year round. The animal's silvery white pelt, prized for its warmth, provides excellent camouflage for the furry mountain denizen. A larger, more fearsome variety of the snow hare has been rumored to exist lurking close to the opening of high mountain caves. These creatures seem to exhibit a cruel intelligence and are rumored to frenzy upon provocation. This description was given by a traveller after returning half-crazed from the mountains: "It had huge ... well I mean gigantic ... just big teeth."

aspect.en: A large daylight-flying bat of coastal wetlands and eastern marshes — keen-eyed and long-snouted, hunting rodents and biting wild berries. Widely held to be an omen of evil magic. Toward travellers: harmless in itself, though feared and ill-regarded wherever it appears.

lore.en: A variety of large bat, the Flying Fox makes its home amid brambles or in the tops of dense, partially-submerged trees of the coastal wetlands. They are most common in the marshes and scrublands of the East, although a few smaller varieties make their homes in Rhun and one group lives in southern Eriador. Unlike most bats, the Flying Fox thrives in daylight, having good eyesight and a refined sense of smell. Using its long snout, it hunts rodents in the scrub and bites wild berries which might elude its more flatfaced cousins. The Flying Fox is considered synonymous with evil magic in many areas of eastern Middle-earth.

aspect.en: The small creatures of field, hedge and burrow — hares, foxes, squirrels, weasels, mice and the like. Toward travellers: seldom any threat; the everyday life of the land, and the prey larger hunters depend on.

lore.en: The small creatures of field, hedge and burrow — hares, foxes, squirrels, weasels, mice and the like. Seldom a threat, they are the everyday life of the land and the prey on which larger hunters depend.

aspect.en: Frogs, toads and other amphibians of pond, marsh and damp wood — loud in the breeding season and harmless to all but insects, though some marsh-toads carry an acrid skin-poison that sickens any beast that mouths them. Toward travellers: harmless, a danger only to a dog or beast foolish enough to bite one.

lore.en: Frogs, toads and other amphibians of pond, marsh and damp wood, loud in the breeding season and harmless to all but insects. Some marsh-toads carry an acrid skin-poison that sickens any beast foolish enough to mouth them.

aspect.en: The big, shaggy herding-dogs favoured by shepherds across Middle-earth — hardy, loyal, intelligent and fierce, a single collared hound a match for two or three wolves, also used by the Dúnedain for hunting and guarding. Toward travellers: friendly to their masters and guests, but formidable guardians that will face down a wolf or a thief.

lore.en: Popular among shepherds throughout Middle-earth, the favourite being the large, short-muzzled, long-haired Sheep Hound (Q. Huoton). It endures harsh weather and performs even when fatigued, and its size, stealth and speed ward off predators; very loyal, intelligent and fierce, a collared hound is a match for two or three Wolves. The Dunedain also use them for hunting and as guard dogs, though war-dog experiments failed; a smaller breed is kept as a pet for women and children.

aspect.en: A sudden slide of snow or rock down a steep slope, set off by thaw, storm or even a careless shout, that can bury a party in moments — worst in the high passes in spring and after heavy snow. Toward travellers: a swift, smothering killer of the mountains; move quietly and choose the hour.

lore.en: A sudden slide of snow or rock down a steep slope, triggered by thaw, storm or a careless noise, that can bury a party in moments. The high passes are most treacherous in spring and after heavy snow.

aspect.en: Great hunting eagles of mountain and moor — sharp-eyed takers of hare, fowl and lamb, larger and prouder than other raptors, nesting among the high crags. Toward travellers: little threat to people, a majestic sight wheeling over the heights.

lore.en: Great hunting eagles of mountain and moor, sharp-eyed takers of hare, fowl and lamb. Larger and prouder than other raptors, they nest among high crags and are seldom troubled by any beast of the lowlands.

aspect.en: Strong, imposing Men of Dúnedain blood descended from the Númenoreans who turned from the Valar to dark idols and the service of Sauron — proud, long-lived and steeped in old enmity for the Faithful. Toward travellers: arrogant and dangerous enemies of the free peoples, often allied with the Shadow.

lore.en: The term "Black Númenorean" (S. "Mornúmenedain") is used to describe Men of Dúnedain stock who are descended from the "Unfaithful" Númenorean colonists and conquerers who came to Middle-earth during the middle and late Second Age. These Unfaithful had broken with the Valar and Elves who had bequeathed them the island kingdom of Númenor at the beginning of the Second Age, and many worshipped their own idols or paid homage to the Dark Lord Sauron. Physical Character: Strong and imposing, with angular features. Men average 225 pounds, women 150 pounds. After long years in the hot South, the Black Númenoreans have tanned, grey-brown skin, and black hair. Their piercing eyes are various shades of grey. Considerable endurance. Men average 6'4", women 5'10". Lifespan: 90-175 years. +25 to Sailing maneuvers. +10 to melee Offensive Bonuses, -10 to Defensive Bonus. Black and gold are their favored colors. They wear rich clothing made of dyed silk and cotton. Their societies are well-ordered and ruled by force of personality, backed by harsh law. Dictators and oligarchs hold sway over the people.

aspect.en: A tiny gliding tree-frog of southeastern rainforest — bright red and blue, with skin-flaps that let it sail between trees — and among the deadliest creatures of those woods, its back-spines injecting a lethal poison at a touch. Toward travellers: small and beautiful but lethal, never to be handled.

lore.en: An arboreal creature, the Trusa (P. "Leaf Frog"; pl. "Trusavi") is adapted for gliding from tree to tree. It has a broad head, a long slim body, and elongated limbs with webbed feet. Flaps of skin fringe the forelimbs and heels, permitting the creature to extend its body and create a bizarre but effective set of "wings." This bright red and blue frog grows no larger than about 3 inches in length, but it is among the deadliest animals in the humid woodlands of southeastern Middle-earth. If touched, the spines on the back of the Trusa will inject a strong (lvl 4) poison which acts in 1-10 rds. A victim who fails his RR by 21 or more dies, while one who fails by 11-20 becomes blind and falls into a coma; a RR failure of 01-10 leaves the victim blind in 1-2 eyes.

aspect.en: Lady of Lórien — a great Noldorin princess, Ring-bearer, and one of the wisest and most far-seeing of Elves, whose foresight and power guard her realm against the Shadow. Toward travellers: regal, ancient and searching; gracious to the worthy who reach her wood, but her gaze reads the heart.

lore.en: Lady of Lórien, a Noldorin princess and Ring-bearer, whose wisdom and foresight shape the realm's defenses and long-term stance against Sauron.

aspect.en: The many healing herbs of the Anduin Vales — simples to ease fever, restore strength, close wounds or clear the lungs — known to Woodmen, Beornings and wandering healers along streams, glades and sunlit hills. Toward travellers: harmless and valuable, a boon to anyone who knows where to look.

lore.en: This term covers the many healing herbs found in the Anduin Vales: simples that ease fever, restore strength, close wounds or clear the lungs. Woodmen, Beornings and wandering healers know where to find such plants along stream-banks, in forest glades and on sunlit hills.

aspect.en: Durin's Folk of the Lonely Mountain, using its caverns as halls, mines and treasure-vaults and bound tightly to the trade of the River Running. Toward travellers: proud, industrious and rich, wary of strangers but fair to honest dealers and staunch in alliance.

lore.en: A community of Durin's Folk dwelling in the Lonely Mountain, a great isolated peak north of Long Lake, using its caverns as halls, mines and treasure vaults; tightly connected to trade along the River Running.

aspect.en: Marsh-folk who cut reed for thatch and dig peat for fuel, working the bogs by flat-bottomed boat — poor and little regarded, but knowing the safe paths through mires that swallow the unwary. Toward travellers: humble fen-folk and a precious guide through treacherous marsh for those who treat them kindly.

lore.en: Marsh-folk who cut reed for thatch and dig peat for fuel from the bogs and fens, working the wetlands by flat-bottomed boat. Poor and little regarded, they know the safe paths through mires that swallow the unwary.

aspect.en: The mixed Elf-folk of Rivendell — Noldor lords and craftsmen, Sindar, and many Silvan Elves who tend its grounds and patrols — tall, ageless and hardy, gathered in willing service around the Lord of the House. Toward travellers: gracious hosts within their hidden valley, giving rest, healing and counsel to the worthy, and ready to defend it at need.

lore.en: Rivendell is home to a mixed Elven population: Noldor lords and craftsmen, Sindar and numerous Silvan Elves who tend the grounds, agriculture and patrols.[file:244] Elves are tall, ageless, disease-immune, highly resistant to heat and cold, and in Rivendell they live in a hierarchical but willing social structure centred on Elrond as Lord of the House, with Silvan Elves often delighting in service and colourful dress, Sindar and Noldor taking leadership and craft roles, and nearly all residents trained to aid in defence when needed.[file:244]

aspect.en: A train of orcs hauling supplies, plunder or slaves across the Enemy's lands, plodding under whip and guard between Nurn's fields and the towers of Mordor — slow, ill-tempered, heavily watched but vulnerable in the open. Toward travellers: hostile and well-guarded; a thing to avoid or ambush, not to meet head-on.

lore.en: A train of Orcs hauling supplies, plunder or slaves across the Enemy's lands, plodding under whip and guard between Nurn's fields and the towers of Mordor. Slow and ill-tempered, it is heavily watched but vulnerable if caught in the open.

aspect.en: A place of the Elves — a hidden refuge, garden, white tower or carved fountain, often beautiful and lightly guarded by enchantment, that time and the world pass by. Toward travellers: serene and lovely, but seldom found unbidden; the enchantment that hides it may also turn the unwelcome away.

lore.en: A place of the Elves — a hidden refuge, garden, white tower or carved fountain, often beautiful and lightly guarded by enchantment. Time and the world pass it by, and few mortals find it unbidden.

aspect.en: A huge, rare grey cat with faint camouflaging stripes and enormous 5-7 inch fangs, hunting by night in northern hills and mountains; a tapered, powerful body that makes prodigious leaps. Toward travellers: a stealthy ambush hunter of the high country, rarely seen until it strikes.

lore.en: Huge, rare grey cat (pl. "Chetmíg") with faint tabby markings for camouflage. A nocturnal predator with massive 5-7 inch forequarter fangs; its body tapers to strong, compact hindquarters and it uses its long tail to balance prodigious leaps (up to 150 ft horizontally, 40 ft vertically). Found in the northern hills and mountains.

aspect.en: Elrond Half-elven, lord and founder of Rivendell — descended from both Elves and Men, keeper of Arnor's heirlooms and bearer of one of the Three Rings; a healer, loremaster and host of the wise. Toward travellers: a noble, kindly and far-sighted lord, a giver of shelter, healing and counsel to those who reach his house in need.
