lore.en: Elrond Half-elven, descended from both Eldar and Edain, founded Imladris in S.A. 1697 after the fall of Eregion and has since served as Lord of Rivendell, keeper of heirlooms of Arnor and wielder of Vilya, the Ring of Air.[file:244] His household includes his family (Celebrian, Elladan and Elrohir), other Noldorin lords, craftsmen, scholars and hosts, forming a cultured, self-sustaining enclave that also serves as headquarters for the Rangers and meeting place for the White Council in the late Third Age.[file:244]

aspect.en: Large, clever songbirds, nearly as wise as ravens — keen-eyed, curious, and used as messengers and scouts by Radagast and by wise folk, especially around Erebor and Dale. They speak too high and fast for Dwarves to follow. Toward travellers: harmless and inquisitive; a friend to the well-meaning and a sharp watcher of all who pass.

lore.en: Thrushes are large songbirds. Nearly as intelligent and gifted as ravens, they are among Radagast the Brown's principal messengers and scouts. They are also long-time friends of wise Men in many regions, but especially in Erebor and the Dale. Dwarves admire them, but cannot communicate with them because the Thrushes speak too quickly and in too high pitched voices (one would imagine that Ents would have similar problems). The Thrush language can, however, be learned by Men and Elves who care enough to make a study of such things. Thrushes are very keen eyed and have a strong streak of curiosity in them, so they make excellent scouts. The Old Thrush of Erebor helped Thorin and Company find the secret entrance to Smaug's cave, and warned Bard the Bowman of Smaug's weak spot.

aspect.en: A glossy black snake banded bright yellow, of forests and copses — docile and shy, hunting large insects and avoiding people; but its venom is among the most lethal in Middle-earth. Toward travellers: deadly only to the fool who handles the "pretty snake" — leave it be and it leaves you be.

lore.en: This inoffensive snake inhabits forests and heavy copses; it can be readily identified by the bright yellow bands on its glossy black body. It is generally docile and will avoid people. Most bites occur when witless folk try to pick up this "pretty snake." Instead, the Coireal is happy to hunt large insects. It should be left alone, for its venom is highly potent (10th lvl), one of the most lethal natural poisons in Middle-earth. Symptoms appear in one to four hours, resulting in all but certain death from paralysis.

aspect.en: Freshwater and marsh turtles of river, pond and fen — slow on land, at home in the water, mostly harmless grazers and scavengers, though the larger snapping kinds can take a finger or a duckling. Toward travellers: harmless; only a careless hand near a big snapper risks a bite.

lore.en: Freshwater and marsh turtles of river, pond and fen, slow on land but at home in the water. Most are harmless grazers and scavengers, though the larger snapping kinds can take a finger or a duckling.

aspect.en: A large, long-legged wild cat of the open plains, now rare; its thick buff fur tinges an eerie yellow-green in summer. Hunts by springing onto its prey's back and tearing at the throat — and has killed men this way — and shrieks unsettlingly on winter nights. Toward travellers: shuns people, but deadly if cornered or driven by hunger.

lore.en: Handsome, long-legged hunter of the plains of Calenardhon, now quite rare since Men have killed or domesticated most of its prey and hunt it for fear of losing sheep, goats or kine. Its thick buff fur absorbs grass pollen in summer, turning an eerie yellow-green. It hunts by leaping onto prey's back and driving its claws into throat and neck, and has killed Men this way; in heat or combat it gives off terrifying high-pitched shrieks on winter nights.

aspect.en: Slow, inoffensive land tortoises with prized green-and-grey shells, once common in southern Eriador and western Gondor, now near-extinct — hunted for tasty meat, for shells valued as armour, and for ground shell used against blood-ailments. Toward travellers: utterly harmless; valuable chiefly as a rare find.

lore.en: Land Tortoises were once common in southern Eriador and western Gondor, particularly in the Gwathló basin. Unfortunately, they are extremely tasty and nutritious, so they are favored by Eriadoran hunters and are nearly extinct. Their beautiful green and grey shells are now exceptionally rare. Prized for their value as armor (the shell makes excellent reinforcement) and (when ground) as a source of medicine to combat blood diseases and ailments, a Land Tortoise shell can bring up to two hundred gold pieces on the open market. Very slow and inoffensive, the Land Tortoise's primary defense is its size: the average specimen is five feet long and three high, weighing about three hundred pounds; a few older ones reach six feet and over a quarter ton. When attacked they retreat until cornered, then ground themselves and pull into their shells, or lash out with their necks and hard, sharp beaks. They feed on nearly every type of vegetation and roam the highlands for richer grass or shrubs. Females dig holes along river banks or on the seashore, lay 11-20 eggs, cover them with moist soil, and abandon them.

aspect.en: A small, rare owl that nests in open barrows and old burrows of Eriador — nearly blind in bright light, easily startled, swarming like bees when threatened, and carrying many diseases to which it is immune. Toward travellers: harmless singly, but a startled colony in a barrow can swarm and is foul with sickness.

lore.en: The Barrow Owl is a small, rare Owl which has taken to living in the open barrows and abandoned gopher tunnels of Eriador (especially in northern Cardolan). Nocturnal and exceedingly specialized, they are virtually blind when confronted with bright light (e.g., in day- or torchlight). This is important, for they startle easily and swarm like Bees when confronted with a potential foe. They carry numerous diseases, including rabies and lycanthresis, to which they are immune. (Normally 2nd-3rd level, the latter disease is a severe psychiatric infliction that affects victims in 110 days and leaves them with the false belief that they are wild animals.)

aspect.en: Sindar and Green-elves of Harlindon and southern Lindon — many of them survivors of drowned Beleriand — who shape the woodland culture of the western shores, some chafing under Noldorin rule. Toward travellers: woodland Elf-folk of the coast, courteous but reserved with outsiders.

lore.en: Sindar (Iathrim) and Green-elves (Laegrim) occupy Harlindon and southern Lindon, many as survivors of drowned Beleriand. Some resist living under Noldorin rule and eventually leave eastward to join Silvan realms, but others remain and shape Lindon's woodland culture and rituals described in the culture and lifestyle sections.[file:99]

aspect.en: The "Southrons" — the many peoples of the hot, arid lands south of Gondor and Mordor, mostly small and wiry, settling along coasts, rivers and bays as herders, farmers, traders and warriors, some swayed to the Enemy's banner. Toward travellers: varied folk, hospitable or hostile by tribe and allegiance, and often suspicious of northerners.

lore.en: This is a collective name for the peoples who occupy the great arid and semi-arid lands south of Harondor and Mordor, the land called Harad. Since this is rough and unblessed territory, their greatest populations lie beside the seacoast, rivers, and bays; however, Harad contains little true desert and sparse groups settle or roam the whole region. Haradrim (S. "Southmen") are also called "Southrons" or "Haradwaith" (a term also referring to the land). Physical Character: North and central desert - Most groups are small and wiry, particularly those of the open country: males average 130 pounds, women 100 pounds. Coastal areas and Far Harad- Most are related to the Men of Mûmakan, and are tall and wiry: males average 180 pounds, women 140 pounds. Northern groups have light/medium grey or brown skin, straight black hair, and dark brown eyes. Southern groups have dark grey, brown, or black skin; straight or curly black hair; and dark brown or black eyes. +10 bonus versus heat/fire attacks; -10 bonus versus cold/ice attacks. Their eyes are attuned to extremely bright light and they are unaffected by brilliant displays which might blind others.

aspect.en: Malevolent grave-spirits that haunt the burial mounds of ancient Men, lying in wait to seize victims and clothe them in grave-treasure for the dead. Toward travellers: a deadly haunt of the barrow-downs that traps and entombs the living, above all after dark.

lore.en: Malevolent spirits that haunt the Barrow-downs (Tyrn Gorthad), inhabiting the burial mounds of ancient Men and dressing their victims in grave-treasure.

aspect.en: Semi-nomadic herders and horse-masters who roam the pastures, clashing with Easterling tribes over grazing-land. Toward travellers: proud horse-folk, wary but hospitable to those who respect them, and hard on trespassers.

lore.en: Semi-nomadic herders and horse-masters who clash with the Easterling tribes over pasture lands.

aspect.en: Sauron's elite troll-breed — as huge and strong as common trolls but cunning, organized and fearless, with black scaly hides and black blood, bearing war-hammers and shields; unlike older trolls they endure sunlight and shrug off wounds. Toward travellers: superb, bloodthirsty warriors that know no fear, among the deadliest foes on any road near the Enemy's lands.

lore.en: The Olog-hai have been bred by Sauron from lesser Troll stock, and have until late been a rare breed. Cunning and organized - yet as big and strong as their lesser brethren - the Olog-hai are superb Warriors. They know no fear, and thirst for blood and victory. Olog-hai are also called Black Trolls, for they have black scaly hides and black blood. Most carry blank shields and war hammers, although they are adept at using almost any weapon. They differ from older Troll varieties in other ways as well: (1) they ignore bleeding or stun results when given a critical strike from a normal weapon, since they are more resistant to unenchanted weapons; (2) they can operate freely in daylight; (3) they are relatively quick; and (4) they are capable of using normal language properly, and speak Black Speech (Rank 5) and Westron (Rank 3).

aspect.en: Durin's Folk in their ancestral glory at Moria, trading ore and craft with the Elves of Eregion in a famed friendship of shared learning. Toward travellers: proud master-smiths and miners at the height of their power; reserved but fair, and staunch friends to allies.

lore.en: Durin's Folk in their ancestral seat of Khazad-dum (Moria); allied Dwarves who trade extensively with the Noldor of Eregion, exchanging ores and craft for Elven goods and knowledge, a friendship driven by shared interest in craft and learning.

aspect.en: Noisy black-and-purple ducklike water-birds with broad splayed feet that let them dash across mud and pond-weed; strong swimmers and swift flyers, hardy and widespread. Toward travellers: harmless, but their racket can give away a quiet camp by the water.

lore.en: A black-and-purple ducklike species, the Crake is known as a noisy and obnoxious waterbird. It has wide, splayed feet, allowing it to dash across pondweed and mudflats. Crakes are also excellent swimmers and remarkably swift flyers. They are among the most flexible and adaptable species in all of Middle-earth, ranging as far north as Forodwaith, Mur, and Urb. The Crake closest relative, the Coot, builds island nests up to three or four feet across from reeds and weeds.

aspect.en: Vicious blood-sucking flies that swarm the wastes of Mordor, where Orcs call them "Orcflies" — large and dun-grey with red eyes and a red mark on the back like a watching eye, rumoured to be the Dark Lord's own breeding. Toward travellers: a maddening, biting torment to any beast or person crossing their lands.

lore.en: Vicious, biting, parasitic insects, Morgai Flies are one of the nasty nuisances of life in Mordor. They can found all over the Black Land, particularly in Gorgoroth, where they are known as Orcflies. Their sole food is blood, but enjoy feeding off nearly any beast they can find. Relatives of common Horseflies, Morgai Flies are large and dun, gray, or black in color, with red eyes and a red blotch, like Sauron's Lidless Eye, on their backs. Many chroniclers believe them to be monsters of the Dark Lord's design. This may be true of some of the larger subgroups, but those of the basic variety are simply huge, primeval vermin. Morgai Flies carry virtually all bloodborne diseases, and they played a major part in spreading the Great Plague of T.A. 1636-1637.

aspect.en: The greatest constructs of the Wild-men — animated stone or metal that lies unseen until roused, then rises as a slender man-shape glowing with fierce blue light, some hurling lightning. Toward travellers: a hidden guardian that wakes to strike; what seemed dead stone comes alive in blue fire.

lore.en: Pukel-creatures, the strongest and most clever works of the Druedain and the Daen Coentis: animated stone or metal that stays unseen until activated, then takes the form of attenuated manlike beings glowing with fierce blue light, some casting lightning bolts.

aspect.en: Ducks, geese, swans and other water-birds of river, lake and shore, gathering in flocks to feed and nest. Toward travellers: harmless game — and a noisy alarm that betrays anyone moving along the water's edge.

lore.en: Ducks, geese, swans and other water-birds of river, lake, marsh and shore, gathering in flocks to feed and nest. A ready quarry for hunters and a noisy alarm that betrays anyone moving along the water's edge.

aspect.en: Wild honeybees and bumblebees of meadow, heath and woodland, nesting in hollow trees and banks. Toward travellers: their nests yield honey and wax to the bold, but a disturbed swarm can drive off a bear or a careless gatherer.

lore.en: Wild honeybees and bumblebees of meadow, heath and woodland, nesting in hollow trees and banks. Their hives yield honey and wax to those bold enough to take them, and a disturbed swarm can drive off a bear or a careless gatherer.

aspect.en: A rare, striking-plumaged bird of the eastern wilds, prized and little understood, met only in remote country and keeping far from the haunts of Men. Toward travellers: harmless and elusive, a wondrous fleeting sight in far-off lands.

lore.en: A rare bird of the eastern wilds, prized and little understood, met only in remote country. Wary and striking in plumage, it keeps far from the haunts of Men.

aspect.en: A wall of water that roars down a dry wash or gorge after sudden rain upstream, sweeping away all in the channel with little warning — deadly in narrow defiles even when the sky overhead is clear. Toward travellers: a sudden, drowning danger; never camp in a dry streambed in storm-country.

lore.en: A wall of water that roars down a dry wash or gorge after sudden rain upstream, sweeping away anything in the channel with little warning. Deadly in narrow defiles where the sky above may be clear.

aspect.en: The Ringwraiths — nine wraith-kings, the mightiest undead ever to walk Middle-earth, serving the Dark Lord from Minas Morgul and Dol Guldur; cloaked and unseen, they wield paralysing terror. Toward travellers: an overwhelming, soul-freezing dread — to be hunted by one is near-certain doom.

lore.en: The Nazgul or Ringwraiths, true Lords of the Undead and the single most powerful beings of their kind ever to walk Middle-earth; the nine Wraith-kings serve from Mordor (Minas Morgul) and Dol Guldur. (Detailed in ICE's Peoples of Middle-earth series.)

aspect.en: The perils of fire-mountains and hot ground — lava, ash, choking fumes, scalding steam-vents and bubbling mud — found chiefly about Orodruin and other live peaks where the very earth is treacherous. Toward travellers: a land that can burn, choke or scald; every step near the fire-mountains is a gamble.

lore.en: The perils of fire-mountains and hot ground — lava, ash, choking fumes, scalding steam-vents and bubbling mud-pots. Found chiefly about Orodruin and other live peaks, where the very earth is treacherous.

aspect.en: Beautiful blue-and-white dolphins — the most intelligent and blessed of sea-creatures, servants of the Lord of Waters and friends of the Sea-elves, living in great playful, hierarchical schools that can act with sudden unity. Toward travellers: friendly and benevolent to seafarers, sometimes aiding ships or the drowning.

lore.en: No water creature is as intelligent or blessed as the Ulmodili (Q. "Friend of Ulmo"; pl. "Ulmodili"), the beautiful blue and white Dolphin (Porpoise). Seaborne mammals, they are servants of Ulmo (as opposed to Ossë) and fast allies of the Teleri. Their complex society and wide-ranging schools enable them to act with startling unity when summoned by their master or friends, or when aroused by their enemies. The gregarious Ulmodili live in hierarchical groups of 10-200 individuals, which in turn join to form schools of 100-2000 creatures. Playful and agile, they roll and leap along the surface of the open sea, moving at speeds of up to 40 miles an hour. When they submerge, they can dive as deep as 1000 feet and stay down for as long as five minutes before they need to resurface (they breathe through lungs, not gills). An Ulmodili has smooth blue (top) and white (bottom) skin and a long beaked snout. This snout is a formidable, mace-like weapon that contains an array of short, sharp teeth. Its bulging forehead encases a pad of fat that houses a sonar-like organ that enables the creature to detect objects with stunning accuracy.

aspect.en: Men from distant lands marked by strange dress, speech and custom — traders, envoys, mercenaries or wanderers far from home. Toward travellers: regarded with curiosity or suspicion, their intent unknown until shown — anywhere from friendly to dangerous.

lore.en: Men from distant lands, marked by strange dress, speech and custom — traders, envoys, mercenaries or wanderers far from home, regarded with curiosity or suspicion depending on where their road has brought them.

aspect.en: Steeds bent to evil — black horses stolen as foals and raised to darkness, fortified by spell and potion to be swift, tireless and fearless; the worst reshaped into enlarged, carnivorous, fiery-eyed monsters. Toward travellers: war-mounts of the Enemy's servants; the reshaped kind are predatory horrors, not natural beasts.

lore.en: The forces of Evil, most notably the corrupted Maia Sauron, have bent Horses to their nefarious purposes. Sauron originally had his Nazgûl mounted on black Horses stolen as foals and thus accustomed to evil at an early age; these beasts were fortified by spells and potions to make them swift, tireless, and unafraid of things that would terrify a normal steed. By the end of the Third Age the Dark Lord had succeeded in reshaping some of the stolen foals: enlarged and strengthened, given carnivorous foreteeth, fiery night-sighted eyes, and steaming, smoking breath, their faces became skull-like and their hooves like polished iron. One such was the Mount of the Mouth of Sauron, which bore its master to the parley at the Black Gate during the War of the Ring; exceedingly large and powerful, it could run almost as fast as a Meara, with sharp-edged hooves and saw-like jaws that penetrated armor. Its greatest weapon was its foul steam, akin to the Nazgûl's Black Breath (a 30-foot range, affecting any target within a 5-foot radius). Note: this creature can be characterized as a monster; see Section 6.0 regarding Evil Horses.

aspect.en: Durin's Folk who mine and smelt the rich iron of the Iron Hills east of Mirkwood — renowned smiths of weapons and armour, trading with the Men of Dale and the Lake. Toward travellers: proud, industrious and stout in war; wary of strangers but fair to honest dealers and staunch allies.

lore.en: Durin's Folk who mine and smelt rich iron deposits in the Iron Hills east of Mirkwood, providing metalwork, weapons and armor and maintaining trade links with Dalemen and Lake-men.

aspect.en: "Sharp-claws" — huge eight-limbed sea-creatures like a cross between a crab and a squid, dwelling in the briny inland seas and coastal shallows of the East and South. Toward travellers: a dangerous denizen of salt and brackish waters whose claws make wading or swimming its haunts a risk.

lore.en: Sharp-claws (Q. "Mabelmaikli") are huge creatures with eight appendages. They resemble a cross between a Crab and a Squid and inhabit the inland seas of Rhûnen, Nûrnen, Dushera and the sheltered coastal shelves between the Bay of Helcar (in the Romenëar) and the Bay of Ormal (in the Haragaer). Because they are enamoured of rich, somewhat briny water, though, Mabelmaikli can thrive in any marsh, delta, lake, or ocean where there is a little salt. They are most common in Mordor and in the waters off Arg-Simorîg. Mabelmaikli feed on Starfish, Shellfish, and submarine Worms, but they will attack any animal that comes within reach of their four nimble, steely claws. Each of these pincers is 1-2 feet in diameter and can crush a Man with ease. Together, they present a frightening array. Actually, they are simply the creature's four forward, grasping appendages, and are used to immobilize prey. The Mabelmaikla tears its victims apart with nine inch mandibles and four pairs of mouth parts. Like their Crab relatives, Sharp-claws propel themselves backwards when they swim, but they move much faster, often at speeds of up to fifteen miles an hour. Generally, though, they prefer to burrow and remain inactive until their prey happens by. Their ability to lay an ambush is legend, especially among the slave-fishermen of Nûrn. After all, Mabelmaikli are huge, bright purple denizens that one would expect to see with relative ease. By using refined instincts and the cover of their burrows and murky waters, however, these beasts hide very well. Sharp-claws make excellent feeding machines. They 'hear' with sensors in their four legs and smell and feel with their three foot long antennae. Pain does not affect them. (They cannot be stunned.) Once a Mabelmaikla senses a prospective kill, it darts forward and embraces its victim with one or more pincers. Then it smells the prey with its feet, analyzing the pinioned creature's worth as food.

aspect.en: Fierce giant falcons bred as mounts for evil Air-lords of the far south — perhaps developed from the great falcons of Mirkwood — the fiercest magically bound to a single master that none else can ride. Toward travellers: war-mounts of dark lords, a deadly aerial threat where their riders hold sway.

lore.en: These fierce creatures were the preferred mounts of the Lords of the Air of the Court of Ardor in southern Middle-earth. They were perhaps developed from the Great Falcons of Mirkwood. This fact would have been known to Sauron, who could have shared his knowledge with the evil Elda Court. The fiercest of these Falcons were tied to specific Windlords by magical means; their loyalty to their masters was unswerving, and no one else could ride them unless they could somehow overcome the will of the Falcons by magical means.

aspect.en: A small tentacled squid of the warm southern coast, hunted for its ink, which southern alchemists prize for camouflage paste and invisible ink. Toward travellers: harmless; of interest only to those who trade in its ink.

lore.en: This small tentacled sea creature is found along the Mumakani coast, in the warm South Sea. It is hunted by alchemists and others who prepare magical substances for its ink. The exact use of this solution in magical preparations is not known to those outside this isolated southern region of Middle-earth. Mumakani and Kiran peoples, however, prize the substance for its ability to produce camouflage paste and invisible ink.

aspect.en: Settled country folk working a farm or stretch of woodland at the edge of the wild — tilling, herding, felling and charcoal-burning; hospitable but guarded, and the first to suffer when raiders or beasts come out of the wilderness. Toward travellers: kindly to honest folk and a source of food and shelter, but wary on an exposed frontier.

lore.en: Settled country folk who work a farm or a stretch of woodland at the edge of the wild — tilling, herding, felling and charcoal-burning. Hospitable but guarded, they are the first to suffer when raiders or beasts come out of the wilderness.

aspect.en: Wise-women and herb-keepers of the Dunlending clans, tending wounds and sickness with simples, charms and old craft — respected and a little feared, guarding remedies and rites older than Rohan. Toward travellers: a possible source of healing and lore, though wary of outsiders and protective of their secrets.

lore.en: Wise-women and herb-lore keepers of the Dunlending clans, tending wounds and sickness with simples, charms and old craft. Respected and a little feared among their own folk, they guard remedies and rites handed down since before Rohan came.

aspect.en: Nandor Elves and northern Sindar houses of Lindon, holding parts of its forlands and shores — an old woodland Elven lineage among the western realms. Toward travellers: secretive forest-Elves, wary of strangers but not hostile without cause.

lore.en: Nandor Elves (Lindellim) and Mithrim-related northern Sindar houses contribute additional Elven lineages within Lindon. The appendices detail house histories, territories and military forces, showing how they occupy various parts of Forlindon, Harlindon and Rhûnlindon and how their demographic share grows relative to the Noldor over time.[file:99]

aspect.en: A chance meeting with Elves abroad — usually a small party on the road: travellers between the havens, a company keeping to the dusk, or hunters far afield. Toward travellers: courteous but reserved with strangers, gracious to the worthy, and seldom lingering long.

lore.en: A chance meeting with Elves abroad in the wider lands — usually a small party on the road rather than the folk of a settled realm: travellers between the havens, a wandering company keeping to the dusk, or hunters far afield. Courteous but reserved with strangers, they seldom linger long.

aspect.en: "Leaf-demons" — nocturnal wood-spirits twisted by Morgoth into savage tree-top predators; tall, featureless and green-hided, with senses keener than Elven sight, racing along branches faster than a bird and freezing motionless by day, often mistaken for statues. Toward travellers: an almost unkillable forest horror that strikes from the canopy in the dark.

lore.en: Leaf-demons (Q. "Lassarauko"), nocturnal wood-spirits seduced and corrupted by Morgoth into savage arboreal predators. Immortal and unbreedable, with hearing and smell beyond Elven sight, they race along branches faster than a Swift flies and can stop instantly only at predetermined spots. Tall, featureless and greenish-hided, they live in "lats" of six (five Lesser led by one Greater) and rest motionless most of the day, often mistaken for statues (their eyes worth 500 gp).

aspect.en: An Elf who has forsaken his people — outlawed for some old deed, soured by grief, or gone solitary and strange in the wild — wary, unpredictable, and answering to no lord. Toward travellers: a wild card who may aid a stranger as readily as rob one, and not to be trusted on sight.

lore.en: An Elf who has forsaken his people — outlawed for some old deed, soured by grief, or gone solitary and strange in the wilder corners of Lindon. Wary and unpredictable, a renegade may aid a traveller as readily as rob one, and answers to no lord.

aspect.en: The great desert eagle of Far Harad — like the northern eagles but forced to scavenge as well as hunt, taking prey in the air or on the ground and eating carrion; bold enough to strike at people on the southern caravan roads. Toward travellers: unusually aggressive for an eagle, and may harass or attack those crossing its desert.

lore.en: The Desert Orao is the principal native Eagle of Far Harad. It is quite similar to the Eagles of the North, except that the environment has forced him to play the role of scavenger as well as hunter. These soaring hunters swoop to attack smaller birds or prey on the ground. Unlike the northern birds, the desert Eagle will as readily eat carrion as fresh meat, an adaptation made necessary by the environment. They are aggressive enough to strike travellers along Harad's southern caravan roads. Aside from Men, the Orao are the dominant hunters on the vast plains of southwestern Harad. Their eyries are set in the caverns of the northern Yellow Mountains, and in wind-hollowed caves the highest of the hilly Raj region to the north. In size, they are no match for the Great Eagles, but they are large enough to carry off a shepherd's goat or lamb.

aspect.en: The farming folk of Gondor's heartland vales — Anórien, Ithilien and Lebennin — of mixed Númenórean and local blood, working fields and pastures and supplying the great roads and the river. Toward travellers: settled, ordinary country people, generally peaceable and used to traffic on the roads.

lore.en: The founding of Gondor concentrated people in the Anduin valley, settling Anórien, Ithilien and Lebennin together as early heartlands.[file:216] By the War of the Ring, Anórien's lowlands host scattered villages and farmsteads of Gondorians of mixed Númenórean and local descent, who work fields and pastures and supply traffic along the Great West Road and river.

aspect.en: Agents on secret business — watching roads and garrisons, carrying word, or worming into the trust of the powerful — passing as travellers, merchants or servants. Toward travellers: outwardly harmless but dangerous in what they serve; a careless word to one may travel far.

lore.en: Agents abroad on someone's secret business — watching roads and garrisons, carrying word, or worming into the confidence of the powerful. They pass as travellers, merchants or servants, and a careless one is as dangerous to its master as to its mark.

aspect.en: Swift coastal eagles of the eastern seas — smaller kin of the Red Eagles — hunting sea-mammals, surface fish and even sea-turtles, bane of water-drakes and worshipped as saviours by some island tribes; gold-and-blue-green plumed. Toward travellers: little threat to people, a majestic hunter of the coasts and a good omen to seafarers.

lore.en: Smaller, swifter kinsmen of the fierce Red Eagles, Sea Eagles live along the coasts of the Romenear (Q. "East Sea") and the eastern Haragaer (S. "South Sea"). There, they hunt sea mammals, large fish that swim near the surface, and even sea turtles. The bane of Water Drakes, Sea Eagles are often worshipped as saviors by the seafaring tribes of the remote eastern isles. Sea Eagles have yellowish-gold underplumage and blue-green feathers on the tops of their backs and wings. They have golden beaks.

aspect.en: Stout, venomous lizards of the dry southern scrub, marked with bead-like scales — slow but ill-tempered, delivering a painful, lingering bite when handled or trodden on. Toward travellers: easily avoided, but a nasty venomous bite if disturbed.

lore.en: Stout, venomous lizards of the dry southern scrub, marked with bead-like scales. Slow but ill-tempered, they deliver a painful, lingering bite when handled or trodden on.

aspect.en: A pale, clinging moss of dark, damp hollows and rotting trunks in the shadowed forest — deadly to touch or eat, and carefully harvested for the most virulent poisons. Toward travellers: a quiet, lethal hazard underfoot in deep woods, not to be touched.

lore.en: A pale, clinging moss that grows in dark, damp hollows and on rotting trunks in the shadowed forest. Contact or ingestion can be deadly; it is carefully harvested for use in the most virulent poisons.

aspect.en: A jawless, eel-like fish with a round, rasping sucker-mouth — a water parasite that latches onto larger creatures and bores in to feed on blood until full. Toward travellers: a foul hazard of swimming or fording, fastening on unseen and leaving a slow-bleeding wound.

lore.en: A cylindrical, grey, jawless fish, the Lamprey is a parasite that attaches itself to other creatures, like a leech with a circular maw. It then remains in place, slowly burrowing into the flesh and swallowing blood until sated. (A wound from a Lamprey will bleed at a rate of two hits/round for each round it was in place.)

aspect.en: The great worms bred by Morgoth in the Elder Days and their lingering descendants — vast, cunning and malevolent, scaled in armour and, the greatest of them, gifted with fire and a spellbinding voice. Toward travellers: any one is a peril to a whole kingdom; to meet one is mortal danger.

lore.en: Dragons and drakes of Middle-earth — the great worms bred by Morgoth in the Elder Days and their lingering descendants. Vast, cunning and malevolent, armoured in scale and (the greatest) gifted with fire and a spellbinding voice; any one is a peril to a whole realm.

aspect.en: Industrious ants whose great earthen nests dot wood and plain; most harmless, but the biting and soldier kinds swarm to defend, and the largest southern species can strip a carcass with frightening speed. Toward travellers: a nuisance at most, unless one disturbs an aggressive or southern nest.

lore.en: Industrious ants whose great earthen nests dot wood and plain; most are harmless, but the biting and soldier kinds swarm in defense, and the largest southern species can strip a carcass with frightening speed.

aspect.en: Bats of cave, ruin and hollow tree that pour out at dusk to hunt insects over water and wood. Harmless singly, though vast colonies haunt the deeper caverns. Toward travellers: no threat — a flutter of wings in the dark, or an unsettling living ceiling in a cave.

lore.en: Bats of cave, ruin and hollow tree, emerging at dusk to hunt insects over water and woodland. Harmless singly, though great colonies haunt the darker caverns and some far-eastern kinds grow large and bold.

aspect.en: The oldest of beings — a merry, mysterious master of his own small country who sings to quiet the angry trees and fears nothing in the world, wholly his own master and untouched by the powers that move others. Toward travellers: kindly and helpful to those who stumble upon him, offering shelter, song and rescue — but bound to no one's errand but his own.

lore.en: The oldest being, who sings songs to calm the angry trees of the forest.

aspect.en: Noble Grey-elves who stayed in Middle-earth rather than sail West — tall, fair-haired and pale-eyed, ancient and learned, carrying themselves with quiet authority. Toward travellers: courteous but reserved, measuring a stranger before they trust.

lore.en: The Sindar or "Grey-elves" are Eldar and were originally part of the great kindred called the Teleri. Unlike the Noldor, Vanyar, and bulk of the Teleri, the Sindar chose not to cross over the sea to Aman; instead they stayed in Middle-earth. They, like the Silvan Elves, are part of the Moriquendi, those Elves who never saw the Light of Valinor. Physical Character: Thin when compared to Men, the Sindar are nearly as tall as the Noldor but are generally slighter of build. They are more muscular than the Silvan folk. Most have fair hair and pale blue or grey eyes. Like the Noldor, they have light skin. Same endurance as Noldor Elves. Males average 6'5", females 6'1". Same lifespan as Noldor Elves. Cannot become sick or scarred and are virtually immune to disease. +15 bonus versus cold attacks. Vision same as that of Noldor Elves. Less musical than the Vanyar or Silvan Elves, and are less skilled in forging or crafts than the Noldor. Nonetheless, they are adept at all the arts and excel in their special provinces. No race builds better boats or ships. The Sindar are the most open and cooperative of Middle-earth's Elves. They are great teachers and borrowers and have an interest in the works of all races. Scattered through the eastern woods and the realms of their Silvan kin, they are encountered as counsellors, march-wardens and lords among the Wood-elves of Mirkwood, Lorien and the Vale of Anduin.

aspect.en: Large black jackals with reddish ears and eerie blue eyes that give an innocent look hiding sly, pitiless ways — night-hunters in coordinated packs that encircle prey, decoy its defenders and pick off the choicest victims, scavenging in lean times. Toward travellers: a cunning, dangerous pack-predator of the night, best met with fire and numbers.

lore.en: Large black jackals (Rh. Leavings) that entered the Talath Harroch, the southern Rhovanion plain below Mirkwood, during the Great Plague of T.A. 1636-1637, having migrated from the East; they now range from the western flanks of the Orocarni to the eastern bank of the Anduin. Their reddish ears and eerie blue eyes give an innocent guise that hides sly, pitiless ways. Hunting at night in coordinated packs of 4-20, they encircle prey, decoy the strongest defenders and close on the choicest victims, scavenging carrion in lean times.

aspect.en: A Sindarin warden set to keep some threshold of the Elven lands — a ford, a forest-eaves, a hidden path — silent and watchful, clad to melt into wood and shadow. Toward travellers: challenges intruders from hiding but speeds friends quietly on their way; a guardian, not a hunter.

lore.en: A Sindarin warden set to keep some threshold of the Elven lands — a ford, a forest-eaves, a hidden path. Silent and watchful, clad to melt into wood and shadow, the guardian challenges intruders and speeds friends quietly on their way.

aspect.en: Lively, tree-flitting monkeys of a Far Harad forest, about three feet long, endearing and tame around the local folk but shyer of strangely-dressed outsiders; great troops haunt a temple so respectfully the faithful say they worship there. Toward travellers: harmless and curious, though wary of foreign-looking visitors.

lore.en: Hordes of lively monkeys living among the trees of the forest called "Gaj" in western Far Harad, about three feet head to tail and flitting through branches like squirrels. Less intelligent than their more developed relatives but endearing to Men who visit the Gaj, they are neither noisy nor unclean and act tame around typical Haradan, though shyer with outlandishly dressed folk; great swarms haunt the temple grounds so respectfully the faithful insist they worship there. Their attractive gold-and-black fur is speckled with light that glows in the dark, and tales tell of foreign pelt-trappers who met ghastly ends, swarmed by the chattering beasts.

aspect.en: The folk of Dorwinion by the Sea of Rhûn — of mixed Northman and Easterling blood, somewhat stocky and fair with a faint yellowish cast — a people of the wine-lands between the great realms. Toward travellers: traders and vintners of the eastern marches whose welcome depends on the dealings and the day.

lore.en: The Dorwinrim occupy the lower Carnen valley and the region running south from the river to the northwest shore of the Sea of Rhûn - the land called Dorwinion. They are a mixture of Northman and Easterling stock. Physical Character: Dorwinrim are slightly larger than most groups labeled as "Common Men": males average 160 pounds, females 110 pounds. Overall, they are somewhat stocky and have wide features; narrow noses and eye slits are the only exception. Their fair, slightly yellowish complexion is unique. They have subdued eyes which are usually brown (like their straight hair), although some are blue or green. Average endurance. Men average 5'9", women 5'2". Lifespan: 60-80 years. +30 bonus to RR versus poisons. +15 for Acting or Public Speaking situations. +10 for Rowing maneuvers. They are traders and river-men who abandoned their nomadic past in favor of an urban, albeit rustic life. Dorwinion is known for its fine wines and strong oils. Vines cover the land and provide the principal sources of income: grapes, olives, wine, olive oil, etc.

aspect.en: A dull-green venomous snake of Rohan and the northern White Mountains — unusually sociable, denning by the dozens in old burrows and basking together on sunny slopes; fat, sluggish and foul-smelling. Toward travellers: venomous if trodden on or cornered, but torpid and easily avoided.

lore.en: The Green Asp is the only venomous serpent indigenous to Calenardhon (Rohan) and the northern White Mountains. It is a sociable creature (for a snake), making its home in as many as fifty of its fellows in empty Rabbit or Ground Squirrel burrows. On sunny days, the Asp community will come out to sun themselves en masse on the slopes near their subterranean home. Green Asps have dull green skin and are usually fat and torpid, with puffy poison glands below their eyes. They are considered unattractive even by those fond of serpents, and a fetid odor reminiscent of rotting strawberries does nothing to relieve this impression. The (5th lvl) bite is rarely fatal, but the area around the wound becomes necrotic, turning awful shades of violet and yellow-green before sloughing off, usually exposing the bone. In some cases (15% chance, modified by Co bonus) the injection may cause the entire limb to turn gangrenous and fall off; otherwise the victim will be incapacitated for 3-6 days with high fever and hallucinations.

aspect.en: Giraffe-like beasts of the far southeast with long spike-like horns, browsing the tops of trees and scrub and stooping to grass or crops in hard country — swift, fearless and exceedingly fierce in a fight, ridden as war-mounts by some eastern peoples. Toward travellers: peaceable browsers in the wild, but formidable and aggressive when ridden to war.

lore.en: The Zûrafy (V. "Tallnecks"; sing. "Zûrafa") of Núrad, northern Chey, and the Talathrant Valley resemble giraffes with long, spikelike horns. They are related to Deer and feed on the foliage, fruit, and buds found in the upper part of trees or tall scrub; in harsher locales the Zûrafa will stoop to eat grasses, and herds have been known to devastate crops. The Núriags, Variags, and Chey use the Zûrafy as mounts, for they are swift, fearless, and exceedingly fierce combatants. Because of their limited numbers and the difficulty in capturing and domesticating them, only small numbers have been employed outside the circles of royalty. Most Zûrafy have a whitish or light tan coat and brown-and-white striped legs; their horns are covered with short white hair which they never shed. The rare, omnivorous, nocturnal Variag Zûrafa is jet black.

aspect.en: The many wild birds of Middle-earth — songbirds, waterfowl, waders and birds of prey filling wood, fen, shore and sky. Toward travellers: mostly harmless, but their sudden alarm-calls and flights often betray whoever moves below.

lore.en: The many wild birds of Middle-earth — songbirds, waterfowl, waders and birds of prey — filling wood, fen, shore and sky. Most are harmless, but their alarm-calls and sudden flights often betray the movements of those who pass below.

aspect.en: Swift antelope-like grazers of the open steppe, among the fastest beasts of Middle-earth, running in skittish herds that trust to speed and sharp eyes to outpace any pursuer. Toward travellers: harmless; a fleeting sight bounding away across the plains.

lore.en: Swift, antelope-like grazers of the open steppe and plain, among the fastest beasts of Middle-earth. They run in skittish herds and rely on speed and keen eyes to outpace any pursuer.

aspect.en: A broad label for the town and city folk of Eriador and Gondor — the common people of places like Bree, Tharbad, Pelargir and Minas Tirith — of mixed blood and every trade. Toward travellers: ordinary townsfolk used to strangers and traffic, their welcome ranging from busy indifference to friendliness or suspicion.

lore.en: This is a generalized label for the town and city folk of Eriador and Gondor, the Common Men of northwestern Middle-earth. It includes common folk from Annúminas, Fornost, Bree, Tharbad, Calembel, Dol Amroth, Linhir, Pelargir, Osgiliath, Minas Tirith, etc. These folk contain varying degrees of Harnadan, Dunlending, Northman, and Dúnadan blood. Physical Character: All types, but normally medium. Males average 160 pounds, women 125 pounds. Variations of fair to tan or olive skin. All colors of hair and eyes. Average endurance. Males average 5'10", women 5'4". Lifespan: Moderate, averaging 65-85 years. Various types of elaborate or practical wool and linen garb, including cloaks, boots, etc. Tunics are worn in warmer areas; shirts and pants or leggings are worn in cooler locales. Some imported silks and fine cottons are in evidence. Urban folk are a varied, rather cosmopolitan lot. Many are from mercantile or guild backgrounds and some have dealt with enchantments. Urban folk are worldly enough to deal with most outsiders. They hate no race, aside from the Orcs and Wargs.

aspect.en: The master-smith who founded the great Elven craft-guild of Eregion — among the greatest smiths of his people and the maker of the Three Elven Rings. Toward travellers: a noble, brilliant craftsman-lord, gracious to the worthy and wholly absorbed in his art.

lore.en: Master Smith, founder of the Gwaith-i-Mírdain and de facto leader of the craft community; arguably the second-greatest Elven smith after Fëanor, and the maker of the Three Rings.

aspect.en: A train of merchants travelling together for safety — wagons, pack-beasts and hired guards strung along the trade-roads; a rich prize for brigands, and so rarely seen without an armed escort. Toward travellers: welcoming and a source of goods and news, well-guarded and wary of ambush.

lore.en: A train of merchants travelling together for safety — wagons, pack-beasts and hired guards strung along the trade-roads between the great markets. A rich and tempting prize for brigands, and so rarely met without an escort of armed men.

aspect.en: Fierce wild pigs, ancestors of farm swine, ranging temperate woods and fields. Largely nocturnal and exceptionally dangerous when roused: an alarmed boar charges anything, trampling and slashing with its tusks, and barely slows from wounds. Hunted with stout cross-barred spears, because a speared boar runs up the shaft at the hunter. Toward travellers: avoids people, but a startled or cornered boar is a deadly charge.

lore.en: Fierce wild pigs, ancestors of all domesticated breeds, found throughout the temperate regions of Endor; the largest, the Red Boar, lives east of the Orocarni in the easternmost continent (particularly Aegan). Exceptionally dangerous and largely nocturnal, an alarmed Boar charges regardless of size, trampling with hooves and slashing with tusks, and injuries short of a limb hardly slow it. Hunted everywhere with stout cross-barred spears, since a speared Boar runs up the shaft at the hunter. Omnivores travelling in groups of 1-20; the famed Boar of Everholt of the Firien Wood gored King Folca of Rohan to death in T.A. 2864, boar and king dying together.

aspect.en: Plump, chicken-like ground-birds of the grasslands, brown speckled black for camouflage — a favourite, tasty quarry of hunters, foxes and hawks; the male's mating call booms like someone blowing across a bottle. Toward travellers: harmless, chiefly welcome as game.

lore.en: A plump, gallinaceous (chickenlike) bird of the grasslands of Calenardhon (Rohan), the tasty Grass Grouse is the preferred prey of many hunters, be they winged or two- or four-legged. Many a man, Red Fox, or Hawk will pass easier prey by for a crack at a greasy Grass Grouse. Their black-speckled brown plumage provides good camouflage in the tall grasses, so the birds prosper and spread in spite of their inherent appeal to the palate. The male booming mating cry is most reminiscent of a drunk blowing over the neck of a bottle.

aspect.en: Wild pack-hunting wolves of the colder forests, hills and open country, preying on deer, livestock and the occasional stray traveller. Toward travellers: bold and dangerous in numbers, especially in hard winters, but wary of fire and armed men.

lore.en: Wild wolves that hunt in packs across the colder forests, hills and open country, preying on deer, livestock and the occasional unwary traveller. Bold in hard winters, they are dangerous in numbers but wary of fire and armed men.

aspect.en: Tiny, harmless-looking white shrews that carry a dread plague — victims turn blue, break out in boils and bleed — though the shrews themselves are merely immune carriers; superb climbers that avoid notice but bite viciously and spray foulness when cornered. Toward travellers: deceptively deadly, not by tooth but by the sickness they carry; never to be touched.

lore.en: Tiny, mild-looking shrews with soft white fur and blue-grey bellies that carry the dread Blue Hand disease: victims turn bluish, break out in boils, bleed from nose and ears, and many are crippled or kill themselves. The shrews are merely immune carriers. Superb climbers that avoid most encounters, but when cornered they bite exposed skin viciously and secrete a foul spray; their spines can bear a Man's weight.

aspect.en: The common gopher-like rodent of Cardolan — stout, rat-like grass-root eaters living in vast colonies of shallow burrows whose hidden tunnels can snap the leg of a horse or a man. Toward travellers: harmless in itself, but their burrow-riddled ground is a real hazard to mounts.

lore.en: The most common rodent in Cardolan, the Cunaura (Du. "Gophers") of Eriador resemble big stout Rats and live mainly on grass roots. On the plains they are a major nuisance because they live in large colonies of interlocking burrows. Their holes rise up about a foot from ground level but their tunnels run very close to the surface and cannot be easily detected by Sheep, Horses, or Men (leading to many broken legs).

aspect.en: A small, silvery, gliding frog of deep rain-forest — slick-skinned and deadly, carrying venom in its bluish claws and living in huge colonies. Toward travellers: rare but lethal in numbers; stumbling onto a nest of them is a real peril.

lore.en: A slimy, silvery, gliding frog, the Grey Flyer is a small but deadly amphibian. They carry a nasty venom in their bluish claws. Grey Flyers are rare, living only in the depths of thick rain forests, but they live in huge colonies and woe to anyone who stumbles upon their nests!

aspect.en: Wild persimmon trees of warm, sheltered vales and river-terraces in Southern Rhovanion, their orange fruit ripening late to give sweet, sticky food for folk and wildlife. Toward travellers: harmless; a welcome late-season food along the way.

lore.en: Wild persimmon trees growing in warm, sheltered vales and river-terraces of Southern Rhovanion. Their orange fruit ripens late, offering sweet, sticky food for Beijabar, Woodmen and wildlife alike.

aspect.en: Herds of horses grazed on open grassland, prized for riding, war and trade and watched over by mounted herders. Toward travellers: the finest stock is jealously guarded, and to be caught near it uninvited invites suspicion.

lore.en: Herds of horses bred and grazed on the open grasslands, prized for riding, war and trade. Watched by mounted herders, the finest stock is jealously guarded and ranks among the region's most valued exports.

aspect.en: A ruin of the ancient Edain or their early kingdoms — older and ruder than the works of Gondor and Arnor, half-sunk in earth and forest. Toward travellers: it holds old bones, older lore, and sometimes things best left buried — a place to search with care.

lore.en: A ruin of the ancient Edain or their early kingdoms — older and ruder than the works of Gondor and Arnor, half-sunk in earth and forest. Such places hold old bones, older lore, and sometimes things best left buried.

aspect.en: Great wild oxen of the plains — massive and horned, the untamed ancestors of cattle; a charging bull is a peril to any hunter, and even wolves think twice before troubling a herd. Toward travellers: leaves people alone, but immensely dangerous if a bull charges.

lore.en: Great wild oxen of the Ninfiara plains — massive, horned and formidable, untamed forebears of cattle. A charging bull is a peril to any hunter, and even wolves think twice before troubling a herd.

aspect.en: Short, dark, stocky hill-folk of broken Rhudaur, kin to the Dunlendings — superb mountaineers but deeply distrustful of outsiders and prone to treachery and ambush, worshipping vengeful gods with blood; old enemies of Dúnedain and Northmen, and dreading Elves. Toward travellers: dangerous and faithless to strangers, quick to ambush and slow to trust.

lore.en: Short, dark, stocky men of the rugged hills of Rhudaur, distantly related to Dunlendings; superb mountaineers but deeply suspicious of outsiders, prone to treachery and ambush. Worship vengeful petty deities with blood sacrifice. Traditional enemies of both Dúnedain and Northmen; greatly fear Elves. Some served in the hosts of the Witch-king of Angmar alongside Orcs, an uneasy alliance. Survive as hunters, gatherers and occasional brigands in the broken terrain.[file:88]

aspect.en: Huge but rarely-seen falcons of the high Mountains of Mirkwood — surprisingly agile for their size to live in dense forest, and all but untameable. Toward travellers: shy of people and seldom seen; a magnificent, wary hunter of the forest heights.

lore.en: Rarely seen despite their huge size, Great Falcons reside in the remoter and higher reaches of the Forest of Mirkwood (actually most reside in the Emyn-nu-Fuin, the "Mountains of Mirkwood"). They are almost untameable, probably due to the difficulty of hooding and confining such a huge bird, even as an eyas (fledgling). Great Falcons are surprisingly maneuverable for such large birds, as is necessary for any winged beast that would live in the dense forest. Their light build makes them unable to carry more than around 70 lbs, so they make poor mounts.

aspect.en: Dwarves of the halls and mines on the eastern Blue Mountains, including Durin's Folk in exile at Thorin's Halls — enduring miners and smiths who keep their holds even after the Elves have gone. Toward travellers: industrious, proud and clannish; reserved with strangers but fair to honest dealers.

lore.en: Dwarves inhabit halls and mines on the east side of the Blue Mountains, especially south of the Gulf of Lhûn; Thorin's Halls (Durin's Folk in exile) are located in this Lindon-adjacent zone. The introduction notes that even after all Elves depart in later Ages, Dwarves still dwell in their halls and keep mines in use.[file:99]

aspect.en: The devout of Arnor who keep monastic houses, hermitages and small enclaves on hilltops and in defiles, joining contemplative life with simple gardening and herding. Toward travellers: peaceable, retiring religious folk, hospitable to the respectful and keeping to their quiet retreats.

lore.en: For a time the Rammas, like the lower but more abrupt down-lands to the south, serves as a religious retreat for the Faithful of Arnor. Monastic houses, hermitages and small religious enclaves occupy hilltops and defiles, combining contemplative life with subsistence gardening and herding in the sheltered pockets of the ridge.

aspect.en: The mortal soldiery of Angmar — hardened northern fighters in the Witch-king's service, garrisoning his black towers and marching on the Dúnedain; grim and disciplined. Toward travellers: hostile servants of the Iron Crown who hunt and fight all enemies of Angmar.

lore.en: Mannish soldiery of Angmar — hardened northern fighters in the service of the Witch-king, garrisoning his black towers and marching against the Dúnedain of the North. Grim and disciplined, they are the Iron Crown's mortal sword-arm.

aspect.en: Rivers, lakes and coasts worked for fish, marked by drying-racks, weirs and boats, with salt and smoked fish keeping the region fed through winter. Toward travellers: a dependable source of food and a sign of settled waterside folk.

lore.en: Waters worked for their fish — rivers, lakes and coasts where folk net, trap and line their catch. Drying-racks, weirs and fishing-boats mark the settlements, and salt or smoked fish keeps the region fed through winter.

aspect.en: Orcish priests who keep the records and dark lore of goblin-kind across the Ages, guarding secret rituals and tales of their coming from Morgoth's realm in hidden chambers. Toward travellers: malevolent keepers of evil lore, dangerous and fanatical within their hidden sanctums.

lore.en: Orcish priests who preserve records of goblin deeds over two Ages and guard secret lore and rituals in hidden chambers, including tales of the coming from Morgoth's realm.

aspect.en: The Silvan and Sindarin Elves of Lórien, masters of woodcraft and stealth, dwelling in flets high among the great mallorn-trees. Toward travellers: secretive guardians of their golden wood, unseen until they choose; courteous but exacting toward strangers who enter uninvited.

lore.en: The Silvan and Sindarin Elves of Lórien, known for their skill in woodcraft, stealth, and the construction of flets among the mallorn trees.

aspect.en: Large red, centipede-like swarm-creatures of southeastern forests — fast, tree-climbing, able to swim, living in rotting logs and moving in ant-like social hordes. Most are harmless to people, but the "warrior" caste that guards the swarm is venomous. Toward travellers: a crawling horde best left alone; its warriors bite with poison if the swarm is disturbed.

lore.en: Úlceracin (sing. "Úlcarcan") are large, red, centipede-like creatures that move in hordes across the dense forests of southeastern Endor. Nocturnal creatures, they feed on rotting vegetation, insects, carrion, and (occasionally) live prey. They are extremely quick and are capable of scaling trees and swimming across placid water. Like ants, they operate in rigidly-defined social groups, if necessary swarming to defend their lairs. Úlcercain generally reside in rotting logs. Most of the so-called "Evil Fangs" are harmless to the Children of Ilúvatar; however, the "warriors" that comprise about twenty percent of any colony will attack virtually anything and anyone. Immobilized or sleeping folk need be careful around these creatures. Armed with powerful 2-3 inch mandibles and a mild (lvl 0) nerve venom, a group of Warrior Úlcercain can slay and clean a Man in a matter of minutes.

aspect.en: Female orcs, seldom seen abroad and kept mostly in the deep warrens where the breed is reared — met in the tunnels of Moria and like strongholds, as vicious as the males in defence of their broods. Toward travellers: hostile and savage in their lairs, encountered only deep in orc-holds and no less deadly there.

lore.en: Female Orcs, seldom seen abroad and kept mostly within the deep warrens where the breed is reared. Met in the tunnels of Moria and like strongholds, they are as vicious as the males in defense of their broods.

aspect.en: Rare, long-lived horses bred by the Elves — more intelligent and empathetic than common steeds, needing neither bit nor bridle and answering to their rider's mind. Usually grey, silver or dappled, favouring woodland over open plain. Toward travellers: gentle and loyal to those they trust, but they will not suffer a cruel or unworthy rider.

lore.en: The Horses of the Elves, like the Mearas, are directly descended from Nahar, the steed of Oromë. Nahar is immortal; his descendants are not, but Elvish Horses live to great age (100 years is not unusual). They rarely have white markings except for an occasional white "star"; large white patches (painted/piebald/skewbald) are never seen, though all other colors of lesser Horses occur, with white and silvery dappled gray more common. They prefer to live in wooded areas, as the Elves do, rather than the plains home to most Horses. More intelligent than most Horses, they need no bit or bridle, being empathetic enough to receive directions from their riders; most Elves do without a saddle. Finally, Elven Horses stand staunchly in the face of dangers that would terrify most Horses, brave even before supernatural terrors such as Trolls and the Undead. Famous individuals include Nahar (Steed of Oromë), Nimros (Steed of Glorfindel), and Rochallor (Steed of Fingolfin).

aspect.en: A camp or sacred place of the Snowmen of Forochel — snow-houses, sled-caches and bone-marked shrines on the frozen coast, suited to the bitter North. Toward travellers: unwelcoming to outsiders and hard to use without Lossoth knowledge, but a sign that help against the cold may be near.

lore.en: A camp or sacred place of the Lossoth, the Snowmen of Forochel — snow-houses, sled-caches and bone-marked shrines on the frozen coast. Suited to the bitter North and unwelcoming to outsiders.

aspect.en: Elven scouts ranging the wild country about Rivendell and the Trollshaws, watching the fords and old roads — moving unseen, marking the passage of orcs and brigands and carrying word swiftly home. Toward travellers: hidden guardians who observe strangers before showing themselves, and help the worthy in peril.

lore.en: Elven scouts ranging the wild country about Rivendell and the Trollshaws, watching the fords and old roads of Rhudaur. They move unseen, mark the passage of Orcs and brigands, and carry word swiftly back to the Last Homely House.

aspect.en: Traders moving goods between clans and to the great towns; some fronts hide a smugglers' trade in herbs grown for the Corsairs of Umbar. Toward travellers: generally welcoming dealers and a source of goods and news — though a few serve darker masters behind a trader's face.

lore.en: Merchants based in Larach Duhnnan and other sites move goods between clans and to Tharbad, while a hidden Smugglers' Hold grows gort and tartella herbs for Corsairs of Umbar using Dunnish and Dúnadan frontmen.[file:32]

aspect.en: The Men of the grassy plains south of Fangorn — herders and settlers along the Entwash, forerunners of the Rohirrim — who graze and trade near the forest and keep an uneasy peace with its powers. Toward travellers: plain herding folk, cautious but not hostile, ever watchful of the forest at their backs.

lore.en: The Calenardhons are Men inhabiting the plains south of Fangorn (precursors or analogues to the Rohirrim). The 'Borders' chapter (6.11) describes their settlements along the Entwash and their interactions with Fangorn, including trading, grazing near the forest and occasional conflicts or alliances with Ents and border powers.[file:154]

aspect.en: A militant Dunnish faction bitterly hating the Dúnedain, bound to a temple of harsh, sacrificial religion and pushing for war — a dark twisting of the old Daen beliefs. Toward travellers: fanatical and hostile, above all to anyone of Dúnedain blood; dangerous zealots.

lore.en: Militant Dunnish faction exemplified by clan Arailt and their allies, bitterly hating Dúnedain, closely linked to the Temple of Justice, and pushing for war and a harsh, sacrificial religion that twists old Daen beliefs.[file:32]

aspect.en: Quick, chattering tree-squirrels of the woodlands, hoarding nuts and seeds among the branches. Toward travellers: harmless, but their sudden scolding often betrays a predator — or a traveller — moving below.

lore.en: Tree-squirrels of the woodlands, quick and chattering as they hoard nuts and seeds among the branches. Harmless and ever-watchful, their sudden scolding often betrays a predator — or a traveller — moving below.

aspect.en: A swift, pack-hunting lizard of the warm lands, running down small game in coordinated rushes — bold and persistent, a pack able to pull down prey far larger than any one of them. Toward travellers: a single one is minor, but a pack is dangerous and dogged.

lore.en: A swift, pack-hunting lizard of the warm lands, running down small game in coordinated rushes. Bold and persistent, a pack can pull down prey far larger than any single one of them.

aspect.en: Large water-lurking reptiles of warm southern rivers and shores, lying like logs until prey comes near — powerful and armoured, a big one able to drag down a deer, a horse or an unwary man. Toward travellers: a deadly ambush at any warm waterside; safe at a distance, lethal within a lunge.

lore.en: Large water-lurking reptiles of the warm southern rivers, marshes and shores, lying like logs until prey comes near. Powerful and armoured, a big one can drag down a deer, a horse or an unwary man.

aspect.en: Keepers of the old Dunlending faith — leaders of rite and sacrifice who tend the clans' ancestral spirits at hill-shrines and standing stones, holding great sway and deep suspicion of outland gods and ways. Toward travellers: powerful and insular, hostile to outsiders who meddle with their rites or sacred places.

lore.en: Keepers of the old Dunlending faith — leaders of rite and sacrifice who tend the clans' ancestral spirits at hill-shrines and standing stones. They hold great sway over their people and deep suspicion of outland gods and ways.

aspect.en: A small, cat-like highland fox with a striking white mask and ears against reddish-brown fur. Very shy and nocturnal, preying on rodents, birds and lizards; pairs mate for life. Toward travellers: harmless and elusive — far more often heard or glimpsed than met.

lore.en: Small, cat-like fox of the highlands of Eriador, its white mask and ears standing out sharply against reddish-brown fur. Very shy and nocturnal, it preys on rodents, birds, insects and lizards. Pairs mate for life and generally keep to a single burrow over the course of a year.

aspect.en: The everyday perils of wild country — treacherous ground, hidden drops, rotten ice, deadfalls and the like — that threaten the careless as surely as any beast. Toward travellers: the land itself is often the deadliest thing in it; watch your footing and the weather.

lore.en: The everyday perils of wild country — treacherous ground, hidden drops, rotten ice, deadfalls and the like — that threaten the careless traveller as surely as any beast. The land itself is often the deadliest thing in it.

aspect.en: A small black bat that rarely troubles people unless trapped or panicked, but is a notorious carrier of fleas and parasites left behind in camps and empty dwellings — a common source of "Cyclic Fever." Toward travellers: little direct threat, but a spreader of disease in isolated shelters.

lore.en: A small black creature, the Pond Bat rarely attacks Men or Elves unless panicked and confused, or trapped. It is, however, a noted carrier of fleas and other parasites, which it leaves in isolated dwellings and camps. Thus, they are a common cause of Cyclic Fever.

aspect.en: Wild snakes of grass, rock and water — most shy and harmless, some venomous — basking on warm stones and slipping away from heavy feet, striking only when cornered or trodden on. Toward travellers: easily avoided, but a venomous kind underfoot is a real danger.

lore.en: Wild snakes of grass, rock and water, most shy and harmless but some venomous. They bask on warm stones and slip away from heavy feet, striking only when cornered or trodden upon.

aspect.en: Border-wardens of Gondor who hold its southern fortresses and patrol the desert roads, keeping the contested marches nominally in hand — thin on the ground and often harried by nomads and enemy agents. Toward travellers: vigilant, hard-pressed king's men; allies to the lawful, sharp with the suspicious.

lore.en: Gondor maintains border fortresses like Amon Eithel and patrols the Hyarmenti road to keep the Aegardh nominally under control; these rangers are thin on the ground and frequently harassed by nomads, Haruze and Umbarean agents.[file:73]

aspect.en: Reclusive Snow-elves of the far polar wastes, keeping an enchanted ice-city and patrolling the frozen north, guarding an ancient radiance and rarely meddling in mortal affairs. Toward travellers: remote, seldom-seen guardians of the ice; aloof, but not hostile to those who mean no harm.

lore.en: The Lossidil Snow-elves maintain Helloth, an enchanted ice city on the Landless Land, and patrol the polar wastes and Talath Uichel's far north, guarding Helecthil's radiance and intervening occasionally in mortal affairs.[file:39]

aspect.en: A monstrous bluish-grey bear of the southern White Mountains that can sense living things nearby by instinct and often attacks without provocation, fiercely territorial even against Men and Elves. Toward travellers: unusually aggressive — a bear that may hunt or charge people unprovoked, and very dangerous.

lore.en: Monstrous, bluish-grey bear (Q. "Megliluine") found only on the southern slopes of the White Mountains, especially Lamedon (the Morthond Valley) in Gondor. Has a constant innate Presence ability, sensing living beings up to 50 ft. Often attacks without provocation; usually solitary but will hunt in family groups, defending territory even against Men and Elves.

aspect.en: The largest of the true (non-monstrous) "animal" spiders — deep green above and pale below, near-invisible in forest foliage. It hangs above animal trails and drops onto passing prey, injecting a powerful shrinking venom. Toward travellers: a hidden ambush hunter of the woods, dangerous if it drops unseen onto a passer-by.

lore.en: Gelyngyl (S. "Green Spiders"; sing. "Galungol") are the largest of the so-called "Animal Spiders"—that is, Spiders that are not monsters. Deep green on top and light green on their undersides, they are difficult to discern in a thick forest. Their coloring, coupled with their arboreal nature, makes them very hard (-20) to discern when they are in their natural habitat. Hiding in dense foliage, the rapacious Galungol hangs above animal trails and other areas where its prey might be active, waiting to drop upon unwary victims. Then it injects a powerful (6th lvl) reduction poison into any soft tissue it can find, immobilizing its potential kill before carrying it off to the Spider's web home. Gelyngyl webs are located in clusters set high in the trees. Unlike most of its relatives, Green Spiders are exceptionally social and are prone to attack and feed in groups of ten or more. Acting in unison, they are capable of surrounding and herding their victims into traps. Each Galungol has a pad on each of its four rear legs, and the Spider can rub its legs together to create the sounds with which it communicates.

aspect.en: A small, vividly-marked lizard of Harad — dull yellow with a black-and-red striped head and an orange arrow-shape on its back, about a foot long. It has no natural predators because it tastes vile and oozes a mild nerve-toxin from its skin that paralyses for a time. Toward travellers: not aggressive, but handling one risks a numbing paralysis from its skin.

lore.en: The Zurku (Ap. "Trail lizard"; pl. "Zurkuvi") is found throughout Harad, particularly in the south. It is related to the Gorbet of northwestern Endor (Gorbets are especially well known in Dunland). A dull yellow color with black and red stripes on its head and neck, the Zurku is a colorful creature; it has a bright orange, arrow-shaped patch on its back. It typically grows to a length of 12" and can be found in the summer months. The lizard has no natural enemies because it tastes terrible and secretes a mild nerve toxin from its skin; the poison is absorbed through the skin and paralyzes victims for 10-20 minutes (it numbs the limbs of larger attackers for only awhile, but for most animals is an effective deterrent). What is notable about this relatively harmless lizard is its reputation as a pathfinder: it is believed by most Haradrim that if they are lost and follow a Zurku, it will lead them to a trail or road. This legend is shared by the Dunlendings and appears to have originated among the ancient Southrons during the early Second Age. There may be some truth to this belief, since the Zurku apparently understands that where there are trails there are beasts (and beast-droppings), and where there are beasts there are flies.

aspect.en: Tinkers and peddlers who move steading to steading along the roads, doing odd jobs, selling small goods and carrying news and gossip. Toward travellers: friendly and talkative, a ready source of local news and rumour, and welcome company on the road.

lore.en: Tinkers and peddlers move from steading to steading along hardpacked and paved roads, doing odd jobs, selling goods and carrying news and gossip. They are described as friendly and talkative, equal in information value to merchants and often more approachable, shaping the social fabric of the hills.[file:179]

aspect.en: Folk who live by the water — netting fish, gathering shellfish along the shores, poling boats through the shallows — weathered, close-knit, and reading the water better than any map. Toward travellers: settled waterside folk, helpful for passage and food, keeping to their own stretch of bank or coast.

lore.en: Folk who live by the water — netting fish in river and lake, gathering shellfish and shrimp along the shores, and poling boats through the shallows. Weathered and close-knit, they keep to their own stretch of bank or coast and read the water better than any map.

aspect.en: Groves and wild stands harvested for nuts — beech-mast, hazel and walnut — gathered in autumn for food, oil and trade, the mast also fattening the pigs loosed to forage. Toward travellers: a welcome source of food in season, and a sign of woods worked by nearby folk.

lore.en: Groves and wild stands harvested for nuts — beech-mast, hazel and walnut — gathered in autumn for food, oil and trade. The mast also fattens the pigs turned loose to forage in the woods.

aspect.en: Animated bare bones, flesh long gone, held together by evil power — they rush at the living with teeth and claws, and their lords still bear grave-weapons and simple magic; they feel no pain or bleeding. Toward travellers: a terrifying, relentless attacker, unsettling but mindless.

lore.en: Skeletons are similar to Ghouls, except that they have been picked clean of all flesh. Somehow their bleached bones hang together, animated by evil forces. While not as inherently disgusting as Ghouls, the sight of an animated Skeleton bearing weapons is still terrifying. The common Skeleton attacks alter the manner of a Ghoul, rushing headlong at its foe and using i t s teeth and claws. Skeleton Lords often bear the weapons that were buried w i t h them and can utilize simple magical items. Having no organs or blood. Skeletons are not affected by bleeding criticals, and all Puncture criticals become Crushes.

aspect.en: Tall, feather-crowned palms of the warm southern coasts and river-mouth oases, marking irrigated gardens and orchards in Lamedon and the Ethir Anduin and giving sweet fruit, shade and fibre. Toward travellers: harmless; a welcome source of food and shade in warm country.

lore.en: Date palms grow along the warm southern coasts of Gondor and in sheltered river-mouth oases. In Lamedon and the Ethir Anduin their tall, feather-fronded crowns mark irrigated gardens and estate orchards, providing sweet fruit, shade and fibre.

aspect.en: Tilled fields of wheat, barley, rye and oats — a patchwork of green and gold dotted with farmsteads and granaries in season. Toward travellers: a sign of settled, fed country, and once the harvest is in, a tempting target for raiders.

lore.en: Tilled fields of wheat, barley, rye and oats that feed the settled folk. In season the land is a patchwork of green and gold dotted with farmsteads and granaries — and a tempting target for raiders once the harvest is in.

aspect.en: A large carnivorous bat of the White Mountains, drawn to the smell of blood — it pounces on a bleeding victim and tears flesh with razor teeth, and spreads disease; it haunts cave-mouths, cliffs and ruins. Toward travellers: dangerous to the wounded, swarming onto anything that bleeds in its haunts.

lore.en: A large, carnivorous bat of the White Mountains, Hunting Bats are attracted to the smell of blood. They will pounce upon a bleeding victim, tearing flesh from bone with their small, razor-sharp teeth. In addition, they are notorious carriers of disease. Hunting Bats usually dwell near the entrance of a cave (on the inside, of course), but they can also be found in the crevices of cliffs and in abandoned buildings.

aspect.en: Dark-scaled lizards of rocky, broken country, basking by day and sheltering in crevices — most harmless insect-hunters, though larger kinds take small prey. Toward travellers: harmless to people, a sign of dry, stony ground.

lore.en: Dark-scaled lizards of rocky, broken country, basking by day and sheltering in crevices. Most are harmless hunters of insects, though larger kinds will take small prey.

aspect.en: Freshwater kin of the water-drakes, dwelling in shallows and lakes and lairing near water. Toward travellers: a dangerous water-dragon of rivers and meres.

lore.en: Rain-drakes (Q. "Aelinileki") are relatives of the true Water-drakes that dwell in fresh water, spending much time in shallows and building lairs near it.

aspect.en: The High Elves of Círdan's Grey Havens, who keep the western tower and road and crew the grey ships that bear the Eldar over Sea into the West. Toward travellers: ancient, serene and bittersweet sea-elves; courteous but remote, their faces ever turned toward the West.

lore.en: High Elves of Cirdan's haven who keep watch over the Elostirion tower and the western road, and crew the grey ships — the Sunset-rounders that bear the Eldar from the Grey Havens into the Undying West.

aspect.en: A wandering Elven sage — keeper of histories, songs and ancient craft — journeying between libraries, ruins and the houses of the Wise, who remembers Ages Men have wholly forgotten. Toward travellers: gracious and generous with knowledge to the courteous, a priceless source of lore and counsel.

lore.en: A wandering Elven sage — keeper of histories, songs and ancient craft — journeying between libraries, ruins and the houses of the Wise. Met on the road or at a hearth, a loremaster trades knowledge freely with the courteous and remembers Ages that Men have wholly forgotten.

aspect.en: A huge (nine-foot) tree-dwelling predator of southern rainforest, immensely strong and colour-shifting to match its surroundings, with friction-padded feet that let it cling to any vertical surface — a deadly, agile climber that hunts large mammals. Toward travellers: a dominant ambush hunter of the canopy, lethal and very hard to see.

lore.en: The Slow-fang is one of the most dangerous and dominant creatures in the rain forests of southern Endor. Large (9' long) and exceptionally strong, it lives in trees and hunts large mammals and smaller reptiles. Its body coloration varies with the surface it happens to cross, although it is usually brownish and has mottled green stripes. They have friction pads on their feet and specialized scales that enable them to stick to vertical surfaces for indefinite periods, making them naturally agile tree-climbers; this impairs their movement on the jungle floor, where they are awkward runners. Endowed with a strong, 6' long prehensile tongue that acts like a whip or bola, they can strike a foe quickly. Then they bite the immobilized victim with a pair of 7" fangs, injecting a mild (2nd lvl) muscle poison; this disables the prey long enough for the Slow-fang to slowly discard any inedible trappings (e.g., clothing) before swallowing the meal in one long gulp.
