aspect.en: Smooth-barked hardwoods with dense high canopies over a carpet of leaf-litter, lingering in upland groves and ravines of southern Gondor amid cleared farmland — a mark of older, cooler forest. Toward travellers: harmless; pleasant shade and a sign of remnant old woodland.

lore.en: Beeches are smooth-barked hardwoods with dense, high canopies and a carpet of leaf-litter beneath. In southern Gondor they linger in upland groves and ravines, marking older, cooler forest pockets amid cleared farmland.

aspect.en: Smooth-trunked, beech-like trees with tight crowns that interweave with the furry oaks to form the shadowed, fog-bound forest of Mirkwood's southern eaves. Toward travellers: harmless, but part of what makes that forest dim, tangled and disorienting.

lore.en: Companion beech-like trees with smooth trunks and tight crowns that interweave with furry oaks. Together they form the shadowed, foggy forest typical of the southern eaves of Mirkwood.

aspect.en: Shaggy, black-horned goats descended from escaped domestic stock, ranging all over Middle-earth — nimble climbers and strong swimmers, though slowed in boggy ground. Toward travellers: harmless; a sign of rough, broken country.

lore.en: Essentially descendants of various escaped domestic varieties, the Wild Goats have dirty, shaggy coats and short, black horns. They range all over Middle-earth. Their small, sharp hooves make them agile climbers, and they can swim remarkably well; however, they restrict the beasts' movements in the boglands, where wide feet provide stability in the muck.

aspect.en: Riders and military columns of Rohan and Gondor moving along the Great West Road — couriers, troops and supply trains, especially in time of war. Toward travellers: purposeful and in haste; no threat to honest folk, but they will question strangers near the war-roads.

lore.en: Anórien's Great West Road is heavily used by Gondorian messengers and troops, and during the War of the Ring the Rohirrim ride through its northern strip on their way to Minas Tirith; Tolkien explicitly describes the beacon fires behind Anórien and the riders answering them.[web:234][web:235] The region's population therefore includes transient military columns and supply trains on top of the resident peasantry.

aspect.en: An ugly, scaleless cavern-fish common in Moria — eyes set atop its head and gaping shark-like jaws of many rows of teeth, colourless but for a bright red jaw and luminous flicking fins; it can swallow a goat whole or take off a leg in seconds. Toward travellers: a lethal lurker of dark underground water, where a single bite can maim or kill.

lore.en: Ugly, scaleless cavern fish especially common in Moria, with eyes set on top of its head and gaping shark-like jaws of up to seven rows of teeth (harmless to Dwarves). Colorless save for a bright red jaw and luminescent fins that flick brilliantly in dark water; it swallows a dog or goat whole or devours a Dwarf's leg in seconds.

aspect.en: "Iron Unbirds" — unique warm-blooded reptiles akin to flightless birds, found almost everywhere but the coldest lands; deep grey or black with bright red eyes, in kinds that run on four legs, run on two, or hop. Toward travellers: a strange, hardy beast of the wilds; most are no great threat, though their oddness unsettles.

lore.en: Found virtually anywhere in Middle-earth, save in the coldest climes, the Angusaiwë (Q. "Iron Unbirds"; pl. "Angusaiwéli") is the most resilient, advanced, and common of the larger Rávatsar. This is due to the fact that they are, unlike any other reptile or amphibian, warm-blooded. The Angusaiwéli constitute a unique branch of the Rávatsar and are closely related to flightless birds; thus their name. There are nine species: those that run on four legs (three species), those that run on two legs (five species), and those that hop (one species). All are deep grey or black with bright red eyes. The two-legged species walk upright using their tails for balance and can travel over rugged terrain at speeds exceeding 35 miles an hour. Poisonous carnivores, Unbirds hunt lizards, frogs, birds, large insects, and small mammals, swallowing smaller prey whole. Against larger foes they bare hollow, needle-like fangs and inject a potent (3rd lvl) venom that immobilizes (1-100 rds with RR failure 01-65) or kills (1-10 rds with RR failure 66+). Aside from their speed, they rely on cunning and horny body armor, with a ridge of pointed scales and scales as tough as iron.

aspect.en: A broadleaf evergreen with holly-like leaves and hanging blood-red flowers, whose nectar makes a dark, mildly intoxicating red honey prized by the Beijabar for mead. Toward travellers: harmless; a source of fine honey and a sign of bee-keeping folk nearby.

lore.en: A broadleaf evergreen with large, holly-like leaves and downward-hanging blood-red flowers. Its nectar yields a dark red honey that can be mildly intoxicating, prized by the Beijabar for brewing magnolia mead.

aspect.en: Domesticated cattle of the Wilderland — dark-brown bodied with paler legs and brows, the bulls bearing large curving horns; they migrate with the seasons and roam widely. Toward travellers: ordinary herd-cattle, harmless unless a bull is provoked.

lore.en: The Auroch (pl. "Aurych") is a domesticated breed of the wild cattle or Kine that roam Rhovanion (Wilderland). They vary in color, but most have medium length, dark brown fur on their bodies, and shorter, whiter fur on their legs and foreheads. Males have larger, curving, conical horns. Like all Kine, Aurych migrate with the seasons and tend to wander wide areas whenever breeding.

aspect.en: A smaller highland cousin of the plains snake (2-3 feet), denning under rocks and in caves of cold uplands and northern wastes; easily angered and quick to bite, with a venom weaker and slower-acting than its lowland kin's. Toward travellers: a venomous hazard among highland rocks, defending itself viciously.

lore.en: The Nethairin Erdyr (sing. "Nathair Ardor") live in burrows beneath rocks or within caverns and favor highland locales or the cool wastelands of the North. While very similar in coloration to the Nathair of the Plains, the Nathair Ardor attains a length of only 2-3 feet. It angers easily and will defend itself viciously. Its poison is similar to that of the common Nathair, however it is weaker (5th lvl) and takes longer (6 vs 2 minutes) to affect the victim.

aspect.en: A hardy yellow-flowering herb of fields and river-banks, its seeds and leaves used in poultices and teas to ease fevers, clear the chest and restore appetite; common in the Anduin vales and farmlands. Toward travellers: harmless and useful, a familiar healing herb of settled country.

lore.en: A hardy yellow-flowering herb of fields and river-banks whose seeds and leaves are used in poultices and teas to ease fevers, clear the chest and restore appetite. Common in the Anduin vales and Talath Harroch farmsteads.

aspect.en: A giant pronghorn antelope of the Eriadoran highlands — about four feet tall, dull yellow with short black horns and a conspicuous white rump — travelling in inquisitive but skittish herds and bolting at great speed when alarmed. Toward travellers: harmless; a swift, wary grazer that flashes its white tail and flees.

lore.en: The Astabanhe or Giant Pronghorn is an antelope-like creature found mainly in the Pinnath Ceren (S. "Red Fells") and the Girithlin highlands of Eriador. They stand about 4' tall and are dull yellow in color. While renowned for their loud white rump, their short black horns give the Astabanhéli their name. Pronghorns travel in small herds (10-100) and are inquisitive, but they are quick to flee. Movements of their white tail fur signal danger when there is danger or when they have taken to flight. They can travel at speeds of up to forty miles per hour and can swim quite well.

aspect.en: The smallest of the fishing-birds and the most beautiful — a jewel of silver, blue, orange and white perched by the water, diving for fish, insects and small lizards; its riverbank nest, though, is a foul hole of bones and rot. Toward travellers: harmless, a bright flash of colour along any river.

lore.en: The smallest of Endor's fisherfowl, the Kingfisher is also the most attractive. It has a large, silvery bill and silver, blue, orange and white feathers. The Kingfisher's riverbank home belies its beauty, though, for it is little more than a dirty hole full of old fish bones and rotting mess. Besides fish, the Kingfisher preys on insects, centipedes, and small lizards and amphibians.

aspect.en: The deadliest sharks of the seas — "White Sea-death" to the Elves — large (fifteen feet and more), tireless and always hungry, tearing apart anything with flesh, even wounded whales, with rows of replaceable triangular teeth. Toward travellers: a lethal hunter of any open or coastal water; nothing afloat or swimming is safe near it.

lore.en: Elves call the deadliest of Endor's Sharks Nímaeargurth: "White Seadeath" (pl. "Nímaeargyrth"). Typically large (15+ feet) and always hungry, these unsleeping killers hunt virtually anything that has flesh that they can tear apart and eat. Even wounded Whales have felt the wrath of these white (underparts) and grey (overparts) denizens of the sea. The Nímaeargurth's long, pointed snout is equipped with nine rows of flat, triangular teeth. Those of the outermost row are six to eight inches long. When broken off, the teeth are replaced by those of the next row, enabling the Shark to replenish its saw-like weaponry. Like all Sharks, the Nímaeargurth is a cartilage-skeletoned fish. It bears live young, usually in litters of 7-9 Sharklings.

aspect.en: Northmen who dwell in and beneath the trees of Mirkwood as loose clans of hunters and gatherers — fair, strong and bearded, and expert climbers at home in the branches. Toward travellers: self-reliant forest folk, wary of strangers but fair to those who respect the woods, and foes of the forest's evils.

lore.en: The Woodmen are Northmen who have long lived in Mirkwood, the great forest in Rhovanion. They are a loose tribe of hunter/gatherers who live in or below the trees as extended families, bands, or clans. Physical Character: Average to stocky, with strong but angular features and large amounts of facial hair. Fair skin with reddish highlights. They have blond hair and blue or green eyes. Average endurance. Men average 6'1", women 5'5". Lifespan: 45-85 years. They can climb and move along tree limbs exceedingly well: +20 to Climbing and Acrobatics maneuvers. +10 to Foraging maneuvers. They wear crude woolen tunics and short pants with leggings. Most favor coats, cloaks, and fur hats. They are an independent lot who have no formal political structure. Living off the gifts of the forest, they reside in small, close groups secluded from other races. They interact with few other than the Beornings and Silvan Elves. Woodmen hate Orcs, Wargs, Trolls, and Giant Spiders.

aspect.en: The ordinary folk of the settled lands — farmers, herders, townspeople, traders and drifters of mixed ancestry who make up most of the population. No single people, but the everyday humanity of road and field. Toward travellers: reactions range from open hospitality to wary suspicion with the times and the place.

lore.en: A broad label for the Common Men of Eriador and Gondor: the rural and urban folk of mixed stock who make up the bulk of the ordinary population, including farmers, herders, townsfolk, traders and the rootless roles of road and frontier. They are not a single lineage but the everyday people among whom the older Edain, Dunedain and Dunnish bloodlines have long mingled.

aspect.en: Meadows, woods and tended gardens worked for herbs — for medicine, cooking, dye and craft — whose healing simples are valued far beyond the region. Toward travellers: a source of remedies and food for those who know the plants, and a sign of herb-wise folk nearby.

lore.en: Meadows, woods and tended gardens worked for herbs — for medicine, cooking, dye and craft. Herb-wives know the right seasons and places, and healing simples from such lands are valued far beyond the region.

aspect.en: Blood-drinking apes of a far-southern jungle who once destroyed the Men and Elves that tried to settle there — fiercely territorial, living chiefly on blood, and taking horrible vengeance on any who kill one of their own, leaving drained corpses on display. Toward travellers: a deadly, vengeful jungle-dweller; to enter their forest or harm one is to invite slaughter.

lore.en: Blood-drinking apes of the Tanturak jungle of the Mumakan in southernmost Endor, who defeated the Men and Elves that once sought to settle the region. Intensely territorial, they will not leave their jungle unless food becomes scarce; blood is their primary and preferred nutrition, though they eat flesh in lean times. Fiercely protective of their own, they exact horrible vengeance on any who kill one of their kind, leaving the blood-drained corpses of their victims where other would-be exterminators are sure to see them.

aspect.en: Huge pale-grey or white bears of the icy northern bay — solitary, superb swimmers with a keen nose that scents intruders from miles off, living mostly on seal and fish across wide coastal territories. Toward travellers: avoid people, but immense and dangerous if met — and they know you are coming long before you see them.

lore.en: Huge, pale-grey or white bears (Q. Megliformen) found around the Ice Bay of Forochel. Usually solitary, with an excellent sense of smell and superb swimming, they subsist mainly on seal and fish and range across well-defined coastal territories of about a hundred square miles, smelling intruders up to two miles off. In the brief northern summer they wander beyond their range to find a mate and gorge on roots and berries.

aspect.en: Huge ocean eels of warm southern reefs — among the most dangerous of sea-beasts, ever-hungry, preying on sharks and battling kraken and whales for the deep waters, fiercest in spring. Toward travellers: a grave peril to any boat or swimmer in their reef-waters.

lore.en: Huge ocean-dwelling Eels, the Carnantor (Q. "Red Maws"; sing. "Carnanto") are among the most dangerous of water beasts. They reside in the reefs in the eastern portions of the South Sea (S. "Haragaer") and the southern reaches of the East Sea (Q. "Romenear"), favoring the ample shelter, rich food sources, and warm waters off Endor southeastern coast. These seemingly ever-hungry denizens of the undersea shelf subsist on sharks and other large fish, battling Kraken, Whales, and Fell Turtles for control of the waters. Carnantor are particularly dominant and dangerous in the spring, when the Eels return to their spawning grounds off the coasts of Waw, Cevra, Arth, and Vulm Shryac, crowding the reefs and feeding and mating in an awe-inspiring frenzy. The male is up to 12 feet long, while the female reaches lengths of 45 feet.

aspect.en: A band of folk travelling the roads together — players, pilgrims, displaced families or companions on a long road — sharing fire and the safety of numbers. Toward travellers: friendliness and fortunes vary, but a company on the move always carries news from afar and welcomes company on a lonely stretch.

lore.en: A band of folk travelling the roads together — players, pilgrims, displaced families or companions on a long road, sharing fire and protection in numbers. Their fortunes and friendliness vary, but a company on the move always carries news from afar.

aspect.en: A truly red-furred, prized fox of the Rohan plains — cleverer than the common kind, wily about Men and traps, a canny thief of hens, rabbits and small bright things, and (rare among beasts) able to see some colour. Toward travellers: harmless and elusive, a sly raider of coops rather than any danger.

lore.en: Unlike the common variety, the Red Fox of Calenardhon has truly red rather than rust-coloured fur, making it a prized fur target. Fortunately it is also cleverer than the average fox, wily about avoiding Men and traps, and rarely stumbles into death, so it must be actively hunted. A canny thief, it steals hens, rabbits and small bright objects, and unlike most carnivores enjoys some colour vision.

aspect.en: Huge carnivorous whales of the icy northern bay, white or grey, with five-inch teeth that shear steel and jaws that can swallow a man whole; they shatter boats and overturn ships. Toward travellers: catastrophic to any vessel — a leviathan that wrecks ships and devours the crew.

lore.en: Huge carnivorous white or grey creatures of the Ice Bay of Forochel, with five-inch steel-tearing teeth that can swallow a man whole (survival in the acidic stomach being unlikely). They often shatter whale-boats or overturn larger vessels.

aspect.en: The tortured spirits of men lost in desert sandstorms, lingering as whirlwind-like beings that roam the wastes hunting victims to engulf within their swirling form. Toward travellers: a deadly haunt of the open desert — a living sandstorm that seeks out and smothers the lone wanderer.

lore.en: Tortured spirits of Men who died in desert sandstorms, lingering as whirlwind-like beings that roam the open wastes searching for victims, whom they envelop within their swirling form.

aspect.en: A rare, magnificent white hart — the largest and most imposing deer of the northwest, with a lustrous silver pelt, haunting ancient forests like the Old Forest and Fangorn. Reputed to be mystical; hunted for its prized pelt and for horns said to brew an age-slowing potion. Toward travellers: shy and elusive, a near-mythical glimpse rather than any threat.

lore.en: Larger and rarer than Elk, the Nimfiara (S./Du. "White Hart") is the strongest and most imposing breed of Deer found in northwestern Middle-earth. Reputedly mystical creatures, they range in the ancient woodlands of Rhovanion, Gondor, Calenardhon, and Eriador, and are found deep within the Old Forest and the Dark Wood, and a few have been spotted in Fangorn. The Nimfiara's lustrous silver pelt is prized for fine garments, so it is hunted and trapped by woodsmen. Worse, its horns are said to produce a potion which retards aging. Thus, the beast's value threatens its survival and, aside from the inaccessibility of their habitat, the Nimfiara has few defenses against extinction. They are, however, very wily, and they will put up a good fight when cornered.

aspect.en: Yellow-and-black striped but furry like true bees, nesting in abandoned burrows; social insects whose well-hidden nests are hard to spot, and when one is disturbed the swarm boils out to mob the intruder. Toward travellers: a hidden hazard underfoot — a careless step can bring a storm of stings.

lore.en: Striped with bright yellow and black like their distant cousins the yellowjackets, but fuzzy like any true bee, Ground Bees make their nests in abandoned burrows previously belonging to such creatures as Rabbits, Ground Squirrels, and Culcarnix. They are social insects who present a hazard because of their numbers and astounding coordination. Worse, their carefully hidden nests are hard (-20) to spot; when any unfortunate being steps in or near the nest, the Ground Bees, warned by the vibrations, swarm out and mob the unlucky intruder. Multiple stings can cause temporary weakness and even paralysis. Like other Bees, Ground Bees produce honey, but their underground location makes the prospect of stunning the Bees with smoke and harvesting the honey rather unattractive, so any Ground Bees that have made their nests far from Bear-infested regions (such as forests or hills) can hoard their treasure unmolested.

aspect.en: A highland fox prized as quarry — silvery-grey most of the year and white only in winter (its summer coat even tinges faint green from grass pollen). Dens in shallow burrows, hunting small mammals, ground-birds, eggs and large insects. Toward travellers: harmless and elusive, a hunting foe more than any danger.

lore.en: Found throughout the temperate highlands and northern plains of Middle-earth, the White Fox is especially famous in Calenardhon (Rohan), where it is rare and prized as a hunting foe by Gondorian frontiersmen and Rohir lords. It is only white in winter; its dense pelt is normally bright silvery grey and, like the Grass Cat, picks up grass pollen to look oddly light green, while black-tipped guard hairs keep even the winter coat from being truly white. It dens in shallow burrows and eats small mammals, ground birds and their eggs, and large insects such as grasshoppers.

aspect.en: A lone hobbit far from home — an oddity among his kind, driven by restlessness, exile or some half-mad errand; footsore and out of place yet surprisingly hardy, turning up in the strangest corners of the world. Toward travellers: harmless and out of his depth, but good company and tougher than he looks.

lore.en: A lone Hobbit far from home, an oddity among his kind driven by restlessness, exile or some half-mad errand of the sort that gets a Hobbit 'talked about.' Footsore and out of place yet surprisingly hardy, such wanderers turn up in the strangest corners of the world.

aspect.en: Former soldiers of Angmar settled as freemen in fortified border villages, who farm, patrol daily, escort supply-trains and turn out as troops in war. Toward travellers: hardened soldier-farmers, watchful and disciplined, wary of strangers on the marches.

lore.en: Ex-soldiers of Angmar settled as freemen in fortified villages along the borders; they farm, patrol daily, escort supply trains, and provide additional troops in wartime.

aspect.en: Pallid mushrooms, molds and lichen-growths thriving in the damp, lightless tunnels under the High Pass, feeding on rotting timber, refuse and Goblin leavings. Toward travellers: mostly harmless, but a sign one is in Goblin-haunted tunnels — and some such growths are best not eaten.

lore.en: Goblin-gate cave fungi are a collection of pallid mushrooms, molds and lichen-like growths that thrive in the damp, lightless tunnels under the High Pass. They feed on rotting timbers, refuse and the leavings of Goblin feasts.

aspect.en: The den of some beast or monster — a cave, burrow, ruin or thicket strewn with bones and leavings; to stumble on an occupied one is a peril in itself, and even an empty one may hold a fight or a find. Toward travellers: a dangerous place to blunder into, but sometimes shelter or treasure if its tenant is gone.

lore.en: The den of some beast or monster — a cave, burrow, ruin or thicket strewn with bones and leavings. Stumbling on an occupied lair is a peril in itself, and even an empty one may hold a fight or a find.

aspect.en: A rider bearing messages to and from Minas Ithil — an honest courier of Gondor in the realm's good days, but a servant of the Nazgûl carrying foul word once the tower became Minas Morgul. Toward travellers: in good times a lawful messenger; in evil times something to avoid — its errand is dark.

lore.en: A rider bearing messages to and from Minas Ithil — once a fair tower of Gondor, later the dread Minas Morgul. In the realm's good days an honest courier of the South Kingdom; in its evil days, a servant of the Nazgûl carrying word no honest man should read.

aspect.en: Men who live by the chase — hunting game in forest, hill and fen for meat and hides, skilled with bow and snare and at home far from any settlement, reading sign townsfolk would miss. Toward travellers: self-reliant woodsfolk, helpful and knowledgeable, wary but rarely hostile.

lore.en: Men who live by the chase, hunting game in forest, hill and fen for meat and hides. Skilled with bow and snare and at home in the wild, they range far from any settlement and read sign that townsfolk would never notice.

aspect.en: Captives and subjugated folk of many origins, worked under the lash to support a warrior elite — broken and desperate people. Toward travellers: pitiable more than threatening, but the desperate can turn dangerous, and where they toil their cruel masters are near.

lore.en: Captives and subjugated people from various backgrounds who work the land to support the warrior elite, although the harsh climate forces some warriors to continue agricultural labor.

aspect.en: Wild deer of forest, woodland edge and grassland — swift, wary grazers that bolt at the first hint of danger. Toward travellers: harmless and shy; a mainstay of hunters and a sign of green, living country.

lore.en: Wild deer of the forests, woodland edges and grasslands — swift, wary grazers that flee at the first hint of danger. A mainstay of hunters and predators alike, they range almost everywhere green country is found.

aspect.en: The horse-lords of Rohan — tall, fair, blond and bearded Northmen who live much of the year in seasonal pasture-camps, herding, hunting and fishing; proud riders with old hatreds for Dunlendings and orcs. Toward travellers: hospitable to honest, respectful folk, but suspicious of strangers and swift to challenge intruders on their lands.

lore.en: The Rohirrim (S. "Masters of Horses") are the Northmen of Rohan and have a complex ancestry. They have considerable amounts of facial hair. Blond, with fair skin and blue eyes. Herders and horse-masters, they spend much of their year living in various semi-permanent camps set out on a circuit of pastures. They return to their permanent homes for the winter. Some garden or farm. Most Rohirrim are also accomplished hunters and fishermen. The Rohirrim hate the Dunlendings and consider the Woses as lesser beings. They also have an age-old hatred of Orcs, Wargs, Easterlings, and Dragons.

aspect.en: Disgusting animated corpses with lengthened teeth and nails, preserved by swamp-water or dry air and driven by hunger and territory; stupid and memoryless, they rush and tear with teeth and claws, and their look instils fear. Toward travellers: a mindless, terrifying attacker of graveyards and waste places after dark.

lore.en: Ghouls are disgusting animated corpses that have the lengthened teeth and nails considered typical of a one- or two-month old corpse. They are preserved by the conditions around them, either tannin-loaded swampy water or drying winds, and they are animated by some evil power. Stupid and remembering little if any of their past, Ghouls are dominated by thoughts of hunger for energy and defense of their territory. The average Ghoul simply rushes at its victims, tearing with teeth and nails. Their gruesome appearance i n s t i l l s Fear (victims must make a successful RR or flee), while their filthy and rotting bodies create wounds that often (01-30) become infected. the Undead. They are the single most powerful beings of this nature ever to walk Middle-earth. All nine of these Wraithkings are described in detail in ICE's Lords of Middle-earth, Volume II.

aspect.en: Herds of cattle on meadow and river-plain, raised for beef, hides, milk and labour and driven to market along droving roads. Toward travellers: a mark of local wealth and well-kept land, watched against rustlers.

lore.en: Herds of cattle pastured on meadow and river-plain, raised for beef, hides, milk and draught. Driven to market along the droving roads, they are a mainstay of local wealth and an easy prize for rustlers.

aspect.en: A dark, fine-grained hardwood of Gondor valued for strength and smooth finish, used for walking-sticks, spear-shafts, carved fittings and choice timbers. Toward travellers: harmless; a prized wood marking Gondorian woodland.

lore.en: Lebethron is a dark, fine-grained hardwood of Gondor, valued for its strength and smooth finish. It is used for walking-sticks, spear-shafts, carved fittings and select ship and house timbers.

aspect.en: Soldiers of a Gondorian garrison on their rounds — keeping the walls, roads and watch-posts, checking travellers and watching the borders; disciplined men of the South Kingdom. Toward travellers: courteous to the lawful and hard on the suspect; they will stop and question strangers.

lore.en: Soldiers of a Gondorian garrison out on their rounds — keeping the walls, roads and watch-posts of a town or fortress, checking travellers and watching the borders. Disciplined men of the South Kingdom, courteous to the lawful and hard on the suspect.

aspect.en: Sharp-witted solitary wild foxes of wood, hill and field, hunting rabbits, fowl and mice and scavenging. Bold around farms but quick to vanish. Toward travellers: no threat — more often known by their tracks and raided hen-roosts than by sight.

lore.en: Wild foxes of wood, hill and field — sharp-witted solitary hunters of rabbits, fowl, mice and carrion. Bold around farms and middens, they slip away at the first sign of danger and are more often known by their tracks and raided hen-roosts than by sight.

aspect.en: Fierce steppe nomads of mixed southern blood, the old inhabitants of the Aegardh, now mostly driven east or scattered into small bandit-like groups by Gondorian pressure. Toward travellers: a displaced, hard-pressed nomad folk, some reduced to raiding to survive.

lore.en: Fierce steppe nomads of mixed Haruze and Nórniag lineage, the Eraguk roamed the Aegardh since ancient times as the original inhabitants; after centuries of Gondorian pressure, most were driven east or assimilated, surviving in small, often bandit-style groups by T.A. 1640.[file:73]

aspect.en: Domestic and feral sheep raised across the settled lands for wool, milk and meat — timid and herd-bound. Toward travellers: harmless; a mark of settled pasture, and easy prey that draws wolves and rustlers.

lore.en: Domestic and feral sheep, raised across the settled lands for wool, milk and meat and run half-wild in rougher country. Timid and herd-bound, they are easy prey for wolves and a common target of raiders.

aspect.en: Ghosts wholly decayed into small bright lights that lure the unwary into bogs, quicksand and deep pools, draining their life as they drown or sink. Toward travellers: a beckoning light over the marsh at night that means only death.

lore.en: Ghosts that have wholly degenerated into small bright lights which lure the unwary (5th-level Luring) into bogs, quicksand or deep marsh pools, draining life-energy as the victim drowns or is immobilised.

aspect.en: The many spiders of wood, cave and ruin — most small and harmless, but some grown large and venomous in dark, tainted places, their webs choking old passages and forest hollows. Toward travellers: mostly no threat, but the larger kinds in dark places can bite and bind, and their webs foul the way.

lore.en: The many spiders of wood, cave and ruin, most small and harmless but some grown large and venomous in dark, tainted places. Their webs choke old passages and forest hollows, and the bigger kinds take birds and small beasts.

aspect.en: Northern kin of the dire wolves, built for brutal cold with hollow-haired coats and furred feet — even cleverer and bolder than their southern cousins, preying on anything from rodents and carrion to armed men, and drifting south in harsh winters. Toward travellers: a cunning, fearless pack-hunter of the snows, dangerous to lone or weakened folk.

lore.en: Northerly kin of the Dire Wolves (S. Drauglos, Q. Lossanarmo), distantly related to the common Grey Wolf and true denizens of the cold, thriving at temperatures as low as -60 degrees F. Most at home in the Far North, they have been seen as far south as the Shire in Eriador and the Celduin Valley in Rhovanion during especially bad winters. The harsh fight to survive makes them even cleverer and bolder than Dire Wolves, preying on everything from rodents and carrion to well-armed Lossoth, with a glistening coat of hollow hairs, two-chambered nostrils and furred feet fit for ice and snow.

aspect.en: A small grey snake with a ruff of loose scales that gives a faint rattling sound when startled, native to Rhudaur; its potent venom causes massive internal bleeding and often death. Toward travellers: a deadly bite for so small a snake — heed the dry rattle and give it room.

lore.en: This small, gray snake has a distinctive ruff of loose scales that give off a faint, odd rattling sound when the serpent is startled or about to strike. Its potent venom (level 8) causes massive internal hemorrhage, causing tremendous (24-60 hits) shock and often (with 26+ RR failure) death. The Shaking Asp is a native of Rhudaur, the region in eastern Eriador between the Mitheithel (Hoarwell) and Bruinen (Loudwater) Rivers.

aspect.en: A lesser drake — smaller and weaker than the great dragons, often wingless or fireless, yet still huge, armoured and deadly, lairing in mountain, marsh and waste and raiding herds and folk. Toward travellers: still a mortal danger, hoarding what plunder it can take.

lore.en: A lesser drake — smaller and less mighty than the great dragons, often wingless or fireless, yet still huge, armoured and deadly. Such worms lair in mountain, marsh and waste, raiding herds and folk and hoarding what plunder they can.

aspect.en: Flocks of sheep on hills, downs and rough pasture, worked for wool, milk and meat by shepherds and their dogs. Toward travellers: a sign of peaceful, settled uplands; the wool-clip is a cornerstone of local trade.

lore.en: Flocks of sheep grazing the hills, downs and rough pasture for wool, milk and meat. Shepherds and their dogs work the high ground through the seasons, and the wool-clip is a cornerstone of local trade.

aspect.en: Rough hill-dwelling folk of the uplands — herders, hunters and raiders who answer to clan and feud rather than king, hardy and clannish, holding the high valleys softer folk avoid. Toward travellers: wary of lowlanders and quick to arms; their welcome depends on clan and circumstance.

lore.en: Rough hill-dwelling folk of the upland country — herders, hunters and raiders who answer to clan and feud rather than king. Hardy and clannish, wary of lowlanders and quick to take up arms, they hold the high valleys and moors that softer folk avoid.

aspect.en: The vast hosts of Mordor — orcs, Olog-hai trolls and Easterling and Haradrim auxiliaries — garrisoning the black towers and marching to war. Toward travellers: overwhelming and merciless; to be caught by a marching host of the Enemy is doom.

lore.en: Huge armies of Orcs, Olog-hai (trolls), and Easterling/Haradrim auxiliaries garrisoning the black towers.

aspect.en: Loose stone and scree breaking from cliff and slope — a rattling rockfall or a single plunging boulder that can crush or sweep a climber from a narrow path, worst on weathered crags and after rain or frost. Toward travellers: a sudden danger on mountain ways; move quickly and quietly beneath loose slopes.

lore.en: Loose stone and scree breaking from cliff and slope — a rattling rockfall or a single plunging boulder that can crush or sweep a climber from a narrow path. Worst on weathered crags and after rain or frost.

aspect.en: A snowy-white lion of southwestern Middle-earth, solitary and shy, keeping to near-sheer terrain and hunting at dawn and dusk, striking swiftly at the nape of goats, sheep and small game. Toward travellers: avoids people, but a powerful ambush killer of the crags if surprised.

lore.en: Snowy-white lion (Q. "Rálimba") of southwestern Middle-earth, its core territory around the Bay of Drel and the lower reaches of the Yellow Mountains near Lake Aeluin. Solitary and shy of virtually sheer terrain; active morning and evening, hunting goats, sheep, rodents and carrion, striking swiftly at the nape of its prey.

aspect.en: The tyrant-overlord of Mount Gundabad who claims mastery over all the mountain orc-tribes, ruling a spire-court rife with intrigue, murder and revolt. Toward travellers: a cruel and dangerous orc-lord; to fall into his domain is to face capture or death.

lore.en: Title for the tyrannical overlord who rules Mount Gundabad and claims suzerainty over all Orc tribes of the mountains; his court in the spires is rife with intrigue, assassination, and revolt.

aspect.en: A large fox of the Misty Mountain foothills and chief small predator of Rhudaur — named "changer" for its coat (black in summer, white in winter, striped while moulting), which the superstitious hold sacred and weapon-proof; it eats small game, fruit and carrion. Toward travellers: harmless to people, a wary hunter steeped in local superstition.

lore.en: Large fox (pl. "Gích") found throughout the foothills of the Misty Mountains and the chief small predator of Rhudaur. Its name means "changer": black in summer, white in winter, and striped while moulting, a phase the superstitious Rhudaurans hold sacrosanct and believe weapon-proof. Eats small mammals, eggs, ripe fruit and carrion; its fur is marketable but not especially valuable.

aspect.en: The Lord of the Nazgûl — once the dread king of Angmar who warred on the northern Dúnedain, later the leader of Sauron's armies from Minas Morgul; mightiest of the nine Ringwraiths. Toward travellers: an overwhelming terror beyond any ordinary foe; his presence is paralysing dread, and to be marked by him is doom.

lore.en: The Lord of the Nazgul, the Witch-king who ruled the realm of Angmar against the Dunedain of the North and later led Sauron's forces from Minas Morgul; mightiest of the nine Ringwraiths.

aspect.en: A giant catfish — an ugly, flat-headed brute up to ten feet and hundreds of pounds, with long sensory whiskers, swallowing prey whole and sometimes battering boats to see what spills out. Toward travellers: little threat to a person, but its size can startle and even upset a small boat.

lore.en: A species of giant catfish, the Wels is an ugly brute. They are usually up to 4-5' long, but sometimes reach 10'. A larger Wels weighs nearly 700 lbs. It has a rounded body with a flattened head and a wide, horizontal mouth, around which are two long sensory barbels and four short ones. Wels are known to swallow prey whole and will sometimes bash boats to see what falls out.

aspect.en: Long-legged hares of open down and upland — swifter and warier than rabbits, lying up in shallow forms by day and feeding at dusk, bolting in great bounds when flushed. Toward travellers: harmless; prized game for hawk, fox and hunter.

lore.en: Long-legged hares of open down, plain and upland — swifter and warier than rabbits, lying up in shallow forms by day and feeding at dusk. A staple of hawks, foxes and hunters, they bolt in great bounding leaps when flushed.

aspect.en: A large, tailless, blunt-nosed burrowing rodent of the plains south of Mirkwood — wholly harmless and unaggressive, though it can strip a farm field, often seen sniffing the air atop its burrow-mound. Toward travellers: utterly harmless, a wary, almost comical sight on the open plain.

lore.en: This large, ground-dwelling rodent is found on the Talath Harroch, the plain south of Mirkwood. They are reported to be totally harmless, an opinion which owes much to the lack of farmsteads in the Talath Harroch. Culcarnix can devastate a farm field. Nevertheless, they are totally unaggressive toward other living beings. Tailless and blunt-nosed, Culcarnix live in burrows beneath the earth, and can occasionally be seen standing on the mounds of earth by the entrances to their burrows, sniffing the air for any scent of approaching enemies. They have thick, red-brown fur that has at various times been much in demand by furriers. The Wainriders, for instance, raised them in great numbers for their hides. Thus, they have become scarce in areas where there is widespread settlement.

aspect.en: Gondorian labourers who work the ancient stone quarries on the forest's northern margins. Toward travellers: ordinary working men, no threat — a sign of organized Gondorian industry nearby.

lore.en: Gondorian laborers who occasionally work the ancient limestone quarries (like Nardol Quarry) on the forest's northern margins.

aspect.en: A huge white marsh-bird standing some nine feet tall, swan-necked and long-legged, with a scarlet band across the eyes and a hooked, indigo-ridged beak. Despite the crane-like look it is a true bird of prey, taking snakes, fish and small animals with taloned legs and tearing beak. Toward travellers: wary of people, but its size and beak make it dangerous if provoked.

lore.en: The Jatewoone is also known as the cleaverbeak or marsh bird. Standing 9 feet tall and endowed with Swan-like necks and long, powerful legs, these white waterfowl sport a scarlet band across the eyes. From a distance they might look like a large crane, although they are not of that family. Their beak is a light grey with the exception of the sharp, brilliant indigo dorsal ridge from which they get their name. Birds of prey in every sense, their legs end in talons that can grip even small creatures tightly, and their beaks are made for tearing. Jatewoones live on snakes, fish, and small mammals. Their reputation for hostility comes from their protection of their nests, usually hidden in swampy areas; they will also attack when surprised by noisy people, and can split a skull. They mate for life and produce one or two eggs every year or every other year; the young grow at a remarkable pace. Jatewoones can fly, but if the need to escape danger arises, it is more common to see them running at high speeds, using stillwater areas for cover.

aspect.en: Men who live and work the great rivers — boatmen, ferriers, fishers and traders moving goods and folk by water, knowing every shoal and landing and keeping a shrewd independence from the land's lords. Toward travellers: useful for passage and river-lore, independent-minded but generally fair to honest custom.

lore.en: Men who live and work along the great rivers — boatmen, ferriers, fishers and traders who move goods and folk by water. They know every shoal, landing and backwater, and keep a shrewd independence from the lords of the dry land.

aspect.en: A high-born Elf of one of the great houses, travelling with attendants on errands of state, kinship or lore, bearing authority lightly but unmistakably. Toward travellers: gracious and dignified but remote; a meeting feels like an audience as much as an encounter.

lore.en: A high-born Elf of one of the great houses, travelling with attendants between the Elven realms on errands of state, kinship or lore. Met in Lindon, the Ered Luin and the eastern woods alike, such a lord or lady bears authority lightly but unmistakably.

aspect.en: A vicious freshwater fish — "the shark of the rivers" — with powerful jaws and wicked teeth that lock on and won't let go, growing up to seven feet in some rivers; it rarely attacks swimmers, preying on fish and small mammals. Toward travellers: little threat to people, but a fierce fighter and a danger to small creatures at the water's edge.

lore.en: The Pike is vicious, and is renowned as the shark of the freshwaters. It has a powerful jaw and wicked teeth, and once it has a hold it will not let go unless it is seriously wounded or it succeeds in biting off a healthy piece of its victim. Pike feed on crustaceans and shellfish when young, graduating to larger prey as they age. Adults eat fish and small mammals. Fortunately, Pike rarely attack a swimmer. This is particularly reassuring to the Rivermen of Calenardhon (Rohan), since Pike grow up to 7' in length in the Onodló (Entwash). Note: Once bitten, a victim will not be attacked again, but they must roll an additional attack to knock the fish loose, with no subtractions for DB, armor etc.

aspect.en: The fish of river, lake and sea — from minnows to great pike, salmon and sea-fish — a staple food for folk and beasts alike. Toward travellers: a dependable food source; only the great predators of deep water are any danger.

lore.en: The fish of river, lake and sea — from small fry to great pike, salmon and sea-fish — a staple food for folk and beasts alike. Their abundance shapes where fishers settle, and the greater predators of the deep are not to be taken lightly.

aspect.en: Slug-like blood-sucking creatures of still, marshy water that fasten onto any warm-blooded body, rasp through the skin and gorge until full. A foul nuisance more than a danger. Toward travellers: a hazard of wading or camping by stagnant water, latching on unnoticed.

lore.en: While lauded for its medicinal qualities in some cultures, the Leech is only considered a nuisance in the delta. These nasty, slug-like creatures fasten to anything warm-blooded and use their serrated tongue to rasp through to a blood vessel. Then they remain fixed to their prey, gorging themselves until they are so full they slip off.

aspect.en: The restless dead in many forms — wights, ghosts, ghouls, skeletons and worse — animated by old curses, evil will or the Enemy's malice; cold, tireless and hating the living, haunting barrows, ruins and battlefields mostly by night. Toward travellers: implacably hostile, they do not bargain, only harm.

lore.en: The restless dead in their many forms — wights, ghosts, ghouls, skeletons and worse, animated by old curses, evil will or the malice of the Enemy. Cold, tireless and hateful of the living, they haunt barrows, ruins and battlefields, chiefly by night.

aspect.en: The many woodland birds that gather about Radagast's home, befriended by the bird-tamer — quick to carry word through the forest and serving as his eyes and messengers. Toward travellers: harmless and watchful; through them, friendly word may reach the Brown Wizard.

lore.en: The many woodland birds that gather about Rhosgobel, home of Radagast the Brown, who befriends and speaks with them. Quick to carry word through the forest, they serve as eyes and messengers for the bird-tamer of the Wood.

aspect.en: Nomadic horsemen and chariot-riders who range the open pastures. Toward travellers: a warlike steppe people, raiders quick to fall upon the unwary.

lore.en: Nomadic horsemen and chariot-riders who frequent the pastures.

aspect.en: Lord of Lórien and consort of Galadriel — a wise Sindarin lord who gives the Golden Wood its military and diplomatic leadership and embodies its ancient traditions. Toward travellers: stately and reserved, courteous to the worthy who enter his realm but exacting of any who come uninvited.

lore.en: Lord of Lórien and consort of Galadriel, providing military and diplomatic leadership and embodying Sindarin traditions within the Golden Wood.

aspect.en: Pale, thick-furred great cats of the northern mountains and snow-fields, camouflaged against ice and stone — powerful ambush hunters of goats, deer and elk, seldom seen until they strike. Toward travellers: a stealthy, dangerous predator of the cold heights, rarely seen but deadly when it springs.

lore.en: Pale, thick-furred great cats of the northern mountains and snow-fields, well camouflaged against ice and stone. Powerful ambush hunters of goats, deer and elk, they are seldom seen until they strike.

aspect.en: Handsome ground-birds — the cocks emerald-feathered with long trailing plumes, famed for fierce shoving-duels over mates; tasty but tough, needing to be hung before eating. Toward travellers: harmless; sought as game.

lore.en: The Great Green Pheasant is a handsome bird. Females and their immature offspring sport lustrous bronze-green plumage. Emerald green feathers and long, trailing tail plumes adorn the male. The cocks are famous for their ferocious duels over potential mates: they rush at each other fiercely, broadsiding their rivals in clouds of emerald green down, until one or the other retreats, exhausted and bedraggled. Great Green Pheasants, like the Grass Grouse, are considered tasty, but this larger bird must be hung before eating, as it is tougher (in every way) than the passive Grass Grouse.

aspect.en: The Wood-elves of northern Mirkwood, dwelling in caverns and halls under their king — lovers of feasting, song and tongues, keeping to themselves and largely indifferent to Men and Dwarves unless threatened. Toward travellers: merry among their own but guarded with outsiders, suspicious of strangers in their woods and quick to detain trespassers.

lore.en: Silvan Elves under Thranduil living in caverns and halls near the eastern eaves of the forest, lovers of feasting, song and languages and largely indifferent to neighboring Men and Dwarves unless threatened.

aspect.en: Frontier shepherds and watch-forts of Arthedain's bleak northwestern marches, grazing the uplands and standing as staging-ground and militia against Angmar. Toward travellers: hard-pressed frontier folk and watchmen, wary on an exposed and war-torn border.

lore.en: Frontier shepherds, small steads and watch-forts on the northwestern marches of Arthedain use the fringes of Talath Muil for grazing and as a staging ground, but the bleak climate and exposure prevent large-scale settlement. During the wars with Angmar, local militias are pinned on frontiers and armies cross these uplands, as described in the accounts of battles around Fornost and the Emyn Uial.[file:179][file:132]

aspect.en: Trolls of the deep woods — mossy, bark-hided and blending with the timber until they move, lurking on the southern eaves of Mirkwood and the forest marches. Toward travellers: they ambush those who stray from the path and drag them back to their lairs.

lore.en: Trolls that haunt the deep woods — Mirkwood's southern eaves, Fangorn's marches and the tangled forests of the wild lands. Mossy and bark-hided, they blend with the timber until they move, ambushing travellers who stray from the path and dragging them back to their lairs.

aspect.en: Wingless cold-drakes of the earth, keeping to the northern highlands and plains. Toward travellers: a huge, armoured ground-dragon, deadly if met in its cold country.

lore.en: Land-drakes are one of the three wingless varieties of Cold-drake (Earth element), keeping to northern highlands and plains.

aspect.en: A fair flower of Gondor bearing soft golden trumpets on slender stems, growing in sunny meadows and sheltered coastal lawns, often among alfirin. Toward travellers: harmless and lovely, a mark of gentle, peaceful country.

lore.en: Mallos is a fair flower of Gondor, bearing soft golden trumpets on slender stems. It grows in sunny meadows and sheltered coastal lawns, often mingled with alfirin.

aspect.en: Merchants and settlers of the Celduin valley who came to share in eastern trade — town-dwellers of fortified places, close to Gondor in culture but proud of their Northman roots. Toward travellers: trade-minded townsfolk, generally welcoming to honest dealers.

lore.en: Merchants and settlers from the Nan Celduin valley, speaking Rhovanion and Westron, who came to share in eastern trade and now inhabit fortified towns, culturally close to Gondor but proud of their Northman identity.[file:37]

aspect.en: Folk fleeing pestilence — driven from a stricken town, carrying what little they could and perhaps the sickness itself; desperate and shunned, begging shelter and food. Toward travellers: pitiable but a real danger — the wary turn them away for fear of the plague they may carry.

lore.en: Folk fleeing pestilence — driven from a stricken town or village, carrying what little they could and perhaps the sickness itself. Desperate and shunned, refugees beg shelter and food, and the wary turn them away for fear of what they bring.

aspect.en: Gondorians who garrison the forts and farm the pockets of the eastern marches, guarding the fords and asserting Gondor's claimed dominion. Toward travellers: settled frontier folk and soldiers; correct with the lawful, watchful of strangers near the borders.

lore.en: Gondorians of Calenardhron and Dor Rhûnen who garrison forts like Thorontir and farm pockets such as Tharlorien and the Undeeps, guarding the fords and asserting Gondor's claimed dominion.

aspect.en: A roving Noldor war-band of the Blue Mountains and northern Lindon, watching the passes of the Ered Luin for orcs out of the ruined North and escorting travellers between scattered Elven settlements. Toward travellers: vigilant Elven guards — protective of the free and a help to honest wayfarers, sharp toward anything that smells of the Enemy.

lore.en: A roving war-band of Noldor of Mithrim descent that keeps the old marches of the Blue Mountains and northern Lindon. They watch the passes of the Ered Luin and the wooded vales below for Orcs out of the ruined North, and escort travellers between the scattered Elven settlements.

aspect.en: Light-barked, fast-spreading trees of cooler slopes and disturbed ground, their white trunks and fluttering leaves brightening the higher vales, often in mixed groves with oak and beech. Toward travellers: harmless; bright, open woodland and a sign of cool upland country.

lore.en: Birches are light-barked, fast-colonising trees that favor cooler slopes and disturbed ground. Their white trunks and fluttering leaves brighten Lamedon's higher vales, often forming mixed groves with oak and beech on the edges of older forests.

aspect.en: Sea-raiders who prey on coastal shipping and settlements, putting in to plunder and slipping away with their spoil — lawless and dangerous, sometimes in league with the Corsairs, sometimes for themselves. Toward travellers: a direct danger by sea and shore; they rob, take captives and kill.

lore.en: Sea-raiders who prey on coastal shipping and settlements, putting in to plunder and slipping away with their spoil. Lawless and dangerous, they range the western and southern coasts, sometimes in league with the Corsairs of Umbar, sometimes for themselves alone.

aspect.en: A signal-beacon set on hill or tower, lit in war or need so that warning may leap from height to height across the land — a landmark by day, a summons by night. Toward travellers: harmless in itself; a sign of watch and warding, and word that something is afoot when it burns.

lore.en: A signal-beacon set on hill or tower, lit in time of war or need so that warning may leap from height to height across the land. A landmark by day and a summons by night.

aspect.en: An Elven ship-master of Círdan's folk, commanding one of the grey vessels of the Gulf of Lhûn and the Harlindon coasts — long-sighted and sea-hardened, carrying messages, goods and passengers between the havens, and at the last those bound west. Toward travellers: courteous and capable, a means of passage and sea-lore for the worthy.

lore.en: An Elven ship-master of Cirdan's folk, commanding one of the grey vessels that ply the Gulf of Lhun and the coasts of Harlindon. Long-sighted and sea-hardened, such captains carry messages, goods and passengers between the havens — and, at the last, those bound west.

aspect.en: A person of rank abroad with their retinue — a lord, lady, captain or chieftain on some errand of state, war or kinship, travelling attended and armed. Toward travellers: they expect deference and can prove a powerful friend or a perilous enemy; mind your manners.

lore.en: A person of rank and authority abroad with their retinue — a lord, lady, captain or chieftain on some errand of state, war or kinship. Such folk travel attended and armed, expect deference, and can prove a powerful friend or a perilous enemy.

aspect.en: Orchards and wild fruit-lands bearing apples, plums, berries or olives in season, gathered fresh or pressed and brewed. Toward travellers: a welcome source of food along the road — though bears and other foragers are drawn to the same bounty.

lore.en: Orchards and wild fruit-lands yielding apples, plums, berries or olives in season — gathered fresh, dried, pressed or brewed. A welcome bounty that draws foragers, birds and the occasional bear.

aspect.en: A blinding storm of wind-driven sand and grit that scours skin, chokes the lungs and erases the trail, common in the southern deserts — robbing a caravan of its bearings and burying landmarks in hours. Toward travellers: a disorienting, choking peril of the desert; cover the face, halt, and wait it out.

lore.en: A blinding storm of wind-driven sand and grit that scours skin, chokes the lungs and erases the trail, common in the southern deserts. It can rob a caravan of its bearings and bury landmarks in hours.

aspect.en: Wingless, breathless earth-dragons of the cave-drake kind, dwelling deep underground in cavern systems. Toward travellers: a blind, burrowing horror of the deep places, lethal to any who delve into its tunnels.

lore.en: Wingless, breathless earth-element Drakes of the Cave-drake family that dwell deep underground in cavern systems.

aspect.en: Tall, hedge-forming shrubs or small trees massed with rose, burgundy and white blossom from spring to autumn, their needle-sharp thorns making formidable living walls — first planted by Elves as boundaries, later valued by healers for their nectar. Toward travellers: a thorny barrier to push through, but beautiful and otherwise harmless.

lore.en: Tall, hedge-forming shrubs or small trees bearing masses of rose, burgundy and white blossoms from late spring to autumn. Needle-sharp thorns make them formidable living walls, first planted by Elves as boundaries and later valued by healers for their nectar.

aspect.en: A "forest-strangler" — a fearsome ambush snake of the oases and scattered woods of Far Harad, mottled brown for perfect camouflage. It drops from branches or strikes from pools, gripping prey in powerful jaws and constricting. Toward travellers: a hidden killer of waterside woods, striking from above or below before it is seen.

lore.en: The Petla (pl. "Petlavi"), or "Forest-strangler," of southwestern Endor is commonly found in the scattered woodlands of Far Harad (particularly in the Forest of Tears). It haunts the oases between Umbar and Drel, lurking in the branches and pools that the Haradrim prize so dearly. One of Middle-earth's most fearsome reptiles, the Petla is an able hunter who has perfected the arts of camouflage and ambush. It is mottled brown in color and blends perfectly with woodland hues. Dropping from above or entangling its prey in water, the snake attacks by using its powerful jaws to gain a grip and then coils its length around its hapless victim. Petlavi reach lengths exceeding thirty feet (one specimen measured forty-five), are over a foot wide at their thickest, and have been known to swallow a whole goat. Their principal weapon is their coiling, constricting body: after a grip is taken (typically after a "B" critical), the body coils around the target over one to ten rounds; it is extremely hard (-30) to break free, and the victim perishes by suffocation in three to thirty minutes. Defenseless against groups, the snake will not often stand and fight when confronted by more than one enemy.

aspect.en: A trapping spider quite unlike the web-spinners — it digs a deep pit and roofs it with a camouflaged silk lid hidden under leaves, almost impossible to spot. Anything breaking through falls onto knife-like silk spikes while the spider waits in a side tunnel. Toward travellers: a lethal hidden trap on slopes and trails; the danger is the ground itself.

lore.en: King Spiders are similar to but unlike the Giant Spiders of Mirkwood. They do not build large webs but rather dig deep pits, 2-3 ft wide and 8-10 ft deep. A King Spider caps this pit with a lid cleverly woven from a small amount of spider-silk, disguising the covering with leaves and other vegetation so that it is extremely hard (-30) to detect. Victims falling through the lid receive one to three +25 short sword attacks from the strong, knife-like silk tendrils. The pits are usually built on slopes. They support no more than 40 pounds of weight. The K i n g Spider, who has been waiting in a small side passage, leaps upon the victim and biles it, injecting its special poison, Kennesank. A RR f a i l u r e of 1-50 results in paralysis; a failure of 51+ results in death as the internal organs dissolve. If the victim dies, the spider will eat it. If not, the thrifty spider saves the meal. If it is a female who has recently mated, she may lay 6-12 eggs on top of the helpless prey and leave, sealing the hole more sturdily behind her. In two days, when the spiderlings hatch, they will spend three weeks living on the food left behind by their mother. Surely one of Endor's most vicious insects, the rare but often lethal Hummerhorn is the stuff of legend. Each weighs 6-8 lbs and has a razor sharp, pointed proboscis of chitin (transparent horn). It gores a victim to death, then feasts on the corpse with three sets of mandibles. They resemble gigantic black and grey wasps, and their only failing is the noise they make whenever they approach.

aspect.en: Strange tree-dwelling creatures of remote southeastern islands — four- or five-armed beasts like a cross between a squid and a starfish, green or red-striped, with a beaked mouth and an ink-sac, racing through the forest canopy. Fast carnivores that envelop and immobilise their prey. Toward travellers: alien and predatory, but found only on far-off islands few will ever reach.

lore.en: Strange arboreal creatures (the Slird, pl. "Slirdu") found only in the forests of the remote islands off the southeast coast of Middle-earth, most in colonies of 2-40 on the isle of Vulm Shryac. Green or green-with-red-stripes, they are four- or five-armed invertebrates resembling both squids and starfish, adapted to land with true lungs and a quasi-skeleton of thick insulated nerves; each prehensile arm joins a squid-like trunk holding two eyes, a beak-like mouth and an ink sack. Nesting near treetops and moving fast through the canopy, these true carnivores eat ~20 lbs of meat a day, enveloping prey, immobilising it with suction pads and spraying toxic ink that stuns, blinds or knocks out; their rudimentary nerve-stem brain makes them little more than honed killing organisms.

aspect.en: Easterling warriors of the lands beyond Rhûn who ride under Sauron's banners as auxiliaries — horse-borne, lightly armed, fighting for plunder and dark lords' promises. Toward travellers: hostile raiders of the eastern marches, a danger to any of the free peoples they meet.

lore.en: Warriors of the Asdriag and Sagath, Easterling tribes of the lands beyond Rhûn who serve Sauron's banners as auxiliaries. Horse-borne and lightly armed, they fight for plunder and the promises of dark lords, and trouble the eastern bounds of the free realms.

aspect.en: Worked woodlands felled for timber and firewood, the logs floated downriver to mill and market, with woodcutters' camps and sawpits along the forest edge. Toward travellers: a place of industry and rough company rather than wilderness.

lore.en: Worked woodlands felled for timber and firewood, the logs hauled and floated downriver to mill and market. Woodcutters' camps and sawpits dot the forest edge, and good timber is a steady source of wealth.

aspect.en: Forest-dwelling Elves who never crossed the Sea, living hidden in the deep woods of the East. Slight and lithe, ruddy-skinned with sandy hair, secretive and deeply bound to their woodland realms. Toward travellers: unseen until they choose to be seen; suspicious of strangers in their woods, but not hostile without cause.

lore.en: When the Eldar departed from the original Elven homeland during the Elder Days, a number of their brethren remained behind. They decided not to seek the light of the Aman and were labeled as the Avari (Q. "Unwilling, Refusers"). These kindreds were left to fend for themselves during the days when Morgoth's Shadow swept over the East. During these dark times they were forced into the secluded safety of the forests of eastern Middle-earth, where they wandered and hid from the wild Men who dominated most of the lands. They became known as the Silvan or Wood-elves. Physical Character: Most are slight of build, and all are thin by mannish standards. Ruddy of complexion, with sandy hair and blue or green eyes. Generalizations are difficult, however, since there are many kindreds and there is wide variation among them. Same endurance as for Noldor Elves. Males average 6'0", females 5'9". Same lifespan as for Noldor Elves. Cannot become sick or scarred and are virtually immune to disease. -10 bonus versus cold attacks. Their vision is the same as that of Noldor Elves. The Silvan folk are superb musicians and have tremendous hearing, even for Elves. +10 to Bardic spell attacks. They are also elusive. +10 for trickery and Stalking/Hiding maneuvers. The culture of the Silvan Elves is best characterized as unstructured and rustic by Elven standards, but rich and relatively advanced when compared to the ways of Men. They have always been independent, but as of late many have settled in kingdoms ruled by the Noldor or Sindar. They are met as the common folk of the woodland realms — hunters, foresters and bowmen of Mirkwood, Lorien and the eastern eaves — wary of strangers and seldom straying far from the trees.

aspect.en: A natural cave or cave-system winding into hill and mountain — shelter, lair or hidden way, dark and easy to be lost in, drawing beasts, outlaws and miners alike. Toward travellers: useful shelter or passage, but the deeper dark holds its own perils and unknown tenants.

lore.en: A natural cave or cave-system winding into hill and mountain — shelter, lair or hidden way, dark and easy to be lost in. Caverns draw beasts, outlaws and miners alike, and the deeper ones hold their own perils.

aspect.en: The "High Elves" — the noblest and most learned of Elf-kind in Middle-earth, the only ones who once dwelt in the Blessed Realm, close to the Valar and unmatched in craft, lore and war. Toward travellers: proud, ancient and formidable; gracious to the worthy, but carrying a weight of age and command that holds mortals in awe.

lore.en: The Noldor are often called "High Elves" or "Deep Elves", ostensibly because they are considered to be the most noble of the Quendi in Middle-earth. In reality, they are so named because they are the only Elves living in Endor who have ever resided in the Blessed Realm of Aman across the sea. This exalted status is accentuated by their close ties with the Valar, a relationship which accounts for their unique cultural and linguistic roots. Other names for the Noldor include Deep-elves, Golodhrim or Gelydh (Sindarin labels), and Nómin (Edain label). Physical Character: Of all the Elves, the Noldor are the strongest and sturdiest of build, although they are still slimmer than Men. Most are dark haired and have greyish eyes which betray a proud looking manner. Descendants of the Fingolfin and Finarfin are often fair haired and blue eyed, for their blood contains Vanyar influences. They do not carry great burdens, but they are capable of traveling 16-20 hours a day. The Noldor do not sleep; instead they rest in a trance for 1-3 hours a day. Males average 6'7", females 6'3". Immortal and will only die due to violence or if they weary of life and lose the will to live. Cannot become sick or scarred and are virtually immune to disease. +20 bonus versus cold attacks. Unparalleled at understanding and working with crafts. +20 for Item Use rolls. Across Endor they are met in different guises: as lords, smiths and loremasters in Lindon, Rivendell and the ruined craft-halls of Eregion, and as wary wandering companies, scouts or exiles in the wild lands between.

aspect.en: The largest cattle in Middle-earth — great white oxen said to be a gift of the Vala Oromë, found by the Sea of Rhûn and the eastern plains. Revered by some peoples and used by the Easterlings as powerful draught-beasts to haul their great wains. Toward travellers: placid and imposing; a wonder to see, and sacred to many who herd them.

lore.en: The Kine of Araw are the largest of Middle-earth's bovids, that is creatures with split, even-toed hoofs. It is believed that these large, white cattle are the gift of the Vala Oromë (Araw). This is quite possibly true. The beasts are found on the shores of the Sea of Rhûn and on the Plain of Talath Harroch, east and south of Mirkwood. As far as anyone can tell, the Easterling tribes are the only people to have domesticated these creatures and used them as draft beasts, since the Rhovanion Northmen revered the Kine and used them only for breeding other cattle. Easterlings employed Kine to pull the Great Wains of their chiefs. During the brief existence of the Wainrider Kingdom in Wilderland (T.A. 1854-99), dozens of these magnificent beasts were pressed into service, and many perished in the raiding and wars that accompanied the Wain-easterlings' occupation. Many people of central Middle-earth value the long gray horns of these cattle, both to use as trumpets and drinking horns and to cut into sections for superb compound bows.

aspect.en: A slender-leaved, sweet-scented healing herb found along old roads, in sheltered dells and near springs — to most a humble plant for poultices, but in the hands of a true king or great healer its leaves, steeped in hot water, can call the wounded back from the shadow. Toward travellers: harmless and precious, a herb of healing for those who know its worth.

lore.en: Athelas, or Kingsfoil, is a slender-leaved healing herb found along old ways, in sheltered dells and near springs. To most it is only a pleasantly scented plant used in simples and poultices, but in the hands of the rightful kings and those with great healing power its leaves, bruised in hot water, can recall the wounded from the shadow.

aspect.en: Sea-elves of the Lindon coast met at their daily craft — casting nets in the river-mouths, mending boats on the strand, working a small smack along the gulf — weathered and unhurried, knowing every current and tide. Toward travellers: calm, courteous coast-folk and a good source of passage and sea-lore for the respectful.

lore.en: Falathrim of the Lindon coasts met about their daily craft — casting nets in the river-mouths, mending boats on the strand, or working a small smack along the Gulf of Lhun. Weathered and unhurried, they know every current and tide of Harlindon's shores.

aspect.en: Large, armour-skinned freshwater eels whose grey horny scales let them burrow in riverbeds and lie disguised as stones; brought long ago from Númenor and now the dominant hunters of the southern Yellow Mountain rivers. Toward travellers: a hidden ambusher of the riverbed — what looks like a rock may strike.

lore.en: Distantly related to the Carnantor, the Sarnúmeni (Q. "West-stones"; sing. "Sarnúmen") are large, hard-skinned, freshwater Eels. Their name is derived from their grey, horny scales, which lend a Sarnúmen tremendous protection and enable them to burrow in riverbeds, camouflaging themselves as rocks. Since the mid-Second Age, when they came from their original home in Númenor and were carelessly introduced into the rivers and lakes of southern Endor, they have become the dominant hunter in the watershed of the Yellow Mountains (S. "Ered Laranor"; Q. "Orolanari"). Aside from great strength and huge teeth, Sarnúmeni are noted for having deadly barbs along their spine. These barbs are connected with poison glands, and anyone stepping on or handling one of these formidable Eels is in danger of being injected with a bluish nerve poison named for the Sarnúmen. Herbalists have been known to refine this liquid, creating a lethal (30th) poison that is feared all over southern Middle-earth. Fortunately, the liquid has an exceedingly limited life of its own and is extremely hard (-30) to handle without exposing oneself to its effects.

aspect.en: Hardy, ill-tempered cattle bred in the grey fields of Nurn to feed Mordor's armies — lean, half-wild beasts tended by slaves under the lash and suited to their harsh land. Toward travellers: bad-tempered and half-wild; no predator, but a sign one is deep in the Enemy's country.

lore.en: Hardy, ill-tempered cattle bred in the grey fields of Nurn to feed the armies of Mordor. Tended by slaves under the lash, they are lean, half-wild beasts suited to the harsh land that raises them.

aspect.en: A delicate white or pale, star- or bell-shaped flower of Gondor, blossoming in quiet meadows and on gentle slopes, often alongside mallos. Toward travellers: harmless and lovely, a sign of peaceful, tended country.

lore.en: Alfirin is a delicate white or pale flower of Gondor, often described as star-like or bell-shaped. It blossoms in quiet meads and along gentle slopes, frequently found together with mallos.

aspect.en: Grasshopper-like insects that breed in dry years into vast devouring swarms, stripping fields and pasture bare in hours. Toward travellers: a locust-year means famine; the darkening cloud of their flight is dreaded by every farmer.

lore.en: Grasshopper-like insects that breed in dry seasons into vast devouring swarms, stripping field and pasture bare in hours. A locust-year spells famine, and the darkening cloud of their flight is dreaded by every farmer.

aspect.en: Hardy nomadic herders grazing their sheep through the southern valleys. Toward travellers: tough, self-sufficient hill-folk, guarded with strangers but rarely aggressors.

lore.en: Hardy nomadic herders who graze their sheep in the southern valleys.

aspect.en: Trolls bred and kept at the hill of sorcery in southern Mirkwood, hardened to the Necromancer's service — crueller and better-handled than wild trolls, set to guard the dark hill and loosed on intruders and the local Elves and Woodmen. Toward travellers: disciplined, malevolent guard-beasts of an evil stronghold.

lore.en: Trolls kept and bred at Dol Guldur in southern Mirkwood, hardened to the Necromancer's service. Set to guard the hill of sorcery and its approaches, they are crueller and better-handled than wild Trolls, and are loosed on intruders and on the Wood-elves and Woodmen of the southern forest.

aspect.en: A site of the Dúnedain — a ranger-shelter, boundary-stone, cache or ruined steading of the Men of Westernesse, plainly made and well-hidden. Toward travellers: often still useful to those who know its secrets, a likely refuge for the ranger-wise.

lore.en: A site of the Dúnedain — a ranger-shelter, boundary-stone, cache or ruined steading of the Men of Westernesse. Plainly made and well-hidden, such places often still serve those who know their secrets.

aspect.en: A column of wretched captives — men, lesser orcs and other thralls — driven to labour under the whips of brutal orc slave-drivers. Toward travellers: the guards are violent and watchful; the broken slaves may beg for help, or turn on their masters given any chance.

lore.en: A column of wretched thralls — Men, lesser Orcs and other captives — driven to labor under the lash of Orc slave-drivers. The guards are brutal and watchful; the slaves, broken and desperate, may turn on their masters given the smallest chance.

aspect.en: A small, large-eared desert fox of Harad, abroad in the cool of the night, hunting in pairs or family groups for rodents and large insects and digging out sleeping reptiles; hunted for its bright auburn coat. Toward travellers: harmless and shy, a quick big-eared shape slipping through the desert dusk.

lore.en: Small, large-eared desert fox (Ap. Nightears, pl. Lisicavi) found in Harad, thriving in the cool of the desert night. It hunts in pairs or small family groups for rodents and large insects and digs out sleeping reptiles. It is hunted for its brilliant auburn coat.

aspect.en: A brutal, semi-nomadic people of Khand, southeast of Mordor — very dark-skinned, black-haired and red-eyed, tireless horsemen long swayed by Mordor and hardened by constant war. Toward travellers: hostile and warlike, allies of the Enemy — dangerous to meet on their lands or in war.

lore.en: The Variags live in the region of Khand, a semi-arid plateau which lies southeast of Mordor. They are a distinct race, but are occasionally confused with the Haradrim of Far Harad. In reality, they have as many ties to the Easterlings. Brutal and semi-nomadic, they have long been influenced by Mordor and the constant wars with their neighbors. Physical Character: Medium; men average 160 pounds, women 125 pounds. Extremely dark grey or black skin, straight black hair, and red or reddish brown eyes. Variags can travel for extreme periods on horseback with little or no rest. Medium; men average 5'9", women 5'3". Lifespan: Short, about 50-70 years. Variags are superb riders and handle both horses and camels well. +10 bonus to Offensive Bonuses when fighting from horseback (+5 bonus when fighting from camelback). Variags favor black and red clothing and wear richly adorned garb. Their armor is designed around hideous, frightening beast designs. They carry gold or gilded weapons. Always at war, Variags live a brutal and exciting life. Most are herders and raid the stocks of their enemies.

aspect.en: Old, dark-needled pines clinging to the steep valleys of Rhudaur and the upper Anduin, deeply rooted and enduring cold winds, thin soils and heavy snow. Toward travellers: harmless; a stern mark of high, cold, broken country.

lore.en: These ancient mountain pines cling to the steep valleys and hillsides of Rhudaur and the upper Anduin basin. Tall, dark-needled and deeply rooted, they endure cold winds, thin soils and heavy snow.

aspect.en: Small, dark-haired, independent tribes of the southern marshes and the mouths of Anduin, of mixed Daen and Southron blood, living as swamp-fishers largely beyond Gondor's reach. Toward travellers: keep to themselves in their fens, wary of outsiders and of any authority.

lore.en: Small, dark-haired, independent tribes in the Loeg Balimur and remote Ethir Anduin, believed to be of mixed Daen and Southron stock; they live as swamp fishermen largely outside Gondorian authority.[file:73]

aspect.en: A monstrous freshwater kraken of the lightless deeps — many-tentacled and immense; one lurks in the dammed lake before Moria's West Gate, set by Sauron's hatred to seize prey from the water's edge. Toward travellers: a lethal ambush from the water — long arms that snatch the unwary into the dark depths.

lore.en: Freshwater Kraken that normally reside in the pools of the Underdeeps. One emerged into the Sirannon by the West Gate of Moria, damming it into a gloomy lake and, driven by Sauron's hatred, preying on Dwarves and Orcs before it nearly seized Frodo as the Fellowship entered Moria in T.A. 3019.

aspect.en: Captains and intriguers of Umbar who stir the nomad clans against Gondor, using the southern borderlands as a staging-ground and the trade-roads as their target. Toward travellers: covert and dangerous — agitators and spies who work in the shadows against Gondor.

lore.en: After the Kin-strife, Umbarean and Haruze captains encouraged nomadic clans to migrate into the Aegardh, using Harondor as a staging ground against Gondor and the Hyarmenti trade road.[file:73]

aspect.en: The renowned horses bred and ridden by the Rohirrim, famed above all for speed and endurance. Toward travellers: spirited, loyal mounts — the pride of the Horse-lords, and not lightly parted with.

lore.en: Horses bred and ridden by the Rohirrim, known for their speed and endurance.

aspect.en: Bold red-tipped, gold-plumed eagles that rule the eastern skies — smaller kin of the Great Eagles but numerous, usually hunting goats, sheep and wild horses, and a real threat to travellers in their mountains. Toward travellers: aggressive for an eagle; they may stoop on people crossing their high ranges.

lore.en: The Red Eagle dominates the skies of the East. Smaller relatives of the Great Eagles, who are rare in eastern Endor, these magnificent predators are relatively numerous and pose a threat to travellers in the Red Mountains and Mountains of the Wind.
